Right, yeah? I’ve 'eard a bit about that. Bit of a fad, innit? Seems like everything’s got CBD in it now. Even dog treats! Bit mad, really. What’ve you been lookin’ at then? It's not really a fad, Liam. Think of it as, like, a natural alternative. Loads of people are finding it helps. I've read articles, seen the science… it’s genuinely interesting. Ben, have  you  ever considered trying it? You've been looking a bit stressed with uni lately. Nah, not for me. I’m alright. Bit of a sceptic, I am. All this fancy stuff… I just go for a run. Always has worked for me. Sorting out the head, you know? Plus, I'm saving up for that new graphics card. Priorities. Run’s good, Ben. Proper good. I’ve been getting back into it myself. Did a five-mile loop down by the canal yesterday. Felt brilliant. Though, you know, those new smartwatches are tempting. Tracking everything… steps, heart rate… it’s a bit much, isn’t it? A bit much maybe, Tom, but I’m addicted! Mine just buzzed, telling me I need to move. I'm halfway through a documentary on Netflix. Don’t tell it, but I might ignore it for another ten minutes. What’s everyone been watching lately? My mum’s obsessed with that Australian soap,  Neighbours . Utter rubbish, but she’s got the theme tune stuck in her head.  Neighbours ! Classic! My Auntie Brenda used to be glued to that. I'm more of a  Line of Duty  man, myself. Proper gripping, that. Though, Lizzie McAllister... she was something else, wasn't she? Gets right under your skin.  Line of Duty ’s brilliant. Adrian Dunbar, amazing. Actually, speaking of families, my cousin’s having a right drama. His dad’s decided to learn Parkour. At sixty-five! Apparently, he's watching YouTube tutorials and trying to jump over fences. My mum’s terrified. Sixty-five?! Parkour? That’s mental! My Grandpa tried to learn TikTok dances last year. Nearly pulled a muscle just trying to do that… what's it called? The Renegade? Looked like he was having a seizure. Oh, that’s brilliant! My Nan tried to join a Zumba class. Ended up just standing around feeling a bit flustered. Bless her. Has anyone seen those new Doc Martens everyone's wearing? The chunky platform ones?

…and don't forget the bug spray, Mum. Seriously, they're everywhere this year. Little beasties are proper eating us alive! I got bitten three times just sittin' in the garden yesterday. Right on me ankles, they were. Aye, they are a nuisance, lass. This summer's been a right breeding ground for 'em. You alright with the stuff I got last time? That citronella one? It’s alright, but it doesn't seem to be doin' much, does it? I reckon we need somethin' stronger. Like, a proper industrial-strength spray. Remember Dad used to use that stuff on the roses? Smelled like a chemical plant, but it worked. Dad just used to swat 'em. Worked most of the time. Your dad had a certain… approach, didn’t he, love? Bit more direct than a chemical plant. Right, bug spray it is. Should I add it to the list with the milk and bread? Actually, before we get too carried away with the chemical warfare, has anyone considered why there are so many insects this year? It could be linked to the unseasonably warm weather, the shift in rainfall patterns… just a thought. Oh, here we go, Mr. Consultant. Analyzing the insect population boom. I just want to  not  be eaten alive, Uncle David! Just observing, Eleanor. There’s a difference. And thinking about potential solutions beyond spraying everything. Perhaps some natural deterrents? Lavender, for example, can be quite effective. Lavender… now that's a thought. I've got some in the garden. Might put some sachets out. Speaking of solutions, you got that bite on your arm, Eleanor? Still itchy? It’s drivin’ me mad! It's swelling up a bit too. I've put cream on it, but it's not making much of a difference. It's right on the back of me hand, so I keep touching it and making it worse. Mum used to put vinegar on mine. Stopped the itch pretty quick. Vinegar’s good. Or baking soda paste. We’ve got both, haven't we? I'll grab some. Do you think you need to see a doctor, love? Nah, I don’t think so. Just a bit grumpy and itchy. I'll try the vinegar. Anything's better than this. Right, list then – bug spray, milk, bread, vinegar, dishwasher tablets… Oh, and ham! Gotta have ham for sandwiches tomorrow. Ham’s a good choice.

Honestly, Mrs. Davies is  determined  to make us suffer in P.E. today. Three laps of the field,  then  interval training. Like, who even  does  interval training willingly? Tell me about it! Mr. Harrison’s already got that gleam in his eye. The one that says, “prepare to be exhausted.” Did you see Chloe’s Insta story? She was wearing, like, the  most  amazing leggings. Seriously, where does she get them? Chloe and her expensive sportswear. Don’t even start me on Chloe. And yes, the laps were brutal. I think I pulled a muscle in my calf. A  slight  one, obviously, wouldn't want to feign injury. But still! Dramatic as always, Livvy. Probably just a cramp. Did you at least film it for TikTok? The whole, ‘struggling to breathe after just one lap’ thing is  gold . Nah. Didn’t have the energy. Plus, I was too busy trying not to collapse. Seriously though, Science is killing me. That lab report’s due on Friday and I still haven’t even started it. It's about cellular respiration, and I just... I don't get it. It's all diagrams and complicated words. I can help you with that! I actually understood that lesson a bit. It's basically just how cells get their energy, right? Think of it like… like the food we eat turns into energy for our bodies. Right. But  how ? That’s the bit I’m struggling with. And the mitochondria… all that talk about the ‘powerhouse of the cell’... it’s proper confusing. Okay, okay, I’ll explain. Basically, the food gets broken down, and then… …stuff happens with oxygen, and then bam! Energy. The mitochondria are where all the good stuff happens. I watched that Joe Hanson video about it – you know, 'Smarter Every Day'? He explains it really well. Oh yeah! I love him! He's so good at making science not completely boring. Have you seen his latest one about the hummingbird’s wings? Mental! Speaking of Youtube, did you see that Sarah Magpie video about the new MAC eyeshadow palette? Yes! It’s gorgeous! I’m saving up for it, but it's taking forever. Mum keeps saying I need to be saving for, like, a  house  instead of eyeshadow. Honestly! Don't they understand the importance of a good highlight? Tell me about it. My mum’s just obsessed with sensible things.

…and honestly, I’m convinced it’s not  just  a cold. My sinuses are proper throbbing. Feels like a secondary infection brewing, like something’s lurking. Could be anything, really. You sound awful, love. You've been resting, haven't you? Cambridge isn’t exactly the healthiest place when you’re under the weather, all those students coughing and spluttering everywhere. Have you had any fever? Nah, no fever. Just… this relentless head pressure and a cough that won’t shift. It’s put me right off my food, mind. I had a bit of that lentil soup you made last night, trying to be healthy, and now I’m questioning everything. Remember that time Dad got that awful food poisoning on holiday in Spain? Practically spent the whole week tethered to the bathroom. Terrifying. Oh, God, yes. He was horrifying, wasn’t he? A truly cinematic experience of gastrointestinal distress. But lentils are usually pretty safe. Maybe it was something else entirely? Did you get that flu jab this year? Aye, got it in October. Though honestly, half the time I reckon these jabs are just placebo. Remember all that fuss about the swine flu? They were practically force-feeding us vaccines. Then it was gone. Like, poof. Well, statistically, they help. And even if it's just a little bit of protection, it’s better than nothing. Speaking of protection... I was reading a paper yesterday, fascinating stuff, on AI and body language recognition. They're developing algorithms that can detect subtle changes in micro-expressions, predicting things like discomfort or even deception with surprising accuracy. Deception? Like a computer’s going to know when I’m fibbing about how bad my head hurts? Sounds like something out of a Lloyd Grossman game show. “Spot the Subtle Sign of Sinus Pressure!” It’s more complex than that, but the principle's the same. They analyze minute muscle movements, pupil dilation… even skin temperature. Apparently, hospitals are experimenting with it to monitor patients, flagging potential issues  before  they escalate. Imagine, detecting early signs of sepsis just by watching a patient's face. Blimey. It’s a bit dystopian, innit? All those cameras, tracking our every blip. Makes you feel like you're living in some CCTV-regulated goldfish bowl. I'd much rather just have a hot toddy and a lie-down. There's ethical considerations, certainly. But the potential benefits for healthcare are immense.

Alright, alright, settle down, Eleanor. It's just Facebook. It's trying to anticipate what you want, and occasionally misses the mark spectacularly. At least it’s offering something. I’ve been staring at the same advert for gardening trowels for three days.      It's not just the content, David, it's the sheer volume! I spent nearly an hour last night scrolling, feeling like I should be doing something more productive, yet utterly consumed. And all I learned was that apparently, everyone in Cheshire is obsessed with alpaca farming.      Alpaca farming. Well, that  is  a modern pastime. Though I rather preferred a good croquet match in my day, myself. Did you see Betty’s post about the traffic at the Trafford Centre? Absolute gridlock, she said.      Oh, don't remind me! I braved it this morning to get ingredients for your lemon drizzle, Mum. It was utter chaos. A complete standstill. I felt like I’d aged ten years just inching along. They should really do something about that bottleneck near Debenhams.      Bottlenecks are a fact of life, my dear. Always have been. Try navigating London in the 1950s – that was a bottleneck. Though admittedly, there were fewer SUVs.      Grandpa’s right, Eleanor. Perspective. Besides, you managed to get the lemons, didn't you? And Mum’s delighted. How about that ‘Uncut’ magazine you were mentioning? Any good?      It was fascinating, actually. A retrospective on early Bowie. Really detailed, explored his influences. Quite sad, reading about how unsure he was about ‘Space Oddity’ initially. Thought it was a bit of a throwaway track. Can you imagine?      Oh, David Bowie! Such a talent. Although, I do prefer a bit of Gilbert & Sullivan myself. Much more civilized. I was quite fond of the Savoy Operas when I was Headmistress. The girls used to put on wonderful productions.      Gilbert & Sullivan were admirable. Disciplined. Unlike this modern… noise. All thumping and shouting. Give me a good chorus from ‘The Mikado’ any day.      You two are hopeless! Grandpa, you’re trying to reclaim the 19th century, and Mum’s stuck on the Savoy! Anyway, I was thinking, should I post a picture of the lemon drizzle on Facebook? Show off a bit?      Go for it. Though be prepared for a barrage of comments about using organic lemons and sustainable sugar. People get very passionate about that sort of thing.      A photograph, Eleanor? Goodness. Back in my day, we’d have simply offered a slice to a neighbour.

…and honestly, Bernard, shifting those Victorian hat pins was a right palaver. People just weren’t interested, you see. Said they were 'fussy' and 'unnecessary.' Can you imagine? Proper little works of art, some of 'em, silver filigree and whatnot. Still, a bit of breathing space is welcome, innit? This working party’s been a bit of a slog even with the lovely weather. Absolutely, Penelope. A bit of respite. Though, I confess, I’m finding it quite restorative actually, being outside, getting the hands dirty. Something I haven’t done in decades, truthfully. Reminds one of simpler things. You were saying about the hat pins? A bit like the market for my early prototypes, I suppose. People resistant to change. Oh, did you now? Well, you always did have a clever head on you, Bernard. Something to do with printing, wasn’t it? I can’t rightly recall the details, you see. My mind’s scattered these days, what with the gallery and…well, everything. Printing systems, yes. Quite a long and rather circuitous journey, really. Began with an idea for automating a particular element of offset lithography. It was terribly inefficient then, the registration process. Endless manual tweaks. Honestly, the wastage! I spent years, really, developing a system - a series of lenses and mirrors, ultimately – that could automatically maintain perfect registration. Called it 'OptiAlign'. Silly name in retrospect, isn’t it? Well, it sounds proper technical, that does. Automatic registration… Sounds like sorcery to me! It  felt  like sorcery at the time. The first presentation in Germany, at Drupa in Düsseldorf – that was a pivotal moment. Their dedication to efficiency there is remarkable. They practically  live  for optimised production. The initial reaction was… skepticism. But then they saw it in action. The near-zero error rate. The speed. They were practically fighting over the rights. Germany, you said? Did you have to go live over there then? No, no. It was all exhibitions, initially. We'd set up a demonstration booth, I'd explain the principles... show them how it worked. Initially, I went alone; just me and a briefcase full of diagrams. Awkward, that first time. Trying to explain complex optics to hardened engineers through a translator. Then, we brought in a marketing team, of course. Properly rebranded the whole thing - 'PrecisionPrint' it became. Much catchier. And the company boomed. I was overseeing licensing agreements, travelling all over Europe – France, Italy… the champagne flowed, let me tell you.

Honestly, Dad, Mrs. Davies  still  hasn’t marked my essay on Wordsworth. It was ages ago! And she keeps going on about ‘lexical ambiguity’ and I’m just, like, what even is that? Sounds like something you’d find on a dodgy website. Lexical ambiguity, lass, is just a fancy way of saying a word can have more than one meaning. Wordsworth was full of it, deliberately. Playing with the language, see? Like ‘valley’ – could be a geographical feature, could be a state of mind. Clever, that fella. Yeah, but she's making out like it's some monumental discovery. It's just… words having different meanings. Right? Anyway, what about university? I finally looked at some courses, and the philosophy ones… blimey. So much reading. Are you sure I should even bother? Bother? Course you should bother! Philosophy's not just dry books, love. It’s thinking. Real thinking. About why things are the way they are. And you’re a good thinker, you are. Cambridge has a cracking philosophy course, you know. Or Durham. Nice bit of countryside there. Better than being stuck in Manchester, eh? True. Though I'm not sure about Cambridge, sounds a bit… posh. What’s that service station up ahead? We need a brew, I’m parched. And a pasty! We  are  going to Cornwall, after all. Right you are. Let’s grab ourselves a sausage roll too. Always fancied trying to find a proper Cornish pasty. Not these dodgy versions they sell everywhere else. Speaking of which, are you sure you’ve got the directions sorted for when we get to St Ives? You were looking at the map earlier. Yeah, I think so. It's a bit tricky, all these little lanes. I reckon it’s somewhere near Zennor… or is it Zenor? I can never remember. And is it spelled with two 'n's? Zenor. One 'n'. It's a proper old place, Zenor. Loads of history hiding in them hills. It’s got a proper tongue-twister of a name too - you try saying ‘Penzance’ quickly! Reminds me, you know, the way language changes… when I was a lad, everyone said “Worcestershire” exactly the same as “Worcester.” Now it's all fancy with the extra ‘sh-ire’. So true! It's wild, innit? Like how people used to say  “ain’t”  – everyone thought it was terrible grammar, but now it’s practically everywhere.

Aye, your mum's a worry, innit? Bless her heart, though. She’s always been like that. So, this shepherd’s pie… it smells absolutely banging, by the way. You’ve really outdone yourself, Leo. Cheers, Liv. Just a bit of comfort food, y'know? After the week I’ve had… The building site's a right mess at the moment, the foreman's gone on holiday and the new bloke seems to think concrete flies when you tell it to. Concrete doesn’t fly, does it? Never has. Though, things used to move a bit quicker back then, in me day. Less… fuss. Tell me about it! Deadlines are piling up at the conference centre. Some of these delegates, they want everything perfect. Like, perfectly vegan, perfectly ethically sourced, perfectly aligned with the latest trend… it's exhausting. Did I tell you about the request for edible confetti made from dehydrated kale? Kale confetti? Seriously? That sounds… grim. Kale? Fancy. We used to get glitter. Not edible, mind. Just… glitter. Covered everything for days. Your mum, she used to hate it. Said it got in the stew. Right, my mum's always complaining about something getting in the stew. It’s her thing. She’ll moan if a rogue carrot dares to peek out. Speaking of stew, my nan's making her famous Lancashire hotpot for Sunday. You two fancy coming round? Sunday? Yeah, sounds good. Need a good plateful of proper food after the week I've had. Less kale confetti, I hope. Hotpot… now that’s a meal. Proper comfort food. Gets cold right through you. Good memories of hotpot. My sister used to... well, she was a right handful. Always sneaking bits off me plate. Sounds like a familiar story! My little brother’s the same. Always trying to nick my chocolate. So, Mr. Retired, got anything interesting on your hands these days beyond reminiscing about sneaky siblings? Not much, lass. Keep busy enough feeding the birds in the garden. And watching the telly, of course. Agnes, my niece, keeps trying to get me into these computer courses. Keeps saying I’m missing out. Doesn’t understand, does she? I've lived a full life. Don’t need no computer. I get it. Technology can be a pain sometimes. I’m alright with the basics, but anything beyond that... forget it. I’d rather be laying bricks, honestly.

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt a bit… pointless, ya know? Like, I’m slinging pints all day, serving chips, and trying to remember who ordered a lime and soda with extra ice. It pays the bills, mind, but it’s not exactly using my degree, is it? I mean, I studied History at Uni, for crying out loud. Ancient Rome! Not… sticky floors and spilled lager. I completely get that feeling, Liam. The disconnect between what you studied and what you ended up doing. It’s surprisingly common. I had a similar wobble myself, actually, when I first graduated. I was all set to be a translator, full of romantic notions of working in international diplomacy. Ended up teaching GCSE French to fifteen-year-olds who’d rather be on TikTok. Right? It's mad, isn’t it? Everyone expects you to have a five-year plan after Uni. Like, “So, what’s your grand strategy for world domination?” I just… haven’t got one, really. This bartending gig was just meant to be temporary while I looked for something better. But it's been nearly two years now. Two years is a good chunk of time. But don’t beat yourself up about it. It’s about building experience, finding out what you  don't  want, as much as what you do. Plus, bartending... you develop some seriously transferable skills, don't you? Customer service, problem-solving under pressure, remembering a million different orders… True, I reckon. I’m pretty good at diffusing awkward situations, eh? Had a guy trying to pay for his pint with a Pokemon card last week. That was a fun one to handle. What about you? Still enjoying teaching? Seems pretty hectic, all the marking and lesson planning. It’s a mixed bag, to be honest. Some days are brilliant – when a student finally 'gets' a grammar concept, or they produce a really insightful essay. Other days… well, you know. Teenage angst and forgotten homework. But I genuinely like seeing them learn. It's rewarding, even if it's tiring. I'm actually thinking about doing a CELTA qualification next year. It's a teaching diploma, a bit more advanced. Blimey, ambitious! That’s good though, having a goal. Where have you been driving lately? The traffic around here is awful. Oh, don't even get me started on the M6! I've been mostly sticking to the A38 down to Stourbridge to see my parents.

Honestly, Nigel, you were rattling on about bell ringing for a good fifteen minutes! I'm parched, and I’m sure Margaret’s getting peckish. We’re late for break time, you know. Now, now, Brenda. A bit of Norfolk heritage isn’t hurtin’ nobody. A good peal o’ bells, it’s a thing o’ beauty, it is. Keeps you sharp, mind. Requires a good memory, you see. Not like nowadays, where everyone’s glued to their little… rectangles. I find it quite soothing, actually. The rhythm. Reminds me a bit of a well-balanced quarterly report, come to think of it. Predictable, yet capable of surprising nuance. Oh, here we go with the business metaphors again, David. Right, Nigel, about driving… you still absolutely refuse to let Margaret near the wheel, don’t you? Even for a short hop to the shops? Now, Brenda, you know I’m only lookin’ out for ‘er. Her eyesight ain’t what it used to be. And that roundabout down by the Tesco, it's a trial, it is. Goin' ‘round and ‘round like a… like a dizzy pigeon. Best I keep hold o' the reins, I reckon. Nigel, with all due respect, you haven't driven further than the village green in five years. Margaret's perfectly capable. Plenty of older drivers out there… Easier said than done, David. Easier said than done. Besides, I’m thinkin’ about that trip to Gambia, remember? We're gonna need to be sure I can handle long distances. Gambia! Oh, that sounds lovely. Remember we looked at those brochures? The beaches… all those lovely bright colours… But Nigel, honestly, you need to build up your confidence. We can start small, just a drive to Norwich. Perhaps a driving refresher course? I’m sure there are excellent programs out there. And we can look into it. While we’re on the subject of helping people, I was thinking... Margaret mentioned wanting to do something for that local childminding charity. Yes! That's a smashing idea, David. I used to love it, mind you, looking after the little ones. It kept me busy. We could make a donation box. Decorate it nicely. Something eye-catching. And perhaps a banner? "Support Local Childminders" or something like that. Somewhere visible in the village. A banner, eh? Might need somethin’ strong, the wind 'ere can be fierce. And we'll need a good spot.

You're having a laugh, right? That sounds terrifying! I’d delete it instantly. I’m still trying to figure out Duolingo - getting decent at Spanish is a much more productive obsession. Nah, it’s actually pretty unnerving. It uses AI, apparently. It learns your patterns. But hey, at least it's more interesting than learning verb conjugations. Speaking of unnerving, did you guys see the trailer for "The Hollow"? The one everyone's talking about? Oh my god, yes! Liam sent me a link last night. The cinematography alone is giving me serious anxiety. And the story...locked-in-a-cabin-with-monsters? Hard pass. I'm sticking to rom-coms. My heart can’t take any more existential dread. Rom-coms are fine, but even those are starting to feel…formulaic. At least "The Hollow" looks visually striking. Though, I agree, Liam has terrible taste. Remember that Norwegian horror film he made us watch last year? I couldn’t sleep for a week! Oh, the one with the…goat ritual? God, that was awful! Seriously, Liam needs to broaden his horizons. Anyway, did you hear from Chloe? She was supposed to be back from Ibiza yesterday. No! I sent her a message this morning, nothing. I’m starting to worry. She promised she’d send pics. I want to see if Jake was actually being a sweetheart, or if he was just putting on a show for Instagram. Jake. He's all surface, isn’t he? He’s probably already moved on to someone else. Girls in Ibiza…it’s a revolving door, isn’t it? Harsh, but probably true. Remember when she said he’d booked a private beach club for her? Seems extravagant for someone who’s apparently still 'finding himself' as a musician. Right? My gut says she's being strung along. She needs to come home and we need to go out and drown her sorrows in…what are we in the mood for? Pizza? Thai? I'm starving. This discussion about boy drama has made me appreciate a dependable carbohydrate. Pizza sounds amazing. Definitely pizza. Massive one with everything. So, Chloe's drama aside, anyone else thinking about holidays themselves? I looked at flights to Greece last night. Super cheap in September. Greece! Oh, that’s tempting. Rhodes looked beautiful, apparently. But…work’s been insane. I don't know if I could swing it.

…and I’m tellin’ ya, Bernard, that automatic gearbox in that new Jag, it’s a right travesty. A travesty, I say! All the feelin’ gone. The connection to the road. Used to be, you  knew  what your engine was doin’. Now it’s just…whirr, click, go. No sense of it at all. You always were a stickler for a good gear change, Arthur. Remember that Morris Minor you had? The one that kept jumpin’ out of second? Jumpin’ out of second? That’s puttin’ it mildly. It was practically tryin’ to escape the chassis! Still, it had character, didn't it? Unlike these modern things. All polished chrome and digital this and that. No backbone. There you are, both of you. Help yourselves. Arthur, you’re going on again about cars, aren't you? Honestly, you could talk about the internal combustion engine for hours. Can’t help it, Doreen. It's a fascination. I spent my life buildin’ bridges, Doreen. Understandin' how things  worked , how they connected. A car’s just a smaller, more complicated bridge, innit? Movin’ instead of stayin’ still. Bridges are all well and good, Arthur, but they don't get you home in the evening. Exactly! Which brings me to a point. How’s everyone gettin’ back tonight? Doreen, you catchin’ the bus? Yes, the 47. Leaves at half past five. Should be alright. Though last week it was twenty minutes late. Absolute chaos. Twenty minutes! That’s scandalous. Bernard? You got your nephew comin’ for you again? Aye. Young Kevin. Gets me back. Though he drives like a maniac. Swerves all over the place. Gives me the jitters, it does. Should learn to relax a bit. Being a young lad shouldn’t be that stressful. Youngsters today, eh? Always in a rush. Always wanting it all right now. Back in  my  day… Arthur, please. We’ve all heard the stories about your day. Let Bernard get a word in edgeways. Thanks, Doreen. I was just thinkin', mind you, that Kevin’s got a right smart car. One of them electrics. Quiet as a mouse, it is. Electric, you say? Tera-rific! Zero emissions and probably about as much connection to the road as a trolley. Tell you what, Bernard, I'd rather take the Morris Minor, jumpin’ second gear and all, than one of those battery-powered contraptions. You’re impossible, Arthur. At least they're better for the environment.

…and honestly, the sat nav kept trying to send us down this tiny lane! A lane, Mary! On the M6! It was utterly ridiculous. I had to override it completely. I swear, these things are more trouble than they're worth sometimes. Oh, you know how they are. Technology, isn’t it? Promises the world, delivers… well, something else entirely. Reminds me of the time I tried to teach myself to use one of those fancy calculators for the Leaving Cert. Had the manual thicker than a novel, and I still ended up using a ruler and doing it all manually! Much more reliable, really. Reliable’s a relative term, love. Remember those slide rules? Now  that’s  unreliable. You squint at those little numbers and hope for the best. At least the sat nav gives you a direction, even if it’s a spectacularly wrong one. Fair point, Dad. Alright, so we managed to navigate the horrifying shortcut attempt, and we’re almost at your place, Mary. How are you feeling about the move? Still convinced you’re going to miss Dublin terribly? Oh, I am, love. Terribly. Forty years I lived there. It’s not just the place itself, you know? It’s the familiarity. The routines. Knowing where the best bakeries are, which bus to catch… It's all going. I keep picturing myself wandering around this new village, utterly lost, even with that…that contraption . You'll adapt, Mary. You always do. Remember when you decided to take up watercolour painting? Thought you'd have a gallery showing in a month. Oh, don't remind me! That was a disaster. My hydrangeas looked like exploding purple cabbages. Still, I persevered. See? Perseverance. Exactly what you’ll need for the move. And honestly, the house looks lovely in the pictures. Much bigger than your flat. Space for all your books, at least! It is, thank goodness. Though downsizing has been…an experience. All those years accumulating things… old textbooks, dusty journals… you wouldn’t believe it. I feel like I'm throwing away pieces of my life. Rubbish, love. You’re just decluttering. That’s what Sarah keeps telling me, anyway. Decluttering. Easier said than done, though, when you've got a lifetime of memories wrapped up in every chipped teacup. Dad’s right, it's hard. I'm the same with photos. I have boxes of them.

Honestly, Mum, it’s just… infuriating. People are so awful. Like, posting those videos of cats falling? Cruel! And then stealing bikes… seriously? Right? That’s what I was saying. Though, speaking of infuriating, I have some good news about your bike. My bike? What? You’re joking! Did… did they find it? I am not joking, love. The police called this morning. They found it. In St. Leonards, of all places. Apparently, a couple of lads tried to strip it down for parts, but thankfully a local shop owner recognised it from the pictures you posted on Insta. No way! Seriously? Insta? Oh my god! That's amazing. How, like, did they even… did you send them the post? No, darling,  you  did. Remember when you tagged the bike shop, 'Ride Hastings', in that picture of you cycling down the seafront last week? The owner, Dave, he saw the "missing" post you made and put two and two together. He called the police straight away. He's a good egg, that Dave. Said he’s seen this happen too many times. Honestly, social media, eh? Used for posting cat videos  and  helping find stolen bikes. That's brilliant! Ride Hastings! I’ll have to thank him properly. I can't believe it. I was so gutted when it got nicked. I mean, that bike was practically an extension of me. I use it to get everywhere – college, the beach with Chloe, even just for getting a pasty! Well, it's back now. They said it's a bit scuffed up, and one of the lights is broken, but otherwise it seems okay. I'm picking it up this afternoon. Fancy a ride out later? Maybe down to the High Street for an ice cream? Oh my god, yes! Definitely! I'm starving anyway. What are you having for lunch? I was thinking maybe we could order that new pizza place, 'The Slice of Life’? They do that spicy one with the chorizo and jalapenos… That sounds lovely, darling. Though, if we're being honest, I'm craving a proper Sunday roast. All the trimmings. Remember Grandma's roasts? Yeah, but they were  huge ! And the gravy was a bit… much. Still, it was always nice having everyone round. Thinking about college, actually, I had a chat with Mr. Davies, the Head of Art. He reckons I should apply for the Foundation year.

Speaker_1 :   Oh, goodness! Sounds like my commute on a Monday morning, just with fewer spreadsheets. Right, I’m claiming Birmingham. That’s gotta give me a strategic advantage.   Speaker_2 :   Birmingham? Eleanor, you’ve left me completely exposed! You know I needed that route to Cardiff! Honestly, you're ruthless. This is why I prefer building railroads - less direct confrontation. Not like playing with a South African teacher!      Ruthless? I’m strategic! Besides, you’ve got plenty of options, Rhys. Don’t be such a drama queen. And let's not start on where I was born. It's a perfectly respectable place, just with better sunshine!   Speaker_3 :   You were always a whirlwind, Elen. Even as a little girl climbing the jacaranda tree in your garden. Always aiming for the highest branches.      See, Gwyn remembers! Unlike some people who are too busy accusing me of railway sabotage.   Speaker_4 :   Sabotage? Now, now, Rhys. Let the girl have her Birmingham! Besides, you Welsh are known for your cunning, aren't you? I remember when I was working in Singapore, a Welsh accountant practically ran that entire branch. Sharpest bloke I ever met. Good at figures, he was. Nearly as good as my mam used to be with a bara brith - that's a fruit cake, for those of you not from around here.   Speaker_5 :   Dai, you always bring up mam’s bara brith! You and your memories. It was good, mind you, but you exaggerate. It wasn’t  that  good. And frankly, bringing food into this conversation makes me ravenous. Are we ordering pizza again tonight? I'm absolutely starving after that trek up from the station.      Pizza  again , Mairwen? We had pizza last night! Plus, that awful buffet car food is still lingering in my memory. Shouldn't we try to be a bit more… adventurous? Maybe find a decent pub grub place?      Adventurous? Rhys, you spent the entire train journey complaining about the lack of decent Wi-Fi. "Adventurous" isn't exactly your style.      Rhodes is right, though. Maybe something with some proper Welsh flavour. A bit of cawl, perhaps?      Cawl? Now that’s an idea! With a bit of Welsh cheese on the side. Proper comfort food. Though, good cawl takes time, doesn’t it? Not something you can just whip up after a long day of train travel and Ticket to Ride.      Good point, Dai. And honestly, after wrestling with those train tickets and trying to decipher that timetable, I’m not exactly up for a gourmet cooking experience.

Right, that’s it. I’m officially declaring war on Baltic. Three years running, you’ve monopolized it. It's just… unfair. Unfair? Come on, love. It’s Monopoly. Strategic acquisition, that's all. And I’ve been  remarkably  strategic. Besides, you were dithering about whether to buy Reading. Reading! No one ever lands on Reading. Dithering? I was assessing the risk! You just blindly snap things up without a second thought. Remember last Christmas at your Aunt Penelope’s? You bought Park Lane before I’d even finished saying "should I…?" It was a steal! And Aunt Penelope's sherry was flowing freely. Makes you more decisive, doesn’t it? Speaking of which, are you having another glass of that rather questionable cider your dad’s brewed this year? It smells… fungal. It’s rustic! And yes, I am. It balances out the sheer intensity of your capitalist hoarding. Honestly, it's exhausting playing Monopoly with you. You treat it like a full-time profession. Well, someone’s got to bring order to the chaos. It's a microcosm of the free market, isn’t it? Supply and demand, ruthless competition… fascinating, really. Though, perhaps a little better applied to, you know, actual economics. Oh, I’m sure your students are  thrilled  to be learning about supply and demand from a hardened Monopoly player. Do you ever feel guilty about bankrupting people? Even in a game? Only if they resist. It's a game of dominance, Elara! Like pubs in this country, really. It's all about claiming territory. Look at the history of pub culture – the old alehouses, the rivalries between brewers, landlords fighting over their clientele. It's a constant power struggle, slightly less formalized than Monopoly, but the principle's the same. That's… unexpectedly insightful. I hadn’t thought of it like that. It's true, isn’t it? The whole pub ritual. It's not just about the drinks themselves. It's about belonging, about staking a claim on a social space. The designated table, your usual spot at the bar… it's all part of building your little kingdom. Exactly! And the rituals around drinking – the rounds, the toasts, the conversations… it's a carefully constructed system of social interaction. And quite British, wouldn't you say? I doubt you'd find quite the same level of formalized drinking culture in, say, Scandinavia. Much more relaxed.

Tell me about it! My flat in London had a communal bin area that was perpetually overflowing with… well, let's just say things you don’t  want  to see at 8 am. This feels almost luxurious in comparison, having individual bins. Though learning the system  is  a bit daunting. I've printed out Kerrie's guide, though. Twice. You and your guides! It's bins, Elara, not rocket science. Just chuck it in the right one. Though I did accidentally put a pizza box in the recycling last week. Kerrie nearly had a heart attack. Said something about contamination and the whole lot being rejected. Oh, don't fuss, Liam. It happens. The council back home in Swansea, they're pretty lenient. They just leave a little note on the bin sometimes. You’ll adapt. Speaking of adapting, you two moving house so soon after finishing your postgrad and… Liam, your project coordination gig? Bit ambitious, isn’t it? It feels that way sometimes, yes. But the flat was tiny, and ridiculously expensive for what it was. Plus, everything’s so close to Kerrie here, it makes sense. I'm hoping to make a proper go of my freelance admin work from the new place. My postgraduate actually gave me a good foundation, didn't it? All that research, organisation… comes in handy. Don’t undersell yourself, Elara. Your masters was seriously impressive. Kerrie was saying just the other day how clever you are. And the project… it’s a chance to work on some really exciting stuff, big renewable energy initiatives. It's not stable, but… it’s worth the risk. Least I think so. Renewable energy, eh? That’s a good shout. My nephew's doing something similar at Cardiff University. Bless him, always with the eco-friendly schemes. Makes me proud, though. Although, thinking of energy, have you looked at the energy ratings on the white goods? Liam, did you check the washing machine? These newer ones guzzle less water, apparently. Important for the environment, and the bills! We haven't started appliance shopping yet. It's all a bit overwhelming! I’ve been researching induction hobs – Kerrie raves about hers. It’s supposed to be easier to clean. And safer, apparently, no hot surfaces. Yeah, inductions are good. Less chance of burning yourself trying to retrieve a stray dinner. Speaking of which, this roast is fantastic, Kerrie.

Honestly, Mum, this traffic is mental. Absolutely mental. I swear, the North Circular is a vortex of stressed-out drivers and exhaust fumes. It is a bit heavy, yes. Though you’ve always said that, haven't you? Every single time we’ve driven anywhere remotely busy. You were complaining about traffic when you were practically five, kicking the back of my seat. Okay, fair. But this is different! Look at that bloke in the van, flashing his lights like he owns the road. Road rage is a real thing, innit? I nearly had a heart attack when he cut us off. Don’t let him get to you, love. It's not worth it. Some people just aren’t having a good day, or a good life even. Focus on the driving. So, about TLS... you secured your ticket? Yeah, got it just as the slots opened. Thankfully. Nearly missed out. I’m so hyped, Mum! You know how much I love that festival. The atmosphere, the writers... It’s brilliant. Proper brilliant. Hoping to snag a few signed copies this year. Think I’ll go for Sebald this time. Sebald, good choice. Proper thoughtful stuff. Much better than that influencer you were raving about last year. Remember? The one who writes about… lifestyle, was it? Don’t remind me. I was young and easily swayed by algorithms. My bad. It was a phase. Anyway, talking of things I’m hyped about… did you sort out your present for Auntie Carol’s birthday? I’m thinking about it. It's proving difficult. She’s got everything, you know? I was toying with getting her a first edition of something… maybe a TLS reprint from the 1950s. Something with a bit of history. That’s actually a really good idea! Classy. Way better than another scented candle, which is all she ever seems to get. Though, you said first edition… how much are those going for these days? Far too much for my budget, I’m afraid. More likely a nice reprint. Speaking of budgets… work’s been chaotic. That young chap, Jeremy, submitted a manuscript; it was utterly dreadful – prose like wet cardboard, and a plot that resembled a tangled ball of yarn. Trying to tell him it needs a complete overhaul is going to be… interesting. Ouch. That’s a tough one. So, digital or print for submissions these days, then?

Aye, reet mortified! You were fair shoutin', weren't ya? I could 'ear you all the way back at the caravan! Did you see 'is face, though? Little blighter just looked at me like I’d offered ‘im a free dinner. You were waving your arms about like you were conducting an orchestra, Sarah! Proper theatre. Poor dad just stood there, open-mouthed. Honestly, it was a highlight of the whole holiday! We were all knackered from the sun, and you provided the entertainment. Did you manage to get a photo of it? Nah, the adrenaline was pumpin' too much! I was tryin' to salvage what was left of the chips, ya know? Thankfully Kev managed to get a picture from across the beach. Should send it to you lot. Right mess, that was. You looked like a right lunatic, love. But in a good way, mind. Better than me struggling with the inflatable flamingo, anyway. Remember that, lads? Nearly drowned myself trying to get the thing in the sea. Oh, I remember the flamingo incident, Tom. The lifeguard nearly had a fit! Honestly, you wrestled that thing like you were in a WWE match. I thought you were going to give it a headbutt! He did look a bit desperate, didn’t he? Still, at least  someone  was havin' a laugh. This holiday’s been a right corker, though, proper good memories. Remember that little cafe in St Ives? The one with the pasties? Oh god yes! Those pasties were incredible! Best I've ever tasted. I'm still dreaming about them. We should try and find somewhere that does similar ones back here. 'Kay, you and me can open a pasty shop then! You do the fancy customer service, and I'll be in the kitchen makin' 'em. We’ll be millionaires! Don’t be daft, Liam! I've got accounts to do, remember? Semi-Senior, I am. Got to maintain a respectable image, ya know. Can't be managin' a pasty shop down the street! Let her dream, Sarah. Everyone needs a side hustle. Besides, you're good at numbers. You could figure out the best way to make a profit on pasties. Right, right. Let's stick to reminiscing for now. Anyone remember the karaoke night? Kev tried to sing Bohemian Rhapsody. Oh, don't remind me! That was... something else. Like a strangled cat trying to yodel.

…and the beauty of it, Moira, really is the sheer isolation. Just you, the canvas tent, and the blizzard swirling around you. It's… cleansing, you know? Strips away all the noise. Proper calming for the mind. Cleansing, aye, but brutal too, isn't it, Arthur? I understand the appeal of the solitude, I do. Years in nursing teach you to value quiet. But facing a Scottish winter, on purpose? I’m still trying to wrap my head around it. You're not exactly spring chickens, you know! Come on, Mum, don't be like that. Dad's been prepping for this for months. He showed me his new down sleeping bag – looked like a giant marshmallow! He even got those heated socks. Luxury wild camping, that’s what he’s doing! Luxury? Don't be daft, laddie. The socks are just a bit of insurance, that's all. Helps ward off frostbite. It's about preparation, see? Layers, waterproofs, knowing your route, understanding the weather patterns. It's not reckless, it’s... calculated risk. And the training! Don’t forget the cross-country skiing I’ve been doing. Keeps the old legs ticking over. Calculated risk? Last time you went climbing in the Lake District, you ended up stuck on a ledge for six hours waiting for the rescue team. ‘Calculated’ wasn’t the word I’d have used back then. That was… an unfortunate incident. Lessons were learned, Moira. I'm far more cautious now. And besides, this is different. This is about respecting the environment, becoming part of it. You notice things you wouldn't otherwise. How the snow crystals form, the way the wind whispers through the trees… the silence. It's… spiritual, in a way. I can see that, Dad. I mean, I’ve done a bit of hiking, but never anything like this. What’s the biggest difference you find from, say, a normal camping trip? Oh, colossal difference, Robbie. A normal camping trip is… superficial. You're observing nature. Wild winter camping, you're  in  nature. You're experiencing it on its rawest terms. It teaches you resilience, young man. You learn to rely on yourself, to solve problems with limited resources. And the views! The landscapes are utterly transformed by a blanket of snow. It’s… untouched. I suppose there's something to be said for pushing yourself. I see it in my patients all the time, the need to overcome adversity.

Honestly, Liam, you wouldn’t  believe  the email I got today. About a corrupted corpus file. It was, like, the entire early 20th-century dialect collection. Just…gone. Poof. Like someone dropped it in the North Sea. Corrupted? That's…intense, for a Tuesday. Did you manage to recover anything? Aye, eventually. It took hours. Hours I could’ve spent reading “Wuthering Heights” again! Honestly, that Heathcliff and Cathy thing… it's just gut-wrenching every time. I’m starting to think Cathy was deliberately being difficult. Difficult? She was torn between societal expectations and passionate love. Hardly a simple case of being difficult, Elara. Bronte was brilliant at portraying the complexities of human emotion. I know, I know, academically speaking. But just, like,  communicate  a bit, lass! He’s offering you a life, security… and she chooses miserable moors and a brooding millionaire who shouts a lot? Bit mad, innit? Reminds me a bit of my Auntie Brenda and that bloke who collected gnomes. A whole garden full of ceramic gnomes. Ceramic gnomes? Right. Well, Heathcliff's brooding and shouting at least offer a degree of dramatic flair over garden ornaments. Speaking of dramatic, have you seen "Oppenheimer"? I finally got around to it. No! Still haven't! Everyone was going on about it, but… well, history's never been my strongest suit. And all that science… Makes me brain hurt just thinking about it. Is it proper dark, though? Like, genuinely unsettling? It is. Nolan’s done a fantastic job depicting the moral weight of what they were doing. The ticking clock anxiety… it's relentless. And Cillian Murphy is incredible. Utterly captivating. Though, admittedly, the pace could be a  bit  slow for some. See, that’s what I’m worried about! I’d rather watch something a bit… lighter. Maybe something with a cracking soundtrack. Did you ever see "Sing Street"? That Irish film? The music's brilliant. And it's lovely. Proper feel-good. Needed something like that after today’s digital disaster. "Sing Street" is brilliant! Such an infectious energy. They actually recreate those 80s bands really well. Reminds me of when I was trying to form a band in secondary school. Epic fail, obviously. I couldn't play a single instrument. I bet! You, a rock star? You'd be figuring out stress calculations for the amplifiers, wouldn’t you? Proper logical, as always. Anyway, thinking about feel-good things… fancy that Indian place on Grey Street tonight?

…and then the dragon, see, he wasn’t  really  angry, just misunderstood! He’d lost his favourite sparkly rock, you know? And everyone just assumed he was going to breathe fire all over the village. Turns out, a little boy found it and gave it back. Right, that's enough stories for tonight, isn't it? Are you both tired? No! Tell another one about the robots! The ones with the wobbly arms! Oh, the clanky robots? Those are a bit complicated for bedtime tonight, aren’t they? We'll do those tomorrow. Remember, we talked about how they needed Excel to keep track of all their spare parts? Remember Excel, darling? Numbers… Exactly! Numbers and lists and, and… well, it’s a bit grown-up. But the robots definitely needed it. What about another story about the typewriter then? We haven’t done that one in ages. Yes! The one where it typed all the secrets! Was it a spooky typewriter? A bit spooky, yes. It was an old one, see, and it started typing things all by itself. Things like, "The gingerbread man ran away to Antarctica," and "The cat is secretly a pirate." Silly things, really. It was very confusing for Mr. Fitzwilliam, the owner. He kept thinking he’d accidentally left a letter half-written! He was a lovely old man, Mr. Fitzwilliam. I used to help him sort his papers. Did the pirate cat find treasure? Well, that’s what  you  have to imagine, isn’t it? That’s the best bit about stories – you get to make up the rest. Speaking of making things up… Brownie Promise evening was a bit… chaotic, wasn’t it? Miss Davies kept saying "On my honour," even when she wasn't saying the Promise! It was funny! It was! She got terribly flustered. You know, I almost said it wrong too! I nearly said "On my  honour ," instead of "On my  honour , I promise…" Honestly, it's easy to trip over those words. It's all about the pauses. Little pauses make all the difference. Can I play on the PlayStation tomorrow? Please? Well, we can see. Do you promise to finish your Lego first? It’s been sitting there unfinished for three days. You're building a spaceship, remember? A really important spaceship for… rescuing the sparkly dragon’s rock! Yes! And I’ll help! We can build a laser!

Aye, well, it's comfortable, isn't it? Didn't fancy putting on anything proper for breakfast with your sister. She'd have a fit. You know how she is, always fussing about appearances. More worried about the crease in your trousers than whether you’ve eaten your toast. Margaret does have a flair for the dramatic, doesn’t she? Though, I do think a clean shirt every now and then wouldn't go amiss. This one's seen better days. Speaking of better days, remember that fruit farm we visited near York? The one with the apple orchards stretching further than the eye could see? Oh, aye! That was lovely. Proper Yorkshire air, clean and crisp. Got some lovely damsons there, didn’t we? Remember trying to get photos of those deserted medieval villages nearby? The ones they reckon were abandoned when the Black Death hit. So eerie, standing there amongst the crumbling walls. Felt like we were walking through history. Indeed. Fascinating stuff. Though getting to it was a nightmare, wasn't it? Those roadworks outside of Selby… absolute chaos. Took us twice as long as it should have. Now, are you having any luck with that raspberry jam you promised you'd bring? It wouldn't go amiss with this apple. It's in the pantry, love. I made it myself, you know. From the garden. It's not quite as tart as last year's. The weather just didn't cooperate. Speaking of the garden, I'm thinking of putting in a little herb patch. Rosemary, thyme… maybe some lavender. Good for you. Keeps you busy, doesn’t it? That’s what older folks need to do. Stop sitting about complaining about their knees. This is good, by the way. Proper crisp. Though I’m dreading the pile of junk mail I’m going to get when I get back. Endless catalogues and mailing lists no matter what you do. Tell me about it! I swear, I fill out those tick-boxes saying ‘no unsolicited mail’ and within a week, I’m drowning in takeaway menus. It’s a bliddy conspiracy, I tell you. And don't even get me started on mobiles. These new fangled phones… they’re impenetrable! My granddaughter had to show me how to send a simple text the other day. Embarrassing, it was. You're not alone, dear. My wife struggles with them too.

Honestly, John, I’m absolutely knackered. Another double shift. The flu’s really taken hold, hasn't it? Half the ward’s got it. Aye, you’ve earned that cuppa, love. Heard Mrs. Patterson in 3B practically screaming for paracetamol yesterday. Kids are bringing it in, aren't they? The young ones. Showing more initiative than some of the nurses, truth be told. Morning, you two! What’s all this about the flu? I’m starting to feel a bit… sniffly. Should I stock up on tissues? Is it the same strain as last year? Oh, you're not looking good, Liv. It's nasty, this one. Definitely get the tissues. And a good Vitamin C supplement. I’ve been taking these elderberry ones, they seem to help a bit, though Dr. Davies reckons it’s all just placebo effect. Pooh to Dr. Davies, I say. Placebo or not, if it makes you feel better, Liv, take ‘em. Remember that time you got a bee sting and swore honey sorted you right out? Oh, God, yes! Mum nearly had a heart attack. But it  did  calm the sting, I swear. Anyway, Christmas presents - any brilliant ideas yet? I'm drawing a complete blank. Dad wants something "practical," which basically means socks. Socks are always practical, darling! But for you, I was thinking… remember that lavender bath oil you mentioned liking last month? The one with the little pumice stones? I saw a lovely set in The Body Shop, on offer. Good shout, love. Pampering’s always a winner. I was thinking about getting you that new noise-cancelling headphones, Liv. You're always complaining about the café noise when you're working. Oh, John! That would be amazing! Seriously, thank you. The café is a nightmare. They play that awful motivational music… you know, the stuff that makes you feel guilty for not being productive. You sound just like your Aunt Susan! She hates those motivational podcasts. Says they give her palpitations. Speaking of palpitations, have you seen Brenda’s Facebook post? That picture of her in Tenerife… sunshine, cocktails, and barely covering herself! Honestly! Some people. Brenda, eh? Always showing off. I saw it. Told her she looks like a flamingo in that outfit. She didn’t take it well, naturally. You know Brenda. Classic Brenda. I’m trying to detox from Facebook myself. It’s just endless comparison and fake happiness.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails I get about that new ad campaign is ridiculous. Like, everyone has an opinion. My boss keeps saying it needs ‘more pizzazz’ - what even  is  pizzazz? It’s not a measurable metric, is it? It's just... vague! Sounds like a nightmare. You’d think after all this time, people would realize copywriting isn’t just about slapping words on a page. It’s... psychology, right? Knowing what makes people  tick . Exactly! And it’s really frustrating when people who… are not in marketing, are suddenly the experts. My Aunt Carol keeps sending me links to articles about font choice. Font choice, honestly! I’m dealing with a multi-million pound budget and she's worried about Comic Sans. Oh, bless her. Family’s like that, aren't they? Always got a piece of advice, whether you asked for it or not. My mum’s just been going on about my dissertation. "Are you sure you're referencing  enough , darling?" As if I'm not painstakingly cross-referencing every single thought I've ever had! They mean well, of course. So, how’s the dissertation going, then? Still drowning in Victorian literature? Trying not to. It’s... intense. This particular chapter, on gender roles in Dickens’ novels, is sucking the life out of me. It's fascinating, don't get me wrong, but wading through all the social commentary is exhausting. Plus, my part-time job at the survey company is rather unpredictable. Some weeks I'm earning proper money, other weeks it’s barely enough for a pint. Oh, the classic student struggle. I remember those days. Still, it’s good you're building up skills, even if it’s a bit erratic. Speaking of money… things are tight at work. They're 'streamlining' which basically means trying to do twice the work with half the budget. I'm constantly worried about redundancies. That’s awful! Have they said anything concrete? Vague murmurs. Lots of corporate buzzwords about ‘rightsizing’ and ‘optimizing workflows’. You know the drill. It makes you feel… disposable, doesn't it? Like a cog in a machine. Absolutely. It’s so impersonal. Have you been looking at other jobs? Just for peace of mind? I've had a little peek. Nothing serious. The job market's bonkers at the moment. Everyone wants five years’ experience for an entry-level position.

Tell me about it, Eleanor. I was looking at some lettings in the village – just a couple of rooms, really, for a friend who's moving south – and they’re asking upwards of £900 a month. £900! For something that smells faintly of damp and has wallpaper from the seventies. It’s robbery. Robinson Crusoe prices, wouldn’t you say? Though, dear, that's London-adjacent now, isn't it? Isleworth was always pricey, but the further out you go… it’s obscene. Remember when a decent flat in Chiswick would cost you, what, three hundred a week? Progress, eh? Though I’m not sure ‘progress’ is the right word. Progress for the landlords, perhaps. I'm seeing similar figures in Edinburgh. It's driven up by short-term lets, mostly. Airbnb. The city's practically become a giant hotel. Makes finding anything permanently affordable incredibly difficult. My sister's struggling to buy a flat for her daughter. She's a teacher, you know, working endlessly. It’s so unfair. They work their fingers to the bone and are punished for it. Speaking of working, I’ve been trying to be more disciplined with the exercise, you know? The transcription work… it's a sedentary life. My back’s been protesting lately. Oh, yes. I can relate to the back complaints. Though I try to combat that with pottering in the garden. You really should, darling. Nothing beats a bit of weeding to clear the head. Have you tried Pilates? My neighbour swears by it. Pilates is good, yeah. But finding the time... that’s the killer. I’ve been doing a bit of running, though. Trying to build up to a 5k. Footing's a nightmare in some places, though. The pavements in some parts of Edinburgh are practically medieval. Oh, the pavements! Don’t get me started. Cracked and uneven everywhere. It’s a tripping hazard waiting to happen. I do a bit of yoga, mostly. Helps with the flexibility. Although, getting my leggings on is a minor victory in itself these days. Don't we all know it! Listen, I was thinking about you the other day. I've been experimenting with that slow cooker recipe I found – the Moroccan tagine. It’s ridiculously easy and makes the most wonderful thing. Do you fancy me making a big batch and freezing some portions for you? You could just pop it in the oven on a weeknight.

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it all is just…intimidating. This beam deflection calculation for the new bridge over the River Cam? It's a beast. I've been running simulations all week. Keeps throwing errors. I'm starting to think I need another pot of coffee. Aye, sounds proper mental, that does. Beams and rivers…civil engineering, eh? Never quite wrapped me 'ead roond it. I’m surrounded by words all day, you know? Less structural integrity, more semantic nuances. Semantic nuances? You’re still dealing with that massive Shakespeare corpus, aren’t you? That must be fascinating, though. Picking apart the nuances of language… Is it all just metadata and tagging though, or do you actually…read it? Oh, I read a fair bit, yeah. Can’t just ping everything through a machine, can I? Gotta, like,  feel  the flow of it. It's horrifying, sometimes, proper grim poetry. But aye, mostly it’s tagging, annotation, checking for consistency… making sure "thee" and "thou" are accurately categorized. Want to know a funny thing? Apparently, determining the emotional valence of a comma is a major research area now. A comma! A comma’s emotional valence? Seriously? That’s ridiculous. Honestly, I'm finding government budget proposals easier to understand. Have you seen what they're doing with infrastructure spending? It’s a disaster. Roads are crumbling, railways are delayed, everything’s in perpetual ‘planning stage’. I 'ad a look. It’s bleak, isn’t it? They’re cutting everything that doesn’t directly lead to economic growth, and what  does  lead to economic growth seems to be…more cuts. It's a vicious cycle. My mam’s proper worried about it. She’s always been sensible wi' money, and she's saying we're heading for trouble. Exactly! And the impact on young people… it's insane. My student loan interest rates just keep climbing. I'm starting to feel like I'm digging myself deeper. You must get loads of freelance requests for your corpus work, right? Is it helping you out? It does, aye. Enough to keep the wolves from the door, as they say. Freelance tagging can be a lifesaver. But it's inconsistent. One month I'm swamped, the next I'm sitting trying to convince myself that cleaning out the fridge is a valid career pursuit. Speaking of things that distract me... did you hear about  Wicked  coming back to London?

Right then, seein’ this light… it’s bleedin’ all over the brickwork, innit? Makes it look positively Tuscan. Though, I suspect Anon's budget won't stretch to a Tuscan villa any time soon. Tuscan, eh? You’re gettin' fancy, Karl. It’s a bleedin' brick wall, mate. Looked better before you started fiddlin’ with it. You're makin’ it look like somethin’ out of a historical drama. That’s the aim, isn't it? Inject a little… romanticism. This whole area's goin' to pot, you know? All these new builds, all glass and steel. No character. Remember when this was just fields down here? Proper green stuff, not like this sad little patch of scrub. They’re buildin’ another block of flats, aren't they? Heard it through Anon. Yeah, heard that. More overpriced shoeboxes for folk who don’t appreciate a bit of honest rain. Developers don’t give a toss about character, Karl. Just about pound signs. They’ll even tear down a perfectly good pub for a line of “luxury apartments.” Remember The Red Lion? Used to be a proper haunt. Appalling. It’s the same everywhere, isn’t it? No investment in the existing community. Speaking of which, I was watching that stage adaptation of ‘Wuthering Heights’ last week. Absolute disaster. The casting was dreadful. The Heathcliff had the emotional range of a damp sponge. Acting, eh? Never been much of a fan, myself. Unless it’s a good action film. Anything with car chases and explosions. More my speed. You ever seen ‘Mad Max: Fury Road’? Now  that's  acting, even if they're mostly shoutin'. Not really my thing, though I appreciate the… kinetic energy. I’m more drawn to the subtleties. Like… the way a painter can convey emotion through colour. You know, I picked up a rather interesting landscape at a second-hand shop on Smithdown Road the other day. Early 20th century, I think. Slightly damaged, hence the price. Smithdown Road, you say? Found a right bargain there myself last week. Actually, I need to borrow your stepladder, Karl. Got a leaky gutter on the house, proper drippin’. Think I can fix it myself, don’t want to be payin' someone a fortune. Certainly. It's in the shed. Be careful, though. It’s a bit wobbly. What’s the goal these days, then, Barry? Anything you're aiming for?

Blimey, this is a lot less… dramatic than the mountains, innit? Just fields and, like, little villages all the way. Bit drab, really. Though, I do like that little church spire over there. Looks proper ancient. It is, love. Poland’s full of them. Centuries of history layered on top of each other. Quite remarkable, really. Much more interesting than Basingstoke, anyway. Though, I do miss a proper garden. All this countryside… it’s rather overwhelming really. So much  green . Overwhelming green? You've been in the mountains for a week! You'd think you'd be craving a bit of nature, surely? And don’t go on about Basingstoke, you only ever mention it when you’re feeling particularly nostalgic for… well, nothing much, let's be honest. Nostalgic? It’s a point of reference! It’s  home , loosely speaking. And it’s not nothing. It's familiar. Speaking of home... how are we doing on the budget? Did you manage to work out what we owe for fuel? Yeah, it’s looking a bit tight, to be fair. About eighty quid, I reckon. And that doesn’t include the pierogi we demolished last night. Those were worth every zloty, though. Honestly, the best food of the entire trip. Did you see that amazing sunset in Zakopane? Wish you’d been outside to see it, instead of… cataloguing your biscuit crumbs. I was organizing! It’s vital. Traveling with you, Sarah, is… chaotic. Keeps me on my toes, I suppose. And the sunset  was  lovely, I saw it through the window. Anyway, we should probably cut back a bit. Maybe fewer pierogi? Though, that’s a difficult decree. What about Liam and Chloe? Are they still up for meeting us in Krakow? Yeah, they’re still good for it. Liam's being a bit flaky about travel plans as usual – apparently his uncle's cat needs emergency knitted sweaters – but Chloe’s sorted everything. She’s even booked us a really nice Airbnb. It’s got a balcony! Imagine, a balcony! Oh, that  is  lovely. I do miss having a balcony. Somewhere to put a pot of geraniums. It reminds me... I really must get rid of some things when I get back. The attic is positively overflowing. So much accumulated… stuff. All testament to a life not quite… lived, I suppose. Don't start with the existential crisis again, Auntie Penelope!

Are we nearly there yet, Dad? My legs are killin' after all that beach dodging. Not long now, love. Just gotta navigate this roundabout chaos. Preston's comin' up, honest. You moanin' already? You only did a quick paddle, didn’t ya? It was freezing! Honestly, the sea is a shock to the system this time of year. Reminds me of swimming in the Hornaděj pond back home as a kid. No heating, just… bracing. Hornaděj? Sounds like somethin' you’d find in a swamp! Anyway, Mum, you were saying… about the Hay Festival? Sounds a bit posh, that, doesn't it? Like for people who wear tweed and drink Earl Grey all day. Not really, darling. It's brilliant. All sorts of authors, poets, thinkers… you’d love it. They have workshops, too. You’re brilliant at creative writing, remember? Aye, she entered that competition last year, didn’t she? The one about the lost cat. Got a commendation, she did. Proper proud she was. True, but they’re talkin' about ‘post-modern narrative structures' and stuff, which sounds a bit… much for a Thursday afternoon. Is it expensive though? Because that history textbook isn’t payin’ for itself, is it? Exams are loom in’, yer know. We'll have a look at the website, love. See what they offer. Don’t get yourself worked up about it. It’s just an idea. Speaking of which, are you all set for that mock exam next week? Don’t want you panickin’ like you did last time. Remember when you thought you’d forgotten how to spell 'photosynthesis'? Don't remind me! I swore I was going to fail. Mum kept telling me to breathe. I did! Deep breaths, remember? It's just pressure. You're smart, you’ll do fine. You always do. Did you remember to pack your revision notes? I did, yeah. And remember Grandma telling that story about the time she got lost at Blackpool Pleasure Beach when she was little? Aye, that's a classic. Little Elsie, runnin’ off after a clown, ended up near the pirate ship. Her dad nearly had a heart attack, apparently. She was only four, wasn't she? It’s amazing how much people remember from their childhoods, isn’t it? My own childhood feels like a different lifetime. Living in Kosice, everything felt so… different. Much smaller, quieter. I was thinkin’ about that, actually.

It is, lass, it is. Though, you know, a good clear-out can be rather… liberating. Reminds you what’s truly important, doesn’t it? Though, I do find myself clinging to things. Sentimental fool, I am. This little ceramic robin here, for instance. Your grandad gave it to me when we went crabbing in Cornwall. Sixty years ago! Can you imagine?      Aye, Mum. I can imagine. Sixty years is a long time. Don't go getting yourself worked up over it though. Liam’s been a massive help, hasn’t he? He’s tackled a whole load of the attic already, hasn't he, lad?      Yeah, mostly. Found loads of old comics though. Proper vintage stuff. Some of it’s worth a bit, apparently. Bit dusty though. Had to wear a mask. Smelled like… old newspapers and mothballs. Not the best.      Comics, you say? Good heavens. Your grandad collected those, didn’t he? Terrible habit. Always hoarding things. Though he had a good sense of humour, your grandad. Remember that joke he used to tell about the vicar and the… oh, what  was  it? It involved a prize marrow and a mishap with a sheep, I think.      Oh, Mum, you and your grandad’s jokes! They were always a bit… eccentric. Liam, you’ve heard the marrow one, haven’t you?      Uh, yeah. A few times. It’s not that funny, to be honest. It's just… random.      Random is the best kind, lad! That's what made it funny. It's about finding the absurdity in things, isn't it? Life  is  absurd, really. Especially these days. All this technology… I can’t make head nor tail of it. Your niece, Emily, tried to show me how to use that… what is it called? TikTok?      TikTok, Mum. It's mostly dancing and silly challenges. Don't worry, it's a rabbit hole you don’t need to jump down.      Exactly! It frightens me, all this constant connection. No privacy. And everyone’s so preoccupied with what everyone else is doing. It reminds me a bit of… well, never mind. It’s a delicate subject.      Mum, are you alright? You seem a bit… off. Is this clear-out bringing up some tough memories? Restoring old boxes can be a trigger.      Just… thinking about your grandfather. It’s been… a long time. And sometimes, the sadness just creeps back in. All these years, and still… it feels very present.

Right, so it’s doing it again. That little spinning wheel of doom. Honestly, I spent all morning trying to get these logos rendered for the new bakery website, and now this. Proper frustrating, innit? Yeah, that's a bummer, Liam. What’ve you got running? Too many tabs open, like always? Nah, not really. Just Photoshop and InDesign. Nothing crazy. I closed everything down properly, you know. Gave it a good reboot. It’s just…laggy. Feels clunky. Let me have a look. Is it the RAM? Or maybe the hard drive’s knackered? You know, I was looking at some old PCs the other day, for a customer. They’re miraculous things, really. Folks were doing amazing stuff on those dinosaurs. Remember those beige boxes with the floppy disk drives? Oh, yeah, proper relics! My dad used to have one of those. Took him three hours to load up Doom. So, what do you reckon, Leon? RAM or drive? Leon’s right, it could be the hard drive. It’s probably spinning down constantly, trying to catch up. Did you upgrade to an SSD? Seriously, it’s night and day difference, Liam. Makes even an old computer feel new. I thought about it. Cost was a bit of a barrier, to be honest. Besides, I barely use it, to be fair. Mostly YouTube and Netflix. Thinking about maybe getting a bigger TV, actually. The neighbour got a massive OLED, 65 inch, flickering away like a disco ball. Makes mine look like a postage stamp. You should come hiking with us next weekend, proper get some fresh air. We're heading up to Whipsnash Slough. It’s not a massive trek, but the views are brilliant. Helps clear the head, doesn't it? That's a good shout, Leon. Liam could use some exercise, too. He's been glued to that computer all week. Speaking of which, you still doing that MMA class? Nah, stopped that. Killer on the joints, it was. Though I do miss it. Maybe if I had a bit more time...and a laptop that didn’t constantly freeze when I’m trying to earn a living. Right. Back to the laptop. You installed that antivirus software, right? Sometimes those things hog resources. Also, have you checked for driver updates? Drivers... yeah. I think so. I don’t really fancy messing about with that stuff, to be honest.

…and honestly, the pierogi were  spot on . Didn’t taste like anything I've had before, but in a good way! Like, a proper, comforting good way. This bistro, "U Babci," is brilliant, isn't it? So unexpected in Tarnow. I thought all we'd get were these, like, really basic, functional cafes. It is lovely, yes. Very… cheerful. And the furniture isn't all mismatched like half the places here. It's a little oasis, really. Though, I can’t help but wonder if it will last. Tarnow isn’t exactly booming, is it? Maybe not, but people need nice places to go, don't they? Especially when you’ve traveled as far as we have. So, how are the lessons going? Still getting a decent flow of students? Sporadic. Really sporadic. I had a lovely German chap last week, very enthusiastic about Chaucer. But he went home. It's the nature of the beast, I suppose. TEFL isn’t exactly a career path for someone whose last  real  job was… well, it was a very long time ago. Makes you feel a bit… obsolete. Don't be daft, Aunt Penelope. You’re brilliant at it. You make it fun. Honestly, I learned more from you about Shakespeare than I ever did at uni! It's just… finding the right fit, isn’t it? This place… makes you think about fresh starts, doesn't it? It does. It does. It reminds me of dreams I had, you know. When I was younger. Becoming a translator, maybe. Or a screenwriter. Things that felt… possible. You could still do those things, you know. Nothing's ever truly ‘too late.’ You've always got a fantastically vivid imagination. Besides, you’re fitter than I am, and I go to the gym three times a week! That walk you did around the lake the other day… you were practically gliding! It's mostly sheer stubbornness, I think. And a desperate attempt to stave off the… the feeling. The feeling? The… well, you know. The shadow. It's been trying to catch up with me for years. It's peculiar, isn’t it? How a thing like addiction changes your identity. You don’t just stop  doing  it; you lose a chunk of  who  you are. It shapes everything. Even the things you want. I can’t really imagine… but I get it, in a way.

Right, so tickets are officially sold out for Saturday at the Dorset Steam Fair. Honestly, Dad, you were right, should have booked ages ago! Sunday still has some left, though. Are you sure you can manage it then? It's a bit later in the day. Later's fine, love. I’ve got all the time in the world now, innit? Just a shame about Saturday. Wanted to see that big Burrell engine, you know, the one with the brass fittings. Proper fancy. Sunday’s lovely too, Arthur. And they've got more demonstrations then, I think. More of the stationary engines, which you enjoy. Don't fret about it. At least we can go. Listen, did you check the website for accessibility information, Brenda? I’m a bit worried about getting you around. Yeah, Mum, I looked. It says they've got a shuttle bus service running from the main car park to the showground area, and designated disabled viewing areas. They’ve also got accessible toilets, which is vital. It doesn’t mention anything about ramps though, so we might need to be careful. Bournemouth is a nightmare for pavements sometimes. Ramps don't bother me. I used to be a dab hand at a bit of DIY, you know. Could build a ramp outta pallets and some wood, no problem. Days are gone, those. Joints aren’t what they used to be. We'll manage, Arthur. They usually do their best to accommodate. Speaking of accommodation... have you thought about what we're going to do about that storage space when we move? The flat Sarah’s getting is tiny. That's what I was thinking. Right, massive pile of stuff. Honestly, Dad, you’ve got more memorabilia than a museum! That old gramophone, all those model trains… Where are we going to put it all? Property prices round here are ridiculous, you know. Securing a storage facility is another expense. Those model trains are an investment, love! Mint condition, they are. And the gramophone plays a proper tune. You wouldn’t understand. You and your… your modern music. Oh, Arthur. Don't start. The gramophone is lovely, dear, but we’re running out of room! Maybe we could have a clear-out? You have got quite a few chipped mugs. Definitely a clear-out is needed. Speaking of things that need a move... how's Mittens doing?

Weary is putting it mildly, Mum. It's ridiculous. A simple misunderstanding blown completely out of proportion. People leaping to conclusions without a shred of evidence. The sheer volume of angry replies… it's exhausting just watching it. You shouldn't even be looking at Twitter, honestly. It's a cesspool sometimes. Aye, but it’s become the new village green, hasn’t it? Everyone gathers, everyone shouts. Used to be you’d have a good barney down at the church hall, now it’s…this. And the anonymity! People saying things they’d never utter to your face. It’s appalling. You’re right, Margaret. It’s a proper shambles. But David, don't dismiss it  completely . There's good to be found, connection too. I use it to keep up with teaching resources and to connect with other teachers from all over the country. It's got its uses. So, is Grandma gonna be alright then? About the tweet thing? All this fuss is a bit much, innit? I’m fine, Liam, dear. Don’t you worry your head. It's just... frustrating. This house move, the Twitter nonsense, it’s all piled on at once. It makes me long for the days of a good cup of tea and a quiet read, doesn't it? Do you think we’ll have time for a game of Scrabble this evening, David? Absolutely, Mum. Scrabble's the perfect antidote to Twitter. Speaking of which, Carol, how was your day? Did you manage to catch up with that pottery studio you were telling me about? I did! 'Clayful Creations' near Ripon. Absolutely charming. The artisan was lovely, a real character. Makes these stunning little bowls with wildflowers pressed into the clay. I’m thinking of getting some for the new cottage. It’s coming along nicely, isn’t it? Thirsk's a lovely place. It is, dear. Although no Kendal, that's for certain. The hills are much gentler here. I miss the fells. Remember chasing rabbits up Brant Fell as a child? That sounds pretty boring, Grandma. Can we go to the cinema later? There's that new Marvel thing. Maybe, Liam. Let’s see how Mum is feeling first. We need to finish unpacking her study, you know. She’s insisted on having a proper library. It  is  a Margaret thing, isn't it? Surrounded by books. Well, someone needs a bit of culture in this family!

“…and honestly, the dentist’s just a formality for them both this year. Just a check-up. It’s Elsie who needs to worry. She’s been complaining about her ears again, isn't she, love? I’ve booked her in for a hearing test. Just to be on the safe side.” "A hearing test? Will it be fun, Mummy? Will they have toys?" "Well, I don’t know if they’ll have  toys , sweetheart. But they’ll have things to listen to, I expect. Different sounds. It's just to see if she can hear everything properly, that's all. Don't you worry." "Sounds boring." "It’s not boring, Finn! It’s important. Elsie needs to hear everything clearly so she can hear me reading her stories, right?" "Right." "Right. Now, back to this chaos of birthdays! Honestly, it’s like everyone’s suddenly decided to have theirs within a fortnight. Ashaad’s has been moved again, too. Apparently, his mum’s trying to juggle two different venues this year. Can you believe it? She’s stressed already." "Ashaad has a party with bouncy castles?" "Possibly, darling. I'm not entirely sure.
