Get them onto Dropbox or Flickr, you know? Before they all… dissintegrait. Dropbox? What's that? It's a place to store stuff online, Liam. Pictures, videos... keeps them safe. Gets rid of the worry about losing them. Your mother’s got a mountain of old photos on her phone. They’re memories, Conor. Valuable memories. And I’m perfectly capable of backing them up. It’s just… things are a bit hectic at the moment. Little Thomas has been a handful, bless him. He found a hedgehog in the garden yesterday. Nearly gave me a heart attack! A hedgehog! Jaysus! Did it have its spines up? Absolutely! Little prickleball. I had to shoo it away. Liam kept trying to pick it up.

Honestly, David, you won’t  believe  what I managed to snag on eBay this afternoon. Just came up, practically blinking at me - a Paragon teacup and saucer set. Floral, lovely little gold detailing… it’s going to look gorgeous with the willow pattern ones. Paragon, eh? Not bad. You've got quite the collection building up, haven't you? Nearly makes one feel like we need a dedicated china cabinet. Though, knowing us, it'll just end up balanced on a stack of old biscuit tins. Don't be ridiculous. Biscuit tins are part of the charm! Besides, it's all so affordable, the vintage stuff. People just want to get rid of it, you know? It’s a treasure trove, if you’re diligent enough to look. Did you see that listing for the Shelley pieces? Nearly had a heart attack. Shelley’s a bit rich for our blood, I think. Though, a lovely idea for Christmas presents, perhaps? Assuming we  ever  clear the backlog of half-finished craft projects. Speaking of backlogs… how's that transcription piling up? Still wrestling with the railway enthusiast's memoirs? Don’t remind me. He’s gone into excruciating detail about signal boxes. Signal boxes, David! Honestly, I need a holiday. At least the leaving do for Philippa sounds like it'll be fun. Did you manage to RSVP for me? Of course. Said you were definitely coming. It’s next Friday, isn't it? Apparently, they're doing a full-blown karaoke session. Brace yourself. Philippa’s got a surprisingly powerful rendition of “Bohemian Rhapsody.” Oh, heaven help us. Right, right. Need to prepare for that. Any chance you could tackle the buckwheat bread tonight? I’m a bit frazzled after eBay and signal boxes. Buckwheat bread it is. Although, I still maintain it’s slightly…dusty tasting. A bit like eating finely-ground floorboards. It’s rustic! Rustic and healthy. And last time you complained about no fibre. Don’t be a grump. Did you pick up any nice tomatoes at the market this morning? Remember how we were saying we needed some for that ratatouille? I did. Got a fantastic haul actually. Heirloom varieties, bursting with flavour. Mrs. Peterson had a stall – the one with the prize-winning roses. She’s started selling those little pickled onions too. So good. Oh, excellent! I love those pickled onions. It’s just… the market’s been getting busier, hasn't it?

…and then he just said, "The transfer's flagged, love. Standard procedure." Standard procedure, like it's not a five-figure sum moving from a shell company in the Caymans to your grandma's account! Honestly, it’s stressing me rotten. Right. I told you using Grandma’s account was a risky strategy, El. It’s traceable. It  always  is. Look, I get you’re trying to help your cousin, Finn, but you have to be smarter about this. Think about the implications. Relax, Liv. It'll be fine. She’s just panicking. They’ll probably just ask a few questions, nobody's going to arrest your grandma for accidentally receiving a bit of dodgy cash. "A bit of dodgy cash"? Finn’s in a right pickle, Finn! That’s why I’m doing this! He owes some… unsavoury people. And he's not exactly known for his financial responsibility, is he? Remember that motorbike? Oh yes, the motorbike. A fine investment, that one. Look, El, I appreciate you stepping in, genuinely. But this is the sort of thing you need to be incredibly careful with. I’ve seen… things. In my line of work, you learn to recognise patterns. And that transfer shouts red flags a mile off. What do you mean, patterns, Dad? You always do this, speak in riddles! What am I supposed to do? Let Finn get hurt? He's my cousin, for crying out loud! He needs to sort his own mess out, El. Protecting him like this... it’s enabling him. And you’re putting yourself – and Grandma – at serious risk. Have you considered the fines alone? Not to mention the reputational damage. Think about your uni course. I  have  considered it! I’m not stupid, Liv! I just... I don't know what else to do! He's saying they’ll take his van, then his flat… then… He should have thought about that before he got mixed up with those blokes then, shouldn’t he? Honestly, El, you bend over backwards for everyone. You need to learn to say no. Easy for you to say, Finn! You’re not dealing with the fallout! Dad, seriously, you’ve seen this stuff. Is there a way to… to make it look legit? Like, a loan agreement or something? Anything? It's not as simple as just creating a document, El. They’ll look beyond that.

Tell me about it, Sarah! Little Leo was up at five this morning, demanding toast with  exactly  three blueberries. Three, Mum! Who are we raising here, a tiny tyrant? Sounds about right. Remember when Tom used to insist on having his socks pulled up  just  so? It never ends, does it? Good to see you both looking well though. And Anita, you look lovely. Thanks, Sarah. It's good to be here. Work's been a bit of a whirlwind. New stock coming in, trying to keep the staff motivated... It's all go, go, go. You wouldn’t believe the queues we had for the new trainers yesterday. Absolute madness. Queues for trainers…typical. Still, keeps you busy, eh? Speaking of busy, I’ve got a fundraising gala next Saturday night. Black tie, the whole shebang. Hoping to raise a decent amount for the children’s ward at the hospital. Oh, that’s brilliant, Dad! You’re amazing. Will you be needing a date? Don’t you worry about that, love. I’m a dab hand at charming potential donors. More importantly, how’s the sign language class going, Emily? You sounded excited about it last time. It's actually really wonderful! I'm picking it up surprisingly quickly. I’ve got a neighbour who’s partially deaf, and I thought it would be lovely to be able to communicate with her properly. It's more practical than I initially thought - thinking about how to explain things to the kids in a visually led way. That’s lovely, Emily. Sounds really rewarding. I wish I had the time for something like that. I’ve been meaning to get back into painting. It's just... life, isn't it? Always something taking priority. Although, I did manage a little sketching last weekend. Nothing fancy. You should! It'd be nice to see you doing something for yourself, Sarah. You give so much to everyone else. You’re right, Anita. I need to prioritise that. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I'm juggling chainsaws. How's your mum doing, by the way? She's alright. A bit stiff in the mornings, but nothing to worry about. She's been badgering me about the village fete. Apparently, she  needs  to win the cake competition this year. Says Doreen from next door has been getting complacent. Sounds like your mum! Competition is in her blood.

Honestly, I’m still wrapped up in this corpus error. The annotation guidelines are  so  vague on distinguishing between colloquial verb contractions and genuine elision. It's driving me absolutely barmy, it is. Like, does “gonna” count as elision or is it just, you know, lazy speech? Tell me about it! I spent ages yesterday trying to figure out whether to flag “sort of” as a hedge. It feels almost meaningless on its own, but the frequency of its occurrence in spoken narratives suggests it  is  performing a function. Difficult to pin down, innit? Linguistic functions… right. Sounds intense. I’m just battling formatting errors on the new poetry anthology. You wouldn’t believe the number of people who don’t understand the importance of using a proper em dash. They just,  randomly  insert hyphens. It’s barbaric. Is...is an em dash the long dash? Like, the one used for dramatic effect? Exactly! The correct one. And yes, dramatic effect is the whole  point  of it. It’s about creating a pause, a sense of… breathlessness. Trying to explain this to the interns is like talking to a brick wall. They’re all on Twitter, you know? Short, snappy sentences. No room for nuance or… em dashes. Speaking of snaps, did you all see Anya's Instagram story from the Fitzwilliam? She managed to get a photo with that ancient Egyptian sarcophagus. The lighting was  amazing . Completely transformed it. Oh my god, yes! I was just thinking about her feed. She has such a good eye. I wish I could take photos like that. Everything I take looks washed out and bleak, even in bright sunlight. You and half the population. It's all about composition, darling. And filters, obviously. But my research brain tends to over-analyse things. I’ll be trying to work out the principle of diffraction rather than appreciating the beauty of the light. I try to look for...the angles. My grandmother, she was a photographer. She taught me to look for lines. Shapes. How the light hits the edges. But…sometimes I forget. I get overwhelmed. Being temporary... it's hard to focus. Temporary? You haven’t said anything about that. Yeah. Just covering the maternity leave. Three months. It  is  good experience, I suppose. But it also feels… fleeting. Like I’m just observing. That’s rubbish. Three months is a decent chunk of time.

Right, so, visa applications. Absolute nightmare, innit? I've been staring at this form for three hours and I still don't know if they want my mum's maiden name or not. It's like they're deliberately trying to confuse ya. Tell me about it. I’ve got worse. They want a full itinerary. Like, minute-by-minute. "Please detail your planned activities between 14:37 and 14:42 on July 18th in Ulaanbaatar." Seriously? How am I supposed to know what we’ll be doing then? Proper taking the mick, aren't they? Listen, mine's asking for financial proof. Like, proof I can afford to eat a packet of crisps in Mongolia. I mean, we've got the donations coming in, haven't we? We should just whip up a spreadsheet with everything. Already on it. See? Got all the pledges so far. We’re at just over £1200. Not bad, eh? Still a fair bit to go, though. We need to ramp up the Gumtree adds. Yours are a bit…sparse, lad. Sparse? They're concise! I ain't writing a novel for a rally, are I? They need to know it's for a good cause, and that we're gonna be ridin' across Mongolia. Simple as that, like. And get this – I tried to get passport photos done. Little shop down the street, right? The bloke kept telling me to smile more. I said, “I’m tryin’ to look like I’m about to ride a Triumph across a desert, not win a beauty pageant!” He didn’t get it. Classic. You’ll need to go somewhere else then. I reckon Boots will be better. They got those digital ones, easy peasy. We should book a slot for both of us while we’re at it. Sorted. Good shout. And about the donations… I was thinking, we could do a sponsored car wash down at the market on Saturday? Get the local paper involved? That's brilliant! We could put up a banner, have someone with a microphone... get some proper hustle going on. I'll have a word with my auntie, she's got connections with the local paper. She’s a busybody, but useful for this kind of thing. You know she organised the village fete for thirty years running? Aye, I remember her fete. Mountains of soggy sandwiches and raffles nobody wins.

…and honestly, the A&E was mental. Proper rammed. Just rows and rows of people all lookin' miserable. They gave me some gas and air, bless ‘em. Felt like I was floating for a bit there. Still achey though, proper stiff, innit? Gas and air? Ooh, fancy! So, they think it’s just a bad sprain then? No break? Nah, they said it’s probably a strain, maybe a slight ligament damage. Just need to rest it, apparently. Which, knowing me, is gonna be a challenge. I’m used to bein' on the go. Morning, you two. Drama central in here, I see. You look knackered, Liv. Didn't realise you'd been to hospital last night! What happened exactly? You were so quiet last night just slumped on the sofa. Tellin' ya, it was daft. I was tryin' to reach for that box of biscuits – the ones you bought – and completely overstretched. Proper felt it pop. Should’ve just let it go, shouldn’t I? Stubborn, that's me. Don’t beat yourself up about it. Biscuits are important. Seriously though, are you okay? You look completely drained. And you’re pale as a sheet. I am tired. Proper knackered, yeah. Didn't sleep a wink after gettin' back. Kept thinkin’ about that fella in the bed next to me. Big bloke, looked right miserable, coughin’ and splutterin’ all night. Proper gave me the creeps. Right, well, rest is exactly what you need. And a big cup of tea. You need to put your feet up and try and relax. Are you gonna go to lectures today? I don't know. I feel like I might collapse if I try. But I can't miss them all, can I? That History lecture is important. Just don’t push yourself. Uni's a marathon, not a sprint. And remember, there’s always recorded lectures if you really can’t face it. Moving this to the kitchen, right? I'm starving. So, apart from a near-hospital experience and biscuit-related injuries, how was your night? Anything… exciting happen? You seemed a bit flustered earlier. Liam text you didn't he? Ugh, yeah. Liam. He was… persistent. Kept sendin’ me little messages after I left the party. Persistent? Sounds promising! What did he say? Don't be shy. Not promising! Annoying, more like. Just… "Are you okay? Where are you? Need a hand?”

…and then Auntie Maureen, bless her cotton socks, tried to tell Uncle Derek that the gravy was lumpy. Right in front of everyone! Honestly, the drama. Could’ve waited ‘til he wasn’t busy carving the roast, couldn’t she? Typical Auntie Maureen, though, isn’t it? Always gotta find something to fuss about. Did she actually say 'lumpy'? That's a strong word for gravy. Aye, she did. Loud as you please. “Derek, love, the gravy’s a bit…lumpy.” He just looked at her, proper gobsmacked, didn’t even say a word. Just carried on carving. That's when your grandma stepped in, bless her. Said something about it being “rustic” gravy, and everyone started laughing. Took the heat off him nicely, it did. Grandma's good at that. Defusing situations. Did anyone mention my A-Level results yet? I didn’t really hear much other than Auntie Maureen’s gravy critique. Of course they did! Soon as they realized I was handing out the vol-au-vents. Everyone wanted to know. Your Uncle Paul was practically bouncing about, asking if I'd got the call from Cambridge yet. As if that’s a guarantee! Told him to calm down and let them release the offers properly, didn't I? Still, they were all delighted for you, love. Really pleased. Even Maureen managed a grudging compliment. A grudging compliment from Maureen counts for about, like, half a compliment, right? So, not that exciting. But it was good to see everyone. It felt...old-fashioned, you know? All the family together. It’s not often we all manage to get in the same room. It is that, isn’t it? Your grandad was chuffed, though. Really chuffed. Kept saying how proud he was, and reminiscing about when he and your grandma first got together. Thirty-five years, can you believe it? Time flies, doesn't it? Thirty-five years! That’s…a lot. What were they like when they were younger? Grandma always says she was a proper wild one, but I can't imagine it. She’s so…sensible now. Oh, she was. A right little scrapper, she was. Worked in a chip shop straight outta school, saved every penny she could. Your grandad, he was a quiet lad then, always reading. They were completely different, you two, but they just…fit. Like a pair of good boots, they do.

Honestly, Dad, I'm  starving . Are we stopping soon for something? Like, proper food? Not just crisps and biscuits. Aye, lass, we’ll stop. I was thinking somewhere around Exeter, maybe. Got a bit of a rumbling myself, I’ll admit. Though, remember that time we went to the Lake District and I tried to live on Kendal Mint Cake for three days? Not a good look. Don’t remind me. You were a zombie. I’m thinking sandwiches. Or, even better, something from Holland and Barrett. They’ve got those amazing falafel wraps. Holland and Barrett, eh? Bit pricey for lunches, aren’t they? Though I suppose it’s healthier. Me stomach’s been a bit off again, mind. IBS acting up something awful. Think it's the stress of all this moving. Moving  is  a nightmare. Have you sorted out about the removal van? Did you confirm the booking? I keep worrying we'll end up needing to pile all our stuff in the car. Aye, all sorted. They're coming next Wednesday. It’s just the thought of it all, innit? Boxes everywhere, trying to remember where everything goes… And that new washing machine... Honestly, these modern things. Remember the old Beko we had? Solid as a rock. It was a dinosaur! It took forever to wash anything! This one’s got, like, fifteen different cycles. Heated drying, steam… I don't even know what half of them do. It's all a bit much, isn't it? Like these cars, too. All these fancy gadgets. Too much. Don’t need it all. Remember when a car was just a car? You could fix it yourself with a spanner and a bit of duct tape. Speaking of fixing things, I saw a cat flap the other day – one of those fancy automatic ones. Made me think of Mr. Tibbles. Miss that little fella. Me too. He’d probably hate Cornwall. No mice, probably. Remember that time he got into the sugar? He was bouncing off the walls for hours. Aye! Just like a little whirlwind! Right, Exeter then. Thinking we might have a roast supper when we get there. Something hearty. I’ve been meaning to try that new recipe for Yorkshire puddings. Reckon I can master it? Oh, I'm sure you can, Dad. As long as it doesn't resemble volcanic rock. Although, I do fancy some chocolate after all this driving.

I mean, moving the entire archive…to Carmarthen? Of all places? We’ve been using London for decades. It’s central. It’s got the infrastructure. It's... practical. Practicality isn’t always the prime motivator, Sarah. Your Aunt Moira’s been pretty insistent. She feels it’s about more than just moving boxes of documents. It’s about…reconnecting with her roots, establishing a Scottish presence outside of Edinburgh. It's a legacy thing, you know? Legacy? Don’t be facetious, David. It's about proper stewardship. London has become…overwhelmed. Too much transient traffic. Too many eyes. These genealogical records, they deserve a quiet, stable environment. Carmarthen has offered us a beautifully renovated Georgian house, purpose-built for storage and research. And Gareth, of course, already has contacts there. He understands the importance of safeguarding these histories. It’s a good space, alright. Solid stone. Lovely light in the archive rooms. I’ve been doing some renovations, you know, bolstering the floors, ensuring proper climate control. Aunt Moira’s very particular about the temperature, naturally. Keen to avoid any damp damage. Particular is an understatement, Moira! And bolstering floors? It’s not a castle, Gareth. It's a house! What kind of climate control are we talking about? Is it going to cost a fortune to keep a damp-free environment in…well, Wales? Seriously, David, you're letting your aunt dictate this. It’s impacting the entire organisation. We're talking about re-routing researchers, paying for extra travel... Now, Sarah, calm down. It’s not ‘dictating’, it’s…consultation. Moira founded the society, remember? She has a significant voice. And Gareth ensures the physical integrity of the archives. It’s a collaborative effort. Honestly, Sarah, have you seen the house? It’s rather spectacular. And the funding is secured. It’s not going to bankrupt us. David is right to highlight the funding, Sarah. The Jenkins Foundation pledged a considerable sum specifically for a dedicated Welsh location. It was a genuine opportunity we couldn't afford to pass up. And it’s not about escaping London, it’s about diversifying. Reaching a new audience. We’ve been too focused on a central hub for too long. We need to engage communities further afield. Think of the research possibilities opened up by being closer to the people who  are  the history! Aye, and the local community's been right welcoming.

“…and then Mrs. Davies asked me, absolutely deadpan, “Is a willow tree sad, Miss Ellis? Because it’s always weeping!” Honestly, I nearly choked on my tea. Where do they get these questions? It’s brilliant, isn't it? Little imaginations running wild." Weeping! Like when I fall over? Exactly, sweetheart! Like when you tumble and need a cuddle. But a willow tree doesn't  really  feel sad, does it? It’s just… that’s what it  looks  like. It's an expression. Like saying "raining cats and dogs!" Cats and dogs falling? That's silly! Yes, it  is  a bit silly, isn't it? But nobody  actually  means cats and dogs are falling from the sky, love. It means it’s raining really, really hard. It's an… an idiom! See? Like a little code we use to talk about things in interesting ways. Is "raining cats and dogs" a code? Like a secret message? Sort of! It’s an old way of speaking. We don't use it so much anymore, but it's fun to know. Now, about Mother’s Day… I was thinking we could make something special for Grandma. What do you both think? Can we make her a crown? Like a king! You think Grandma wants a  king  crown, do you? She'd probably prefer something a bit more… flowery. How about a flower crown  and  a card? We can press some flowers from the garden, and you two can decorate the card with all sorts of sparkly things. Can we use the glitter? LOTS of glitter? A reasonable amount of glitter. We don't want the house looking like a disco ball, do we? Remember what happened last Christmas? Shiny! Everything was shiny! Exactly. Now, after we've done that, I thought we could try and get to Forest School on Sunday. The weather’s looking good. It would be a nice treat for everyone, wouldn't it? We can build a den, look for minibeasts… maybe even find some more willow trees to see if they're weeping! Can we make a fairy house? Of course, darling! A fairy house is a brilliant idea! We’ll need lots of leaves and twigs and berries. We can even collect some of those little pine cones. It’ll be grand! Aw! Oh, no! Don't worry, love. We can build it again. Maybe even a bigger one.

…and honestly, the consultant just kept saying, "We're doing everything we can, Sarah. Everything we can." It's a right platitude, innit? "Everything we can." As if I don’t know that! As if  she  doesn’t know what she's facing. You know, poor Mum, she's always been so…contained, hasn't she? Never one for showing emotion. Now she's just... quiet. Just staring out the window. That's awful, love. Absolutely awful. It's the not knowing, isn’t it? That limbo state. My Claire at work, she's dealing with her dad's COPD, and she says it’s the same. The waiting game, the not being able to plan anything. It just hangs over everything. It does. And poor Ben – he's trying to be strong for her, of course. He’s always been the practical one, hasn’t he? But I saw him yesterday, just for a minute, and his eyes… they looked drained. Like he hadn’t slept in a week. He doesn’t talk about it, not really. Just says “Mum’s being Mum.” Bless him. He’s carrying so much. Men are like that, aren’t they? Bottle it up. Sometimes I think it's worse for them, having to appear stoic for everyone else. My Geoff… he’s been trying to be extra helpful around the house, doing the washing and everything. But you can see the worry etched on his face. He asks after your Mum, of course, but he doesn’t  say  how worried he is. Exactly! It’s heartbreaking, really. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About how fragile everything is. I was thinking yesterday, about Daisy and Tom. They’re getting so big now, aren't they? Seven and five. It feels like only yesterday they were babies. And all I can think about is… what if she doesn’t see them grow up? That's a truly rotten thought. It is, love. It really is. It’s the unfairness of it all, isn’t it? Cancer… it just picks on people. My Auntie Maureen, remember her? Such a vibrant woman. Gone within six months. It’s just… cruel. Are they talking about palliative care with your Mum? They are, but she won't entertain it. Absolutely refuses. Says she wants to fight it. And I don’t blame her, do you? Who wouldn't want to fight?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of marking is ridiculous. I swear, half of them just parrot phrases they’ve heard, no actual understanding of the grammatical structure. It's exhausting trying to gently nudge them towards… well, towards anything resembling independent thought. Sounds brutal. You’ve got that look, you know? The ‘I haven’t slept properly in three days’ look. Did you manage to sort out that timetable clash with the Korean Studies society? Ms. Davies was giving me the side-eye last week when I mentioned I was trying to juggle it. Nearly. Apparently, Professor Lee is incredibly particular about attendance. He’s agreed to let me miss one session a month, but only if I email him a detailed summary of the content I missed beforehand. Which, naturally, I’ll have to research  myself  on top of everything else. It's a bit much, isn't it? A bit? He sounds like he thinks you’re trying to sabotage his Korean empire. Seriously, though, how's your research going? Still wrestling with the passive voice in Korean academic writing? Still wrestling, yes. It’s fascinating, though, how subtly different the constructions are compared to Japanese passive forms. I was reading this paper on… actually, don’t get me started, it’ll take hours. It was a dense read, anyway. Anyway, the seminar on Chomsky this afternoon is going to be a nightmare. Half the class are convinced he’s a genius, the other half think he’s a pretentious charlatan. Oh, joy. Sounds like a productive afternoon then. Did you get to the supermarket yesterday? We’re practically out of everything. I was thinking maybe a veggie curry for dinner? I did, yeah. Got a load of butternut squash – thinking we could roast it with a bit of paprika and maple syrup. Simple and relatively painless cooking. Got some halloumi too, need to use that up. I saw they’re doing two for one on those frozen spring rolls… might grab a few for lunch throughout the week. Ooh, spring rolls are good. I read this article the other day – apparently, in South Korea, it's generally seen as more polite for men to pay for everything on a date. Do you think that's still the case? Or are things changing with the younger generations? That's interesting. From what I’ve gathered, it's definitely ingrained in the culture, though it's evolving, as all cultures do.

No, you're not. You’re writing an essay on the implications of thermodynamics on Victorian industrial society. Which, by the way, is due next week.      Don’t remind me! The library's a warzone. And speaking of warzones, did you see the state of Lancaster city centre after the flooding? It was mental! I walked past the Market Square this morning, still got a load of sandbags out.      Aye, it were awful. Poor Mrs. Higgins’ flower shop got properly flooded. You know, the one near the Sugarhouse? Makes you wonder if we should just relocate permanently to somewhere drier, like... Africa?      Africa? Seriously, Chloe? After you nearly had a panic attack trying to pitch a tent in the Lake District? Remember that camping trip?      Don't you dare bring that up! The wind nearly blew it away! And the midges! It felt like I’d donated all my blood to them! Besides, Africa would be  different . Proper adventure. Imagine, seeing the Serengeti... reading  Chaos Walking  while listening to lions roar!      It wouldn't be all sunshine and safari, Chloe. You’d be battling mosquitoes, probably get some weird tropical illness and definitely miss  The Vampire Diaries .      You’re obsessed with  The Vampire Diaries , El! It’s cheesy as anything. Though, I’ll admit, Stefan was dreamy. Speaking of cheesy, anyone else see Jack Whitehall's tour last year? Killed me!      He's brilliant! Remember that bit about his nan and the Secret Santa present? Foot spa? Classic. We need to play Articulate tonight. I'm feeling competitive.      Ooh, yes! Articulate! But only if we can get through this pizza first. I'm starving. I had that weird nightmare last night, remember? About being chased by Hungry Hippos? Proper stressful.      Don’t even mention Hungry Hippos! That was the bane of my childhood. Actually, remembering primary school… remember Mrs. Davies’ religious studies lessons? So awkward.      Oh god, yes! She used to make us all sing hymns whether you liked it or not! I don’t think I’ve sung ‘Amazing Grace’ since. Did you ever crack your knuckles like me, El? It’s weirdly satisfying.      Only when I'm stressed about my module assessment. Speaking of stress, have you looked at the University Challenge questions this year? They're brutal. I'm honestly thinking of just giving up and becoming a professional pizza taster.      Don’t be silly! We all know you could ace it.

Honestly, it’s just… bewildering, isn’t it? Like, I spend all day wrestling with these massive databases, cleaning up data anomalies, ensuring consistency... and for what? So someone can decide the best way to phrase a bloody supermarket flyer? Welcome to the wonderful world of applied linguistics, love. It's rarely glamorous. You’re a vital cog, you know. That flyer wouldn’t exist in a legible format without your dedication to tidying up the digital mess behind it. Vital cog that's slowly being ground down, more like. I mean, I got a query today, a  serious  query. They wanted me to cross-reference regional purchasing habits with sentiment analysis of Twitter responses to Brexit. Brexit! Honestly, I nearly spat out me tea. What even is the logical conclusion of that? “People in Hull are sad about Brexit, therefore sell more pickled onions”? That’s… niche, even for marketing. But I can see why it would be frustrating. It's disconnected from the actual work. Do you think they even understand what you do beyond “deals with computers”? Nah, not a clue. They think I’m a wizard. Or a robot. “Can you make the spreadsheet do x?” is the usual. Don’t get me wrong, I like the spreadsheets. I really do. It’s just… the  reasons  they want me to do things. This week it's Brexit, last week it was trying to predict the optimal time to launch a new brand of dog biscuits based on lunar cycles. Lunar cycles! Only you would get asked something like that. Seriously, though, you're doing impressive work. You’ve got a postgraduate qualification, you're building a career... and you're used to being told you’re basically a technical support agent. Remember what your mum always says? “Keep yer chin up, pet. You’re cleverer than they think.” Aye, she does. She always said I'd go far. I just picture her now, shaking her head in disbelief at me explaining sentiment analysis to a bloke who probably thinks a hashtag is a type of fence post. Speaking of far… remember when I was interviewing for that internship at Balfour Beatty, back in uni? I was a complete wreck. Couldn’t remember anything I'd learned. Practically tripped over the carpet. Oh my god, you did! Nearly took out their potted fern! You were sweating buckets. I was hiding in the coffee area, terrified they’d notice you and cancel the interview.

Blimey, Doreen, that’s the third time this year. Three times! Shouldn’t’ve bought that cheap set from Argos, should’ve known better. All this newfangled electronics, it’s a right faff, innit? Back in my day, a telly lasted you twenty year, easy. Twenty year! These days…poof! Gone. Now, Arthur, don't start complaining. It's just a television. We've got each other, haven't we? And the rain's stopped, finally. Look out the window, the sun's peeking through. Lovely. Though it was a right downpour earlier. Drenched me gardening gloves. It  is  a bit brighter now, Mum. Dad, did you try turning it off and on again? That usually works, doesn’t it? Obvious solution, I know, but sometimes... Tried that, didn't I? Several times. Proper fiddled about with it. Pointless, though. Honestly, these things are built to break, I reckon. Designed obsolescence, they call it. Money-grabbing, that's what it is. Remember that old valve radio I had? Lasted me through the war, that did! Nothing fancy, mind you. Just static and voices, but it worked. Proper reliable. You’re going on about valve radios again, Arthur? We’re living in the 21st century, you know. Though, I agree about the planned obsolescence thing. My laptop's already showing signs of wear and tear, and it's barely two years old. It’s infuriating. Speaking of things going wrong, my hip’s been playing up something awful today. This damp weather doesn't help, does it? It aches something fierce. I’ve been taking those paracetamol, but they only take the edge off. Doctor says I’m getting old, says it's just wear and tear. Wear and tear! Like a pair of shoes! Mum, have you tried those heat packs Sarah recommended? They worked well for her knee. And have you made an appointment to see the doctor? Just to get it checked properly. I know, I know. But the waiting lists are so long now. You’re lucky, darling, with your fancy job and all your studies. Getting appointments is easy for you. It's not always easy, Mum. It’s busy. But I understand your concerns. Sarah's heat pack idea is a good one, definitely try that. And maybe I can call the surgery for you, see if they can squeeze you in. You youngsters and your fancy gadgets and healthcare.

Tell me about it. Seating plans are the epitome of stressful. I mean, weddings are supposed to be joy, not logistics puzzles. It’s just…what if Chloe and Liam end up next to Colin? He’ll just launch into a monologue about cryptocurrency again. Oh god, Colin. He’s the worst. You’re right, total monologue man. Look, don't stress too much. It's  their  wedding, they’ll be too busy being blissfully unaware of the seating drama to notice. Anyway, speaking of bliss… did you hear back from that bloke, Tom, you were chatting with? Well, he texted. He said he had a really great time and suggested we grab coffee next week. Oh! So,  potential ? A potential Tom! Progress! You were looking a bit…stuck. Don't be dramatic, Sarah. He’s just a bloke who wants to get coffee. Don’t start planning our wedding, please. It’s only been three days. But a coffee! That's a hopeful sign, Elodie. Trust us, we've all been there. Remember when Ben texted me back after two weeks of radio silence? I practically fainted with excitement. That was a truly legendary overreaction, Lucy. How did that one end, anyway? Tragedy! Pure, unadulterated tragedy. Turns out he was already married. Thankfully, he didn't admit it  during  our first date. Awkward doesn't even begin to cover it. Seriously?! You should write a book! "My Date with a Married Man: A Cautionary Tale." You'd be a bestseller! Though, maybe skip that. It does sound a bit... bleak. So, seriously, Elodie, Tom? Coffee? What are your hopes? Secretly, are you plotting a future involving tiny jumpers and afternoon tea? Don't be ridiculous. Tiny jumpers are  not  on my agenda. Although… I did notice he mentioned something about a dog in his profile. He likes dogs. That’s a good sign, right? Dogs are  always  a good sign. Shows responsibility, a potential for cuddles…and someone to blame for chewed shoes. True. Though, be warned, responsibility can curdle into spreadsheet-based dog walk schedules. You’ve been warned. You’re all terrible at reassuring me. Seriously. But I'm enjoying this. It's been so long since we all just properly caught up. It's nice to be amongst friends who understand the chaos of dating in your twenties. Absolutely. And speaking of chaos, did you finalize the menu for the hen do?

Oh, children! They all do that at first, don’t they? My little Thomas did the very same thing when I first got a smartphone. Thought it was magic, he did. Just  poof , grandma appeared on the little screen! It’s lovely, though, isn't it? Keeps them connected. Though, I must say, I miss sending postcards. Proper, paper ones with stamps. Postcards! Now there’s somethin’ I remember. My Auntie Mabel used to send the loveliest postcards from Blackpool. Real colourful, they were. Used to stick ‘em on the fridge. Don't see much of that now, do ya? This internet… it’s all a bit much, innit? Too fast. Makes me dizzy. It  is  a bit overwhelming, I agree. Though, from a teaching perspective, it's been revolutionary. Imagine trying to research anything before the internet! Access to information is incredible. Of course, the downside is the misinformation… and the endless distractions. Trying to keep Year 7 focused on Shakespeare with TikTok buzzing in their pockets? A constant battle, I can tell you. Shakespeare! Fancy. I did a bit of Shakespeare at school, but mostly it went over my head. More interested in the history, I was. Always did like a good historical drama. Remember that one with Elizabeth, the one with Cate Blanchett? Lovely show. Aye, ‘er she were. Gave me a bit of a fright, though, first time I saw ‘er. Looked right regal, she did. Like a queen, proper. Still, it’s a long way to London, ain’t it? Never been. Always wanted to, mind you. See the Tower, see Buckingham Palace… but never had the money, nor the chance. Lack of opportunity, and resources… it's a recurring theme, isn't it? Even with decent pay as a teacher, it’s getting harder to make ends meet. House prices are out of control in Birmingham. My son’s struggling to save a deposit. Oh, the money worries! Don't get me started. It's tighter than ever, even with the state pension. Everything’s gone up, hasn’t it? Food, heating… you name it. These bills…they just keep piling up. Thankfully, I do have a little savings from my childminding days, but it’s dwindling fast. Tell me about it. Been a bit rough, lately. Just tryin’ to make ends meet, you know? Never worked, mind you. Long story. But relied on the benefits and… well, you know how it is.

…and honestly, the sheer number of conjugations in German! It’s just relentless. I mean, you think you’ve mastered one tense, and then BAM, there’s another declension you need to grapple with. It’s brilliant, of course, from a linguistic perspective, but sometimes, as a teacher, I just want to shout, “Just stick to ‘is’ and ‘are’ for a bit!” Aye, languages. Always a bit of a bother, weren't they? Not that I ever really bothered learning 'em properly, mind you. Always had enough English to get by. Essex boy, you see. Never needed a foreign tongue. Though, I did pick up a few phrases on holiday, naturally. "Una cerveza, por favor!" That sort of thing. That’s fair enough! I love travelling, though, and knowing even a few basic phrases really enriches the experience. Last year, I was in Seville, and even just a passable ‘gracias’ and ‘por favor’ opened so many doors. People are much more welcoming when you make an effort, you know? Quite right, quite right. Shows respect, doesn't it? Though, I always found a friendly smile and a bit of a nod worked wonders wherever I went. Never put much stock in the language, myself. Though, you’re doing a good thing, teaching them. These young’uns need to be worldly. Back in my day, you stayed put. Found a job, settled down. Never thought much about seeing the world. It's definitely a different world now. What did you do, exactly? You mentioned being a Managing Director? That sounds rather grand. Right, well...it was a transport company. Haulage, mostly. Big lorries, routes all over the country. Started at the bottom, swept the yard, really. Worked my way up. Long hours, mind you. But it kept a roof over my head. And provided for my family, of course. Funny, isn’t it? All that effort…and now I potter about, watching the telly. It’s a different kind of effort, isn't it? Staying busy, staying engaged. My mum always says retirement is the hardest transition. So, are you doing much these days, besides telly? I've taken up a bit of wood carving, actually. Found some old chisels in the shed. Been whittling away at things. Not particularly brilliant, mind you. Mostly little animals for the grandkids. You know how it is. Keeps your hands busy, your mind occupied. Trying to avoid thinking about… well, never mind.

Honestly, it was mental, wasn’t it? The whole Valentine’s Day thing. Like, everyone just suddenly becomes obsessed with overpriced roses and having to pretend you’re deeply romantic. Tell me about it! My mum was going on  forever  about how I needed to be "prepared" and have a “special plan.” Like I’m some sort of event planner. She kept suggesting Italian restaurants. Italian! Like that’s revolutionary. Right?! It's always Italian. Or a fancy steakhouse. My nan was giving me the same advice. "A bit of red wine, dear, it sets the mood." Red wine! I'm nineteen, Nan! I'd probably just spill it all down myself. Proper classic Nan advice. Mine just keeps saying I need a "proper gentleman" to even  consider  going out for Valentine’s. As if I’m on the market for a trophy. Honestly, the pressure! I ended up just watching 'Everything Everywhere All at Once' with Liam. Quiet night in, pizza, and absolute bliss. Way better than battling crowds for a table at Nando's. Ooh, good choice! I heard that’s brilliant. We ended up at the Odeon, which was rammed. Saw that new romcom, ‘Love & Lattes’. Predictable, but fluffy and needed after Mum’s constant nagging, you know? Ugh, romcoms. They’re always the same plot, aren't they? Meet cute, misunderstanding, dramatic fall out, grand gesture, happy ending. Yawn. Exactly! But sometimes, that's what you need, yeah? A bit of mindless escape. Though, I did notice the accent of the lead actor was all over the place. He was supposed to be from Birmingham, but he kept slipping into a sort of posher, generic British thing. Blimey, yeah! You've got a good ear for that, haven’t you? I reckon it’s 'cause he’s been trying to sound posh for years. It’s like, no matter how hard you try, your roots always poke through. You're so good at picking up on accents. Remember when you thought Mr. Davies was secretly from Cornwall because of the slight lilt? He denied it to the hilt! But I was convinced. It's just... the way he said 'pasties'. It was dead obvious. My mum says it's because I grew up around so many different accents, you know? My lola  always  insisted we spoke Tagalog at home, then the school was full of Midlands kids...

…and that’s what’s so frustrating, isn’t it? The official line is always about ‘economic growth’ and ‘opportunity for all,’ but it just doesn't  feel  like that, does it? Especially when you look at what’s happening with housing. Tell me about it. I just saw another article - five-bedroom house in Ealing, asking for £1.2 million. Seriously? Who  can  afford that? My nan's flat in Kensal Rise, the one she’s been trying to sell for ages, is still £450k and barely moving. And that's a one-bed! Exactly! It's utterly detached from reality. And the thing is, it's not just about affordability, is it? It’s about the kind of society we're creating. Everyone crammed into tiny, overpriced boxes, commuting hours just to sleep. It’s soul-crushing. My uncle, he’s constantly complaining. He’s trying to help my cousin, Aisha, get on the property ladder. She’s a doctor, working ridiculous hours, pays her taxes…and she’s still getting outbid by investors from Dubai. It’s…it’s just not fair. It feels like the entire system is rigged. It  is  rigged. That’s the crux of it, isn't it? It’s capitalism, pure and simple. Unfettered capitalism. And intertwined with that is this casual, institutionalised racism that allows the system to function. Think about who benefits the most from these inflated property prices - it’s not the people who live and work here. It’s international corporations, foreign investors... people who don’t have any real stake in the community. You’re right. When I was reporting on that protest outside Parliament last month, about the new developments displacing local businesses in Brixton, the common thread was people saying they didn't recognise their neighbourhood anymore. Footloose investors coming in, promising regeneration, but really just pricing out the original community. It's gentrification dressed up as progress. It’s a deliberate policy, in many ways. Look at the incentives offered to developers. They're incentivized to build luxury flats, not affordable homes. And then there’s the whole NIMBY thing - “Not In My Backyard” – so everyone wants affordable housing, just not near  their  house. That’s so true. My mum keeps saying we should move further out, to Surrey or something. More space, "better schools"—the usual spiel. But then I think, what's the point of having more space if you're spending three hours a day on a train?

…and honestly, Lizzie, the waiting list was ridiculous. Absolutely ridiculous. People putting their babies’ names down before they’re even born, practically! I had to be quite assertive with Mrs. Davies down at the council, you know. Had to mention your dad’s position and...well, let’s just say a little bit of gentle persuasion helped. Yeah, I can imagine. Sutton Coldfield nurseries are a nightmare. Mum, are you worried about her? Starting nursery next week? Little Willow’s only just turned one! Seems a bit…big, doesn't it? It does, doesn’t it? But the right time is the tricky thing, innit? I’m nervous, of course I am. Leaving her with strangers…well, not strangers exactly, but…you know. But she needs the interaction, love. She’s got plenty of me, you and your dad, but she needs to learn to socialise, make friends, you know, learn to share her toys. It’s important for her development. And frankly… …I need to go back to work. Right, yeah. Speaking of work, have you had any luck with finding something? Remember you were looking at that marketing role at Johnson's? No, not yet. Apparently, they needed someone with more…digital experience. Which, let’s be honest, is everything these days, isn’t it? I feel like I’m ten years behind. It's disheartening, really. It's not like I haven’t got experience, I’ve just been busy being a mum! That’s ridiculous, Mum. Your experience is invaluable. You're brilliant at project management - remember organising your dad’s surprise birthday? That was like a military operation! They’re daft if they don’t see that. Don’t let them knock your confidence. You always were the optimist. Alright, alright. Thanks, love. It’s good to hear you say that. So, nursery…and work. Then there's the weaning! That’s another entire saga. She’s absolutely refusing anything that’s not pureed carrots! Oh god, Willow! Typical. Have you tried baby-led weaning? It's pretty popular now, letting her explore soft foods herself. Might be more engaging than being spoon-fed. I’ve looked into it, but I’m a bit apprehensive. Seems a bit messy, doesn’t it? And I worry about choking hazards. It  is  messy, I’m not gonna lie! But there's loads of guidance online. And the benefits, apparently, are brilliant.

Right, so, Detective Miller was… well, he was surprisingly pleasant, all things considered. He just wanted to get everything down on record, you know? A formal statement. About the incident at the gallery. Pleasant? That doesn’t sound right. Galleries are usually full of posh people who don’t like having police poking around. Was he being ironic? You alright, love? You don't look it. No, no irony. Just… professional. Thorough. He kept saying how appreciative they were of me being willing to help. Apparently, the CCTV footage is a bit… grainy. My description of the chap fleeing is key, he said. I gave him as much detail as I could remember. The tweed jacket, the slightly wonky tie… Wonky tie? Sounds like a right dodgy character. Did he get away with anything? Any paintings nicked? They’re still assessing, Liv. It looks like  one  small landscape was taken. Not one of the big hitters, thankfully. More a watercolour than anything else. But still, it’s awful, isn’t it? The thought of someone just waltzing in and stealing something. Waltzing is a bit strong, Mum. It's probably some impulsive kid. Likely needs the money. Wouldn’t be the first time someone’s helped themselves to something they wouldn't otherwise afford. Though, having said that, a tweed jacket and a wonky tie? Sounds like a caricature rather than a desperate youth. Don’t be flippant, Daniel. Your mother’s just been giving a statement to the police about a theft! And besides, impulsive or not, they're still breaking the law. Did they ask about the security? Seemed a bit lax from what I heard. They did, Dad. They were asking about security procedures. Apparently, it’s been flagged for an upgrade for a while, but funding hasn’t come through. Classic, isn’t it? Speaking of funding, I’ve got a nightmare with EE. My bill is through the roof again. Seriously, I’m only using it for data! I barely even call anyone. They keep trying to sell me extras. Oh, don’t even get me started on phone companies. Have you checked your data usage, Liv? Maybe there’s an app running in the background chewing up gigabytes. I’ve checked! It's normal. I swear they’re just putting the prices up. I’m thinking of switching, but the hassle… Switching is genuinely easier these days.

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it all! You know, we talked about Hadrian's Wall in class the other day – tiny little thing compared to what they were building in Italy and Gaul. It’s just… humbling, isn't it? Knowing they were wrestling with logistics like that, moving legions, building roads, all without, you know, lorries or anything. Yeah, well, they weren’t exactly having a laugh, were they? All that building for a bunch of emperors wanting to build bigger and better things. I did a bit of digging around on a job once – new garden for this bloke near Dunstable. Found a few Roman coins, actually. Nothing worth a fortune, mind, just little copper things. Still, a bit of history under your spade. Proper cool! Did you keep them? Nah, handed ‘em in to the local museum. Wouldn't feel right pocketing ‘em. Though, I did think about asking for a finders fee. Speaking of cool, you seen that new Spartacus show on Sky? It's mental. All the gladiatorial combat. Proper gory, though. Not for the faint of heart. Yeah, I’ve watched a couple of episodes. Pretty brutal. It’s fascinating though, isn’t it? The whole slave rebellion thing. I mean, you read about all these emperors and their excesses, but then you see these guys, fighting for their freedom. It’s powerful. All those early deaths… Right? Makes you think. My grandad, he was a big fan of Roman stuff. Always going on about the legions and the conquest. Used to make me ginger biscuits shaped like shields. Not very good at it, mind. Looked more like wonky moons. That’s brilliant! My mum makes a cracking lemon drizzle cake, if you want a slice. She’s put the kettle on, actually. Fancy a cuppa? I’ve got some proper Earl Grey. Sounds good. Earl Grey's always a winner. You been using those herbs you brought back from Cyprus? That rosemary you got? Yeah! Made a killer chickpea and rosemary stew last night. Used a mortar and pestle to grind the spices, felt authentically Mediterranean, you know? Makes a difference, grinding them fresh. It's definitely an upgrade from pre-ground stuff. Thinking about getting some proper Aleppo pepper, you know, the kind you’d use with pistachios. Pistachios! Nice. You got any nuts knocking about? I'm proper peckish. And some of that bread you’ve got, the sourdough?

Tell me about it, Liv. I’m completely swamped. The English test was awful too, wasn't it? I think I completely blanked on the symbolism in the second poem. Did you at least remember what a metaphor was? Because I felt like my brain just…stopped working. Oh, absolutely dreadful. Mrs. Peterson was marking it like she was personally trying to fail us. The symbolism one was a killer! I wrote about the, like, the recurrent image of…birds? I think? I just grabbed for something. It couldn't have been worse, realistically. But at least we got the essay question about Shakespeare's use of dramatic irony. I felt fairly confident on that one. Did you? I did, yeah. I felt okay about that. It's the poetry I just can’t get my head around sometimes. It’s all so…vague. Speaking of things that are vague, how’s the wind band going? You’re practicing for the concert, aren't you? Loads! It's going really well. Miss Hawthorne’s cracked the whip, though. We’re doing that ridiculously complicated Mozart piece. The clarinet section needs  serious  work. Honestly, poor Chloe's fingers are practically bleeding. But it sounds amazing when we get it right. Are you playing your flute solo yet? Not yet. I’m still struggling with the trills, you know? It sounds like a strangled pigeon more than a musical flourish. Miss Hawthorne is being surprisingly patient though, which is a relief. Art lessons are a bit of a laugh this term. We’re doing still life, and half the class are just drawing slightly wonky apples. Oh, typical. Liam spent the whole lesson staring at the pear, pretending it was a spaceship. I’m trying to go for a more moody, Caravaggio vibe, but it’s hard when you’re surrounded by squashed fruit! Have you started the French vocab lists yet? Madame Dubois is being mega strict about those. Don't remind me. I think I need to dedicate an entire evening to just French. It's just piling up. It’s really not my strong suit, you know? I just forget all the words. Unlike you, you’re practically fluent. Please! I just annoy everyone with my terrible accent. And I keep mixing up  être  and  avoir . It’s mortifying. You know, Sarah from Year 10 was saying she thinks Mr. Henderson is going to ask us to write a comparative essay on  Hamlet  and  The Tempest .

Aye, that sounds familiar, lad. They've always been good at making things complicated, haven't they? When I were teachin’, it were the same. Mountains of paperwork, tick boxes... used to drain the life right out of ya. You still got Mr. Davies for History, haven't ya? Good man, that. Though he does go on a bit about the Romans, doesn't he? Yeah, Mr. Davies. He’s alright, I suppose. He keeps showing us these pictures of Hadrian’s Wall. It’s just… grey stones. Like, when are we gonna learn about World War II properly? All we seem to do is Roman baths. Roman baths, eh? Sounds like my nephew’s lessons. He’s obsessed with dinosaurs, the lad is. All “T-Rex! Triceratops!” and no manners. And don’t even get me started on the tablets they give ‘em now. They cost a fortune, and half the time they don't even work properly. Remember when we used to learn everything from a textbook, Doreen? Aye, Mare! A good old textbook. You could scribble in it, underline important bits… now it's all interactive and ‘engaging.’ Seems more distracting than anything to me. My electric bill alone... Honestly, these tablets are drainin' the power grid! And young Liam's always complainin’ about the battery dyin' when he’s halfway through a research project. It's proper annoying! And my mum keeps on about 'screen time.' Like, what else am I supposed to do? There's nowt else to do in Newcastle! At least the football's been good this season. Did you see the game against Sunderland on Saturday? I did, lad! A cracking game! Though I nearly swallowed my tea when they conceded that goal in the first half. Should’ve been offside! Typical referee. Still, we pulled it back, didn't we? Always good to beat the lads from down South. Football, football, football. Always the same. My Uncle George used to say, "It's just a bunch of fellas kicking a ball around a field." He preferred pigeon racing, you know. Had dozens of 'em. Champion pigeon, that one was. Shame about the fox, though... Aye, every hobby's got its ups and downs, Mare. Speaking of downs, how's your knee feelin’ today? Still achin’? Aye, it’s playin’ up something fierce. The rheumatologist keeps jabberin’ on about exercises and strength training.

Roundabouts, eh? Always been a nightmare, innit? You gotta anticipate, you gotta plan. Used to tell my grandson, little Alfie, "See that car coming? He's thinking he can sneak through! Don't let him!"      It's not just about anticipating, Dad. It’s about… reaction time. And the surgeon said it’ll take a while to fully recover. It’s not the same as a rusty car, you know? It’s my brain.      Oh, dear, that does sound a bit worrying, love. Are you taking those supplements the doctor told you about? For your nerves?      Yes, Mum, I am. Though, between you and me, I think they’re mostly placebo. Anything’s better than not doing anything, I suppose. Anyway, changing the subject – have you seen the state of young Timmy Perkins? He’s absolutely massive now. Honestly, it’s quite concerning. I’ve been reading about the genetic link to obesity, and…      Genetics play a role, certainly, but it’s overwhelmingly environmental. Dietary habits, lack of exercise… processed food is the real culprit. We teach about the physiological impacts in my lectures. The cascade of hormonal responses… fascinating, but deeply troubling when you see it manifesting.      Fascinating, he says! He’s got a slide rule for everything, that one! Timmy just needs a good kick up the backside and a bit of honest graft, that's what he needs. Back in my day…      Now, now, Arthur. Don’t go on about “back in your day.” Things were different then. And Timmy’s a lovely boy, just a bit… round. Remember when little Georgie next door used to say he was going to be a priest?      Oh, that's right! He became a tax inspector. Quite a shock to everyone. So, about Timmy… I’m not sure a kick up the backside is the best approach. His parents are struggling, you know. They’re working multiple jobs.      Precisely. Socioeconomic factors are inextricably linked. Access to healthy food, safe spaces for exercise… it’s a complex interplay. Do you think, Eleanor, that religious belief might offer some comfort to families facing these challenges? Finding strength in faith, perhaps?      Possibly. Though I personally find more solace in a good jigsaw. Speaking of which, Mum, have you finished that one of the Norfolk Broads?      Nearly! Just a few bits left. I found a piece under the sofa yesterday. Such a tricky one, though.

Honestly, this Moodle update is giving me a headache. I’ve spent the last hour trying to figure out how to embed these interactive simulations properly, and it just… refuses. It keeps displaying them as links instead of actually playing within the page. Right, I’ve seen that. It's a nightmare, isn't it? Did you try the iframe embedding? That seemed to work slightly better for me with the virtual chemistry lab. Though, it's still clunky. I did, I did! And it just spat out an error message. Something about security protocols. I’m starting to think they deliberately make it difficult to use anything outside of their incredibly basic file upload function. It's like they  want  us to only post static PDFs. They probably do. It's classic institutional inertia, isn't it? They implemented Moodle ages ago, it vaguely functions, so they're resistant to any significant change. It's easier to just keep patching it than to overhaul the entire system. You know, like the NHS IT system. Exactly! Speaking of systems crashing, the students are moaning about the lack of clear instructions on the module page. Apparently, several of them missed the deadline for the first formative assessment because they couldn’t find it. Oh, bless them. Did you reorganize it? I thought I’d made it a bit clearer after last week’s feedback. I put everything under a main 'Assessment' tab, and then sub-tabs for each piece of work. I tried that, but it’s still not pointing them in the right direction. I even added a huge, bright yellow banner at the top of the page saying “IMPORTANT - Assessment Deadline Approaching!” and they  still  missed it. Their dedication to avoiding obvious information is truly remarkable. It is, isn't it? You know, I was playing around with the announcement function. You can create these little pop-up messages that appear on the main page every time someone logs in. It's a bit intrusive, but maybe it would grab their attention better than a static banner? That’s… actually quite clever! I hadn't thought of that. It might feel a bit aggressive, though. I don’t want to annoy them further. Maybe a gentle reminder, not a full-blown lecture. Yeah, exactly. Something along the lines of: "Quick Reminder! Formative Assessment deadline is on Friday. Links found under the 'Assessment' tab."

Honestly, this jetlag is kicking my socks. I feel like I’m operating at about 50% brainpower. Did you manage to sleep at all on the flight back? Not really, no. Dozed a bit, I suppose, but nothing proper. The little one kept kicking the back of my seat. Worth it, though. Seeing Mum and Dad was brilliant. How was your side of things? Did Maisie enjoy the zoo? She absolutely adored the penguins. Spent a good twenty minutes just… staring. I managed to get some decent pictures. It’s just… travelling with a toddler is tiring, isn't it? Even a short hop like that. Speaking of which, I totally forgot to ask - have you confirmed tickets for "A Midsummer Night's Dream" at the theatre next week? Right, good point. Yes, I did! Got the ones we wanted, reasonably central. Tuesday the 16th, 7:30 curtain up. I’ll print them out later, shall I? Fancy a little pre-theatre dinner somewhere decent too? Somewhere that won’t make me feel too guilty about indulging after living off baby snacks for the last few days. That sounds lovely. Maybe that little Italian place on Elm Street? The one with the pasta carbonara. I've been craving it. Though, knowing Maisie, she'll probably decide that the restaurant itself is a giant climbing frame. That’s a distinct possibility. Maybe we should see if Granny's free to look after her then? It would be much more relaxing for us. And she loves having her. That's a brilliant idea, actually. I'll give her a ring later. It'll be a massive weight off our minds. I was thinking, while I was at the zoo, I saw this amazing children’s bookshop. They had a really lovely section for toddlers. I was thinking we could pop in before dinner, maybe buy Maisie something to keep her entertained. Sounds good. She's been a bit restless this week. Anything specific you had in mind? Not another dinosaur book, I hope. The current collection is bordering on overwhelming. No, no dinosaurs. I was thinking something about animals. Perhaps a pop-up book. They're always a hit with her. Honestly, though, I'm still trying to remember what day it is. This tiredness is genuinely bizarre. I feel like I’ve aged ten years in the last 48 hours. I know the feeling.

…so, yeah, Miriam’s still absolutely adamant about moving back to Dusseldorf. Says she can't stand another London winter, bless ‘er. Thinks the air’s thicker, you know? Like you could cut it with a knife. It's a bit ridiculous, really, considering she spent her whole childhood moaning about the grey skies in Germany! People are funny like that, aren’t they? Always wanting what they don’t have. My cousin, Azad, he’s got that same thing. Keeps going on about how he misses the mountains of Kurdistan. Says the flat horizons here are depressing. He’s living in Birmingham though, so… a bit of a stretch, isn’t it? Not exactly the Zagros mountains. Tell me about it. It’s funny, isn’t it? We all romanticise the past. Miriam's remembering sunshine and strudel, I’m remembering… well, I’m remembering being a teenager and moaning about my parents! But she’s serious about the visa, though. That’s the tricky bit, innit? Brexit’s made everything a right palaver. Aye, it has. It's a nightmare. She needs to get her paperwork sorted quickly. I can have a look at it if you want. My work, with the NRPSI, I deal with a lot of visa applications, particularly for asylum seekers. I might be able to spot something, offer some advice at least. Depends on what she's applying for, obviously. Is she trying to get residency or just a longer tourist visa? Residency. She wants to move permanently. She's got a potential job lined up teaching German, ironically enough. Little independent school, rather lovely it sounds. Honestly, the recruitment agent was banging on about 'rich, enthusiastic pupils'. Made me want a bit of that myself! Right, let me just send you a copy of the application form and her documents... . There you go. Have a butcher’s. Cheers, mate. I'll have a look tonight. Something tells me it’ll be the usual bureaucratic hoops to jump through. Though, honestly, the whole situation is just… frustrating, isn't it? Especially when you think about the larger picture. Take Libya, for example. They're in such a mess, and it's always connected back to oil, innit? And the money... it gets into the wrong hands. Absolutely. The oil money, it's like a curse, isn't it? Attracts all sorts. That Wahabi influence creeping further and further across the Middle East…it’s deeply unsettling.

Honestly, that lamb was divine, wasn’t it? You’ve really mastered the roast, David. Better than my attempts, definitely. Though, I did sneak a little extra gravy. Glad you enjoyed it, love. It’s all about the resting time, you know? Can’t rush a good roast. And don’t worry about the gravy, it wouldn’t be the same without it. Though, your attempts  are  improving. Remember that one last Christmas? We practically set off the smoke alarm. It was a memorable Christmas, that's for sure. Not the best-smelling lamb I've ever encountered, I’ll admit. Though, the effort was admirable, Eleanor. Effort is half the battle. Now, David, about that dining room... Frankly, I still think a television in the dining room is a rather ghastly idea. Mum! We’ve been over this. It’s just for dreary evenings, rainy weekends. It's not like we watch daytime telly in there. It's more… atmospheric, somehow. Especially with the fireplace. She’s got a point, love. It’s a bit… unusual. But, honestly, it's your house, your rules. Besides, it does allow us to watch those nature documentaries without having to lug the TV into the living room. Nature documentaries are perfectly acceptable. Reality television, however… well, let’s just say it doesn't elevate the dining experience. Speaking of elevated experiences, are you two still considering that cruise? I heard they’re lovely. The Caribbean, perhaps? We are, Mum. We've been looking at some brochures. The Eastern Mediterranean looks tempting, actually. Lots of history, proper sunshine. Eleanor’s been trying to convince me to start a workout regime to prepare. Apparently, endless buffets require some… mitigation. He needs to build up his stamina for all the sightseeing! It’s not just about the food, darling. Though, I’m not arguing about the food. Have you ever had Scottish tablet? It's simply divine. You  must  try some. I brought a little box over. Tablet! Now you’re talking. A proper indulgence. Keeps you going, you know. Unlike these dreadful low-fat biscuits they try and fob you off with these days. Truly appalling. And speaking of keeping going, how's Jasper doing? Still chewing on everything he can get his paws on? He is a menace. Absolutely obsessed with my slippers. It’s a running battle, I tell you. He knows he shouldn't, of course, but the temptation is just too great.

is sprawled on the sofa, flicking through channels with the remote. Chloe is meticulously highlighting notes at the table. Maya , with a slight German accent, is sketching in a notebook. Ben is pacing, looking agitated.)     Ben:   Honestly, I’m starving. Did anyone even think about getting more than a single pizza? It’s gone, innit? Just crumbs and regret now.   Chloe:   Relax, Ben. I was gonna order something. Just finishing up this paragraph on Elizabethan sonnets. They're like, trying to rhyme everything seemingly at random.   Liam:   Elizabethan what-now? Sounds proper boring, that does. You're alright, Chloe, buried in your books as always. Fancy a Chinese? My treat… well, when I  have  a treat to offer.   Maya:   Chinese would be lovely! I’m craving something with rice. But, Liam, you’re still saying you’re short for money? You haven’t had any luck with those applications?   Liam:   Nah. Zilch. Sendin’ out loads, like. All soundin’ the same to me, though. “Experienced candidate preferred…” Experienced at what? Breathing? I’ve been breathin' for nearly twenty years, hasn't I? Seems like enough experience to me.   Ben:   You need to tailor your CV, mate. Seriously. All that history stuff… It's brilliant, don't get me wrong, but no one needs to know you can recite the Battle of Culloden when you’re applying for a warehouse job.   Liam:   Aye, I know, I know. Just… feelin' a bit lost, ya know? Everyone else seems to be gallivanting off to uni or gettin’ proper jobs. Me, I’m still here, stuck in me mum’s, endin' up tryin' to mooch off takeaway and watchin’ telly all day.   Chloe:   Don’t talk like that, Liam. You're a clever lad. Remember that essay you wrote on the Tudors? Mr. Davies were absolutely raving about it. You could use that, you know. Frame it as research skills, analytical thinking…   Liam:   Mr. Davies also thought I was being disruptive in class. Keeps gettin’ mentioned, that does.   Maya:   You were being passionate, Liam. There's a difference. And Whitehaven's not exactly overflowing with opportunities, is it? It’s tough for everyone. Just gotta keep trying. Have you considered volunteering somewhere? It looks good on a CV.   Ben:   There's that thing at the community centre, running the kids’ games. Pretty dull, but it’s something. And it’d keep you busy.   Liam:   Aye, I did think about that.

“…and then I was thinking, right, I’ll get them to measure out the ingredients, but not  all  of them. Maybe just the flour and the sugar? That way they’re practicing fractions without realizing it's fractions! Cheeky, innit?” Cheeky! Like a fox, Mummy! I want sprinkles! Lots and lots of sprinkles! Well, we’ll see about the sprinkles, Tom. Too many and the gingerbread men will collapse, won't they? Poppy, you’re right, a bit cheeky! But it’s a good way to get them engaged. It’s Year 2, remember, they still respond so well to a bit of hands-on learning. How do you think it'll go, eh? Last time I tried baking with Year 2, it ended with a flour explosion and three sticky faces. Really, Mummy? Sticky faces? Like mine sometimes after breakfast? Exactly like yours, love. But we’ll be much more organised this time. I've got little bowls for everyone and I’ll be right on hand to mediate any flour-based disagreements. What about this afternoon? Can you two help me make the gingerbread dough? Yes! Can I roll it out? Like a big, big circle? You can definitely help, Tom, but rolling out a big circle is a bit tricky, isn’t it? Maybe you can help me cut out the shapes? We can use those gingerbread man cutters. Ooh, and can we decorate them  after  we bake them? Like real gingerbread men! Absolutely! That's the best bit, isn’t it? Now, speaking of best bits… did you guys have fun playing Tomodachi Life? Liam’s little Mii went and proposed to a sunflower! Honestly, the things that game throws at you. He married the sunflower! Is that real? Not real, silly. It's just a game. But it’s funny, isn’t it? Actually, it reminded me… I was in Morrisons earlier and saw that new book, 'The Boy Who Grew Flowers.' Do you think the class would like that? It’s got some lovely illustrations. Flowers! Like the ones in our garden! Yes, just like our garden, Poppy. It’s about a boy who can grow anything he plants. It’s a bit sad in places, but mostly hopeful. Can we look at it later, Mummy? Please? Of course, sweetheart. We’ll have a proper look after we’ve measured out the flour. And actually, that reminds me… it’s Leo’s half birthday next week!

Honestly, Mark, I still don’t get it. Why a bloody Tesla? Seriously? It's all just… show, isn't it? Show? Come on, love. It’s not  just  show. There’s genuine engineering behind it. And it’s not like I’m buying a ludicrously expensive one. It’s a Model 3, perfectly sensible. And think of the environmental impact! Environmental impact? You’re driving around in a computer on wheels that needs lithium mined from…where exactly? Somewhere that's probably devastating a local ecosystem. Not to mention the electricity it guzzles. Is it all genuinely greener, or just  appearing  greener? It's a process, isn't it? Things aren't perfect. But the overall footprint is significantly lower than a petrol car, especially over its lifespan. And the battery technology is constantly improving. Think about the reduction in emissions in the city. Remember dodging that awful exhaust fumes from old Mrs. Higgins’ Rover on the way to the shops? Blissful, silent motoring, that's what it is. Blissful? Sounds dystopian to me. It’s all so reliant on technology, isn't it? What happens when the software glitches? You're stranded. My little Fiesta, bless its heart, might be a bit…ordinary, but it starts every single time, rain or shine. It doesn't need a firmware update every other week. That’s a valid point, I'll admit. The software updates can be a bit annoying. But that’s a minor inconvenience compared to the benefits. Autonomous driving features, for a start. The traffic on the A11 is a nightmare; autopilot can take some of the stress out of the commute. Autonomous driving? You’d put your life in the hands of a computer?! No, thank you. I enjoy driving. I enjoy…feeling in control. Speaking of computers and things…did you see what Brenda posted on Facebook last night? Brenda? Let me guess, another panoramic picture of her cats wearing tiny hats? Even better! She's posted a conspiracy theory about the internet being controlled by pigeons. Pigeons, Mark! Actual pigeons! Brenda! Seriously? She's always had a slightly…eccentric outlook, hasn't she? It's the algorithm, I reckon. The more bizarre stuff you look at, the more bizarre stuff it feeds you. It’s a rabbit hole. Exactly! It  is  a rabbit hole. It makes you wonder about the data they're collecting on us, doesn’t it?

…and then the giant cheeseburger just  fell ! Like,  splat!  Right on top of the town! Aye, it’s a proper bonkers film, innit? Bet it’d be a nightmare to visualise properly when they were writing it. Imagine pitching that to a studio! “Right, so it’s a world where it rains food…” It’s brilliant! But why did Flint Lockwood invent the machine? Was he just bored? Well, he wanted to solve world hunger, see? Grew up poor, he did, so he wanted to make food accessible to everyone. Bit mad about it, mind you, proper obsessive. He  is  a bit mad. But I like him. Sam Sparks is clever too, though. She’s like, the sensible one. She is, yeah. A bit of a grounding force, isn't she? Makes you think, doesn’t it? It’s almost… a bit like a metaphor, innit? All this abundance, getting out of control, needing someone to rein it in. A metaphor? What's that mean? Right, okay. It means… it's a story on the surface, about food falling from the sky, but underneath it could be about, like, consumerism, or how we sometimes create problems trying to fix other problems. See? It’s deep! It’s just a film about meatballs. You’re probably right. Still, bits of it stick with you. Like, Flint Lockwood doesn't really think about the consequences. He's so focused on the invention itself. It’s a bit like work, actually. Sometimes at the shop, I’m just pushing product out, not really thinking about whether people  need  it, you know? You’re moaning about work already? It's Saturday! I know, I know. It was just… a bit hectic today. Mrs. Higgins was being particularly difficult. Keeps asking for things we don't stock. Says we’re ripping her off if she goes to Tesco. Honestly! Mrs. Higgins is always complaining. Can I have a crisp? Help yourself. You’re going to be the death of these, you are. Still, bet you’ve got more appetite than me. I’m knackered. Dizzy from sorting shelves. Do you think they’d  actually  build a machine like that? Nah. Even with modern tech, it’d be a monumental headache. Think about the electrical load alone! Right, pause the telly for a sec. Where's the remote gone? On the floor, stupid! Behind you. Cheers, love.

…so, aye, you were saying about this Finland fella, this Sanna Marin. Everyone’s having a right go at her over that party video, innit? Seems a bit… harsh, la. Harsh is a generous word, Liam. It’s manufactured outrage, utterly predictable. The papers are having a field day, of course. It reminds me, in a bizarre way, of the attacks on Tony Blair. Remember the constant scrutiny of his personal life? The relentless focus on… well, anything other than policy. Blair? Right. I remember Blair. New Labour, that was the thing, wasn't it? All that ‘Cool Britannia’ stuff. Didn't seem to help much down here, though. The Hillsborough inquests… that's what I remember most about him. Felt like he was avoiding something. A fair point. The complexities of his legacy are, let's say, substantial. But the parallels are striking. The relentless politicisation of personality, the way the media latches onto… perceived flaws… to deflect from larger issues. It’s a tactic as old as politics itself, isn’t it? Distract and conquer. Aye, that sounds about right. Though I still can’t fathom why she had all them people over in the first place, to be honest. A Prime Minister, having a knees-up? Looks a bit daft, don’t it? Liam, you’re a pragmatist, I understand. But politicians are human beings. They're not automatons, spouting policy pronouncements 24/7. A little levity, a social life… Surely that shouldn't be grounds for… this level of condemnation. It’s almost comical, really. I mean, look at the situations governments have been embroiled in! Remember the MPs’ expenses scandal? That was far more egregious. Aye, that was bad. Proper daylight robbery, that was. But at least that was straight-up greed, wasn’t it? This… it feels more like they're just trying to trip her up. Happens all the time. Like with Klopp. Klopp? You’re comparing the Finnish Prime Minister to Jürgen Klopp? That's quite something. Hear me out! They both get stick for being a bit… different. Klopp, with the wild celebrations, the shouting in German… the media were always finding something to pick at. And now, Marin's having a few drinks with some mates, and suddenly she’s unfit to run a country! It's because they're not the grey, predictable types, innit? You know, there’s a surprisingly insightful observation there, Liam.

…and honestly, the transcription quality on some of these BNC recordings is  atrocious . Like, you can barely make out the vowel shifts, especially in the older stuff. It's frustrating because you're trying to glean nuanced linguistic information, but it’s just a muddle. I spent three hours yesterday trying to decipher a single sentence from a bloke talking about… well, never mind what he was talking about, the point is, I heard more static than sentence! Oh, tell me about it. Dealing with old audio is the bane of any archivist’s existence, isn’t it? Though, I find myself slightly obsessed with the older stuff, the way people  used  to speak.
