It's like listening to history, innit? Did you hear back from Liam about the LinkedIn workshop? Not yet. I messaged him last night. Apparently, he’s wrestling with updating his profile. You know Liam. He just wants to list "enthusiastic spreadsheet enthusiast" as a skill. Typical. He’s a brilliant editor, though. So, what else is happening? Did you see Elara’s post about being in the Maldives? The pictures were  insane ! Turquoise water, white sand... makes you want to chuck it all and just... disappear. I did! Seriously, it looked like paradise. I’m properly jealous. We’ve been talking about that for ages, haven’t we? Remember, when we were dreaming of going somewhere really exotic? Absolutely! We were planning on seeing whales in Iceland, weren’t we? I’m still up for that. Although, with the flights... Honestly, even just thinking about getting on a plane makes my palms sweat. I know exactly what you mean! My nan used to say flying was unnatural. I'm not  that  scared, but I definitely get anxious. I've been trying to rationalise it. Probabilities and safety statistics and all that, but…doesn't really stick, does it? Nope. Logic doesn't work with fear. I'd settle for somewhere a bit closer, actually. Spain, maybe? Barcelona, Seville... tapas, sunshine, decent wine... Now you're talking. We definitely need a holiday. Something involving less altitude than 30,000 feet. Honestly, I've been so bogged down in this research, I've forgotten how to relax. This job is brilliant, but the pressure… It is, isn’t it? But remember what you said about work-life balance? You've been a champion of it for  us , don't forget to apply it to yourself!

…Honestly, Mum, I’m still thinking about getting the whole sleeve done. Like, properly. Not just a few bits and bobs. The artist I saw last week, Rhys, he's got some  incredible  work. Real depth, you know? Not just flashy designs. A whole sleeve, Liam? That's...quite committed. And at your age? You'll be regretting it when you’re applying for serious jobs. You're only just finished your grad scheme, remember? Think about your CV. Mum, relax. It's not like I'm getting a portrait of a badger on my forehead. It’ll be intricate stuff, botanical – some old Victorian illustrations woven together. It'll be class. Besides, plenty of people have tattoos. It's not the end of the world. And Rhys knows his stuff, he specialises in fine line work, it’s practically art! Fine line or not, it’s permanent. Still. What are we having with this lamb tagine? Do we need more couscous? I was thinking pomegranate seeds, a little something extra. Yeah, pomegranate sounds good. Loads. And couscous’s sorted. Listen, speaking of serious, how’s that new intern doing? Honestly, the last few have been… a bit lacking. Remember Bethany last year? Spent three days convinced commas were sentient beings. Oh, Bethany. She was a delight, in her own way. This one, Chloe, is rather more diligent. A little… eager, perhaps. Keeps asking for feedback every five minutes. I’m trying to channel her enthusiasm, give her actual projects instead of just proofreading. It’s hard, isn’t it? Finding good people. The industry’s ruthless. Finn: Right, festive overload achieved! Got the cranberry sauce, the mince pies and… smells delicious in here! Lamb tagine? You’re spoiling us! Finn! About time. We were starting to think you’d got lost in a Christmas market. Finn: Never! Just…efficiencies needed. The price of Brussels sprouts is outrageous this year. So, what’s the chatter? Tattoos and intern drama? Standard Thursday evening. Liam’s contemplating permanently decorating his arm. And Chloe, the intern, is proving to be a tiny ball of nervous energy. Finn: Classic. Sounds like a productive day at the office then. So, Christmas plans? Have you two booked anything? I’m still wrestling with my nan – she insists on hosting, of course, which means spending the entire day refereeing arguments about gravy consistency. We haven't really sorted anything yet, to be honest.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of newsletters I get about sustainable fashion is overwhelming. It's all 'ethically sourced this' and 'organic cotton that,' but it feels so…performative sometimes, you know? Like brands are just jumping on the bandwagon. Absolutely. It's a tricky one. There’s definitely a greenwashing issue, isn’t there? I mean, I’ve been trying to be more conscious about what I buy, but it’s exhausting! I ended up almost having a minor meltdown in H&M last week trying to decipher whether a t-shirt was  actually  better than another. Ended up just buying a pair of socks. Basic socks. Classic. I know that feeling. It's like, do you want to feel guilty about supporting fast fashion, or guilty about paying a ridiculous amount for something that might have been made in questionable conditions anyway? Right, this smells incredible, by the way. You’ve outdone yourself with the lentils. Thanks! It’s a really simple recipe, actually. My nan taught me. Lots of vegetables, a good stock cube – don’t tell anyone – and a generous dollop of curry paste. Keeps me going for days. You’re eating much better than me this week, I bet. Still surviving on Deliveroo and anxiety? Pretty much. Deadline hell. The new investigative piece on local council finances is demanding. I’ve been practically living on coffee and instant noodles. My yoga teacher, Anya, nearly had a fit when I admitted that. She practically threatened to revoke my membership if I didn’t promise to eat something green. Anya sounds fierce. I’ve been thinking about trying that body combat class she runs. Apparently, it’s a brilliant stress reliever. Though the thought of hitting pads with that much gusto… I'd probably pull a muscle. I’m still recovering from that ridiculous hamstring tweak I got trying to chase after Finn’s kite in the park last month. Oh God, Finn and kites are a recipe for disaster! Remember last summer when he got it tangled in the branches of that oak tree? You practically scaled it like a ninja. Don't remind me! My knees haven't been the same since. That’s why I need the body combat, I figure some pent-up aggression might do me some good, plus a bit of strengthening. Speaking of travel, you mentioned your trip to Morocco last year, didn't you?

Honestly, Daniel, I’m still fuming about that student, Liam. Absolutely incandescent, I was. Liam again? What did the bright spark do this time? Forget to read the assigned texts? Worse! He actually  argued  with me about the difference between realism and naturalism in Victorian literature. Argued! As if he’d done some independent research proving me wrong. I mean, I appreciate enthusiasm, really I do, but the sheer audacity... It’s exhausting, isn’t it? Sometimes I wonder if they even listen. It is. It truly is. The assumption that Google knows better than a lecturer with a decade of experience… a recurring theme, I’m finding. Remember Sarah’s complaint about Mark in her history class? Same vibe. Oh, absolutely. Typical. Though, I must admit, your lectures on post-structuralism sound far more impenetrable than my Victorian novels. Do you ever get that feeling they’re just nodding along, hoping you'll finish so they can escape? Consistently. I often wonder if half the class is daydreaming about dumplings. Though, they do ask surprisingly intelligent questions afterward, sometimes. It’s a peculiar phenomenon. Speaking of peculiar… have you noticed my big toe is playing up again? Don’t even start. Last week it was verging on grotesque. Are you seriously refusing to get it clipped? You know how much I hate seeing your feet like that. It's rather rebellious, this toe. Refuses to be trimmed, it does. I’ll get around to it. Eventually. Right now, I'm more concerned about Amelia and Ben. Did you hear back from her about that weekend? About the pottery workshop? No, not yet. I texted her yesterday, just a casual “Hope you're well, still thinking about the pottery?” No reply. I'm starting to think they’re dithering. It's such a lovely place, that studio in the Old Town. Perfect for a slightly-out-of-sync couple like them. Yeah, it is. They  need  something like that. Ben's been so stressed with the new project at work. And Amelia...well, Amelia needs to rediscover her creative spark. She keeps saying she’s ‘too busy’ but I suspect it's more about fear of failure, you know? They both are. I know exactly what you mean. It's heartbreaking watching friends get stuck in a rut. Remember how vibrant they were when they first met, all those open mic nights and experimental photography?

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it! He just kept interrupting, correcting my French, even though I  told  him I was just chatting to the waiter! It was mortifying. My French isn’t perfect, obviously, but I can hold a conversation. Sounds like your brother-in-law, then. Classic Rupert. Can’t help showing off, can he? A bit like when he tried to explain the complexities of market fluctuations to me at Carol's wedding. As if I hadn’t spent the last twenty years running a company! Exactly! It’s that little condescending pat on the head, you know? Anyway, it completely threw off my enjoyment of the film. It was supposed to be a lighthearted romantic comedy, but I was too busy mentally composing a polite retort. Did you see "Oppenheimer," by the way? Everyone’s raving about it. I did! Just last week, actually. Absolutely gripping. Nolan's at the top of his game, isn’t he? The way he visualises that… tension, the moral weight of it all… incredible. Didn’t think I’d get so invested in a film about nuclear physics, to be honest. Margot Robbie was fantastic, of course. Though truthfully, Cillian Murphy  was  the film. He just... inhabited the role. Agreed. He was mesmerizing. Though I do think it's getting a bit ridiculous the obsession with Robbie. She's talented, obviously, but people treat her like she’s single-handedly carrying the industry. It reminds me of everything that happened with Meghan Markle, doesn’t it? The over-the-top praise, the sudden vilification… it’s all so bizarre. You've hit on something there. The fickle nature of celebrity is wild. One minute they're being championed, the next they’re being torn apart. It's more than just a bit of online gossip, isn’t it? It feels… manufactured sometimes. Like there's a whole industry dedicated to building them up and knocking them down. It's rather unsettling when you think about it. Absolutely! Which makes you wonder about… well, you know…  everything . Have you been following that whole stuff about the deep state and… well, the usual conspiracy theories? Oh, you know me, always keeping an eye on the alternative narratives. It's not that I believe everything I read, but to completely dismiss them out of hand is, I think, a bit naive. There’s definitely… things that don’t quite add up, isn’t there?

Honestly, Dad, this landscape is just… gray. Everything’s gray! Even the sheep look gray. Now, now, love. Don't be like that. It's a bit overcast, aye, but look at that field over there, bursting with buttercups. See them? Yellow as lemony drops they are. And the heather's just starting to come out. It’ll be purple in a few weeks. I saw one buttercup. One! And the rest are just… drab. Reminds me of the Wicked Witch of the West. Everything in Oz was so colourful, wasn’t it? Emerald City, ruby slippers… a proper contrast to this. Aye, it did. Right you are. Though I always thought the Cowardly Lion showed a bit more spirit than he lets on. Tell ya what, when we get closer, I'll point out some proper colours. Think we'll pass the Jamaica Inn later, won’t we? Remember that from Daphne du Maurier's book? Proper spooky place. Vaguely. I think Mum made me read it when I was, like, ten. All I remember is that she kept hinting it was about proper romantic suspense. It felt a bit… dreary, to be honest. Like this road. Romantic suspense, eh? Your Mum does have a way of putting things. Anyway, right, keep an eye out for a signpost. I think we should be taking the A30 soon. My sat-nav’s being a bit temperamental. Remember when we used to rely on maps? And proper telephone boxes? Sending telegrams. Telegrams? That’s ancient, Dad! People sent texts now. Actually, I just got one from Chloe - ‘almost ready to leave! xx’. She’s still struggling to pack, typical. Texts, aye. Progress, I suppose. It’s all a bit quick for me. I remember my Grandad, he could tap out Morse code faster than you can say ‘chocolate biscuit’. Used to pretend to be a telegraph boy when he was a lad. He even learnt Braille, just out of curiosity. Said he thought it was fascinating. Wow. Braille? You're full of random facts, aren't you? It's like having a Lewis Carroll character in the car with you. All riddles and odd knowledge. Did you ever learn Morse code? Tried. Failed miserably. My brain’s more suited for dealing with irate customers on the phone, I reckon. Speaking of which, did you remember to pack your swimming costume? We’re going to the beach, after all!

Aye, tell me about it. Categorising Victorian railway timetables isn’t exactly setting the world on fire, is it? Though, I did find one from 1888 that went straight through Haltwhistle… weird, innit? Haltwhistle? Right near the Roman Wall, that is. Used to go there on a coach trip, once. Years ago. '58, I reckon. Picturesque, it was. Though the coach driver was a right terror. Kept trying to short-cut through fields. Nearly lost a wheel in a ditch. Remember the smell of petrol back then? Chimney cake flavoured, it seemed. Not like this… this fancy unleaded stuff they’ve got now. Makes you cough just smelling it. My view is, the petrol situation is a complex macroeconomic issue… the supply chain, the geopolitical factors… Och, Liam, not the lecture again! Grandad here’s just reminiscing about coach trips and chimney cake petrol. Let the man be. Chimney cake petrol! That's a good one, lass. Reminds me of the Monopolies and Regulated Industries Act of 1990. Changed everything, it did. Suddenly we weren’t all relying on British Petroleum for everything. Technically, the Act aimed to promote competition in the gas and electricity markets more directly... though it had ripple effects across the board. Did you ever visit those old ESSO stations, Grandad? The ones with the bright red pumps? My father used to take me to them. They felt like a little slice of America. ESSO! Don’t you mention ESSO! Used to work near one. Could smell it for miles. Always a queue. And the prices! Nowadays, you wouldn't  believe  the prices. It’s highway robbery, it is. Saw a bloke filling up the other day, shaking his head. Said a pint of milk was cheaper than a gallon of petrol. Aye, that's the truth of it. Makes you wish you could still pop down to the local miner for a top-up, doesn’t it? Speaking of prices, did you see the Odeon’s showing “Barbie”? Thirty-five quid for three of us! Criminal! Cinema prices  are  exorbitant. I’ve started sticking to streaming, honestly. Better picture quality, considerably less hassle. Though, I do miss the shared experience. Remember going to the Gaumont in Harpenden? Every Saturday. Grease, Breakfast at Tiffany's… Gaumont! That takes me back. Used to go to the Regal in Timperley. Saw "Casablanca" there. Never been the same cinema since.

…and honestly, Mum, I’m still knackered. That flight from Seoul was brutal. Twelve hours, even with those noise-cancelling headphones. Jet lag is a proper beast, isn’t it? I feel like I’m running on fumes. Oh, love, you do. It’ll take a good few days to shake it off. A nice cuppa and a good lie down usually does the trick. Are you eating properly? You know you don't look yourself. You were always a skinny thing. I'm trying, yeah. Had a bit of kimchi fried rice last night. It was alright, but not quite like nan used to make. Speaking of, are you still using her recipe book? It's got all the best bits, hasn’t it? Of course I am! It’s falling apart at the edges, though. Likely needs a new spine. I use it for everything. You remember her plum cake? Absolute heaven. But you need to eat more than just spicy rice, Daniel. You’ll waste away. Have you touched any of this shepherd's pie I made? Proper comfort food. I will, Mum, I promise! It smells amazing. Right, about the packing. I’ve been going through the list. Cushions, definitely. Bed linen, yes. What about that old photo album, the one with pictures from the holiday in Norfolk when I was little? Oh, that one! Keep that safe, sweetheart. There's a lovely picture of you trying to catch a weaver fish on the beach. You were convinced it would grant you three wishes. Remember? You were so serious about it! God, I do! I think I was about six. It's funny the things you remember, isn't it? James says the flat's got tons of space for stuff, but I’m suddenly realizing how much  stuff  I actually have. Well, you've always been a collector of things, haven't you? Just be sensible. Those old football shirts…are you really taking all of them? Most of them, yeah. Sentimental value. And James is surprisingly keen on them. He says they're vintage! He's being very supportive of the move, actually. Very excited about us getting married properly. That's lovely to hear. He seems like a good lad. Are you both getting on alright, then? No silly arguments? The usual, Mum. You know how it is. We had a bit of a disagreement about wallpaper the other day, but nothing major.

Right disaster area, isn't it? I need to get this trimmed. I thought the layers would be easier, but it just looks…ratty. Like a startled badger. Don’t be daft, it looks fine. It suits you. Besides, you’ve been stressing about this research grant application. Not exactly prime time for a salon visit. Aye, well, stressful or not, I’m starting to resemble a woodland creature. It’s all this sitting about, isn’t it? Look at the passionflower on the windowsill, though. Absolutely thriving. You’ve done good bringing a bit o' the jungle in here. Thanks. I’m trying to build up a bit of a mini-greenhouse. Helps my brain, you know? Something to focus on outside of molecular biology. Did you see they’re saying that the new drought-resistant strains could revolutionise agriculture in…well, everywhere really, given the climate situation. Aye, I saw something about it. It's needed. Though I’m proper worried about this petrol crisis, aren't you? Filling up the car last week was a right palaver. Prices are mental. It feels like everything’s going to go through the roof, doesn't it? It’s not looking great, is it? Supply chain issues, geopolitical stuff… a perfect storm. It makes you wonder how people on lower incomes are coping. It's just... galling, isn’t it? Especially when you see how much the NHS is struggling. My aunt’s waiting for a hip replacement, and it’s been ages. Tell me about it. Gran's been having trouble with her arthritis, and getting an appointment with the rheumatologist feels like winning the lottery. It's scandalous, really. They were talking about it on the news this morning – the staff shortages are critical. Absolutely. And they're talking about throwing more money at the problem without addressing the fundamental issues, you know? Burnout, low pay... It feels like a plaster on a gaping wound. Reckon it’s partly down to these ridiculous A-Level reforms, too. Everyone’s crammed into doing fewer subjects, and with such intense pressure, loads of bright kids are just… well, burning out before they even get to university. Remember how much easier it was when you could specialise gradually? Definitely. They’ve narrowed the scope, haven't they? It's supposed to be about depth of understanding, but it just feels like it’s limiting opportunity.

Aye, right. Everything's an opportunity for a lecture with that man. He’d probably find a silver lining in a volcanic eruption. Honestly, I'm startin’ to think History's not for me. Too much doom and gloom. But it  is  fascinating, isn't it? All that stuff about the flagellants? And how the social order completely shifted because everyone was dying! It’s wild! Though, I suppose talking about it over instant noodles isn't exactly setting the scene. It's a bit grim to be dwelling on pestilence, isn't it? Especially when we're all stressed about looming deadlines and whether we can afford next week’s rent. Speaking of which, how’s the waitressing going, Beth? Still decent tips at that bistro? So-so. It's alright, you know? Pays more than working in a clothes shop did, but it’s long hours and me feet are killin’ me. Still gotta pay for books and whatnot, though. And that uni flat's bleedin' me dry. Rent's a joke, innit? Tell me about it! I’m seriously considering picking up extra shifts at the market. Mum’s been goin’ on about it, sayin' I need to be savin’ as much as possible. I’m trying, honest! It’s just… EVERYTHING’s so expensive. You're tellin' me! Look at the price of fags these days! It's daylight robbery, it is. I'm down to me last packet and I'm dreading having to go out and get more. Gonna have to cut back, I reckon. Though, cuttin' back's easier said than done when you're stressed, eh? It's a vicious cycle, isn't it? Stress leads to smoking, smoking empties your bank account, feeling broke leads to more stress… It's almost designed to keep us trapped. It does make you think about, you know, systemic stuff. Like… like feminism and all that? Aye, exactly like that. I mean, how much of this is down to societal pressures, designed to keep us frantic and focused on earning, rather than questioning things? We’re all workin’ our socks off just to keep our heads above water, and for what? Don’t even start me on that! The pressure on girls especially is mental. Restin’ on your laurels just isn't an option; you're always gotta be hustlin'. And then if you  don’t  work, you get judged.

…and honestly, it's not about them doing anything  terrible . It’s just… a shifting. You know? Like tectonic plates. Everything feels a bit strained, a bit forced. We used to just  get  each other, and now it feels like I’m translating their enthusiasm, their anxieties… it’s exhausting. Yeah, I get that. It’s a weird feeling, isn't it? That sense of having outgrown something. Like when you loved a band in sixth form and then, suddenly, their music just sounds… juvenile. But with people, it feels so much more complicated because there’s history, shared memories… guilt. Exactly the guilt! That's a big part of it. I feel awful even  thinking  about distancing myself from Sarah. We've known each other since we were kids. We went through everything together – dodgy haircuts, disastrous boyfriends, the entire university application process. But her life is so… relentlessly  upbeat  now. Posting pictures of organic smoothie bowls and weekend yoga retreats. It's not that I don’t want her to be happy, but it's just… not me. And trying to maintain that facade of enthusiasm feels so inauthentic. Sound familiar. My cousin, Chloe, is exactly like that. Constantly sharing her vegan baking successes and motivational quotes. I'm happy for her, genuinely, but the pressure to participate in the lifestyle is real. The thing is, though, isn’t it just… life? People change. Friendships evolve. It’s not necessarily anyone’s fault. I know, logically. I repeat it to myself. 'People change, friendships evolve'. It feels like a platitude, though, doesn’t it? Like something you say to avoid admitting you’re deliberately choosing to let a connection fade. The problem is, I’m dreading the awkward conversation. "Hey, Sarah, I need a bit of space." It sounds so brutal. Brutal, yes, but honesty is usually better in the long run, isn’t it? Avoiding it just leads to resentment, doesn't it? I’ve been thinking about this with someone myself actually. Not a close friend like Sarah, thank goodness, but a work acquaintance. We used to have a lot in common, theatre and stuff. But she's become… intense. She spends the entire lunch break analysing every nuance of the latest production, and expects me to do the same. I'm just not interested, you know? I like theatre, but I'd rather talk about the weather or what we’re having for dinner.

…and honestly, the seminar on Post-Structuralism just felt like a load of waffle, you know? Everyone’s throwing around Foucault and Derrida like they're gospel, but nobody actually seems to  understand  what they’re on about. I mean, I’m trying, I really am, but sometimes I just want to shout, "Just tell me what it  means !" Oh, academia. It used to be so delightfully obscure, didn’t it? When  I  was at university – Heidelberg, back in the fifties - it felt like a secret society. But at least then, the obscurity felt intentional, part of the charm. Not this… seemingly deliberate cloudiness. Are you struggling with the reading workload as well, darling? Yeah, the reading's insane. Professor Davies sets, like, twenty pages of dense theory per week. It's not even about the content, it's about the language. It’s all inversions and qualifications and… proper head-scratching stuff. Still, I’m enjoying the practical side, the photography module. I’ve been experimenting with long exposures down by the Thames. Got some really interesting shots of the reflections. Photography! Wonderful. That’s always been far more intuitive than most of the artistic mediums. You always had a good eye, even as a little boy. Remember that series you did of pigeons in Hyde Park with your dad’s old camera? Quite remarkable, actually. More expressive than half the things I’ve seen in the Tate. Blimey, you remembered that? I was, like, eight! Dad nearly had a heart attack when I dropped it in a puddle. Speaking of which, Mum’s asking when you’re coming to visit her in Brighton. She’s getting properly stressed about the Christmas decorations. Wants everything perfect. Tell her I’ll be there for the week before, naturally. I refuse to be trapped in a house full of tinsel for Christmas Day itself. It feels… rather fraught, doesn’t it? Brighton is lovely though. Perhaps I'll finally tackle some painting there. I’ve been feeling rather uninspired here lately. It’s the light, I think. Everything is so… grey. You should! You haven't painted much since… well, since Austria. You remember those landscapes you used to do? So vibrant. Are you still thinking about that trip to Tuscany? You were saying you wanted to look at the Renaissance frescoes in Florence again. Oh, yes! I’ve been researching some incredible exhibitions there.

Right, so, realistically, we’re looking at another two hours, minimum, to Tarnow. Are you sure you don’t want something to eat before we hit the gym? Like, a proper bite? We've been munching on those weird Polish supermarket biscuits all morning. Honestly, love, I'm not particularly hungry. And I'm not sure I  want  to eat before a workout. Makes me sluggish, you see. Besides, the gym's the only thing keeping me even vaguely active these days. It's... routine, isn't it? A bit of structure. Routine's good! But, like, a protein bar or something? Or even just an apple? Don't want you keeling over on the treadmill. You know, I did a class this morning with a group of Japanese businessmen. They were obsessed with optimal fuelling, pre and post-workout. Kept asking about BCAA ratios. It was mental! Japanese businessmen and BCAA ratios… sounds about right. It's all become so performative, hasn't it? This fitness thing. Everyone needs to document their progress, their 'journey,' on Instagram. Back in my day, you just… went to the gym. Well, yeah, but it's also helpful for accountability, isn't it? And motivation. Though I agree, it can be a bit overwhelming sometimes. You’re right, it’s become more about the image than the actual… everything. My shoulders are aching like mad, though. Driving for this long is taking its toll. You've been a star, letting me do most of it. Don’t be silly. It’s lovely being driven. It’s… pleasant. Just let me look at the trees. They’re rather nice, aren't they? Much better than trying to navigate those pot-holed roads. You're doing brilliantly, by the way. You drive with such a calm assurance. Not like some of the locals… utterly terrifying. They are, aren't they? Like they’re in a rally! Still, another hour or so. Are you feeling up to a decent session? We talked about squashing those glutes yesterday... Glutes. Yes. Well, I’ll have a go. Honestly, sometimes I feel a bit ridiculous, you know? A woman my age, obsessing over her glutes. It feels… a bit… vulgar. I mean, I know it shouldn’t, but it does. Don’t be daft! There’s absolutely nothing vulgar about being strong and healthy. It's empowering. And besides, you look great!

Oh dear, that's awful! Agnes is a dear, though, isn’t she? Always bringing round those prize-winning marrows. Though, honestly, they’re bigger than my head! And you know how clumsy she can be. Reminds me of trying to wrangle a particularly stubborn wheel of clay the other day. Just wouldn’t cooperate. Clumsy as a badger in a china shop, that woman. But a good heart, a good heart. Just like you, lass. Always fussing about. Tell me, are them mugs finished then? The ones you were showin' me last week? Almost. Just a glaze left to do. They’re hand-thrown, you see, each one a little different. I’m trying a new cobalt blue this time. What do you think of cobalt, eh? Does it go with your kitchen? With your… well, with everything? Cobalt’s a bit bold for my tastes, pet. I always preferred a nice cream, like the milk they used to use. Proper, rich milk, thick enough to stand a spoon in. Not this watered-down nonsense you get nowadays. Shame, that is. Absolutely! It's all changed, hasn't it? Everything's changed. Speaking of which, this weather! It's been proper biblical, hasn’t it? One minute sunshine, the next torrential rain. I spent hours this morning weeding the roses, and then had to run back inside when a proper downpour started. Everything’s dripping. Aye, wet as a week old tea towel. And spiders! I’ve seen more spiders in the last fortnight than I have in the last ten years. Big ones, too! Crawling across the window sill. Gives you a proper fright, it does. I nearly jumped out of me skin this morning when one dropped onto me head. Oh, no! You poor thing! They do seem to be everywhere this year. I had a little one in the fern yesterday. I try to relocate them, you know. Don’t like to squash them. Keeps the garden balanced, I think. You still enjoying your dahlias? They were looking lovely when I popped round last week. Dahlias are blooming well, they are. Best I’ve had in years. Been feeding them with that liquid stuff you gave me. Clever thing, that idea. Though I did have a little fright the other day. Power cut, you see. Went pitch black. Thought the world was ending! Oh, the power cut!

Seriously?! That’s brilliant, Mum! Can she really come? I thought you said it was too crowded. Well, I did, didn't I? But she was very persuasive. And honestly, having another adult to help with you two… it would be a godsend. I’m not going to lie, I’m a bit nervous about three teenagers running around Barcelona on their own. Besides, Sarah’s organised, she'll keep an eye on you all. 'Teenagers running around,' that’s a lovely way to put it, love. More like a whirlwind of energy and requests for gelato. But aye, Barcelona's a good shout. Plenty o' music there too. Saw a bloke playing a mean Catalan guitar in a pub a few years back. Gelato  every  day, definitely! Can we look at which gelaterias are best? There’s gotta be one that does pistachio  and  salted caramel. It’s a vital part of the planning. Of course, darling. Priorities, right? Okay, so Sarah's potentially in. Have you spoken to Liam about it, Finn? Liam’s just sent me a thumbs-up emoji. He’s playing Apex Legends with Ben right now, so he’s not super chatty, but the thumbs-up seems pretty positive. Apparently, Ben’s already researched the Sagrada Familia. He says we  have  to see it. The Sagrada Familia? Right, right. Gaudi’s masterpiece. Grand building, that. Though, it’s always packed. Should get tickets online before you go, otherwise you’ll be standing in line for hours. Reminds me of queuing for tickets to see The Smiths back in ‘86… different sort of architecture, of course. Booking tickets  is  something I need to tackle. And I need to check the accommodation, too. That Airbnb we had last time was… rustic. Let’s just say the shower had character. Rustic is good! It adds to the adventure. But maybe not  too  rustic. No spiders, please, Mum. Please, please, please. Aye, spiders are a problem. Give me a good pub any day. Proper pint and a bit of music. Barcelona's got those too, I reckon. So, Sarah’s coming, Liam's giving it a go, Finn's after gelato… sounds like we’re getting somewhere. What about flights, then? Prices gone sky high, I imagine? They have, haven't they? I had a quick look this morning. It’s looking like it’s going to be the bulk of the budget.

Ugh, honestly, that film was  so  good, though. Like, Heath Ledger? Proper dreamy. I’m still having a full-on Kat Stratford moment. You know? All angsty and quoting poetry. Yeah, it was brilliant. I loved how independent Kat was, even when she was being, like, deliberately difficult. And Joseph Gordon-Levitt was cute, but Heath was just...  Heath . You can’t really argue. Exactly! He totally redeemed the rom-com genre, innit? Most of them are just so predictable. You know he’s going to end up with her in the end, even if they’re fighting the whole time. This one felt...real-ish. Real-ish is a good way to put it. Speaking of real, Mrs. Davies is being  impossible  about the history project. Oh, don’t even  start  on Mrs. Davies. She's got it in for me, I swear. I had a proper chat with my mum about it last night. She doesn’t seem to understand that researching the Magna Carta is boring! I mean, who wants to write three thousand words on bloody old lawyers? Tell me about it! Mine’s about the Industrial Revolution, and I’m finding it really difficult to find anything interesting. Everyone’s focusing on the trains and the factories, but there’s gotta be something more. Maybe look at the impact on women? Or the working conditions? My mum suggested focusing on a particular social reformer. That might spice things up a bit. That’s a good shout. I’ll have a proper look later. Are you, like, actually going to start your project this weekend? ‘Cause I’m panicking already. We’re supposed to hand it in three weeks! Don’t remind me. I was hoping to procrastinate a bit and then have a mega-study session the night before. That usually works…  usually . You’re mad! I’m trying to get a head start. Mum's booked us a day trip to London next month, remember? Need to do well so I can properly enjoy it. Oh yeah! The London thing! I totally forgot. We’re actually going? Like, properly going, not just a quick jaunt to Covent Garden to buy some overpriced ice cream? Properly going. Mum’s got tickets to that new Shakespeare exhibition at the Globe. And she said we can pick one thing we  really  want to do. Ooh! Fancy. Right, okay, rethink the procrastination.

A knitted… what now? A 'double-tap'? Cor, these youngsters and their… their… Facebook. It’s all a bit much, innit? Used to be a nice postcard, you know. A picture of the beach. Simple. It’s okay, Uncle Arthur. Double-tap means liking it, on Facebook. It just… records that you saw it. And yes, Sarah’s dog in a hat is a bit much. But cute! Honestly, the obsession with those platforms. It's all just vying for your attention, isn't it? Used to be you’d have a nice chat, a good cuppa like this. Now, everyone’s glued to their screens. Remember when we used to play proper games, Arthur? Skittles, marbles… Aye, skittles! Now you’re talkin’. That were a proper game. Didn’t need no electricity or… or Facebook nonsense. Used to take hours down the Green, bettin’ a penny or two. Good times, them. It's not all bad, though, is it? I mean, it keeps us connected with people who live further away. My sister in Canada, for instance. I wouldn’t talk to her as often without it. That’s fair, Mark. It has its uses. But it can also be a bit… overwhelming. I’ve been trying to cut back, actually. It’s been triggering my OCD a bit. Your OCD, dear? Are you alright? You've never mentioned that before. It’s not a big deal, Mum. Just… the constant scrolling, comparing yourself to everyone else. You see all these perfect lives, and you start questioning your own. Little rituals creep back in – checking my emails five times consecutively, needing everything to be perfectly aligned on my desk… silly things. OCD, eh? My brother-in-law had that. Used to wash his hands 'til they were raw. Doctor said it were stress-related, you see. It’s definitely linked to anxiety, Amelia. There’s a lot of research on it. It impacts academic performance too, you know. Some of my students struggle with it. Oh dear. Well, you must talk to someone, dear. Don't keep it bottled up. We’re all here for you. It reminds me of little Timmy, actually, when he had chicken pox. Couldn’t stop scratching, poor thing. Drove his mum mad! Chicken pox is a bit different, Mum. But the compulsive behavior is similar. Chicken pox! I remember that. A good scrubbin’ with bicarbonate of soda in water, that’s what you needed.

Oh, Sarah, you are a marvel. Honestly, with technology these days, you'd think it'd be foolproof. Where were you trying to go, then? We were trying to get to that little Gasthof near Heidelberg, you know, the one Dad used to rave about? Apparently, the satnav thought a cow pasture was a perfectly acceptable detour. Ben was absolutely hysterical. Heidelberg, eh? Lovely part of Germany. Reminds me of Southport, in a roundabout way, all the cobbled streets and that. Though, obviously, far less rain usually. Remember that trip we took in '87, Maggie? Nearly washed away! Oh, goodness, yes! Your poor little Rover, Derek. Sounded like a washing machine full of bricks after that. We were trying to get to Rothenburg ob der Tauber, weren't we? Absolutely charming town, though. Wished we'd taken the paper map. Never trust those things! You know, it’s funny, different regions in Germany have such distinct accents. Honestly, when I was there last year for that conference, the Bavarian dialect was barely understandable! I spent half the time nodding and smiling politely. It's amazing how languages evolve, isn’t it? Aye, they do. I had a bloke come into the workshop last week, German chap he was, moving over here. Said he finds the Kent accent a right mouthful. Said it sounds like "a pile of pebbles being shuffled around." Took some explaining, that did. It's a fascinating field, sociolinguistics. The way accent and language become intertwined with identity… It’s not just about understanding the words, is it? It’s about understanding the  feeling  behind them. My dissertation was actually on regional variations in Kentish dialect... Oh, have you now, David? Fancy that! So, you can tell me exactly what’s wrong with my pronunciation of ‘bath’ then? Always been a bugbear of mine. Now, Maggie, let's not start a debate on orthographic pronunciation! It’s perfectly valid, and you’re certainly not alone. It's a reflection of the historical influences on the region. Speaking of history, remember Auntie Brenda’s stories about granddad driving that old Morris Minor all the way to Germany back in the 60s? Apparently, they slept in the car! Ah, the Morris Minor. A legend, that was. Cramped as a sardine tin, but reliable as the sunrise. He was a stubborn one, your granddad, wasn’t he? Wouldn't trust anything newer than 1960.

…and honestly, the raw energy of seeing them live just blows any recording out of the water. It's like, the album 'Echo Bloom' is amazing, proper atmospheric and all that, but experiencing the bass drum thump in your chest at Brixton Academy? Different level entirely. You saw them at End of the Road last year, didn’t you? Yeah, I did! Mad crowd. They were good, really good, but I felt like they were trying a bit too hard to replicate the studio sound, you know? It lost some of that...grit. Less spontaneous, if that makes sense. I’m more into bands that embrace the chaos of a live performance. Like, remember when The Static Rust practically dismantled their drum kit mid-song at the Frog and Fiddle? That was brilliant. Oh, absolutely! Total mayhem. Liam nearly knocked over the bar with a cymbal. Good times. Speaking of drumming, have you been keeping up with Finn’s stuff? He’s been posting some insane videos online. He’s apparently been taking proper lessons now - fancy that, our Finn from school, a proper drummer! No way! Seriously? I thought he just banged on pots and pans when he was bored. He was always a bit wild, wasn't he? Good for him though. It’s nice to see someone pursuing something. Still hanging around with Chloe and Ben, is he? Yeah, same crew, pretty much. Chloe’s killed it with her photography, by the way. She got an internship with a magazine in London. Proper amazing opportunity. No kidding? That's brilliant for her! London, eh? Always fancied giving it a go myself, to be honest. But...devon’s home, innit? Mom would have a heart attack if I moved up there permanently. Totally get that. My Aunt Margaret keeps going on about how I should "settle down" and “get a proper job” instead of traipsing around festivals. But then she tries to talk me into joining her on a cruise to the Bahamas. Makes no sense. What's the kitchen at your mum's been like these days? Still a battlefield after Sunday dinner? Don’t even. It’s improved slightly, I’ll give you that. Mum’s started delegating more – a necessary evil. She's trying to teach my little sister to peel potatoes. Disaster waiting to happen. I’m actually looking at doing another internship, you know?

Right then, lad. Let’s just try and hear ourselves think for a minute, eh? This place is a right racket. Honestly, you’d think they were hosting a brass band competition! It’s busy, Mum. More people than usual, I reckon. Loads of families in. Aye, busy is one thing, this is bordering on chaos. Anyway, about Durham… Did you look at those student halls online? The ones near the Cathedral? I thought that might be a decent option if you decide to apply. I had a quick look. They're a bit pricey though, aren't they? And a bit… stuck-up lookin', if I’m honest. I was thinking maybe something a bit closer to the city centre. Easier to get about. Aye, well, you’re right. Practicality is key, isn't it? Right. Shopping list then. We’re low on teabags, definitely need milk, and those little sausage rolls you like for lunch. Oh, and we’re out of washing detergent completely. Disaster, that is. Remind me to grab some from Asda while we're at it. Speaking of things we need... did you manage to sort out the sleeping bags? For the summer holiday? Nah, haven't booked anything yet. Been busy with football. And, like, history homework. History, eh? Still obsessed with the Romans, are you? Well, can't fault your historical interests. We need those sleeping bags, though. Remember last year and the damp tent? No one wants a repeat of that, do they? Right. Anyway, did you see what they’re doing with the old biscuit factory in Newcastle? Apparently, some entrepreneur is turning it into apartments - luxury ones, apparently. Crazy money, that. Yeah, heard about it. Loads of old buildings being turned into flats now. It's a bit weird, innit? Like, where are all the normal folk going to live? That's exactly what I was thinking! It’s all about business structure these days, isn’t it? Profit, profit, profit. Still, good for the local economy, I suppose. Oh, listen! They're playing 'Brown Eyed Girl' on the radio. Brings back memories, that. Remember when your Dad used to play it in the car? Yeah. He sung along really badly. He did, didn’t he? Absolutely dreadful! But we loved it. Right, serious talk now. Heard on the news this morning about those rising obesity rates… It’s worrying, really.

…and then the student, bless him, genuinely asked me if “going off the rails” meant  literally  leaving a train track! I had to explain it was an idiom, you know? It’s fascinating, isn't it, how language can be so… slippery? I'm trying to record some examples of these moments for my linguistics workshop. It highlights the challenges of teaching figurative language, especially. Aye, right proper. That's mental. You reckon he’d ever used it himself, or just heard it somewhere and got completely muddled? I remember struggling with idioms myself when I first started my job. Loads of Yorkshire phrases flying about that no one explained. “Putting the cat among the pigeons,” for instance? Had no clue! Probably heard it somewhere, I think. He’s from Romania originally, so his English is brilliant, technically perfect, but… culturally, it’s missing that bit of nuance. Anyway, good to see you, Liam! Proper catch-up. You look well. How’s the assurance analyst life treating you? Still wrestling with spreadsheets and corporate jargon? Yeah, pretty much. It's alright, not exactly thrilling, mind. Pays the bills, though. A lot better than stacking shelves at Morrison’s back in Bronsgrove, let me tell you. And you? Still moulding young minds and correcting their grammar? Pretty much. It’s rewarding, in its own frustrating way. Sarah’s doing alright, too. She’s absolutely bursting, you know. Massive bump. No way! Seriously? That’s wonderful news! When’s she due? Crikey, time flies. Seems like only yesterday we were pulling all-nighters in the library at Warwick. Remember that dreadful essay on Chaucer? Don't remind me! I’m still having nightmares about Middle English. Look, I’ve made us some tea. Fancy a digestive? Cheers, mate. Always a winner. So, a little one on the way. Have you started thinking about all that, the…practicalities? The money, the nurseries…? It’s a bit daunting, to be honest. We've been trying to consolidate our finances, you know? Sharing a joint bank account seemed sensible, especially with the cost of living being what it is. You're doing alright on your salary, aren't you? Significantly better than mine, I imagine! It’s decent, yeah. We're looking at getting on the property ladder eventually, but it feels like an impossible dream sometimes. I've been eyeing up a place down near Brighton, but the prices... honestly.

I can imagine. It’s hard, isn't it, when they try to offer help and it just feels… manufactured. Like they’re ticking a box. Did you try anything else? You know, beyond just… being? Not really. I mean, I’ve been walking more. Trying to force myself out into the daylight. It helps a little, the fresh air. But the house… it’s just full of him. Every corner. His slippers by the armchair, his gardening gloves on the windowsill… it’s like he’s still here. You know? And the kids… they’re coping, bless them, but they're quiet. Too quiet. Little Tom keeps asking when Grandad’s coming back to read him stories. Breaks my heart every time. Oh, love. That's… that’s unimaginably tough. My Claire went through something similar when her Nan died. She kept leaving little notes out for her, pretending she was still going to get a reply. It’s a coping mechanism, I think, for the little ones. Maybe Tom needs a special box, somewhere he can put drawings or letters for Grandad. Somewhere he feels like he's still communicating. That’s… actually, that's a really clever idea, Sal. A proper memory box. I’ll suggest it to Jamie. He's been strangely… distant. I think he's bottling it up. He’s always been the strong one, you know? The sensible one. Men often are, aren’t they? Bottling things up until they explode. It's a blinkin' shame. My Geoff used to be like that, until I practically wrestled him into therapy after his mum's stroke. It took a while, but it made a difference. He doesn't hide things so much anymore. It's just… I don’t want to push him. He's got his business to worry about, and the kids... Everything feels so much on me right now. Speaking of worries, how's your back? You mentioned it was giving you gyp last week. Honestly? Not brilliant. The physio says it’s down to stress, which is just… lovely to hear. Basically, I’m hurting myself with worry. It’s sending spasms up my leg. I’ve started doing those Pilates videos I found online, helps a bit. Though falling off the mat in front of the telly isn’t exactly dignified. You are a caution, you are. You need to prioritise yourself, Sal.

But Dad said Liam's mate, Josh, did one at Jaguar and now he’s on proper money. Loads better than what he'd make in a shop. That’s true, lad. Depends on the apprenticeship, doesn’t it? Josh did well, alright. Got himself into a good technical role. Not all of ‘em are rubbish, mind. But you're right, Sarah, there’s a lot of dross out there. Needs proper vetting. Exactly, Mark! Vetting is key. You hear stories – people being exploited, being given completely unrelated tasks, effectively just cheap labour. It's a sales pitch, isn't it? 'Gain skills!' when they're just photocopying for six months. I’ve proofread business plans for several apprenticeship schemes, and some… some are frankly appalling. My uncle did one at Nissan! He builds the engines now. It’s really cool. He let me sit in one once. It’s massive! See, Daniel? That's a fantastic example! That’s what it  should  be. A gateway to a proper career. Not just…grunt work. And even then, university still seems to hold more weight, doesn’t it? Even with all the fees. Well, it depends what you want to do, Sarah. Engineering, like Daniel’s uncle, apprenticeships are brilliant. Straight into the industry, earning whilst you learn. But for something like law, or… design, maybe not. I’ve been thinking about this whole business investment thing again, you know? Might be a better bet than the stock market. What business? You gonna buy a chip shop? Not a chip shop, lad. Something… stable. Maybe a chain of laundrettes. Everyone needs clean clothes, right? Low overheads, good profit margins… Laundrettes? Seriously, Mark? That’s… a very specific vision. Have you actually done the research? Because there's a lot of competition. And the energy bills! I’ve had a look, Sarah, don’t dismiss it so quickly. Demand is consistent. Recession-proof, almost. Plus, there’s the potential to add services – dry cleaning, shoe repairs… a little cafe area. It's an investment with legs, I reckon. Could you put a gaming station in? For people waiting? Now you're talking, Daniel! See? Thinking outside the box. Alright, alright, let’s not get carried away with laundrette empires. Honestly, the thought of it makes me want to lie down. Anyway, back to you two. How was tennis today? I heard you smashed a few serves, Joshua.

…and honestly, the sheer scale of it all is just… jarring, innit? Like, you read about the cockle disaster, you see the pictures, but to actually  be  in Morecambe and see those plaques, the memorial…it really hits you. It’s a lot heavier than I expected. Yeah, I can imagine. I did a bit of reading up on it before, but I think being there will be a completely different experience. It’s just awful, isn’t it? So many lives lost, all because of something that  should  have been predictable. Proper tragic, yeah. And the speed it all happened. Apparently, the tide came in so fast…Dad said he remembers hearing stories about it when he was a kid. He grew up nearby, y'know. Always a risk with coastal work, I suppose, but still. Right, enough doom and gloom! Fish and chips are definitely on the agenda tonight. Gotta soak up some of the sadness, eh? Absolutely! A proper chippy supper is essential. I'm already dreaming about it. Lancaster’s supposed to have a decent one, apparently. Anything else you're looking forward to about the visit? Well, seeing Auntie Maureen and Uncle Barry, of course! They’re both doing alright, as far as I know. Maureen’s been gardening like mad, apparently practically drowning the roses. And Barry’s still obsessed with his miniature railways, bless him. It’s nice to see them, even if it’s only for a couple of days. What about you? Excited to see them too? Definitely. It’s been ages! And I'm rather hoping Aunt Maureen will let me sample whatever culinary masterpiece she’s working on. She’s got such a knack for baking. Speaking of which, are you still thinking about doing a Masters? You mentioned it last time we spoke. Oh, yeah. I’m seriously considering it. I've been looking at some linguistics programs up in Manchester, specifically focusing on sociolinguistics. It’s just…finding the time and the money is the tricky bit. That dissertation prospect is a bit daunting too, innit? What are you up to with your career? Still enjoying the Admin side of things? It's… fine. It’s secure, and I like working with the data, I really do. But sometimes I wonder if I should have pushed for something a bit more…research-heavy, you know? Like you with your Coordinator role.

… nah, seriously, I reckon they've lost it a bit, haven't they? The Arctic Monkeys.  Humbug  was brilliant, proper clever lyrics and that gritty sound. Everything since… feels a bit… manufactured, like they're trying too hard to be something they're not. Aye, I can see that. But I still quite like 'Tranquility Base Hotel & Casino.' It’s different, innit? Not what you’d expect from 'em. It’s got… a vibe. A vibe? That's all you've got to say about it? A vibe? It sounded like a posh library soundtrack! Where's the Sheffield swagger gone, eh? Remember when Alex Turner used to look like he’d rolled out of a chip shop? Now he looks like he's about to critique the floral arrangements at a garden party. Alright, alright, settle down! You’re getting properly riled up about it. It's just music. And he's evolved, hasn’t he? You can’t expect ‘em to keep churning out "I Bet You Look Good on the Dancefloor" forever. I'm not saying they  have  to, but they could at least try to make it a bit… you know…  good . Honestly, I’d rather listen to The Pigeon Detectives again. Don’t tell anyone I said that. You are taking the mick, aren't you? The Pigeon Detectives! Right, well, speaking of bands... have you heard anything from Liam's new project? 'Lunar Echoes?' Liam? From school? Blimey, I hadn't! What’s he playing? Still on the drums? He was always a proper whizz on the skins. Aye, still drumming, but they're doing this… indie-rock-with-a-bit-of-electronica thing. Sounds a bit pretentious, to be honest. I went to their gig at The Salutation last week. It were… interesting. Interesting good or interesting bad? 'Cause interesting can mean a lot of things around here! Interesting… trying-too-hard-to-be-Radiohead bad, probably. But Liam's drumming was solid, as always. He's got that rhythm in his blood, that lad. Definitely the best thing about it. Aye, he did. Remember that charity gig we did for the animal shelter? He kept the whole thing together. Speaking of gigs, are you still going to see The Struts next month? Definitely. Got the tickets sorted. Reckon they'll be banging, live. Proper old-school glam rock. What about you? Yeah, me too.

Well, relax, Sarah. It's just a game! He probably had a strategy. Though, I must admit, it  did  seem a bit random. Did you move the researcher to Atlanta, then? That seemed sensible. Sensible? Gareth, that’s insulting to the scientific community! Atlanta is a nexus! It’s practically a moral imperative to prioritize Atlanta! Anyone else feel like I'm the only one taking this seriously? I’m starving, by the way. Anyone fancy a cheese board? Easy, Ben, easy. You're getting your chef stress out. It's all just tiles and cubes, innit? Remember last year when Dad tried to build a containment zone in Siberia? Now  that  was a disaster. Your father did have a bee in his bonnet about Siberia, didn’t he? He reckoned the permafrost would contain any infection indefinitely. Said it was perfectly logical. I tried to explain it wasn't a logical thing at all. Men… Oh, Dai, you and your father. You’re both the same, stubbornly clever and absolutely hopeless at strategic board games. And Rhys is right. Dad’s Siberian containment zone was legendary. We still laugh about it. Remember how he spent three turns just moving a single researcher around Yakutsk? Exactly! It was pure chaos! That’s why I'm finding this current outbreak so frustrating. We’re all supposed to be working  together ! It’s a cooperative game! But Mark… ...Mark's playing like it's a solo mission. He's bringing us all down with his… idiosyncratic methods! He’s got that look, hasn’t he? The 'I know something you don't know' look. Which, let's be honest, probably means he’s just rolling the dice with our collective fate. But look, his Atlanta cure  did  help. Maybe there's a method to the madness. Method? The method is stubbornly ignoring the established guidelines! Look, the infection rate is spiking in Europe! Do you see me waltzing around Cairo? No! I'm focusing on the hotspots. It's basic pandemic management! Are we even discussing event cards? Anyone check for a 'Surge' card? Chill, Ben. I drew a ‘Forecast’ card earlier. Used it to peek at the next few infection cards. Nothing too horrific. A couple of Seouls, a Jakarta… manageable. But, yeah, it's getting tighter. Do we push for a cure in Asia, or try to stem the European flow for now?

“…and then the giant beanstalk just  appeared ! Didn’t it, Leo? Right in the middle of Jack’s field.” “Big! Beanstalk big!” "Shiny." “Yes, a very, very big beanstalk. And Poppy, look - Mummy’s making cake! It’s got sprinkles!” "Sprinkles! Pink ones?" “Mostly pink, sweetie. Your favourite. It’s a little bit of a practice run, actually. For your birthday next month.” "My birthday! Cakes!" “Yep! We’re thinking of having a little garden party, weather permitting. Remember we talked about it? Little tables, colourful bunting… maybe even a bouncy castle if we can manage it.” "Bouncy castle? Wow!" “It’s a possibility! Now, did you both enjoy the CBeebies pantomime this morning? The one with the Princess and the Frog?” “Ribbit! Ribbit!” “Yes, you did! Leo, what did you think? Did you like the frog?” “Frog silly! He wanted to be a prince!” "He did, didn't he? And he had to learn that being himself was the best thing. Just like in that story we read for World Book Day –  The Little Dragon Who Couldn't Breathe Fire ." “Dragon! Puff! No fire!” “Exactly! He felt a bit different, but then he realized his difference was actually what made him special. It's a good message, isn’t it? Remember what Nana always says – ‘Every little bit helps, even if it’s just a spark!’” "Sparkly!" “You’re right, darling, they  are  sparkly! Now, I was thinking… for your birthday, Poppy, we could have a  really  good CBeebies themed party. Not just the cake, but maybe we could dress up as some of the characters... Do you want to be Bluey?” "Bluey! Yes, please!" “Lovely! And Leo, what about you? Tiger?” "Dinosaur! Rawr!" “A dinosaur! Brilliant! Right then, a dinosaur party it is! Although, it might be tricky to fit a proper dinosaur costume in the kitchen…” "Roar in the kitchen!" “Perhaps not. Speaking of tricky… Mother's Day is coming up. I'm not expecting anything grand, you know. A hug and a drawing will be absolutely perfect. Don't you go stressing yourselves out trying to make me a present. It’s the thought that counts, alright?” "Love you, Mummy!" “Love you too, sweetheart. And you, my little dinosaur?” "Love you, mummy. Cake soon?" “Very soon. Now, I need to finish this cake. And then perhaps we can watch a bit more CBeebies. Maybe  Numberblocks ? They're good for understanding numbers, you know, especially getting ready for school.”

…and honestly, the sheer volume of tumbleweed on dating apps is astonishing. Like, you swipe, swipe, swipe, and it’s all either blurry photos of men holding fish or bios that just say "good vibes only." What  does  that even mean? Good vibes only? Sounds like a dodge, doesn't it? Like they’re trying to scare off anyone who might ask a straightforward question. I haven’t bothered with the apps myself, to be fair. Too much effort. Ends up being more draining than the work, and I’m already dealing with faulty hydraulics all day. I find it fascinating, the whole landscape of online dating. It's so… performative, isn't it? Everyone curating these versions of themselves. It’s like choosing your Instagram filter in real life. I’ve had a few decent conversations, but nothing that’s, you know,  clicked.  My friend Sarah met her fiancé on Bumble, though. Total fairytale. Sarah’s always had incredible luck. She’s like a dating magnet. Whereas I get… well, I got a man who messaged me exclusively about the structural integrity of Victorian bridges. I’m a journalist, not a civil engineer! Victorian bridges? Blimey! Honestly, you'd think having a postgraduate degree would filter some of these folks out. It doesn’t, does it? I remember during my Masters, there were some proper characters. One guy was convinced he could build a self-healing concrete. Brilliant idea, theoretically, utterly impractical. It's the impracticality that makes life interesting, isn’t it? Though sometimes, practicality has its charms. Speaking of which, has anyone heard back about that teaching position in Bristol? The one at the international school? Not yet. I put in an application last week. Fingers crossed, though. It’s a long shot, I know. Relocating again… part of me really wants to. Hereford's lovely, don't get me wrong, but it’s… small. And frankly, the dating pool is even smaller. Bristol’s a good shout. Loads going on there. And closer to me. I'd definitely come and visit. Moving’s a big deal though, innit? My mum keeps giving me grief about moving away from her again. Says I’m abandoning my roots. Being born in Germany doesn't exactly help when she's trying to guilt trip me. It’s always a push and pull, isn't it? Family versus independence. My mum's the same.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of paperwork involved in just onboarding a single new sales rep is astonishing. It’s not just forms, it's compliance checks, GDPR declarations, benefits enrolment, background checks… it’s a full-time job in itself, really. I feel terribly guilty sometimes, delegating so much of it to poor David, but he's got enough on his plate already. Sounds familiar! We're drowning in HR stuff here at the firm. The landscape changes constantly with regulations. Remember when we used to just sign a piece of paper and get started? Simpler times, weren't they? Though, I suppose less protectin' the pointy end of the business. Definitely! It's a world away from my childhood. My mum always just said, "Get to work and be good," and that was it. No contracts, no comprehensive training manuals... Just dive in. Though, thinking about it, that probably explains why I ended up taking an extra accounting qualification at uni. Trying to cover the gaps! Exactly! My mum would’ve expected me to be earning a decent commission within a week, regardless of the mountain of administrative hurdles. She was a staunch believer in "sink or swim". Speaking of childhood... remember those Spirograph toys? My brother and I used to spend hours creating those hypnotic patterns. We practically wore out the little gear. Oh, Spirograph! Now you're talkin'! I had one too! Covered every scrap of paper in the house with those twirly things. Used to drive my mum mad. She said I was wastin' precious paper. I reckon I spent more time fiddlin' with it than doin' me sums, truth be told. Did you have the ones with the glitter pens? Those were the best! I did! Though mine was a hand-me-down and slightly battered. I think my cousin used it to decorate her entire bedroom wall. It was... intense. You know, it's funny, I didn't really appreciate my family's accent growing up. It just  was . I'd hear people mocking it, and I’d cringe, wanting to sound more sophisticated. It’s changed now, though. I’m proud of where I come from. Absolutely. It’s that feeling of trying to shed a part of yourself to fit in, isn’t it? I remember when I was working in London, everyone seemed to be aspiring to a Received Pronunciation. I used to try to mimic it, trying to smooth out my Lincolnshire vowels.

Speaker_3 beamed, gesturing expansively with a slightly chipped teacup. "A feathered carpet, that's a brilliant image, Mum! So, you actually got to see them close up? Dad always says puffins are ridiculously hard to spot." "That's because they are, lass! Little blighters. Always diving, never staying still for a photograph. Spent a fortune on a telephoto lens, I did, and barely got a blurry blob." He chuckled, a low rumble. "Sounds amazing though, Maureen. The Farne Islands, right? I've seen pictures. Were the boat trips crowded?" “Oh, a bit, but it was peak season, weren't it, Arthur? There were a few families with screeching kids, mind you. But the guide was brilliant. Local lad, knew everything about the birds and the seals. He even told us a joke. Said, 'Why did the puffin cross the road?'" She paused for dramatic effect. “Oh god, here we go…" Elise muttered playfully. “'To get to the other tide!'” She roared with laughter, nearly spilling her tea. Liam groaned good-naturedly. "Classic. You and your bird jokes, Maureen." "I remember a better one. What's a puffin's favourite food? Fish and ships!" He doubled over, wheezing slightly. Elise and Liam exchanged amused glances. "You two are terrible," Elise said, shaking her head. "But seriously, Mum, what was the weather like? I remember you were worried about rain." “Well, initially, it was a bit drizzly, but that cleared up quickly. We had three days of sunshine, proper sunshine. Took me completely by surprise, to be honest. Managed to get a tan, even! Didn't think I'd manage that at my age.” She smoothed down her cardigan proudly. “Arthur insisted we go to Bamburgh Castle one afternoon. That was spectacular. Right on the coast, massive thing. You could practically feel the history seeping out of the stones." "Spectacular is right. And the views! You could see for miles. Got some cracking photos, I did – this time they were in focus, I'll have you know!" He pointed to a recently printed photo album resting on the coffee table. Liam flipped through the album. "Wow, that is a good shot of the castle. So, you just did Northumberland then? Didn't you mention you went somewhere else?" "Oh aye! We popped over to Alnwick Garden. Remember that, Arthur? All those topiary sculptures!" "Trying to work out what they were supposed to be!

…and honestly, the sheer volume of clicks on that article about the AI-generated recipe for shepherd’s pie was just  insane . People are terrified of robots taking over the kitchen! Though, I’m not sure a robot can replicate Nan's gravy. That was a skill learned over decades, you know? Robots ain't touchin’ Nan’s gravy. Not a chance. Though, I did read something about machine learning predicting flavour profiles. Apparently, they can analyse chemical compounds and… Oh, please, don’t start with the engineering jargon again, Liam! We’re trying to relax on a Saturday morning. I've got a mountain of marking to get through later. Tell us something non-technical, for once. How’s the new project going at the factory? Right, right. Sorry. It  is  a bit dense stuff, isn't it? The project’s…challenging. Lot of issues with the new automated sorting system. Keeps misidentifying the Grade B widgets as Grade A. Production's backed up. Sounds dreadful. Any chance you can fix it? You always were good at puzzles. That’s the idea, innit? It’s proving trickier than I thought. The algorithm's a mess. They hired some bright spark fresh out of uni, and he's built this thing on, well, a foundation of wishful thinking, essentially. I'm trying to unpick it without completely starting from scratch. Uni grads. Honestly. Still, you know, fresh perspective. Maybe you can learn something from him, even if he is a bit… enthusiastic. Have you had a decent lunch yet? There’s leftover curry from last night if you fancy it. Curry sounds brilliant! I’m starving. I stayed up far too late last night binge-watching that documentary about Harry and Meghan. Honestly, the drama! Don't get me started on the royals. Waste of resources, the lot of ‘em. I'd rather spend my money on decent tools. Speaking of which, I'm thinking of upgrading my multimeter. The one I've got is…well, it’s seen better days. Don't you dare start examining the wiring in the kitchen! You know my dad would have a coronary. Still, need to grab some groceries. Anyone want anything? I’m thinking of popping to Aldi. They’ve got those amazing chocolate digestives. Aldi's surprisingly good. I got some brilliant tins of chopped tomatoes there last week. Much cheaper than Waitrose.

You and your stubborn refusal to look at a proper map, Chloe! You know you're better off with a sat-nav. My old TomTom still works a treat.      Sat-navs are alright, innit? Less arguing about directions. Mum uses one for everything. Last time we went to Skegness, she was convinced we were driving into the sea because the sat-nav told her to turn left onto the beach.      Oi, lad, you’re tellin’ me stories now, are ya? Beach turns? That’s a good one. Used to use them in the army, you know. These fancy GPS things. Used to go mental sometimes, sendin’ you down tracks too narrow for a Land Rover. Still, better than relying on some bloke with a crumpled map, eh?      It's not the sat-nav itself, Reg. It’s Google Maps’ insistence on taking you on the most convoluted route. It prioritizes scenic routes, apparently, and scenic routes often involve bumpy, unpaved roads and sheep!      Well, you were trying to avoid the M6. Remember? You said it was a parking lot.      I did, but I didn't realise I'd be navigating a farm! Anyway, speaking of journeys… Dad’s still out in Saudi, isn’t he? How’s he finding it?      Yeah, send him our love. He said the contract’s going well, apparently. Crazy money, proper laughing. He was saying something about wanting to knock down that awful wallpaper in the living room when he gets back, though.      Oh god, that wallpaper  is  hideous. Remember when we tried to take it down when we were kids? It was like peeling off concrete.      Aye, some wallpaper's a right bugger. You need to get a steamer, lass. Saves a lot of faffing about. Though, mind you, you'll need to protect the skirting boards. Don't wanna end up with a soggy mess.      Speaking of messes, how's your decorating project going, Chloe? Last I heard you were halfway through painting the bedroom a shade of turquoise only found in tropical fish.      It's teal, Liam! And don’t mock my interior design choices. It's coming along, slowly. I’m trying to do it all myself to save money. You know, because I’m practically living off ramen.      You should’ve just let me do it, Chloe. I’m decent with a paintbrush. Don't tell Dad I said that, though, he’ll never let me live it down.

Tell me about it. I’ve been battling a sniffle for the past three days. Thought I was leaving it behind in London, but apparently, jet lag and pollen don't mix well. Bit of a nuisance, really. The Husbands used this brilliant lavender oil last time we were here, said it cleared his sinuses right up. Might have to track some down. You’ve been using that serum, haven’t you, Chloe? The one from…Aesop? Yes, the Parsley Seed. It’s helping a little, but I think I need to invest in a proper humidifier for the apartment. This dry air is a killer. Though, you know, looking around at these incredible specimens… it almost makes you forget about feeling poorly. Did you see that  Digitalis purpurea  over there? Absolutely magnificent. The colour saturation… incredible. It is, isn’t it? Speaking of impressive flora, I was reading an article about the Dahlia collection here. Apparently, they're experimenting with some new cultivars - incredibly resilient, designed specifically to withstand the harsh Swedish winters. They're aiming for a continuous bloom; imagine, colour throughout the year! It’s fascinating, that level of manipulation and adaptation. My niece, Elsie, is obsessed with dahlias. She's trying to grow them in Croydon, poor thing. The slugs devour everything. Croydon. The slugs are probably plotting world domination, honestly. Elsie should try companion planting - garlic and lavender are supposed to deter them. Right, let’s get back to selves. Chloe, skin feeling particularly bad? Any specific areas? My forehead and around my eyes are the worst. It feels… tight. I've been using a heavier moisturiser, but I worry I'm clogging my pores. Perhaps some gentle exfoliation? I might pop into that organic skincare shop on Biblioteksgatan tomorrow. They have a lovely clay mask. Oh, definitely a clay mask. I always swear by that stuff. I find charcoal masks are good too, especially for drawing out impurities. Have you considered a weekly lymphatic drainage facial, Chloe? Honestly, it does wonders for the puffiness. Bit of an indulgence, I know, but worth it. Sounds reasonable. Spend a bit of money to look after yourself. So, health aside… how’s the school year going, Chloe? Last I heard, you were wrestling with some particularly…spirited teenagers. Don’t even  start  with them. One of them tried to convince the class that TikTok was a legitimate historical source.

Honestly, Mum, it’s ridiculous. My phone keeps saying my name wrong! It thinks I’m, like, "Fiona" instead of "Freya." It’s down to the accent, innit? It just isn’t understanding the way I say it. Bit of a Gillingham drawl, I s’pose. Gillingham drawl? Sounds lovely, duck. Nothing wrong with a bit of local flavour. Can’t deny you’ve got a nice way of speakin’, though. Used to be proper London accents everywhere, you know. Now? Sounds like everyone's tryin' to be the same. It  is  frustrating, Freya. Technology's supposed to make things easier, not harder. My Tracey’s got the same thing with her phone – she's from Harlow, you see, and it keeps correcting ‘hare’ to ‘hair.’ Drives her mad! Makes you wonder, doesn’t it, how they expect these things to understand everyone? Phones are useless. Always ‘avin’ a go at you. My ex, Chloe, she used to complain about the same thing. Said I sounded like I was swallowin’ half me words. Probably 'cause I was tryin' not to argue with her. Anyway, arguin' ain’t worth it. It just leads to more mess. Like with Liam and Sarah. Speaking of mess… how are they managing? I spoke to Sarah briefly yesterday, and she sounded completely drained. The custody thing still going on? Awful, sweetheart, absolutely awful. It’s been dragging on for months. Liam's lawyer’s proper bleedin' him dry, and Sarah’s just… trying to hold it together. He's claimin' she's unfit, all on account of… well, you know. The drinkin', yeah. Shame, it really is. A good bloke, Liam, used to be. Remember bringing us some of his mum’s apple crumble once? Proper good. But he’s let it take over, hasn't he? It's the kids what suffer. Little Maisie deserves better than runnin' around with a dad who’s… well, you all know. It's just… heartbreaking. Do you think they'll ever sort it out? And what about his mum? Doesn't she have a responsibility? She practically raised him, didn’t she? Her health hasn't been good, love. She’s got that bad arthritis, remember? Can barely get up and down the stairs. And frankly, she enabled him for years. Never held him accountable for nothin'. Easier to just turn a blind eye, I reckon. Families. Always a kerfuffle, eh?

Right, so, Baked Alaska. Seriously, Mum? You're attempting  that ? For a load of teenagers? It's mental. It’s a bit of a challenge, I'll admit, but it'll be a talking point for the Halloween party, won't it? And honestly, I found a brilliant documentary on Michelin-starred chefs constructing them, it's all about the meringue being applied  just  so to protect the ice cream. It’s almost a science. Science and teenagers crashing on the sofas? Seems… incompatible. What about the cheese? You've got, like, three different blocks of it spread out on the table. Is there a test? Are you secretly grading our cheese-grating skills? No, no grading. Just a bit of variety. Mature cheddar for the pasta, a nice Gruyère for a cheese board later, and something softer, like a Brie, for sandwiches. You know I like to have options. You’re getting good at grating too, by the way. Not like your cousin, remember when he tried to grate Parmesan and just ended up with a pile of crumbs? Oh god, yeah. The Parmesan incident of '17. Legendary. Listen, about the party... are you worried about, like, security? There's bound to be some awkwardness, you know? With the ages. That’s a valid point, actually. We need to be mindful. I'll make sure I have a clear policy on appropriate behaviour, and I'll be present throughout. It’s that time of year, and young people will be young people, searching for… boundaries, let’s say. It’s something I’ve been thinking about a lot recently, to be honest – proper safeguarding. It’s part of my job at work, running training programmes, and it’s something we take incredibly seriously. It’s all about building a culture of respect. Yeah, but… what if…? You know. What if what? Look, the age of consent is there for a reason. It’s not just a random number. It's designed to protect vulnerable young people. And while I trust your friends, and I know you’re a sensible young man, situations can escalate quickly, especially fuelled by… well, let’s just say adolescence. I'm not trying to be a killjoy, alright? I just want everyone to be safe and have a good time without any complications. I get it. It's just... my mate, Liam, he’s been going on about this girl from Year 11.

…and honestly, the bin men were two days late! Two days! You’d think after all these years they’d have a system figured out, wouldn’t you? Living in Shipley, you could set your watch by the refuse collection. Here, it’s like a lottery. That’s Swansea for you, love. Utter chaos, mostly. At least you’ve got a good story to tell. Better than sitting around worrying about overflowing bins, eh? Did you manage to get a picture of that squirrel in the garden yesterday? He was particularly cheeky, trying to steal a bit of your toast. Cheeky little beggar, he was! Managed a blurry one, all right. It's on me phone somewhere. Right, so, New York... It was just spectacular, wasn't it? The sheer scale of it all. All those yellows taxis! Though, getting across Times Square… Goodness me. Like being herded. Absolutely mental. I kept expecting a cowboy to suddenly ride past. Did you finally get to see that show you wanted, the one with the tap dancing penguins? Not quite penguins, dear. It was a Broadway musical, 'Wicked'. Stunning. Proper theatrical, you know? Far removed from lecturing undergraduates on Victorian Poetry. Though, there’s a certain dramatic flair to explaining Tennyson, I suppose. Made me think, really. About performance. All those years teaching, are  we  performing too, in a way? You're getting philosophical over breakfast, aren't you? Typical Brenda. It's a good point, though. We do. But with flying lessons, you remove at least some of the pretence, don’t you? Just you, the machine, and the sky. Exactly! It’s exhilarating, isn't it? Though terrifying, mind. I still get a flutter of nerves before each lesson. Old Mr. Peterson, my instructor… he insists on calling me ‘Captain’. I nearly choked on my tea when he said it. Captain Brenda! Has a ring to it. So, are you closer to solo flying yet? Making progress. Still need a bit of guidance, but I managed a decent landing the other day. Relatively speaking.
