Didn't end up in a hedge, which is always a bonus. What about you? Still glued to Instagram, documenting your every gardening success? Guilty as charged. It’s a relaxing distraction, isn’t it? Though, I’m trying to scale back. I did send a letter to my Auntie Gwyneth yesterday. A proper, handwritten one. She’s not on Facebook, you see.

Speaker_1 slapped the Scrabble board, scattering tiles. Speaker_2 : "You always do that, Tom. A dramatic entrance is your signature move. Honestly, you’d think you’d learned by now. Though, a dachshund? That's a serious offence against canine dignity." She chuckled, carefully arranging letters. "Okay, I’ve got ‘QUITE’ – 14 points." Speaker_3 : "Fourteen? That’s weak. I cleared 28 last turn with 'ZEBRA'. And you wonder why I win most games." He grinned, pushing the board closer to him. "Speaking of spelling, did you know 'zebra' used to be spelt 'sebra'? Apparently, it was just a phonetic thing. Bit odd, innit?" Speaker_4 : "It’s fascinating, isn’t it? How languages evolve. My linguistics lecturer was going on about etymology the other day – tracing words back centuries. She was saying 'knight' comes from 'knecht,' which meant servant. Crazy, right?" "Yeah, but try explaining that to someone struggling to spell 'knight' on Scrabble. All those silent letters! It’s designed to confuse us." He picked up tiles, frowning. "I need a 'U' badly. Right, back to the story – the old lady and the dachshund…she gave me this look. Like I'd personally offended the entire breed.” "You probably did, by nearly trampling her dog. Seriously, Tom, you realize how stressful this is for your dissertation, right? All this gallivanting around." "It’s research! Fieldwork. Understanding human behaviour in stressful situations." He winked. "My dissertation's on the psychological impact of delayed public transport. Turns out, people get  very  creative with their excuses." "Sounds thrilling. I'm stuck prepping for the weekend’s catering gig. High tea for some stuffy old ladies. Cucumber sandwiches, scones, the works. It's…exhausting, honestly. Makes me wish I’d gone into something else." "What about that children's book idea you had? Remember? The one about the talking badger who's a chef?" "Oh, stop dredging that up. It was a half-baked idea. Literally. Badger chefs aren't exactly a market." He paused. "Though, my niece loved  The Gruffalo . Remember that one? Amazing how Julia Donaldson can make something so simple so captivating." "It’s brilliant. I used to read it to my younger cousins all the time. It’s a good reminder that sometimes the simplest stories are the best. Like A Levels, really. Everyone stresses about them so much, but a lot of it just boils down to doing what you’re good at."

…and then young Thomas, bless ‘im, he just smeared the entire plate of mashed potato across his face! Right across his little face! I had to give him a bath, of course, but he was giggling the whole time. Little scamp. Honestly, they keep you on your toes, don’t they? Even after all these years, the memory of it just makes me smile. Potato, eh? Used to grow ‘em in the garden back home, you know. Costessey. Big Maris Pipers. Could feed a whole village with what we got. My Dad… he were right proud of his potatoes. Said they were the backbone of a good Sunday dinner. I can imagine. Your father sounded like a good man. You don't talk about him much, do you, Arthur? No reason to, really, Brenda. He's gone. Been gone a good few years now. Not much to say, 'cept he worked hard. Honest sort. Did what he needed to do. Didn’t fuss. Didn’t complain. Not like some folks today, moanin’ about this and grumbling about that. Now, now, Arthur. Don’t start going on about the modern generation. They’ve got different challenges, you know. Challenges? Challenges were diggin' out a field in November when the frost were bitin’ your fingers off! That were a challenge. This… well, this just seems like everyone wants somethin’ for nothin’. That’s a bit harsh, isn't it? Not everyone’s like that. And things  are  different, Arthur. The world has moved on. You can’t expect everything to be the same as when you were a lad. Electricity wasn't even in every home back then, was it? No, it weren’t. We used paraffin lamps. Safer, in some ways. Less chance of blowin' up the place, I reckon. Remember when they first fitted one? Dad stood there like a lemon, starin’ at the bulb. Said it were unnatural. Said it were takin’ over the world. He sounds like your Uncle George! Always had a thing about newfangled contraptions. Remember him refusing to buy a washing machine? Said his wife's hands were strong enough to do the job. Aye, George were a stubborn one. Wouldn't admit he were wrong, even when he were demonstrably wrong. He’d just huff and puff and say, “It weren’t like that in me day.” Classic George. You’ve got a bit of that in you, you know.

That was absolutely lovely, Annie. Really lovely. Proper Sunday roast, this. Better than anything I used to get at the golf club, truth be told. Though, they tried, bless ‘em. Everything was just… so… beige, wasn’t it? Beige is a very good word for it, Dad. Glad you enjoyed it. Mum really pulled out all the stops this time. She was experimenting with rosemary-infused gravy, you know. Had to Google how to do it properly – apparently, you can’t just bung a sprig in and hope for the best. Don’t you start, Annie! The gravy was superb. Absolutely superb. I’m putting that recipe in my teaching cookbook, I am. The children would love it. Though, getting them to appreciate rosemary… that’s another thing entirely. Tell you what, they’d probably just pick it out. You’re still doing the cookbook, are you, Carol? Good on you. Always admired your initiative. Should’ve taken up something like that myself, when I had the time. So much time… . Dad! Don't go down that rabbit hole again. It’s been a lovely holiday, hasn't it? We all needed this. Have you had a chance to look at this app Mum showed me? “FitLife Pro” it's called. Apparently, it adjusts workouts based on your heart rate. Oh, don’t get him started on the fitness apps, Annie. Remember last year when he tried that virtual cycling thing? Nearly fell off the bike three times and swore he’d seen a badger on the screen. There  was  something in the periphery! Look, it’s about keeping active, isn’t it? Doctor’s orders, you know. Though, a walk down to the beach is plenty active enough for an old bloke like me. Though, the opening of that new train station…that'll change everything, won’t it? It certainly will. It's finally happening. They've been saying it’s opening next month. I saw in the  Devon Gazette  they're running a celebratory event. I might try and get the kids down there. It'll be so much easier for them to come and visit – no more relying on Aunt Carol’s gardening schedule to coordinate car rides! Very funny, Annie. I've not forgotten the trauma of those trips to the garden centre with a screaming toddler. So, FitLife Pro, eh? It does seem a bit… intense, doesn’t it?

…and honestly, the whole thing just felt… staged. Like they were  trying  to recreate Hamlet. It lacked the grit, you know? The immediacy. I mean, Kenneth Branagh’s version was brilliant, but this? Just felt like a dusty school play. Branagh’s was good, yeah, though a bit long for me. I remember my Nan loving it though. She’d sit there for four hours, completely absorbed. You're talking about the RSC one on telly last night, right? My mum made me watch it. Said it was “important cultural enrichment.” Sounds about right. My mum would say something similar. Important cultural enrichment! She probably thinks I’m wasting my life playing FIFA. Which, fair point, sometimes I am. Speaking of which, have you seen the latest Premier League table? City's looking scary. Proper scary. They're just… relentless. I'm sticking with Arsenal, though. Gotta be loyal to the Gunners, innit? Even when they're making me want to pull my hair out. Still, better than watching Spurs crumble, eh? Always. Right, back to Shakespeare for a second. Want to catch ‘The Lie’ at the cinema? Heard good things. Apparently, it’s a proper mind-bender. 'The Lie'? Is that the one everyone’s going on about? The Scandinavian thriller? Yeah, sounds good. I’m a sucker for a twisty plot. Though, honestly, I'm trying to cut back on the cinema. University’s taking all my cash. Trying to stretch it out until the stag do. Speaking of which… Rhys’ stag. Have you got any ideas for it? Because if we're going to involve something involving inflatable flamingos and questionable karaoke, I want an early warning. Don’t even mention flamingos. I’ve got a rough idea, yeah. Was thinking maybe somewhere in Amsterdam? Bit cliché, I know, but… canals, beers, and… generally chaos. What do you reckon? Amsterdam's a classic. Could work. Just need to make sure it's not  too  cliché. We don't want Rhys ending up on a YouTube compilation of stag do disasters. What about a theme? A theme? Like what, a medieval jousting tournament? Something slightly more… achievable. Maybe a spy theme? We could all dress as secret agents. Lots of silly gadgets. That’s actually not bad! Could be hilarious. It’d need a lot of planning though. Right, back to more pressing matters… seminars. Absolutely brutal this week.

…and honestly, the sheer volume of emails. It's relentless. Every five minutes,  ping , another meeting request, another update needed. It’s draining, you know? I swear, I dream in Gantt charts now. Tell me about it! Marketing’s not much better, though in a different way. It's less about the rigid structure and more about constant firefighting. Like, this week we launched a campaign for this new textbook, and the social media engagement is… underwhelming, to put it mildly. My boss is breathing down my neck. Oh, no! That's awful. What’s the textbook about? Medieval pottery. Apparently, teenagers are  thrilled  to learn about glazed jugs. Go figure. Honestly, I’m starting to think I should have studied something more… marketable. Medieval pottery isn't  that  bad! It’s niche, sure, but someone’s going to be interested. You just need to find them. Is it online focused, the campaign? Mostly. We tried a TikTok challenge – disastrous. People mostly just made fun of it. I’m now tasked with brainstorming something “authentic” and “engaging” for the Gen Z demographic about... broken shards of clay. It’s a write-off, really. How’s the construction project going? Still a nightmare with the suppliers? Don't even get me started on the steel beams. Apparently, there's a global shortage. Who knew? We’re running at least three weeks behind schedule now. I had to have  another  very heated conversation with the project manager today. He’s lovely, genuinely, but completely oblivious to the impact of his delays on everyone else. Sounds stressful. You look tired, love. Any chance you’re still seeing that bloke from the pub? The one with the ridiculously sculpted beard? Oh, Liam? No, not anymore. It was… fleeting. He spent more time admiring his reflection than actually talking to me. Plus, his mum kept popping round to “check in” on us.  Every  weekend. Oh, bless. That’s brutal! Staying clear then, good move. Speaking of relationships, Mum's still on about me meeting someone. Says I’m “wasting away with marketing and cats." Your mum's always been…direct. Is she still trying to set you up with her cousin’s nephew, the accountant? The very same. He collects porcelain dolls. Porcelain dolls, Sarah! I tried to explain that maybe I’m just happy on my own for now, but it went straight over her head.

Right, so, that’s the initial findings, wrapped up. Honestly, it’s a right mess, isn’t it? Proving causality with observational data is just… brutal. You’d think after a postgraduate degree I’d be used to frustration, but this is a new level. Brutal, aye. But you're cracking it, aren't you? You always do. Just needs a bit of…what do they say? Refining. Like these herbs. See how they look a bit leggy? Needs pinching back, a bit of pruning to encourage bushier growth. Everything’s a metaphor with you, isn't it? Bushier growth and research findings. You're a proper gardener, you are. Makes me feel like a right heathen. Mam's always tried to get me into gardening, you know? “Get your hands dirty, love, it’ll do you good.” I’d just end up covered in mud and complaining. Still do, probably. It’s calming, though. Therapeutic. Something to focus on outside of… well, complicated things like causality. Besides, a little mud never hurt anyone. Reminds you you’re alive. I’ve got some lovely chamomile here, actually. Fancy some in your tea? Helps with the stress. Aye, maybe. I’m buzzing, that's all. It's the pressure, you know? The grant’s up for renewal soon, and the steering committee are breathing down my neck. They want concrete proof, not just correlations. They’re a lot like these geraniums - needs constant attention to keep 'em blooming. Steering committees. Nightmare fuel. Right, let’s talk about something less stressful. I was thinking about that tagine recipe you mentioned last week – the one your Auntie Carol used to make? Oh, aye! The one with the prunes and the apricots? Blimey, that was good. She used to get the best dates from that little import shop in Sunderland. Never could replicate it properly, though. Something was always missing. I think I’ve figured it out. I was reading about Moroccan cuisine, and apparently, the key is using ras el hanout. It's this spice blend... forty ingredients or more, apparently. Makes a massive difference to the depth of flavour. I ordered some online. Should be here tomorrow. Forty ingredients?! That’s… intense. Auntie Carol wouldn’t have gone near something that complicated. She was a simple woman, love. Chicken, veg, a bit of spice, boom – dinner. But I’m intrigued. Ras el hanout, you say?

Honestly, Bryn, this marking… it’s becoming unbearable. Twenty essays on the socio-economic impact of the British Empire, and they’re  all  variations on the same rather simplistic, Wikipedia-sourced argument. Do they not read beyond the first paragraph? Aye, I know the feeling, Alistair. Though my lot are wrestling with Chaucer. Much more eloquent, mind you, but equally layered in interpretations that seem to bypass the actual text. Did you manage to get out at all this weekend? I pottered about in the garden. The roses are finally blooming; the 'Gertrude Jekyll' is particularly splendid this year. Briefly. Mostly I was battling the creeping ivy that’s threatening to engulf the bougainvillea. It’s infuriating, really. Such a persistent thing. Reminds me of those youngsters these days – no sense of... perseverance. Speaking of youngsters, did you see that article about Ronnie O’Sullivan’s boy? Apparently, he’s showing a remarkable talent for snooker. I did! A chip off the old block, eh? Bit worrying, though, innit? All that pressure at such a young age. Remember Jamie Jones? Brilliant snooker player, used to be around here when we were both starting out. But he burnt out too quickly. Too much expectation. Same with those footballers’ children. Suddenly they’re expected to be the next Messi or Ronaldo just because they were born into it. Exactly! It’s utterly absurd. They need to be allowed to be children, to discover their own passions without the weight of their parents' legacies. Although... I will say, watching these youngsters compete – even with the pressure – does remind you of the sheer talent that emerges. Like Mark Selby. Quiet, unassuming fella, but a ruthless competitor. Aye, Selby was steady as a rock. Nothing flashy, just… effective. Speaking of effectively dealing with… things… my nephew, Gareth, he's applied to join the police force. Seems a sensible lad, Gareth. Wants to make a difference, he says. Brave lad. A difficult profession these days, wouldn’t you agree? The scrutiny, the bureaucracy… and the sheer unpleasantness of what they deal with. My cousin, Edward, was in the Royal Marines for a while. He wouldn’t have anything to do with it now, though. Said it changed him. Not in a bad way, necessarily, but… profoundly. Aye, the armed forces too. It’s a commitment. A big one. My grandson, Rhys, is toying with the idea of joining the RAF.

…and honestly, Sarah, the Henderson account is just  draining  me. They want a complete revamp of the website, five different colour schemes, and they’re changing their minds every five minutes. Honestly, sometimes I feel like I’m herding cats. Uni says ‘meow!’ Not cats, Mummy. Uni says meow! That’s right, pet. Uni says meow. You're right love, you’re a clever girl. But sometimes, things can feel a bit… chaotic, you know? Like this project. Right, cleared my lectures for the week! What's all the heavy sighing about, Auntie Claire? Sounds like you're wrestling a giant. Hello, love! Just moaning about work. The Henderson website is proving to be a nightmare. And it’s just… another thing to add to the list, isn’t it? Still got to sort out little Lily’s Christening, too. Oh yeah, the Christening! How's that coming along? Have you booked the venue? My mum’s been going on about it, saying it needs to be  perfect . As if a baby cares. Your mum’s right - it needs to be lovely, but 'perfect' is a bit much. I’ve provisionally booked the Tithe Barn in Barton-under-Needwood, it's got a lovely feel to it. It’s just… pricey. And that’s before we even get to the catering. What about Uncle David – has he confirmed he’s doing a reading? He texted me yesterday. Said he’s practicing already! Apparently, he used a posh accent for the first attempt, and Mum nearly choked on her tea. He’s going for something a bit more… normal now. Uncle David! Uni wants Uncle David! She does, doesn’t she? She adores him. Right, the birthday party next. That’s proving more tricky. Little Lily wants a princess castle, full of pink balloons and fairy dust. Do you think we should look into hiring some entertainers, Elodie? A princess castle, eh? Sounds like a recipe for sugar overload. Don't think you need to hire entertainers though, Auntie. Little Lily’s entertaining enough on her own! Honestly, she’s got more energy than a swarm of bees. But, yeah, hire the castle. That'll keep her occupied. Have you looked at that bouncy castle company in Tamworth? They did a good job at Amy's party last year. I have, actually. And they’re booked solid for that weekend. That’s just typical, isn’t it?

…and honestly, the council’s plans for the high street are just… baffling. Another artisan cheese shop? Really? Lichfield doesn’t  need  another artisan cheese shop, love. We've got Mrs. Higgins' deli, that's quite enough, innit? I know, right? It's just more of the same. Hipster nonsense. The town needs something for families, something affordable. This little vintage clothing store that opened up, though – that’s actually quite nice. My mum’s been in twice. Oh, that's good, isn't it? Something a bit different. Millie, darling, are you enjoying your porridge? Mmm-hmm! Yummy! Glad to hear it. So, anyway, where were we? Oh yes, the council. They just don't seem to listen. It’s all about attracting these ‘unique’ businesses and ignoring the people who actually live here. Well, it's interesting, isn’t it? How things change. Remember our wedding? The High Street was completely different then. All those old shops, most of them gone now. Don’t remind me! It feels like a lifetime ago. The flower shop where I got my bouquet… they closed down, didn't they? It was such a lovely little place. Remember having to fight through the crowds to get a park, though? It was mayhem! All my Aunt Maureen’s cousins traipsing about, looking for a spot. Absolutely! And Uncle Brian nearly got into a brawl with that bloke over the space outside the bakery. Good times! Thinking about the wedding makes me even more excited about New York. Exactly! New York! Right, so, I was looking at flights… Friday the 17th of October looks like the best option. Direct, not too extortionate. What do you reckon? Friday the 17th works for me. Let me just double-check my shift roster. Oh, brilliant, I can get the 16th and 17th off. So, have you started looking at hotels yet? Somewhere near Central Park would be amazing, wouldn’t it? I've had a quick browse. The Radio City Edison Hotel looks pretty central, and gets decent reviews. A bit pricey, mind you. Or, there's that Embassy Suites hotel near Times Square… bigger rooms, good for Millie, maybe? Bigger rooms would be good. Millie needs space to cart her teddy collection around. Times Square might be a bit much though, all the noise and flashing lights. True. Well, we can shop around. The weather forecast for October is looking pretty good, too, apparently.

…and then, like, the methodology section absolutely decimated me. Honestly, I thought I'd nailed it. I’d read Patel and Bryman cover to cover, cited everything properly – or so I  thought  – but Dr. Harding just kept circling back to this thing about ‘theoretical framing.’ Said it felt… lacking. Theoretical framing, eh? Always gets ya, doesn’t it? Harding's a stickler. My supervisor, Mitchell, used to say, “If you don’t bake the theory  into  the methodology, it's just a checklist of things you did.” Dramatic, Mitchell was. Dramatic sounds about right. I tried explaining I was using a grounded theory approach, that it  emerges  from the data, but he just… looked at me. Like I'd suggested we all join a Morris dancing troupe for research. Right, classic Harding stare. He's got that 'I've seen a thousand students fail' expression permanently etched on his face. Grounded theory is tricky to explain  to  someone who’s stuck in a positivist mindset, isn’t it? Let me see this paperwork... . Is that the annotated bibliography too? It looks like a small forest. Yeah, that’s the beast. And that’s just the beginning. See, I had to go back and add about fifteen more sources after Harding's comments. He said my initial selection was "too narrowly focused on pre-existing pedagogical models and insufficient in exploring the lived experiences of the students themselves." Fancy language, innit? Basically, I needed more qualitative stuff. Right, I see. You've got Bourdieu in here, which is solid grounding, but you're right, needing to bolster it with some phenomenological stuff. Got anything on Van Manen? He’s good for lived experiences. Or Giorgi? Their frameworks are readily adaptable. I've ordered a couple of Van Manen texts. They're still on backorder from Blackwells, naturally. Bloody hell, I'm starting to think I should just give up and become a shepherd in the Lake District. It'd be less stressful than this. Don't be daft. You're practically there. Look, you’ve identified the core problem – Harding wants more depth in your theoretical lens. Let’s think about this. You're looking at academic resilience in first-generation university students, yeah? Yeah, precisely. How they navigate the system, the barriers they face… the whole nine yards. Okay. So, instead of just  mentioning  grounded theory,  show  him how your data collection – the interviews, the focus groups – are informing your theoretical understanding.

…and then I was back at school, right? But it wasn’t  my  school. It was like, a giant, echoing Victorian building, all dark wood and stained glass. And I was supposed to be teaching… history. But I couldn't remember  any  dates. Just… blank. It was mortifying. Classic dream anxiety, innit? Always about failing at something you shouldn't even worry about. Remember when I dreamt I was presenting to the board, and I was wearing a pair of wellies and a dressing gown? That was a good'un. Oh, God, yes! You were ranting about spreadsheets in your wellies. Ruby and Finn were in hysterics when you told us. Wellies! Funny! See? Even she gets it. Right, so history. Makes sense you'd be dreaming about that. Got the essays to mark, haven’t you? Still saving up for that online marking course, yeah? Exactly. The marking mountain feels endless. But it was more than just feeling unprepared. It was... a sense of being trapped. Like I couldn’t escape that endless classroom. It’s prompted me to think about applying for that creative writing course actually, the one at Cambridge. Seriously? Blimey, that’s brilliant, love. That’s a proper commitment though, isn’t it? Afternoons and weekends? It is. But I keep thinking, if I don't do something for  me , I'll just… dissolve into a pile of photocopies and lesson plans. What about you? Had any interesting dreams lately? Apart from the usual battling spreadsheets, I mean. Nah, nothing quite that dramatic. Mostly mundane stuff. Last night I was trying to assemble an IKEA flatpack, but all the instructions were in Swedish. Classic. You know, it does make you think though, doesn’t it? All this dreaming and hoping… makes you wonder what we actually  want  to be doing with our lives. Daddy! Can we play dinosaurs?! Right you are, Finny. Gotta go wrangle some prehistoric creatures. But... speaking of wanting things… We still talkin’ about a dog, yeah? Always. I was looking at some rescue labs online last night. There was one, a little lad called Buster… Labs are a lot of work though, aren't they? Loads of energy. I know, but don’t you think it would be good for the kids? And us? We could go for walks in the fields, proper family time... Yeah. It would be brilliant. Easier said than done, though, with the hours we both work.

Och, it’s mingin’ out here, isn’t it? Proper cold. And my leg feels like someone’s hammered it with a mallet. Honestly, I can barely put any weight on it. Right, that doesn't sound good. You sure you should have walked all the way from the pub? I told you we should have got a cab. And you insisted on showing off your "superior navigation skills." Aye, well, a bit of fresh air never hurt anyone. 'Til I tripped over that rogue paving stone, that is. Honestly, the council should be ashamed. Should’ve put a warning sign up, like. It’s easy to miss it in the dark. It wasn’t exactly deliberate, was it? Anyway, A&E was packed. Absolutely rammed. Folks waitin' like, forever. How long were you there, exactly? And what did they say? Did they X-ray it? You’re not being very…specific. Not for long, love. Got registered, sat for about an hour and a half, and then this student nurse had a poke around and said, "Looks like a sprain, lass. Ice and rest." Ice and rest! Like that’s going to magically make it better. Honestly, I'd have had more luck wraping it in tin foil and wishin' on a star. That's ridiculous. A&E is completely overloaded, isn’t it? It's a disgrace. You should have insisted on an X-ray, at least to rule out a fracture. I mean, you’re practically hopping. I tried, I did! But there were about thirty folks ahead of me, all lookin’ even more poorly than me. And this nurse was rushing around like a headless chicken. Kept muttering about triage and prioritisation. Managed to get a leaflet with some exercises, though. Looked like something from the Stone Age. “Gently rotate your ankle.” Gently! Have you  seen  my ankle? It's throbbing like a drum! Let me have a look. It's definitely swollen. And you're right, it does look quite nasty. They’re probably short-staffed and just trying to get through the queue as quickly as possible. These NHS cuts are a nightmare. Tell me about it! My mam keeps swearin’ it used to be better. Back in her day, she says, you could just waltz into the doctor's and get seen straight away. Nostalgia’s a powerful thing, isn't it? Still, this is beyond a doctor’s visit, I reckon.

…and honestly, the sheer arrogance of it all! That Truss fellow, coming out with pronouncements like that about the markets. Honestly, it's enough to make you despair, isn't it? Remember when Black Wednesday? At least Major had the decency to look a bit shaken. This lot… Shaken? They seemed to be actively  enjoying  the chaos, didn't they? Like it was some sort of game. Though, I’ve got to say, it’s put a real damper on things down at the shop. People are tightening their belts, aren't they? Less impulse buys of the coastal themed bits and bobs. You’re finding that? I thought Brighton folk were fairly resilient. They tend to absorb these things, don't they? Though, I suppose the energy bills are biting everyone. Even the students. Resilient, yes, but even resilient chaps need to eat, old boy. And fancy a seaside ornament when you're worried about heating the house? Not a priority, is it? Still, I've been thinking… about expanding, actually. Expand? Bartholomew, that’s quite something! Expanding what, exactly? You were saying a few weeks ago you were considering just selling online? That’s still on the table, yes. But I’ve had an idea. A small workshop, really. Right near the pier, there's a shop that’s been empty for ages. A bit run down, mind you, but with potential. I could have a workshop in the back, tourists watching me craft things – driftwood sculptures, little model sailboats, that sort of thing. Live display, you see. Adds a bit of authenticity. That's... surprisingly adventurous for you, Bartholomew. You’ve always been about the established supply chains, the wholesalers. This sounds…risky. Risky, perhaps. But also…rewarding, I reckon. It’d put a real spark back into things. Something different. And frankly, I need something. Retirement's proving rather…dull. Mavis keeps insisting I take up pottery, but I'd rather wrestle a shark. Mavis and pottery. A potent combination, that. You know, with your woodworking skills… I always thought you were rather gifted. Remember that little rocking horse you made for Emily when she was little? She still has it, you know. Cherishes it. Ah, yes. That was a good one. Took me weeks, that did. Got splinters in places I didn't even know I  had . So, you think it’s mad, then? This shop idea?

Honestly, this place is… surprisingly nice, isn't it? I wasn’t expecting much from a pub right next to the barracks. They've done a really good job with the décor. It's got a sort of… rustic charm, but not in a forced way, you know? Aye, it’s not bad at all. Bit more character than the Wetherspoons down the road. Though, I still prefer The Oxford Arms in Edinburgh, mind. That’s a proper pub. Good Guinness, proper roaring fire… Edinburgh's always had a better pub scene, I think. More history seeped into the walls. So, food? Are we actually going to order anything, or just nurse these drinks and watch other people eat? I’m properly peckish. Right, food. They've got that pie menu, haven’t they? I’m leaning towards the steak and ale. Classic comfort food. You thinking something lighter? Hmm, maybe. Possibly the fish and chips. Though I’m still not convinced about batter thickness these days. It’s all too much! Remember when batter was just…crisp? Not this massive, fluffy thing. Anyway, before we decide, did you catch last night's  Happy Valley ? Only just finished it! Absolutely gripping, wasn’t it? Sarah Lancashire is brilliant. Seriously brilliant. The tension they build… I was on the edge of my seat the entire time. That ending... brutal. Brutal is an understatement! I honestly thought I was going to need therapy. It was properly dark. I’m still reeling. Makes you wonder what some people are like, doesn’t it? All that desperation… It does. It's believable though, isn’t it? That's what makes it so good. Speaking of things that are believable, are you cold? You’ve got your coat wrapped around you quite tightly. A bit. It's draughty near the window. This coat’s getting a bit thin, actually. I need to treat myself to a new one before winter really sets in. Something warm and woolly. Did you ever wear that tweed one you bought after university? The one your mum adored? Vaguely. Felt a bit… pretentious, to be honest. And itchy. Scottish universities weren't known for their tweed, you know. They were known for cheap beer and questionable fashion choices. I much preferred my band t-shirts then. What about you? What were you listening to back then? Oh, a mishmash, really. A lot of indie stuff, early Radiohead, some PJ Harvey.

…so then young Tam, bless his heart, he’s trying to lift this pallet of bricks, right? And it’s a wee bit wonky, ye ken? Starts teetering, and I'm shouting 'Tam! Watch it!' but it's too late. Proper domino effect, the whole thing came crashing down. Luckily, he just got a bit of a scare, no real harm done, but the pallets... well, let's just say the supervisor wasn't best pleased. Och, Tam. He’s a whirlwind, isn't he? Always causing a bit of a commotion. You'd think after all this time you'd be used to it, Davie. Still, good you were there to shout a warning. Health and safety, eh? Can't be ignoring that. Aye, health and safety. It’s my job, isn't it? Folks think being a trainer’s all paperwork and PowerPoint, but half the time it's just keeping lads like Tam from breaking their legs. Anyway, enough about warehouse drama. You've been quiet. Still got the bug for photography then, Alistair? Saw a couple of your landscapes on Facebook – the one of Loch Lomond was stunning. Thanks, Davie. Glad you liked it. Yeah, I’ve been trying to get out more. Trying, being the operative word. The weather’s been dreadful, hasn't it? Proper dreich for weeks. Makes it hard to get that golden hour light you’re after. Aye, it’s been a washout. Honestly, even  I  was starting to think it would never stop raining. Remember that summer in '98? Barely a drop fell. Vaguely. I was knee-deep in university essays back then, not exactly observing the weather. But I do recall it being exceptionally warm and sunny. I used to go up Arthur’s seat most days, just to clear my head. Thinking of heading back up there soon, actually. Thinking about trying to capture it with a bit more focus this time. Trying to go for something a bit less… scenic postcard-y. Less scenic? What are you on about? Arthur’s Seat is pure iconic! But I get ye. You want something a bit more… artistic. What were you thinking? I'm not entirely sure yet, to be honest. Maybe something focusing on the textures – the rough stone, the heather, the exposed roots of the trees. Focusing on the details, instead of the grand panorama. I was reading about this fella, Ansel Adams – obviously, landscapes are his thing - and he talked about how it's not just about capturing the ‘beauty’ of a scene, but also its inherent character, its… soul, almost.

…and then Mrs. Higgins actually had the cheek to suggest I was  encouraging  Billy to climb on the climbing frame! As if I'm actively orchestrating playground chaos. Honestly, the woman. Oh, Mum, you know Mrs. Higgins. She thrives on drama. She probably gets a kick out of stirring things up. Don't let it wind you up. Easy for you to say, love. You’re not dealing with a room full of five-year-olds intent on dismantling the jungle gym. Anyway, that's enough about my woes. What are your plans for the week? Still stuck in those lesson plans for Year One phonics? Pretty much. It’s the dreaded 'ou' sound this week. 'About', 'loud', 'house'… it's a minefield! They all sound like they're trying to explode. But, aside from that, I’m thinking of trying that new Italian place down on the high street on Wednesday. Wanna come? Wednesday sounds lovely, dear. I’ve got that appointment with the osteopath, remember? My back’s playing up something awful after all that kneeling down trying to retrieve footballs in the park with Harry. Honestly, he's got more energy than a small nuclear reactor. Honestly, he does! He's a little tornado. Right, nursery - any news on that front? Did you hear back from Little Acorns? I’m starting to get a bit anxious. Elsie is nearly crawling, you know, and I desperately need a few hours to actually breathe. I spoke to them this morning. They’ve got a waiting list, of course – everyone does, it seems – but they said they’re expecting a space to become available next month. Fingers crossed! They seemed genuinely lovely though, very focused on outdoor play, which I think is brilliant. Elsie needs to be outside, not cooped up all day. That’s really good to hear. I was worried about some of the places sounding a bit… sterile, you know? All about structured learning from the get-go. Elsie just needs to play with paint and build towers. Exactly. Speaking of towers, have you seen that new series on Channel 4? 'Rise of Empires'? It's ridiculous! All these intricate political machinations and battles… but it's completely addictive. I’ve been binging it every night after Elsie's down. Oh, I saw an advert for that! Is it any good? I need something new to watch. Everything on Netflix feels a bit samey these days.

Aye, reet, I know what you mean. My auntie, bless ‘er, tried to organise a village fete once. The bunting was all wonky and there were wasps everywhere. You just want to hide under a duvet, don’t you?      It sounds… stressful. I can barely handle coordinating a materials order, let alone 300 delegates. So, the dress code was, what, black tie?      Black tie, yes. The CEO’s idea. Apparently, it 'projects an image of sophistication and success.' As if a bunch of people in uncomfortable tuxedos project sophistication, love. They mostly look like they’re regretting their life choices.      Sounds rough, yeah. Still, beats stacking bricks in this weather, that's for sure. Sun's beating down, making the concrete bleed heat. My back’s killing me.      Poor thing. You should get some decent back support. It's awful if you don’t look after your body. Anyway, talking about appearances… I saw Sarah the other day, and she’s completely chopped all her hair off.      Reet? Sarah? She always had such lovely long hair. Why would she do that?      Apparently, a complete ‘reset’ after her breakup with Tom. You know, the architect?      Tom? The one who looked like a grumpy owl? Good riddance, I say.      You’re brutal! But aye, he weren't exactly a ray of sunshine. So, drastic action, then? Do you reckon it suits her?      Actually, yeah. It’s really striking. Short, choppy, and she’s got these amazing silver hoops in her ears. It totally suits her. Makes her look… fierce.      Fierce is good. I’m thinking of shaking things up with my wardrobe a bit myself. I've been stuck in a beige rut for months. All sensible cardigans and trousers. Need a bit of…oomph.      Beige is reliable. Like a good pair of boots. Can't go wrong.      Reliable gets you nowhere, Ben! I need some colour. Maybe a red dress? I saw one in Primark the other day...really cheap, but looked alright. It was a bit…much, mind. All sequins and feathers.      Sequins and feathers might be a bit much for a Tuesday morning, but a red dress is a classic. You should go for it! You deserve to feel good. What about that vintage shop you found in York?      Aye, good shout, that’s it! I forgot about that place. Proper treasures in there. They’ve got a lovely selection of vintage scarves, too.

Lavender, eh? You youngsters and yer experimental tastes. Back in my day, a digestive with a bit of marge was the height of luxury. Proper sustenance, that was. Costessey was a simpler place, you know. Not like these cities, all fuss and bother. Well, Doreen’s always been a bit…ahead of the curve, Arthur. Remember that time she tried to grow sprouts in the living room? Said she was bringing the countryside to the city. It was chaos. But the tea's lovely, Elsie. Did you use loose leaf again? Of course, Margaret. Bags are an abomination. PG Tips, naturally. Wouldn't touch anything else. Though, honestly, the price of everything these days is outrageous. When I was teaching, you could get a proper pound of PG Tips for a shilling! A  shilling ! Quite. Inflation’s been a brutal teacher, hasn't it? Reminds me of the discussions we had in the sixth form about Keynesian economics and the Phillips curve. Youngsters are rarely taught those fundamentals these days. They just worry about likes and influencers. It's a different world entirely. Though, I must say, this tea is rather good, Elsie. Good strength. Aye, strong it is. Right. My mum always said tea needed to be strong enough to stand a spoon up in it. That’s how you knew it was proper. Though, she did have a peculiar thing about adding a bit of vinegar now and then. Said it did wonders for the digestion. Never tried it myself though, mind. Sounds dreadful. Vinegar in tea? Good heavens, Margaret, you haven't! Some people… they're beyond help, really. I always put a splash of milk in mine, though. That’s important. Makes it…settle, you know? And a little bit of sugar. Not too much, mind. Can’t be going around buzzing with energy at our age. I take mine with lemon. Always have. It's ever so refreshing. And it's good for you, apparently. Vitamin C, you see. I try to maintain a reasonable level of health, even in retirement. One must. So much catching up to do with the family, don’t you think? It’s difficult, isn’t it? Keeping up with the grandchildren. They’re all obsessed with these…video games. I try to feign interest, but honestly, it’s beyond me. It’s all flashing lights and noises. Give me a good book any day.

Right? I saw some pictures online. It looked properly chaotic. What were they chanting? Mostly about gentrification, you know, the usual. “Art for the elite, evict the residents!” That sort of thing. My dad would have absolutely  loved  it. He was always one for a good march. Remember those anti-Thatcher demos we went to when we were kids, El? Vaguely… through a haze of teenage angst and questionable eyeliner. It’s amazing how much has changed in Norwich, though. It used to be so… sleepy. Sleepy's good! You need a bit of sleepy in your life. This Norfolk air is doing me the world of good after the traffic around Cardiff, I tell you. Needed a proper break. Think I'll just sink into a proper ale now. Anyone fancy another pint? Absolutely, Rhys. Though I'm still beating myself up about that drive here. Nearly ended up in King’s Lynn instead of Norwich. Should’ve paid more attention to the sat nav. Speaking of drives, Eleanor, are you still getting those worried calls from your mum about DBS checks? Yes, every other day! She’s convinced I'm going to be arrested for working with vulnerable students. It's ridiculous. She keeps asking if having everything meticulously documented is enough. It’s the CRB checks, she worries about the  responsibility . She worries about everything, doesn't she? Remember when she nearly had a breakdown because Jamie refused to wear a hat on the beach? Don’t remind me! It was traumatic. But back to the DBS checks… She somehow convinced herself that a detailed account of my childhood painting activities would put people off. Like, "Oh, she painted landscapes when she was six? Clearly, a risk!" Sounds like my nan. Always worrying about something. I once told her I was going to a karaoke night in Cardiff, and she spent the entire evening praying I wouldn’t embarrass myself. Bless her. You know, brings me back to the debate about, ah… what was it, Daniel? Circumcision? We were talking about that earlier, weren't we? Actually, it's a fascinating piece of cultural history, particularly when you consider the varying religious and societal interpretations. Oh, here we go with the fascinating interpretations! Honestly, Daniel, lay off for five minutes. It’s family dinner! I’m with Sarah. Let’s stick to less… medically charged topics. Though, speaking of different cultures, remember that trip we all took to London a few years back?

…and honestly, the ward was absolutely rammed. We were short-staffed all week, and it just felt like crisis management from the moment I walked in. Old Mrs. Henderson kept calling me 'dear' and asking for her cat, Bartholomew. Bless her, she's so confused. Did you have a good time though, seriously relax? You looked like you needed it. Oh my god, it sounds hectic! A week on the ward, that's tough. Yeah, it was… good. Really good, actually. Needed it probably more than I realized. The weather was incredible in Cornwall, proper sunshine every day. I spent a lot of time just… staring at the sea, you know? Utterly pointless, but restoring. Staring at the sea, that sounds perfect. You should do it more often. Did you do anything adventurous? Surf, climb a cliff, finally wrestle a Cornish pasty into submission? No wrestling pasties, sadly. Though I did eat a lot of them. I did a coastal walk along the South West Coast Path. It was pretty muddy in places, and I nearly tripped over a rogue sheep, but the views were stunning. Oh! I saw this little surf shop, ‘The Salty Dog’, and bought this ridiculously oversized hoodie. It’s so comfy though. I’ll show you. Let me guess, it’s bright orange, covered in palm trees, and smells faintly of seaweed? Pretty much! Okay, fashion disaster, I know. Did you manage to catch any of the football while you were away? I’m having serious withdrawal symptoms. Brighton looked terrible against Wolves. Absolutely terrible. Honestly, I barely watched any sport. Too busy battling anxiety and medication rounds. It’s a bit of a blur, to be honest. Though I did hear Brighton lost. Gutting. Right, I need food. I’m starving. What are you thinking? Pizza? Indian? Trying to be healthy after all that Cornish pasty indulgence and order a salad? Pizza sounds amazing. Extra cheese, definitely. I'm feeling decidedly un-healthy. I’m going to raid the fridge, see what we’ve got. Oh! Mum sent a care package. It's on the kitchen counter. I completely forgot to mention. No way! Mum’s care packages are legendary. Let’s see… homemade flapjacks! Ooh, and marmalade! She knows the way to my heart. Thank you! Seriously, you needed that break. You were looking a bit strung out before you left. Everything with the Henderson project going sideways.

…and then Mrs. Peterson went on for fifteen minutes about the double glazing. Honestly, Gareth, you’d think it was the most pressing issue in the village. Like anyone's  really  bothered about their windows when… you know. Right, double glazing versus potentially life-altering news. Bit of a perspective shift there, isn’t there? Did you actually mention Sarah's scan? I tried. I really did. I brought it up delicately, steered the conversation towards her, said she'd been feeling a bit rough. She just kept talking about energy efficiency. I swear, these village committees are a different species. I ended up saying I needed to dash. Felt a bit rude, but I couldn't bear another minute of it. How are you finding the houses online? Anything remotely promising? There's one on Primrose Lane. Four bedrooms, decent-sized garden… but it’s attached, which isn’t ideal. And the planning application for that extension on Willow Cottage is going to be a nightmare, I can already tell. They’re practically doubling its footprint. It’s ruining the character of the place. Oh, Willow Cottage. I saw that. It’s... ambitious, isn't it? Proper modern glass box slapped onto a thatched roof. It’ll be turned down, surely? The Parish Council will have a field day. But thinking about houses...it feels almost frivolous, doesn't it? Thinking about a new kitchen when Sarah… It's not frivolous, love. It's normal. We need to look ahead. And besides, distracting ourselves for a bit isn’t a bad thing. It’s healthy. Fretting all the time won’t help anyone, least of all us. We're being supportive to Sarah, aren’t we? Trying to be there for her and Mark? We can't just switch off our lives completely. I know, I know. It’s just… the waiting. It’s the waiting that’s the worst. Mark’s being remarkably stoic, which I suspect is masking a tidal wave of worry. And Sarah, bless her, is trying to be positive, but you can see it in her eyes. That… quiet fragility. She's incredibly strong, you know. We’re lucky to have her. We have to focus on that. And when we do, when they get the results, we'll be there. Whatever it is. Have you spoken to her today? Not directly. Sent a text, wished her well.

Honestly, Rach, I’m tellin’ ya, this new bin system… it’s a right pain in the backside. Three different bins? For recycling? Who’s got the brainpower to sort out what goes where, especially when it’s chuckin’ it in the dark after a shift? It’s just pointless. Before, it was one bin, job done. Now, I'm spendin’ five minutes checkin’ a plastic bottle ain’t got any food residue on it. Five minutes I could be spendin' makin' sure some kid hasn’t propped a door open again. Tell me about it, Dave. Don't even get me started. The bins are bad, yeah, a massive faff. But it's the  residents  themselves, honestly. I spent like, an hour yesterday trying to explain to a lad from Ghana why putting his takeaway curry containers in the general waste isn’t sustainable. Like, I’m a Resident Life Support Officer, not an environmental ambassador! He just looked at me like I was speaking Martian. Aye, they’re a special breed, some of ‘em. Remember that time someone left a full bin of… well, let’s just say it wasn’t pleasant… right outside the front door and then complained it smelled? Honestly, you couldn’t make it up. Don’t remind me. That was… memorable. But it's not just the mess, it's the entitled attitude. Like, they think we're their personal cleaning service. I had a girl the other day, asking me to move her car because she “forgot” where she parked. Forgot! On a campus with clearly marked parking zones! Spot on. The parking's a nightmare, innit? They think they’re above the rules. I’ve had to move cars blocking access points more times than I care to remember. And they'll moan when you move it! Like  you're  the one causing the inconvenience. It’s the assumption, isn't it? That we're just… there to deal with everything. I'm a graduate, Dave! I went to Uni, studied film studies! I’m not here to be a glorified parking warden and bin inspector. I feel like I’m constantly nagging. It's draining. Actually, talking about draining… the coffee machine in the staff room. Disaster. It’s never filled, it’s always lukewarm, and half the time it just spits out brown water. A decent cup of tea or coffee would  actually  make a difference to my day.

…and honestly, it was such a weird feeling. Being in Bruges, surrounded by these canals and chocolate shops, and then hearing someone – just  clearly  from Essex – asking directions in a really thick accent. It was proper surreal, innit? Right, yeah. You get that, don't you? End up somewhere exotic, thinking you're the only Brit there, and then  bang  – there's Doris from Basildon. Happened to me in Barcelona once. Package tour, it was. Loudest group of people I’ve ever clapped ears on, they were. Oh, I know exactly what you mean, David. It’s like a reflex, isn't it? We flock together. Remember that Christmas market in Cologne, a few years ago? Felt like half of Herne Bay was there, moaning about the lack of proper mince pies. Exactly! It’s a comfort, though, isn’t it? A little piece of home. I was half tempted to ask her where she was from, just for a chat. But I didn’t want to sound daft. Language learning is proving a right bugger, you know. I’m struggling with the Dutch. It's all “ui” and “eu” and… well, it's confusing. Never been any good with languages myself. Always been that way. Used to be alright at geography, though. Remember Antwerp? Lovely old city. Got stuck in traffic there, mind you. Crippling traffic. Took us hours to get to the zoo. Antwerp’s lovely. We went last summer. I love those cobbled streets. Speaking of summer, are you all going caravanning in Dorset again this year, Chloe? Little Leo would adore that. Probably. Mum’s already planning it, bless her. Getting all stressed about which spot to book. Honestly, she's worse than Santa Claus when it comes to Christmas shopping! Already talking about Christmas markets too - Bruges again maybe? Christmas… it’s just another day to spend worrying, in my book. All that pressure to buy and be jolly. Oh, David, come on. It’s about family, isn't it? Though I do feel a bit sorry for you, not having Sarah around anymore. It must be tough, especially at Christmas. It is. It is. Missing her something awful. Little ones keep me going, though. So do you, Diane. You know you’re always welcome, don’t you? It's funny, isn't it, how the family shrinks and changes? Remember Uncle Barry’s birthday? He'd have been 80 this year.

…No, but like, seriously, Mum. Why even bother voting? It’s always the same. Politicians make promises they don’t keep, and nothing actually changes. It's just…noise. Don’t be like that, Finn. Don’t be so cynical already. You're eleven, for goodness sake. You’ve got your whole life ahead of you. And this equality vote…it matters. But does it  really ? Everyone’s going on about it, loads of people at school are, but it just feels like a lot of fuss for not a lot. Mr. Davies went on and on about it in citizenship today. Drove me mad. Well, Mr. Davies is right to be concerned. This vote, about changing the laws so that everyone is equal under the law… regardless of who they love... it’s important. It's about fairness, Finn. Think about it. Imagine if someone told you couldn't play football just because of what your favourite colour was. Wouldn't that be rubbish? Yeah, but… It’s the same principle. People shouldn't be treated differently because of who they are. Ireland is doing it, right? They had a vote already and it passed. Seems sensible. Why are we always so… complicated? Honestly, I don't know. I just think politicians… remember last year’s election? They all said they’d fix the potholes on our street and they haven't! Still bump my bike every time I go past. You're right about the potholes. Honestly, that council is a joke. But that’s different. This is about people’s basic rights. And you’ll grow up and maybe… maybe you’ll want to stand up for what you believe in. Wouldn’t it be good if you knew how to, right? To be a proper citizen? I dunno. What if I want to be a footballer? Footies don't usually worry about politics. They worry about scoring goals. Well, even footballers deserve equality, darling. And who knows, maybe one day  you  will be a famous footballer and you can use your voice to speak up for people. Or maybe you'll be a politician. Imagine that! The embarrassment! Oh, God, no! Don’t even suggest it. Mum, you'd be horrific. Imagine you trying to give a speech! You'd stop halfway through wishing you had biscuits. I would not! And don't you mock your mother!

Honestly, Brenda, you'd think you’d already cleaned this table three times this morning. It’s spotless! Brenda: One can never be too careful, David. Especially with Arthur’s…  projects  around. You never know what might be lurking. Now, that's a bit harsh, innit? I’m just admiring this old turning tool, that’s all. Found it down the allotment. Must belong to old Mr. Finch, the one who used to grow prize-winning marrows. Proper craftsman, he was. Used it to shape the handles on ‘is walking sticks, 'e did. Lovely work. Marrows and walking sticks, Arthur? That’s quite the skillset. It looks terribly… rusty. Aye, a bit. Needs a bit of elbow grease, that's all. Bit of oil, a bit of sandpaper... Should be right as rain. I was thinking of turning some small bowls, you see. For little seed pots. Brenda: Seed pots? Dear, are we suddenly going to become gardeners? I thought we were sticking to admiring rusty tools. Always been a dab hand with me hands, Brenda. Always 'ave. Remember that bird table I built for yer? Still standin' strong, that do. It did collapse in the first strong wind, Arthur. But it  was  a valiant effort. Speaking of valiant efforts, has anyone seen Barnaby lately? The hamster’s been unusually quiet. Brenda:  Barnaby ? Why are you asking about Barnaby? David, don't you dare bring that up again. What? I’m just asking! I haven’t seen him running on his wheel. He's usually a little whirl of fur and activity. He's not… somewhere he shouldn't be, is he? Now, what's all this fuss about a hamster? I thought you lot were talking about salad dressing. Brenda: Oh, Arthur! Don’t you remember? Don’t  you  remember what happened with Barnaby and the microwave?! Brenda, darling, please. It was a… misunderstanding. A very unfortunate, regrettable misunderstanding. I was just trying to dry his little chew toy! Brenda: "Trying to dry his little chew toy"?! You put a hamster’s toy in the microwave! It was scorching hot and I had to yank it out! Barnaby was terrified! And honestly, David, the look on his face… Never forget it. He was fine, Brenda! Perfectly fine. He had a little cuddle, some extra sunflower seeds, and he was back to his usual antics. It was a momentary lapse in judgment.

Honestly, Robert, the sheer audacity of it. Charging for plastic bags now! It's just another tax on the ordinary shopper, isn’t it? Like we don’t have enough to worry about. Well, Eleanor, it’s about incentivising reusable bags, isn’t it? Trying to reduce waste. Though, I suppose you’re right, it does feel like a drip, drip, drip wearing away at the bank balance. Did you see that story about the pensioner who ended up owing a fiver because he forgot his bag? Appalling. Ridiculous, absolutely ridiculous. Back in my day, you got a brown paper bag with your groceries. Perfectly serviceable. No fuss, no charges. This obsession with plastic is… well, a bit much, even for me, and I’m no stranger to a bit of order. Though, the news this morning  was  rather diverting - that cat who climbed up a chimney and got stuck for three days. Extraordinary, wasn't it? Yes! Poor thing. They had to use a hosepipe to coax it down! Imagine. It’s almost as unbelievable as that article I was reading earlier about mirror-writing. Apparently, there are people who can write perfectly backwards, and it’s legible to them. Mirror-writing? Like Leonardo da Vinci? I remember reading about that. Fascinating, but I’ve never managed it. My attempts at cryptic crosswords are proof enough I'm not intellectually gifted in that direction. I’m stuck on 14 across – "Bank's instability, quite alarming" – six letters. Any ideas? Hmm, 'crunch' perhaps? A bank's crunch time, financial instability... It fits, doesn't it? Though, goodness, bank instability these days… it's concerning. Do you remember when the Northern Rock crisis happened? Sent shivers down everyone's spine. Oh, I do. We were practically glued to the news. It makes you think about your own finances, doesn’t it? We’re lucky, really. This house is paid off, thankfully. I can’t imagine trying to buy a place now. The prices! They’re ludicrous. Absolutely ludicrous. Even here, which is relatively quiet. I was talking to a colleague's daughter the other day; she’s trying to get on the property ladder. Needs a guarantor, of course, and the deposits are just… astronomical. She’s got a good job, a graduate, but she’s still struggling. Reminds me of when I first left Edinburgh, trying to find somewhere to rent in London.

Honestly, you two. Another hour glued to those screens. It's a beautiful day outside! We could be building a den, having a picnic… reading a book! But Mummy, I'm building a new Ninjago temple! It needs to have a secret passage and a spinning dojo! And I’m finally getting to the End City in my Minecraft world. It took, like,  ages  to get enough obsidian. Literally ages! I know, I know, it's impressive what you've built. Truly. But “ages” is a bit dramatic, isn’t it, Finn? You played for three hours straight! And Lily, a temple is brilliant, but have you even  opened  your book today? The one about the brave knight? Knights are boring, Mummy. Ninjas have  swords  and  shadow powers ! It's much cooler. And I’m nearly at the Golden Dragon level! Yeah, reading is slow. In Minecraft you can build anything you want, instantly! You can fly, you can fight monsters... Exactly. Instantly. That's the problem, isn’t it? Building a temple in Lego, or in Minecraft, takes creativity, problem-solving… but it also takes  time . And effort. Reading, Finn, Lily, reading sparks your imagination in a different way. It asks you to  build  the world in your head, not just on a screen. How do you ‘build’ a world in your head? Well, when you read about a character climbing a snowy mountain, you have to imagine what that feels like. You picture the biting wind, the crunch of the snow under their boots, the way the sunlight glints off the ice. It's like… building a movie in your mind. It uses different muscles, different parts of your brain. So, it's like… building a Minecraft world, but… inside your head? Using words? Exactly! It’s fantastic. And it’s amazing training for being able to understand things properly, for writing your own stories. Think about Ninjago – wouldn’t it be brilliant if you could write your own Ninjago adventure? I guess… I could maybe write about Lloyd finding a lost ninja artifact. And it’s hidden in a volcano! I could write about building a giant roller coaster in Minecraft that goes through the nether! But… it would take  forever  to describe everything. It might, but that’s the fun of it! It’s about picking the important bits, making your words vivid and exciting. Look, how about this?

…and honestly, Chloe, I still can’t quite believe how quiet it was in Cornwall. Absolutely  nothing  like the brochures promised. I mean, the beach itself was lovely, don't get me wrong, but the village? Empty. Like a film set waiting for the actors to arrive. Really? I thought it sounded nice, Mum. All those little cream tea shops. Did you at least manage a proper Cornish cream tea? Oh,  plenty  of Cornish cream teas. Sadly, they tasted approximately the same as a cream tea from Marks & Spencer. The authenticity, it was…missing. Though the scones were decent, I’ll give them that. Sarah, you weren't disappointed? You were all for seeing the fishing boats, weren't you? Nah, it was fine, Mum. The boats were there, just…not  doing  much. A few chugging around. Honestly, the best bit was that little pottery shop near the harbour. I got you a little bird, remember? The blue one? Oh! Yes, I do! That was lovely, thank you, darling. Really brightened up the place. Though I suspect the fisherman may have earned more from the tourists buying their overpriced pasties than from actually fishing. Typical, Mum. Finding the negative in everything. I thought the coastal walks were beautiful. Even if the village  was  a bit sleepy. Sleepy is putting it mildly, Chloe. It felt like time had stopped. Anyway, enough about Cornwall. What are you two up to today? Sarah, still battling with that dissertation? Battling is the operative word. I’ve got to finish chapter three by Friday, and I’m staring at this blank page, feeling utterly useless. I think I might just try a coffee shop today, different environment and all that. Need to get out of my room. Good idea. Fresh air might do you good. Chloe, you were saying something about a sale at that boutique in Tamworth? Oh yeah! They're having a massive summer clearance. I was thinking of popping down this morning. Might get a couple of bits before they’re all gone. It's pretty hectic though, be warned, Mum. You wouldn't like it. Queues out the door and all sorts. No, I wouldn't. My idea of a relaxing morning doesn’t involve battling hordes for discounted floral blouses. Although… a new scarf wouldn’t go amiss. I did lose one in the car the other week. Don’t ask.

Right, my turn. Seven of clubs. And honestly, Mr. Davies is  still  going on about the Crimean War in history. Like, seriously? Who even cares about the Crimean War anymore? It's, like, important, Liam. It shaped modern warfare, apparently. Though, I can see why you'd think it's boring. It's drier than my mum's bread. At least we got sandwiches. This one’s actually decent – proper pickle. Yours? Ham and mustard. Standard. Though, I reckon Sarah’s got the best one. She’s got that fancy smoked salmon and cream cheese one. She always does. Ridiculous, really. It's a school lunch, not a Michelin-star meal. Don’t be jealous! It's just, like, Mum makes it for me. Besides, I needed to get my points, Matthew. Go Fish! Go Fish? Seriously, Chloe? You had  two  sets of eights! You’re deliberately trying to mess with me. She is. Chloe cheats at everything. Remember that time she swapped our cards during the Pokemon tournament? I’m still fuming about that. It was a tactical manoeuvre! And besides, you were losing anyway, Josh. Look, anyway, did you hear about that incident with Patel and the prefects yesterday? Patel? What happened? He's usually the cleverest guy in our year. Apparently, he was arguing with Head Prefect Thompson. Something about Thompson accusing him of deliberately bumping into Ms. Harding in the corridor. It’s ridiculous! Everyone knows Thompson's got it in for Patel. Always giving him the stink eye. Probably 'cause Patel called him out on that dodgy essay marking last month. Remember? Yeah! Totally unfair. Thompson’s playing favouritism and it's so obvious. That's what you get for being born into a family who's donated loads of money to the school. It's messed up, innit? It makes you wonder, you know? Like, is everything fair? My cousin, he was saying his mate's dad got unfairly passed over for a promotion at work; it was because someone else’s dad was richer. It’s everywhere, isn't it? Even in school. Remember what happened to Omar last year? The way people treated him after that… it wasn’t right. Yeah… that was awful. I don’t really like talking about it. Don’t have to. But it’s important to remember, yeah? And it’s not just, like, individual stuff. My dad was watching the news – something’s kicking off in that country, Ukraine?

…and then Mr. Davies just  stared  at me! Like I’d personally insulted his entire family. Honestly, I just asked if the formula worked for oblique angles. Oblique! It’s not like I was questioning the laws of physics, was it? You know, you always manage to rile him up. He's just…intimidating, innit? I swear, if I’d asked that same question, he’d have smiled and explained it nicely. Typical. Exactly! It’s the double standards. You get a slightly questioning look from him and it’s like you’ve committed treason. Whereas Liam just messes around the whole lesson, chucking paper airplanes, and he gets a playful warning. It’s so unfair. Liam's got his charm going on, doesn't he? Blagging his way through everything. Remember that time he convinced Mrs. Peterson he'd finished the Dickens essay when he hadn't even started it? Oh my god, yes! And she bought it! He just looked all serious and said, "It’s a rather nuanced exploration of Victorian societal pressures, Mrs. Peterson." Lied straight to her face! Pure genius. Anyway, speaking of teachers... how’s English going with Miss Hawthorne? I'm still struggling with the reading lessons. Like, analysing poetry? It’s just…words, innit? Why do we need to dissect them like frogs? Ugh, I know! It's so dry. But Miss Hawthorne’s really trying, I think. She’s clever, she just…doesn't  get  that most of us just want to read for pleasure. She was going on about symbolism in “The Raven” for a good twenty minutes yesterday. “The Raven”? Seriously? Why are we reading Edgar Allan Poe? It’s all gloomy and depressing. I’d rather be reading something like… well, anything else, really. Right? I'm trying to convince her that maybe we could do something a bit more relatable. Perhaps something by Becky Chambers? "The Long Way to a Small, Angry Planet" is brilliant. Ooh, I’ve heard of that! That sounds way better than gloomy old Poe. You should tell her. You're good at talking to teachers when you're not getting shouted at by Mr. Davies. True. Right, so, did you watch "17 Again" last night? Honestly, Matthew Perry was brilliant. I know it's a bit cheesy, but it made me laugh so much. I did! It was proper good! I kept thinking, what would  we  be like if we were suddenly back in Year Seven?

Right, mate? Like, you’re willingly letting someone zap your eyeballs. Mental. Still, if it means you can ditch those massive glasses, you gotta, yeah? Exactly! They’re a nightmare, especially when I’m covered in flour. It’s like, permanently glued to my face. Plus, I’m trying to travel more. Think of the photos without the smudged lenses! Speaking of travel...Transylvania? Seriously, Chloe? You’re actually going? Yeah! Liv and I are going for a week in August. It sounds a bit spooky, I know, but Liv’s been obsessed with vampire lore since she was a kid. We figured, why not? It’ll be different. Transylvania! Blimey. You’ll be dodging bats and dodgy Dracula impersonators. Send us a postcard. Dodging bats? Crikey! You gotta be right! Just make sure you’ve packed your mozzie spray. Those little buggers are relentless. I’ve spent weeks getting bitten in bushland, it’s brutal. See? Even Rhys knows the dangers. I’ve got mosquito nets and everything. Liv’s even packed garlic… apparently, it helps. Garlic? Seriously? You're tempting the vampires! You know, last week I was having a right laugh with Sarah from down the street. Apparently, Darren finally popped the question! No way! Darren? The one with the dodgy hair? Thought he'd be single forever. Good for her, though. What’s she doing? She's training to be a yoga instructor. Said she needed a ‘spiritual cleanse’ before saying yes. Sounded a bit dramatic, even for Sarah. That's fair dinkum! People get a bit loopy when they find 'the one'. I saw me mate, Liam, proposing to his girlfriend last year. He was a nervous wreck, ended up dropping the ring in the harbour. Had to get divers! Oh, you're having a laugh! That’s mental! Speaking of things going wrong, have you guys heard about Amelia's bakery? Apparently, she’s having trouble with her supplier. Says they’ve been sending her stale ingredients. No! That’s awful. She’s already working so hard. Is she going to be okay? I heard she’s trying to find a new one. Finding a good supplier in this city is like searching for a unicorn, though. I understand her struggles, totally. It took me ages to find mine. Yeah, it’s tough, especially when you’re starting out. Gotta be on your toes.

…and honestly, I think a Spotify wrapped playlist is  way  more engaging than a traditional family photo album, isn't it? At least then everyone gets to hear what we’ve all been blasting. Dinosaurs like music! Roar! It’s boring looking at pictures, Mum. Everyone looks stiff. Can we have cake now? Well, stiff photos are part of the tradition, darling. But yes, agreed. A playlist is modern. We could even include that awful sea shanty you were obsessed with for, like, a week, Leo. It  wasn't  awful! It was epic! "Well blow me down!" Language, please, love. Remember? Grandma doesn't like the…  robust  vocabulary. And anyway, what about Willow? What sort of music has  she  been enjoying? I know she had that phase with the ukulele songs. Uh-huh! Ukulele! Twinkle! Exactly. So, playlist first. Family photos can be a smaller part, a celebratory add-on. What do you think, Leo? About the party, I mean, not the photos. Auntie Carol's still keen to host, yeah? Yeah. But she’ll make that weird beetroot salad again. Sadly, I suspect you are correct. We need to tactfully steer her towards something slightly less...earthy. Maybe a big cheese board? And fairy lights! Definitely fairy lights. Right, so Saturday the 18th, Carol’s, playlist first, photos second, beetroot salad avoided... Can we play "Alice in Wonderland" at the party? Pleeease? Oh, you and your  Alice in Wonderland , Willow. Always. We'll see, sweetie. It depends on the music vibe we go for. We could have a Mad Hatter’s tea party theme with it! Imagine, little cards and stuff… That would be cool. Can I build a giant rabbit out of Lego? Absolutely, you can! Speaking of cool, did you see that aerial hoop video on Instagram? That girl was incredible! Spinning around like a… like a sparkly spider. Can we do that, Mum? Please? Well, it's tricky, love. It takes a lot of strength. And a very good harness. But maybe… maybe we could look into some introductory classes. It would be a fantastic way to get fit. Hoop! Hoop! Just promise me you won't try to hang off the light fitting. Last time, with the climbing frame… I slipped! It wasn’t my fault! Of course, darling. But we need to be careful. We’re going to have fun, but safety first. Right, snack time.

Cor, that sounds like a right carry-on. Reminds me o' me grandson, Alfie. Full o' mischief, that one. Always gettin' up to somethin'. Though not as graceful as Liam sounds, mind you. More like a startled badger. You're painting a vivid picture, Arthur. It was a classic boys being boys moment. Speaking of classic, my daughter, Emily, got her exam results today. A-star in History! Absolutely thrilled, we are. All that revision finally paid off. Oh, that’s wonderful, David! A-star, you say? Well done to her, absolutely brilliant. Makes you worry, doesn’t it, though? All that pressure they put on ‘em. Remember when our children were younger? Going through SATs… such a stressful time. Mum! Don't start! It wasn’t  that  bad. History was my favourite anyway. And I got a B in Maths, which is... okay, I guess. Emily’s really clever, though. I’m trying for a C in Maths. It's a bit tricky. Maths, eh? Never were good at maths. Numbers always swam about in front of me eyes like minnows. Never needed it, not really. Spent me days down the market, countin' apples and pears. Simple arithmetic, that was. Simple and honest work, Arthur. Emily's thinking of studying History at university. Wants to be an archaeologist, can you believe it? Digging up old bones and things. Goodness! That's a bit adventurous, isn’t it? I always imagined her as a teacher, like you, David. She's got her own ideas. That’s the beauty of it, I suppose. Though I did suggest she maybe consider something a little more...stable. Archaeology doesn't exactly scream "job security." Dad, you're so boring! It's exciting! Imagine finding a Roman coin! Or a dinosaur bone! Dinosaurs, eh? Always fancied a bit o' diggin’ myself, I did. Though I reckon I'd stick to findin' old coins, rather than bones. Spooked by bones, I am. Well, let's not worry about bones and universities just yet. Look at this roulade! Absolutely gorgeous. Did you make it, darling? I did. Thought we deserved a treat after all the exam talk. It's got a little Kirsch in it, just a touch. Kirsch, you say? Now  that  sounds proper. Might need a slice o' that to settle me nerves after hearin' about diggin' up dinosaurs! You’re such a grandpa, Arthur!

Sounds like classic bureaucracy, Sarah. You dealing with it okay? It’s tiring, Liam. Always fighting for someone else’s dignity. At least the residents enjoy the singalongs. We did a lovely bit of Vera Lynn yesterday. Did you manage to finish that marking, then? Mark the essays? Still chipping away at it, Sarah. Grad students, eh? They think they're writing the next Shakespeare. Bit dramatic sometimes. They can be. But some of the insights are genuinely good. I had one yesterday on the use of symbolism in  Heart of Darkness  that was rather brilliant, actually. Made me want to re-read it. You've read that, haven't you, David? Of course. Good stuff. Bit bleak though. Always did prefer Churchill, myself. Man of action. Oh, Dad, not again. Churchill’s glory days are a little… glorified, wouldn’t you say? There’s a lot to unpack there, particularly regarding the Empire and… well, everything. Exactly! And it's funny how perceptions change. I was just reading about South Korea, actually. Amazing how they went from being devastated after the war to becoming a global tech powerhouse. It's practically miraculous. They even have their own version of chess, Janggi - have you ever seen it? Janggi? Never heard of it. Better than Chinese chess, I wager. This game’s all about patience, lad. Strategy, of course, but patience is key. Like waiting for a decent crop of raspberries. How are the berries doing this year? Not brilliant, Dad. Slugs got to most of them. I’ve tried slug pellets, beer traps… nothing seems to work! I may just have to give up and buy them from the supermarket. Shame. Speaking of which, are you having beans on toast for lunch? Possible. Depends on what you're thinking of whipping up. Though I might just grill some sausages, you know. Keeps it simple. Simple is good. I’ve got to head off later to see Mrs. Patel. She's struggling with the past tenses, bless her. Trying to explain the difference between ‘went’ and ‘have gone’ is like talking to a brick wall sometimes! It’s fascinating from a linguistics perspective, though – the way people instinctively try to construct meaning, even when the grammar’s all wrong. You always were fascinated by language, Liam. Remember when you used to make up your own words when you were little? Oh, God, yes!

…and honestly, Chloe, the sheer  disinterest  from some of them is baffling. I mean, they're paying for these lessons, ostensibly to improve their English, yet they spend half the time scrolling through TikTok. It's demoralizing, you know? More so than usual, anyway. Aye, I get that. It's the same here with some of the kids. You try to build a lesson around something they’re interested in, like, say, a game or a really engaging YouTube video, and they're just… blank. They’d rather be learning about influencers, I swear. Still, you've been doing it longer than me, haven’t you? How do you keep going? Routine mostly, I suppose. And the occasional spark from a genuinely keen student. It's just... precarious, isn't it? This freelance thing. I keep thinking about my pension, or rather, the distinct lack thereof. Remember how we used to moan about student loans? At least  you  have a proper job with, hopefully, a decent scheme attached. I'm looking at a bleak future, really. Don't say that, Fiona. You've always been clever, you’ll figure something out. And the loans… don’t even get me started. Postgraduate loans are a nightmare. I’m paying over £300 a month, and I still feel like I’m barely making a dent. It’s utterly ridiculous. At least I’m earning something, though. I was thinking, actually, maybe you could look into doing more online lessons? There’s a demand for it. I've looked, but the competition is fierce. It’s all contract work, zero rights. It’s the same old story. Still, I need to be more proactive, I know. And speaking of proactivity, I need to get my car MOT’d. Dread the thought. Do you remember that disaster last time? Oh, God, yes! The mechanic practically shook his head in despair. Honestly, I’m surprised it’s still running. So, are you thinking of getting it done in Tarnów? There's that place just off the Rynek, I saw a sign... Possibly. It's such a hassle, isn’t it? Getting it done abroad. Are you enjoying being out here, though? Actually, teaching in Poland… sounds almost glamorous, doesn’t it? It's good, aye. Different. The kids are bright, the city’s lovely, and the cost of living is considerably better than back home. I was thinking maybe you could come visit for a few weeks next summer?

Yeah, I saw that. My mum had a look at it too and she just said, "Good luck with  that  one, Liam." She's still pushing me towards Maths, you know. Says it’s ‘stable’ and ‘employable’. As if I’m not going to be a stable and employable Human Scientist! Don’t get me wrong, Maths is brilliant. Solid, dependable… like a well-worn rugby ball. But where's the  fun ? Where’s the intriguing social theory? I mean, you can apply Maths to  anything , sure. But Human Sciences… you can just, like,  debate  stuff. All the time. It’s way more engaging. What’s your favourite module then, if you were to pick one? Hmm, probably Cognitive Psychology. The way the brain works is just mind-blowing.
