He built a life here, a good life. Never once thought about movin' back north, even though he missed his family. He saw the chance for somethin’ better, somethin' different. So, you think staying together is better? Even with all the… disagreements? Look, Jamie, I'm not sayin' it’s all rosy. Westminster can be a right mess sometimes. I’ve marked enough GCSE papers to know the politicians in London aren't exactly known for their clear heads. But splitting up? Think of the complications! The border, the currency, the sharing of resources… The disruption! And what about families? What about people with relatives on both sides? We’re all interconnected, you know. Like threads in a tapestry. You pull one thread, and the whole thing starts to unravel. What about the EU? Wouldn't Scotland be better off in the EU on its own? Och, don't even get me started on Brexit!

'Ere, did you 'ear 'er say "should of"? Should  have ! Honestly, it winds me right up. It’s like, people just don't bother learning the rules anymore. Aye, like. It’s a pet peeve o' mine too, love. "Should of," "would of," it's makin' me ears bleed. Proper cringe-worthy, like. Reminds me of me grandad, bless 'im, used to say it all the time. He weren't the quickest learner, our grandad. Oh, my nan does that! She’ll be, “I should of gone to the shops earlier!” And I just want to grab her and go, "Nan, no you shouldn't  have !" It's hilarious, though. Like, a source of endless amusement. So, what's yer point, Liv? You think Jeremy Kyle's cast are deliberately messin' with grammar? Nah, it's not deliberate. It's just how they talk, innit? It’s elision, basically. Dropping bits of words. Happens all the time. My mum does it, especially when she’s rushin' about. Like, "I'm goin' t'the shops." "Going to," but proper quick, yeah? Aye, she's right. It’s about speed, isn't it? Makin' it flow. Even us, we do it, don't we? Sometimes. Well, I try not to. But when I'm proper tired or stressed... Foot and mouth! I say “foot and mouth” when I mean “foot and mouth disease.” It just slips out. I'm mortified when I do it though! I think it's more that people haven't been taught properly. My school was rubbish for grammar. We just learned to pass the exams. Nobody bothered explaining  why  you should say "should have," just that you did. See that fella on the telly there? The one with the dodgy beard? He’s never learned proper. He looks like he’s trying to escape something. Seriously though, I think accents are brilliant. I love listening to different ways of talking. You girls with your Yorkshire… it’s lovely, proper warm and friendly. That’s dead nice of you to say, love. Reckon yer Liverpudlian accent’s dead good yourself. Bit fast for me sometimes though, I have to concentrate! Yeah, like trying to understand me mum when she’s properly wound up. It's a whole different language! Like, her shoutin’ about the price of gas? Forget about it. Remember last Christmas when she was on about the Christmas lights and started yellin’ at the postie?

Right, come on you… oh, blimey, that was a dodgy tackle. Ref needs to have a proper look at that. Honestly, Liam, concentrate on the knitting. It’s more productive than complaining about the ref’s eyesight. Besides, they've got VAR now, haven’t they? Doubt they'll miss that one. Productive? Freya, this is a Saturday afternoon. It's legally mandated relaxation time. And VAR's still rubbish. You know it. It just slows the game down. Aye, well, someone needs to be making proper use of their time. This scarf's for Nana Elsie, and she's expecting it for Christmas. You know how she gets when she doesn't get her Christmas presents on time. Starts sending passive-aggressive postcards. Right, the Elsie Gauntlet. I remember. So, Northumbria revenge knitting then? Exactly. It's a serious business, Liam. Now, are you even watching the game properly, or just waiting for someone to get carded? I am watching! It’s just... underwhelming, to be honest. Remember the Olympics last year? That was proper thrilling. I was glued to that swimming. Adam Peaty was incredible. Aye, he was brilliant. I was more into the gymnastics, though. That American, Simone Biles, she was just phenomenal. The pressure she was under… it took real guts to step back, didn’t it? Took guts to prioritise her mental health over medals. Absolutely. Changed the conversation, really. Made people think. Which is good. Speaking of changing things... have you thought any more about names? A little. Still bouncing ideas around. It's harder than I thought it would be. Everyone has an opinion, don't they? My mam keeps suggesting Kevin.  Kevin . Like I’d name my child Kevin. Don't let her win! Kevin's horrific. Did she say after Kevin, "He'd look lovely in a little Sunderland kit, wouldn't he?" You know she did! The cheek of it! I've been looking at girl names. Amelia's nice, but a bit… overdone, isn't it? And Penelope – I love Penelope – but my dad says it sounds like a posh poodle. Penelope  is  rather posh. My mum was obsessed with Penelope for years, actually. She wanted to name me Penelope. Luckily, my dad put a stop to that. He thought "Penelope Birmingham" sounded… awkward. Fair enough. Although, I reckon a Penelope from Sunderland could pull it off. She’d probably just wear Doc Martens with it.

“…and then Barry the bee just explains the whole economic system! Honestly, it’s brilliant! It's like, they're being exploited, right? And nobody bats an eyelid! It’s surprisingly clever for a film marketed solely to kids.” Barry’s funny, Mummy! He does a silly dance! Bees make honey! Can we get honey on our toast tomorrow? Of course, sweetie. We always do. But did you hear what Poppy said about Buckingham Palace? Apparently, it costs… are you ready for this… forty quid  each  to see the State Rooms! Forty quid! Honestly! Forty? Is that like… a hundred sweets? Nearly! It's a lot of sweets. It makes you think, doesn't it? All that money going into keeping a palace going, and families like ours struggling with bills. I mean, shouldn't the royal palaces be, you know... accessible to everyone? Or even better, shouldn't we be a Republic? A what-lic? Does that mean no kings and queens? Well, yes, darling. A Republic means we elect our leaders. Like a big class vote, but for the whole country. But then who would wear the sparkly hats? There’d still be lovely hats, sweetie. Maybe  you  could design them! You've got amazing ideas. Or, you could be Prime Minister! Or even... Queen! Although, being Prime Minister's rather more practical, isn't it? Less tiaras involved. I want to be Prime Minister! I’ll make everyone have Lego! And pizza every Friday! Sounds like a brilliant platform! You’d win for sure. Right, speaking of brilliant, I need to remember to get some Vitamin D supplements. It’s getting gloomy again. We need to keep our immune systems strong before diving at the Olympic Stadium next week. Diving’s noisy! People shouting! That's true. We'll need to practice staying very, very quiet. Like little ninjas. Just watch, absorb, and applaud politely at the end. It's quite a skill, being a silent audience member, isn't it? Can I clap really loud? Not  too  loud, darling. Just a dignified clap. Like Granny used to do at the village fete. Remember Granny’s old house? That kitchen was so tiny, you could barely turn around! And she always had the most amazing fruit trees. Royal Gala apples, Cox’s Orange Pippin… she practically ran a Royal fruit orchard. Granny’s apples were the best! Especially with crumble!

Aye, they are, lass. Everything’s heavier than you remember after a few years, isn't it? Takes a bit outta ya. Still, good riddance to most of it, I reckon. Didn't need half of that gardening paraphernalia. Spent a fortune on it back in the nineties, thinking I'd be the next Gertrude Jekyll. Hah! More like Gertrude neglectful, really. You and gardening, Margaret, a classic mismatch. Honestly, the state of your borders last summer… even the slugs looked sheepish. Anyway, what else did you manage to ditch? Oh, the usual. Boxes of old newspapers, mostly. Birthday cards going back… well, a long way back, really. Felt awful throwing 'em out, mind. Each one a little memory. Your Auntie Elsie’s handwriting, bless her. You remember those awful Christmas jumpers she used to knit? Were they really bad? Like, really bad? My nan knits sometimes. Bad doesn't even cover it, lad. They were works of abstract expressionism in wool. Bright orange, neon green, reindeer with googly eyes… you name it. Elsie was fearless. Fearless and terrifying, in equal measure! Remember that one with the flashing lights? It nearly gave poor little Thomas a seizure. Aye. And that reminds me… Thomas is asking about Thirsk. He's doing a project on market towns. Said he wants to go to the racecourse. Think he’ll enjoy that? Thirsk’s pleasant enough. Bit touristy now, mind. But the racecourse is a good shout. Could make a day of it. We could go with you two. That sounds lovely. We're free next weekend. Though, I might have to be at a… well, it's a stag do actually. For Ben, you know, Daniel’s lad? A stag do? Heavens to Betsy. All that noise and… and whatever they get up to these days. Daniel’s boy? He’s barely out of school! It's the modern way, Margaret. Apparently, it’s a “sophisticated city break” rather than the usual pub crawl. Still, I’ll likely be doing the damage control. Last time I went to one of these… oh dear. Involved a lost kilt and a fountain. Don’t ask. Seriously? A lost kilt? Don’t encourage him, lad. Some things are best left unsaid. Anyway, back to Thirsk. Should we book a table somewhere or just chance it? Let’s book. I’m not keen on standing around. My legs aren't what they used to be.

…and then young Connor, bless ‘im, tried to explain photosynthesis to a five-year-old. Honestly, it was a right mess! He was drawing diagrams with carrot sticks and everything. Little Maisie just kept asking if plants ate chocolate. Oh, Liam! You’re winding me up, aren't you? Connor's a sweet lad, he’s just a bit… enthusiastic. Still, teaching those kids is good for him, gives him perspective. Much better than just staring at screens all day. Aye well, it's good to see 'em learnin’ somethin'. Anyway, back to us. Right, about the interview for that Masters in Applied Linguistics at Manchester… are you thinkin' I'm overreachin', love? Feels a bit bold, does it? Bold? No! You’re brilliant, Liam. Truly. You’ve got the passion, the experience… the school's desperate for someone who actually  cares  about making language accessible. It's a perfect fit. Don't let self-doubt creep in. Easy for you to say, you’re used to interviews! Assistant psychologist, right? Bit more serious than explainin’ the difference between "there," "their," and "they’re" to a classroom full of ten-year-olds. They're serious, yes, but it’s still about articulating yourself and showcasing your skills. Look, I can do a mock interview with you, if you want? Give you a bit of practice? Would ya? That’d be proper dead helpful, actually. Cheers, pet. Speaking of helpful… what about that parking ticket I got the other day? I swear, that meter was broken. Seriously? Where were you parked? We need to appeal it. Let me look through those revised parking regulations I downloaded – I think there’s a section on faulty meters. Near the Walker Art Gallery. Thought I was bein’ clever, puttin' my ticket on the dashboard while I popped in for five minutes to see that new Egyptian exhibition. Bad move. The Egyptian exhibit  is  amazing though! We should go again. Maybe on Sunday? And before we do, we’ll get that ticket sorted. Right, let’s switch gears. Christmas! Have you had a think about what we're getting nan this year? Still early for Christmas, innit? Don't be daft! It'll sneak up on us. Last year we were scrambling for last-minute presents. I was thinking maybe a nice shawl? She's always complaining about the cold. And what about a little something for the new rescue dog, Alfie?

Honestly, Liam Payne’s new single is  dire . Like, seriously, what was he thinking? It sounds like five different songs crammed into one. Right? I heard it too. Bit of a mess, innit? Though, I did see some cute boys at Fabric on Saturday. Proper tall, dark and handsome types. You were there, weren't you? Did you spot 'em? Fabric? Nah, I was chilling with Chloe and Maya. We ended up crashing at Jess’s after, binge-watching 'The Queen's Gambit'. Have you seen that? It's like…obsessive, but so good. Oh yeah, heard loads about that! Anya Taylor-Joy is gorgeous, yeah? My nan keeps trying to get me to watch it. She says it’s ‘proper clever’. My nan watches everything. She’s obsessed with those detectives on Channel 5. Like, proper horrifying storylines, sometimes. My nan's the same! She'll be going on about some true crime documentary when I just wanna listen to Olivia Rodrigo. Speaking of, her Instagram is giving me serious FOMO. Everyone's at Coachella. I’m stuck revising for this bloody history essay. Ugh, history! Don’t even mention it. I’ve got a massive physics problem set due Monday. I’m proper knackered. Barely slept last night, actually. Just scrolling through TikTok until like three. Tell me about it. Sleep is a distant memory, isn't it? This uni life is brutal. Remember when we used to spend all day watching Disney movies and drawing cartoons with my little cousin? Good times. Oh my gosh, yeah! Remember when we tried to recreate ‘The Little Mermaid’ in your garden? My mum was convinced we'd drown the goldfish. And then we got scolded for getting all the mud on her patio. Proper embarrassing. You ever think about getting a tattoo? I'm thinking about a tiny little crescent moon behind my ear. A tattoo… hmm. I’ve considered it. Something small, probably. Maybe a little phoenix. My mum would have a heart attack, though. She's still moaning about my ear piercings. Remember how long she went on about infection risks? Oh, completely. My mum’s the same. She thinks anything permanent is a disaster waiting to happen. She’s more worried about me getting a decent job than getting inked. So true! But honestly, I need a break from all this studying. What are you doing this weekend?

Mum, seriously? Skinny jeans? They’re  so  last year. Everyone’s wearing wide-leg now. Even Jamie from school. Well, you look smart in them, don’t you, love? And they're clean. Right, Oisin, say ‘thank you.’ Clean doesn't equal fashionable, Mum. Besides, I’m trying to build my Pokémon trainer aesthetic. Gotta look the part, you know? I need something… cooler. Like a character from the new Scarlet and Violet game. Pokémon, Pokémon, that’s all you ever talk about. Have you finished that quest you were on? The one with the… what was it, the electric sheep thing? It's a Wooloo, Mum, and yes! Got it. Finally. Took ages. I was trying to trade with Liam, but he’s being stubborn about his Charizard. Says he won't trade for anything less. Liam always was a tricky one. Oisin, stop pulling at your hair! Honestly, you’re a little whirlwind. Right, let’s try to get you settled with a bit of Peppa Pig. We were Skyping Nana earlier, weren't we? She loved seeing your face. Yeah, she did. She kept asking about my guitar lessons. Says I need to practice more. She’s right, you know. You barely touch it since you got those Pokémon games. Remember how excited you were to learn ‘Wonderwall’? I will, Mum! Just... Pokémon is more engaging right now, okay? It’s, like, a whole world. Besides, Nana’s a bit out of touch. She still thinks Pokémon Go is the height of technology. Well, she’s a sweet woman. Listen, I was thinking… maybe we could go out for Ramen next week? After you’ve finished battling whatever electric sheep you’ve got. It's been ages since we did something fun. Ramen? Yeah! That’s wicked. Can Oisin come? Of course, he can! He loves those noodles. Although he usually ends up covered head-to-toe. Oisin! No eating the slippers! They’re not for eating. Little monster. He’s just exploring, Mum. He's learning. Maybe he’ll become a Pokémon researcher when he's older. Discovering new types of creatures. That's lovely, love. Honestly though, look at your feet. Why are you wearing slippers inside? Aren’t you cold? Nah, I’m alright. They're comfy. Plus, they match my Pokémon vibe... kinda. They're like, trainer slippers. Don't you get it?

Honestly, Doreen, this is ridiculous. I've been at this cupboard for nearly an hour and it's barely lighter! It’s like it multiplies when you're not looking. Well, you know what they say, a lifetime of memories crammed into a cupboard. And your lifetime  is  rather… eclectic, isn't it, dear? More eclectic than mine, certainly. All those university reports and policy documents. Policy documents! Don’t remind me. All that jargon. Made my head spin even when I was  working . This is more my speed, really - chucking out old ceramic birds and reminiscing. Oh! Look, tucked away at the back... Isn't this it? Good heavens! The gardening set! Remember that, Elsie? Such a peculiar set. All plastic, of course. But still. Tiny trowels and watering cans… and that horrifying, bright orange plastic gnome. The gnome! He was positively demonic. I used to bury him alive in the sandpit. Always dreamed of being a formidable gardener, you know. Controlling the weeds and nurturing prize-winning roses. Clearly, I’ve failed spectacularly. We both have, darling. I, on the other hand, always wanted to be a botanist. Studying exotic plants in the Amazon. Though, admittedly, my green fingers were a bit… limited to struggling with a pot of geraniums. Geraniums! You remember Aunt Mabel and her prize-winning geraniums? The ones she’d enter in the village fete every year? Dreadful things, all stiff and red. Absolutely dreadful. And she’d fume if anyone even  looked  at them sideways. Speaking of fete-worthy items… what’s this lurking beneath the gardening set? Oh! The Bako. Blimey, haven't seen this in ages. Remember how obsessed we were with Bako? Obsessed! That's putting it mildly. We built entire cities with those things. Magnificent, wobbly cities with precarious bridges and… I can almost feel the plastic corners digging into my fingers. We spent hours, Elsie. Hours! We did. I remember trying to build a castle. It kept collapsing. You'd patiently rebuild it, saying it needed a stronger foundation. You always were the sensible one. Someone had to be. You were forever zooming off to build a spaceship, leaving the castle to crumble. We  did  make a dreadful mess with those, didn't we? Mum was forever complaining about the plastic bricks all over the carpet. She did. She really did. It's funny, isn't it? All this clutter, all these forgotten toys... it's just… proof we were here.

Honestly, they're  relentless  this year, aren’t they? I've counted at least six bites already. Six! And I'm covered in repellent. You'd think living in Norwich would be safe from these tropical invaders, but obviously not. Six? That  is  impressive. I’ve only had the one on my ankle, thankfully. Though, I swear I heard one buzzing dangerously close to Leo's ear just now. Gave me a fright. Maybe we need to invest in one of those mosquito nets for the buggy? Definitely. I've seen them online, the mesh ones. Might be a bit bulky, though. And then he'll want to sleep in it all the time, won't he? Like a little astronaut. Typical. He’ll probably demand a space helmet too. By the way, did you manage to get tickets for The Black Swans gig next month? I was checking online, and they seem to be selling out fast. Oh, bother! No, I completely forgot about that! I was meaning to, but then the grading deadline loomed, and… well, you know. It’s always something, isn't it? I’m so gutted. They're playing that new album, aren't they? The one everyone’s raving about? They are. Apparently, it’s a real shift in their sound. More experimental. I really wanted to go. It would have been a nice night out, just the two of us. I feel dreadful. I’ll keep checking the resale sites. Maybe someone will have a pair going. If not, we’ll have to console ourselves with a takeaway curry and a documentary about hedgehogs. You know how I get. Hedgehogs it is then. Though a curry does sound pretty good right now. This walk is lovely, don’t get me wrong, but I'm craving some spice. Though, honestly, the traffic getting here was horrendous. Did you see that idiot in the red van trying to pull out from the side street? Nearly took out a cyclist. I did! I nearly yelled at him. Honestly, people have no spatial awareness. It's getting worse, isn't it? All these new developments, more cars on the road… It used to be so quiet around here. It really is. They're supposed to be widening the bypass, but it's been delayed again. Apparently, there's some protected species of newt living nearby. Can you believe it?

…and honestly, the sheer volume of rejection emails is just… demoralising. Like, I know it's a tough market, but it's relentless. Did you see that article about the graduate recruitment slump? Apparently, loads of companies are freezing hiring. Blimey, that's rough, innit? Proper rotten luck. Must be doing your head in. Been on the phone all day, then. Felt like a right sales pitch just to get anyone to look at my CV. Exactly! It’s exhausting pretending you’re brimming with enthusiasm when you’re just… deflated. I need a serious power nap later. You were out hitting balls, right? Did you get a decent session in? Yeah, a couple of hours at the range. Felt alright, actually. My chipping's a bit wonky still, but the driver felt pinging. Proper solid. Though, I spent, like, twenty minutes trying to pair my Bluetooth headphones with my phone afterwards, that was proper frustrating. You know how it is, right? Just keeps saying “connection failed.” Tell me about it! My phone's been playing up all week. Keeps randomly shutting down. Thinking I might have to bite the bullet and get it sorted. Mum keeps going on about getting me a new one, but I’m trying to save. What about that new theatre show you were talking about? The one with the spooky vibes? Yeah, 'The Haunting of Blackwood Manor'! Reckon we should book tickets? Halloween's just around the corner. Might be a laugh, eh? Assuming I can get my phone to work long enough to actually buy them. Proper ghost story, apparently. Though, I don't believe in ghosts, you know. Just silly folk talkin' nonsense. Right, but you'd get a proper fright! Remember that time we went to that old pub in High Wycombe? The one that everyone swore was haunted? Oh God, yeah. And you were proper convinced there was something lurking in the loo. Swore you saw a face in the mirror. I  did ! It was definitely a face. All pale and… shifty. Honestly, I practically sprinted out. Anyway, about work… I had a weird interview today. It was for a marketing assistant position. The interviewer was asking about my "passion for spreadsheets." Spreadsheets! Seriously? Cor, that’s ridiculous! What'd you say? I tried to be enthusiastic, I swear. I told him I enjoyed analyzing data and… something about identifying trends.

is mid-song, a garbled rendition of "Twinkle Twinkle Little Star." Liam , an IT manager, is rubbing his temples, while Ben , his nephew visiting from Bristol, is scrolling through his phone. Sarah , Liam's partner, is attempting to coax Finn into finishing his peas.)     Ben:   Seriously, Aunt Sarah, Finn’s got a really good ear. He's actually hitting some notes. Needs a bit of practice though, yeah?   Sarah:   He certainly does. Bless him. He’s been humming that thing for a solid hour. Liam, you're not looking at him. Appreciate the artistry!   Liam:   Sorry, love. Just... thinking about this cloud migration. It’s a right pain. The bloody thing just keeps throwing errors. They’re expecting it live by Friday. Friday! Before then, I'll be bald.   Ben:   Cloud migration? Sounds… complicated. Is that, like, computers in the sky?   Liam:   Something like that. It’s moving all our data to a different server, basically. Less local storage, more online. Easier to access, in theory. Reality's proving to be anything but.   Sarah:   You'll figure it out, Liam. You always do. Just don't let it consume you. We need you relatively sane for Finn's bedtime story.   Finn:   Story! Story! About dinosaurs!   Liam:   Alright, alright, dinosaurs it is. But  after  the dishes. And after you finish your peas, champ. Don’t be lookin' away from them green fellows.   Ben:   Speaking of films, you guys watch anything good lately? Saw a trailer for this new superhero one. Looks massive.   Liam:   Not really got the time, Ben. Been glued to my laptop most evenings. Sarah's been trying to get me to watch something lighthearted.   Sarah:   I suggested  Paddington 2  again. Honestly, it's a masterpiece. Makes you feel all warm inside.   Liam:   Paddington? I’d look like a right eejit if I admitted I haven’t seen it. The lads in work would never let me live it down. But to be honest, I've been too tired.   Ben:   Paddington’s brilliant! I've seen it loads. My mum makes a mean marmalade sandwich.   Liam:   See? Ben gets it. Finn, you like Paddington, don't ya?   Finn:   Bear! Honey!   Sarah:   Right, well, while we're on films, Liam, have you sorted out the train tickets for Ireland West Airport on Sunday? Mum’s phoning me every five minutes asking if we’re ready to go.   Liam:   Ah, blast it!

Oh, no! Bless him. Was he warm enough? He did look a bit chilly in the photo you sent. Warm enough? He was practically radiating heat! Snoring away, little legs sticking out. Honestly, I nearly woke him just to take a picture, but Sarah would have killed me. She probably would have. She's got a fierce protective streak when it comes to him. Not that I blame her, he’s a character. Remember when he tried to 'fix' the bird feeder with his toy hammer? Oh, yeah! Cement everywhere. Sarah was fuming. But he was so proud of himself, wasn't he? Head held high, covered in grey dust. He just said, "I made it better, didn't I, Daddy?" You can't argue with that logic. Daddy! Birdie! See? Even she's remembered the birdie incident. Speaking of remembering things, I was sketching out some ideas for the extension again. Oh, good! Let me see. Still thinking about a sunroom off the kitchen? Yeah, definitely that. And maybe a proper utility room, not just a cupboard under the stairs. You know, somewhere we can actually  use  without tripping over each other. Imagine having a washing machine and a proper tumble dryer that doesn't rattle the windows. That  would  be heaven. And a pantry! I've been saying this for ages - a proper pantry for all the jam I make and your endless supply of biscuits. Right, right, pantry. Noted. I was thinking, if we put the extension on the back, we could lose that slightly wonky bit of fence. It's always bugging me. Good point. And more light into the garden. I’d love a little patio area out there, somewhere to sit and have a cuppa in the summer. Imagine, honeysuckle climbing up the extension… Honeysuckle. Yeah, sounds beautiful. We'd need to get proper planning permission, obviously. Don't want to upset the neighbours. Mrs. Higginbottom's got eyes like a hawk, you know. Tell me about it. She probably saw Anon in his pants from her kitchen window! Now  that  would be a headline! "Local Child Spotted in Underwear: Extension Plans Cause Neighbourly Concerns." Daddy! Look! Butterfly! Crikey, she's right! Big one, that. Right, you two, let's go and chase butterflies. We can finish talking about the extension later. It’s a beautiful day to be outside. Butterflies! Me too! Alright, let's go then.

Honestly, Alun, this instant stuff is getting on my nerves. It tastes like burnt toast and despair. Did you ever manage to get the proper beans in? Now, now, David, don't be like that! It's perfectly serviceable, and it keeps us afloat. Though, I will admit, I did try to order some decent Sumatran from that online place. Still waiting, mind. The delivery’s been a nightmare. Probably something to do with the new water company taking over, isn’t it? Absolute shambles, they are. Rates are up, pressure’s down, and the invoices are a mystery. Tell me about it. Thames Water, appalling. They’ve been threatening to install a smart meter, you know. As if I need a computer monitoring my toothbrushing habits. It's intrusive, and frankly, I suspect it's just a way to justify further price increases. Have you heard anything back about that funding application, by the way? For the Roman aqueduct project? Not a peep, David. Not a peep. Sent it in weeks ago. They’re being tighter than a drum these days. The Arts and Humanities Research Council... they’re prioritizing apparently, and classical infrastructure isn't “urgent” enough. Can you believe it? Urgent! As if researching the very foundations of civilisation isn’t important. I was telling my daughter, Seren, about it – she’s doing a Master’s in Archaeology – and she said, "Dad, you need to phrase it as 'vital to understanding societal resilience in the face of climate change.'" Cheeky girl. Sounds about right. Framing it within a contemporary context, eh? The modern academic dance. I've had to do similar with my Middle Eastern history work. Spin it as “a contextual understanding of current geo-political instability” – basically, old stuff explains new stuff. Though, I was hoping to simply discuss the brilliance of their engineering… the sheer innovation. Speaking of brilliant engineering, have you been following the updates on the LHC? They're reportedly getting closer to some fascinating particle collisions. Oh, indeed! Remarkable, isn’t it? The Hadron Collider. The scale of it... quite humbling. It makes our little aqueduct project seem rather quaint. But the principles are similar, really, aren't they? Moving things, managing resources… just on vastly different scales. Reminds me of that trip we took to Italy, all those years ago. Remember? Florence. The Duomo. Absolutely breathtaking. I tried to explain the engineering behind Brunelleschi’s dome to a group of students once - they just stared at me blankly.

Right, Operation Sort-and-Conquer is officially underway. Honestly, the sheer volume of these things! Where do you even  begin ? Begin with the red ones, Miss Emily! Red ones are superheroes! You’re absolutely right, darling. Red bricks are superheroes. Very good, Elara. Leo, are you being helpful, or just building a Lego volcano that’s about to erupt? It  is  a volcano! It’s going to… BOOM! And then the dinosaurs come out! Dinosaurs, brilliant! But perhaps we can leave the volcanic eruption for a bit and join in the sorting, eh? We’re trying to get everything organised so you two can build  anything  you want. Imagine, a whole city! Or… or Hogwarts! Hogwarts! Can we build Professor Sprout’s greenhouse? With all the Mandrakes! Oh, absolutely! We can build the whole castle! But we need to find all the grey bricks first. That’s the stone, you see. And then the brown ones are wood. Think of it like... like potions, practically! Ingredient gathering. Can we get Bart Simpson to help us find the grey ones? He's good at finding stuff, isn't he? Bart Simpson? Well, he's certainly resourceful, clever boy. But I think we’re better off sticking to real-life sorting, rather than inviting cartoon characters into the mix. Though, I  do  wonder if he'd be able to find our remote control… Maybe he’d trick us into giving him all the chocolate! You’re both right to be suspicious! Speaking of chocolate, we’ve got a mountain of Easter eggs still to get through. We'll save some for later, though. We've got a cinema trip planned for Saturday, remember? We were going to see that new Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles movie. Cowabunga! Can we get pizza after? Of course! Massive, cheesy pizza. But before the turtles and the pizza, we’ve got to conquer this Lego hoard. It's a bit like Granny's house renovations, isn't it? Just mountains and mountains of… stuff! Granny's house is messy! But she has lots of cushions! She does indeed. And we’re  finally  getting around to clearing out the back porch. Remember Dad was saying it was like an archaeological dig back there? Layers and layers of… well, you know. Old flower pots, broken garden gnomes… Gnomes are protectors! They keep the bad dreams away! They certainly do, darling.

…and honestly, the ward was  wild  on Monday. Absolute chaos after the weekend. We had a patient refusing medication, two escalating arguments, and a scheduled discharge that went completely sideways because his family couldn’t get here. It was just…a lot. I'm so glad I’m back home, even if it's just for a few days before the next shift. Sounds intense. Seriously. You need a proper decompress. Glad you’re back though! So, spill. Holiday – paradise or flop? You were so hyped about Tenerife. Honestly? A bit of both. The weather was incredible, the beaches were stunning, like something out of a postcard. The volcanic landscapes were amazing too – we did that jeep tour which was a bit bumpy but totally worth it. But…it wasn't exactly the relaxing getaway I needed. Oh? Why not? Did something go wrong? Not exactly 'wrong', just...stressful. Turns out, my aunt Carol, you know, the one who’s always complaining about something, decided this was the perfect time to announce she wants to sell her house and move to Florida permanently. Cue two hours of her agonizing over downsizing and what to do with all her cats. She kept dragging me into it! I’m trying to unwind after dealing with people’s mental health all day and I'm stuck listening about Mittens' emotional distress! Oh my god, Carol! Classic Carol. Honestly, you deserve a medal for putting up with her. Did she at least let you have any sun? Some! I managed to sneak in a few hours on the beach. I got a bit of a burn on my shoulders, annoyingly. But I did try some amazing seafood paella – you absolutely  have  to try it when you go. It was phenomenal. Speaking of food, what have you been up to while I’ve been away? Still raiding the cupboards and ordering Deliveroo? Guilty as charged! It’s been pretty chaotic here. Work’s been…work. The Henderson project is a nightmare. They keep changing their minds about the signage, and the contractors are behind schedule. It’s just a constant fire-fighting exercise. I’m seriously considering volunteering for a desk job just to escape the project management madness! Ugh, sounds familiar. Remember when you were complaining about the Baker account last year? They’re all the same. What about Liam? Have you heard from him?

Aye, teenagers. They do test yer patience, don’t they? My own Mark weren’t much better at maths when he were that age. More interested in football, of course. Still is, come to that.      It’s not  all  about football, Auntie Brenda! Some of us have... other interests. And factoring isn't the most thrilling thing in the world, y'know.      Factorizin'? What in tarnation is factorizin'? Sounds like summat a factory does! Back in my day, we learned our sums on a slate with a bit of chalk, and we were grateful for it! No fancy calculators neither.      Slate and chalk, Edna. Reminds me of the time I accidentally rubbed out the teacher’s lesson completely. Oh, she gave me a right earful! Had to clean the whole blackboard after school.      Oh, Arthur, you always were a scamp! See, Tom, that’s why we need factoring - so you don’t end up scrubbing blackboards! Right, so about the visit. Nana and Grandad are due any minute, eh? Have you finished tidying up the sitting room, love? It were lookin' a bit like a bomb site earlier.      Yeah, Auntie Brenda, all done. Dusted everything, hoovered, even straightened out Grandad’s newspapers. Though I think he'll just mess it all up again within five minutes.      Don't you be cheeky about my Albert! He likes his newspapers. Keeps him brain engaged, he says. Though half o' 'em are from last week!      I like the comics, Edna. That 'Beano' and 'Dandy' - still got a soft spot for them. Remember when we used to get a week's worth of comics delivered on a Saturday? Proper treat that were.      That’s lovely to hear, both of you. Actually, I was thinking… should we get a little somethin' for them? Something to nibble on while they’re here? I made a Victoria sponge yesterday - it's in the fridge. But maybe some biscuits too.      Biscuits sound good, Auntie Brenda. Jammies, maybe? Or chocolate digestives? Grandad’s a big fan of them.      Jammies are always a winner, dear. And a cup o' tea, of course. Strong, mind you! I like my tea strong enough to stand a spoon up in.      And a bit o' butter with them biscuits, Edna. Don't forget the butter! Creamy butter, not that spreadable stuff.      Right then, jammies it is. I’ll pop down to the shop. Tom, could you put the kettle on?

“…and that’s why, darling, it’s so important we do what we can. It's not just about sending a few toys, is it? It's about showing them someone cares, that they’re not forgotten.” She stirred the simmering pasta sauce, glancing at the two children perched on stools at the kitchen island. “But Mummy, what's ‘forgotten’?” "Well, imagine if you woke up one morning and nobody remembered your birthday, or your favourite teddy, Mr. Snuggles. It would feel a bit… lonely, wouldn't it? These children at Great Ormond Street, some of them are very, very poorly, and sometimes the world outside feels very far away. Sending them something, even a drawing, helps them feel remembered.” “Like in Peter Pan? When the Lost Boys were lost, they were sad because nobody knew where they were.” "Exactly, love! Spot on. Just like the Lost Boys. And then Wendy came and gave them a home, and showed them they were loved. We’re doing a little bit of that, aren't we?” She smiled warmly at both of them. “Did you see Tinkerbell’s new film, Mummy? The one with the lost fairies?” “I did! It was lovely, wasn't it? Very sparkly. Though I did find it a bit sad that even the fairies have their worries and need help sometimes." “I liked when Terence helped her find Pixie Hollow again! He was really brave.” “He was, wasn't he? And that’s what’s wonderful about Peter Pan and all the films - they’re about being brave, even when you're scared. And helping others, even when you don’t feel like it. Just like Wendy faced Captain Hook!” She chuckled. “Remember how she told him off?” “Yes! She said he was naughty and should be good!” "But Hook was still scary! I don’t like Captain Hook. He has a hook for a hand!” He shivered dramatically. “He  is  a bit scary, isn't he? But Wendy showed him that being kind is more important than being scary.” She turned back to the pasta for a moment, then added, “You know, when they made the original Peter Pan film, lots of people thought Tinkerbell was going to be a real fairy, but they couldn't figure out how to show her properly! That’s why she’s just a silhouette, a sparkly shadow." “Really? Why not?”

Honestly, I'm feeling it today. The early start is really hitting me. Had to be up at five, and I barely slept a wink last night. Just tossing and turning. Five, eh? Blimey. That's a bit early even for me, and I’m usually up with the lark, or at least try to be. Are you alright, love? You look a bit peaked. Are you, darling? Bit rough, are we? It’s a shock to the system, isn’t it? Driving all this way, then up to the airport so early. Remember that cottage we rented near Salcombe, years ago? We were all so excited for a seaside holiday… Oh, the Salcombe cottage. Dripping with damp, that was. But the views were incredible. Much better than that awful place in Taunton, though. Remember that, Dad? The one with the… the… The eccentric neighbour who thought we were spies, yes. With the overflowing hydrangeas and the suspicious glances. Took us weeks to get that sorted. Now, Taunton... that was a long way to commute every day. Still can't believe I used to do that. Postgrad training for a management role, and then… well, you know. Things… shifted. Yes, dear, they did. But it was a good role, wasn't it? Even if things didn't quite work out the way we planned. This Devon life suits you though, doesn't it, Arthur? Much calmer. It does, yes. Much calmer. Though I do miss the… the bustle, sometimes. The energy of a proper office. Still, peace and quiet has its benefits, hasn’t it? Now, about this Christmas… we need to start thinking about it. Sarah and Tom are coming, of course. And little Leo. He'll be running around like a… well, like a little Leo. He'll be a terror. But a cute one. We’re thinking of having a proper Christmas this year, not just a low-key affair. And that housewarming party! I need to get organised. Invitation lists, catering, the whole shebang. It feels quite daunting, actually. Don’t fret, love. You’re brilliant at organising. Remember when you planned that school trip to the Lake District? Everything ran like clockwork. And we’ll all help. I'll do the canapés. Everyone loves my mini-quiches. And Arthur can handle the music, I’m sure. I’ve got a playlist, alright. A very respectable playlist.

Relaxing? Nah, love. Sounds right messy. I 'ad a fella try and flog me one once, down in Skegness. Said it'd cure me lumbago. Nearly gave me another attack! All that proddin' and pokin'. Not for me, that. Give me a nice cuppa and a sit down any day.      Exactly! A sit down is precisely what I need. This working party... bless the volunteers, but moving those old sleepers is a devilish job, isn't it? Especially at our age. Reminds me a bit of trying to shift some antique furniture in a damp Somerset farmhouse – same backache, different century.      Aye, I can appreciate that. Been a good crowd here though, the lads and lasses. Working on the track, y’see, clearin’ up some of the overgrown bits. Reminds me of Wolverhampton station when I started. Just a right state, it was. But then, everything needs a bit of tendin’ to, doesn’t it? Just like… like hospice care, for instance. My Elsie, bless her, she spent a few weeks in St. Mary's, near Birmingham. Lovely place. Looked after her beautifully.      Oh, I’m so sorry to hear that. My dear friend, Penelope, she frequented somewhere like that last year, near Glastonbury. It's rather humbling, isn’t it? Seeing the dedication of those nurses. It makes you appreciate the little things. I’m always saying, it’s a dreadful waste of good talent, all those intelligent women helping tidy up after people when they could be doing somethin' more... something like headin’ up a nursery, for example. I’ve always felt passionately about early childhood education.      Nursery education, eh? Me daughter, Brenda, she's a primary school teacher now. Says it’s all about 'early years' and ‘play-based learning’ these days. Looks a far cry from when I were a lad. We just got a smacked bottom and told to behave! Equality for women, though… that's definitely come on. My Elsie, she never had a chance to really shine, y'know? Stuck at home, lookin' after us kids. Never complained, mind you, but… it wasn't right, was it?      Not right at all. Terminology has changed, obviously. We used to talk about ‘housewives’, now it's ‘domestic engineers’ or something equally awkward. I always preferred ‘homemakers,’ don’t you think? Sounds a bit more… dignified. You’ve got to understand, when I was a girl, the idea of a woman running a business was… eccentric, to say the least.

…and then little Mateo just started throwing pasta at Mrs. Rodriguez! Honestly, it was a full-blown food fight. I managed to break it up, of course, but the classroom looked like a spaghetti explosion. You wouldn't  believe  the mess. Oh, bless him. They’re a handful, aren’t they? Little spark plugs, full of energy. Sounds like you handled it well, love. So, about this holiday...are you still leaning towards Crete? Yeah, I think so. It just feels…doable, doesn’t it? We need something relaxing, properly relaxing. No frantic sightseeing, definitely no packing lists longer than my arm. Remember that disaster in Barcelona? Don't remind me! You nearly had a nervous breakdown trying to navigate the metro system with all the luggage. Crete sounds much more your speed. Good beaches, lovely food, plenty of quiet corners. Have you looked at Elounda? I read a review about a little taverna right on the harbour, supposedly the best seafood for miles. I have, actually! It looks gorgeous, but a little pricey, maybe? I was looking at something a bit further inland, near Agios Nikolaos. A smaller place, self-catering. Less touristy. Self-catering is a brilliant idea. Gives you more freedom, doesn’t it? You can potter about, find local markets, really soak up the atmosphere. It's always better than being tied to a hotel restaurant, even if it  is  seafood. Are you looking at apartments or villas? Mostly apartments, I think. A villa feels a bit...grand. And unnecessarily cleaning. I’m not asking for the Ritz, obviously, but somewhere clean and comfortable. With a little balcony, ideally. Somewhere I can sit with a glass of something and watch the sunset. Now you’re talking. Sounds absolutely perfect. Have you checked out those websites I sent you? The one with the independent rentals? They've got some real gems. I’ve had a quick look, yeah. There’s one in Analipsi that looks promising, but the photos are a little… dodgy. It's hard to tell if it's genuinely charming or just desperately needs an update. Those photos can be misleading, can’t they? Always a risk. Don’t rely on them solely. Look at the reviews, darling. Read between the lines. Things like "friendly locals" are good signs. "Quiet location" is crucial for relaxation. And be wary of anything that mentions "quirky" too many times.

…No, seriously, it was mental. Like, eighty quid just  vanished . And the bank's just saying "unauthorised transaction" and offering me a voucher for a coffee. A coffee! I've lost eighty quid and they're offering me a  coffee ! Proper daylight robbery, innit? Eighty pounds is...considerable. You certain it wasn't a recurring payment you forgot about? Happens all the time, you know. Even to the most careful. Nah, man. I check my direct debits religiously. It's not that. It's… well, it’s flagged as some online thing. Something called “GloboMart Premium Subscription”. I’ve never heard of GloboMart. And I certainly haven't subscribed to anything premium. Sounds like some dodgy American lot, if you ask me. Right. "GloboMart." I don't recognize that name at all. Sounds… expansive, doesn’t it? Like they’re trying to swallow the whole online market. Tell me, you been clicking on any suspicious links lately? Any emails that seemed a bit off? Er… well, my mate Liam sent me a link the other day, saying it was for tickets to that Manchester United game. Real cheap. I clicked it, obviously, thought it was a good shout. But the website looked a bit… flashy. Loads of pop-ups, you know? I just assumed it was just trying to get my email address. Liam. Always Liam causing trouble, eh? He means well, I’m sure, but… caution is key in these digital arenas. It’s like the sea, son. Beautiful, full of wonder, but also hides currents you can’t see until you’re swept away. Cor, proper deep, aren’t we? Right, yeah, fair enough. Should’ve been more careful. So, what do I do now? The bank isn't being helpful. They're just going through the motions. Don’t let them wear you down. File a formal dispute. Put everything in writing. Detail the circumstances, mention the email from Liam, the dodgy website. Be assertive. Don’t let them fob you off with that coffee voucher. I dealt with something similar with the company's payroll system a few years back. Had to fight tooth and nail to get my money back. You did? That's reassuring, actually. Knowing someone's been through it and won. Still not ideal, though. It's a right pain sorting all this out. So, you following the cricket at all? They're doing alright, aren't they?

Lovely cuppa, Brenda. Proper brew. Reminds me of me Nan’s – she always made a good cuppa, she did. Never had no fancy tea bags neither. Loose leaf, always. It is good, Arthur. You know, I was thinking about that Skype call earlier. It did drop out something awful, didn’t it? Poor Simon looked right frustrated. Said his internet's been playing up all week. Aye, right pain that is. Used to be alright, but it’s got slower than a tortoise in treacle, hasn't it? Remember when we got our first one? All the fuss over it. Now it's just…well, a bit bothersome, to be honest. Makes a fella feel his age, fiddling about with all the settings. Tell me about it! Trying to help my daughter set up video conferencing for her staff last week… nearly pulled my hair out! Though, it’s remarkable, innit? Being able to see faces so clearly across thousands of miles. Reminds me of those old globes we used to have in school. Remember tracing the routes of explorers? Oh, globes! Used to have one in me bedroom, I did. All dusty, it was. Pointed at the ‘States mostly. Always wanted to go there, you know. Never did, though. All those miles...and the cost! We did go to America once, remember? That dreadful trip. The underground in New York was frightening! So crowded, and so noisy. I felt completely lost. Though I must say, that Central Park was rather lovely. That’s a good point about the underground. London's isn’t exactly a picnic either, is it? Though, I always found it quite fascinating as a child. My dad used to take me on little expeditions. Used to get on at one station and just get off at the next, just to explore the different platforms and architecture. Funny thing to enjoy, I suppose. You know what I miss? Those youth hostels. Proper adventures. Used to go with a mate, Roger, back in the… oh, must’ve been the sixties. Up to Yorkshire, we did. Hiking across the moors. Slept in barns sometimes. Proper bracing air! Yorkshire! I did a walking holiday in the Dales once. Absolutely beautiful. Though, I did twist my ankle badly. That’s why me leg’s been giving me bother lately. Keeps catching me out. You should really get that looked at, Brenda.

Right, seriously. Jellyfish the size of buses? I need something a bit lighter. Think there’s anything on Netflix we haven’t seen? Not really botherin’, love. Just tryin’ to nail down these flights. Mum’s put me on full power to sort it, innit? Wants everyone to be booked before the weekend. Says it’ll be chaos if we leave it. Chaos? Your mum's always predicting chaos. Remember the Christmas dinner debacle of '18? Don't even start! Aunt Carol and the brussel sprouts! It was mental. Anyway, look at these prices. Return flights to Leeds for next weekend…over two hundred quid?! Are you havin’ a laugh?! That  is  ridiculous. When did flying become this expensive? I remember coming up to Cambridge for uni and it was practically giving them away. I’m checking easyJet… …Okay, slightly better. Around £150 if you’re flexible with the times. Flexible? Mum wants Saturday morning departure and Sunday evening return. She’s got all these plans. Church, garden club, lunch with the neighbours… the whole shebang. Apparently, I’m supposed to be her personal travel agent now. Well, someone has to keep the Yorkshire clans happy, don’t they? You realize, flying back down here on Sunday evening is going to be a killer though, especially after a Sunday roast at your mum’s. Tell me about it! I’ll be full as a tick. Still, gotta do it for Mum. She gets proper mardy if things aren't planned to the minute. She'll be clucking about "disrespect" if I’m even five minutes late. You're a saint, seriously. I’d be booking a train and just lying in a field somewhere to escape the Sunday roast. Though, speaking of trains... have you considered it? Might be cheaper, especially if you book ahead. Yeah, I looked. Actually, it’s only about ten quid cheaper  overall  when you factor in the cost of getting to the station, lugging suitcases around, and the journey taking like, six hours! Plus, I hate those tiny train seats. My knees end up jammed against the tray table. True. The tray table situation is a tragedy. Right, let’s see… this flight with Ryanair… £130, but it departs at 6am on Saturday. Absolutely brutal. 6am?! No way! I'd be a zombie. Mum would be mortified, honestly. She’d say I was “not makin’ an effort.”

…and honestly, Sarah, I don’t know what’s happening with the petrol prices. It's just outrageous, isn’t it? Used to be able to fill the Morris for a tenner, now it's pushing twenty! Tell me about it, Dad. My commute’s getting properly painful. Though, I am trying to cycle more when I can. Keeps me vaguely fit, at least. Speaking of money, how’s your banking transition going? You mentioned you were thinking about switching? Aye well, it's a rum business, this new banking. All these online things are a bit… unnerving, you know? I keep the account simple, just for the pension mostly. Lloyds are giving me the runaround, though. Said I needed to verify identity with a selfie. A selfie! At my age! It felt a bit daft, didn't it? Oh, they do like to make things difficult, don’t they? I had similar issues with the council tax. They wanted a video of me holding my bill. Honestly! It's like they think everyone's trying to pull a fast one. Been with HSBC for years, Clive. Never had any bother. Solid as a rock, they are. That's what Margaret said. HSBC. I’ll look into it. Though, changing banks is a faff, isn't it? All those direct debits to update. It is, but the savings could be worth it. I switched last year and ended up with a slightly better interest rate. Did you hear about Mrs. Peterson's cat getting stuck in a tree again? The police were called. The police? For a cat? That’s a waste of their time, surely. They’ve got proper crimes to be dealing with, haven't they? I read somethin' the other day about rising crime in the city centre. Makes you think, doesn't it? It does. It’s all become a bit much, even in the court. Paperwork's gone digital, which is some improvement, but the delays... absolute nightmare. And the attitude of some of the young officers... well, let’s just say respect seems to be in short supply. It’s so frustrating. I read an article about how the police are stretched so thin, they're having to prioritise. A cat’s stuck up a tree probably falls low on the list. Have you been noticing the price of everything at the supermarket, Mum? It’s absolutely ridiculous.

“…and then the baboon nicked me entire scone! Right out of me hand! Honestly, I was proper gobsmacked. Never seen owt like it. Mum always said South African wildlife was cheeky, but I thought that was just a yarn, ya know?” “A baboon? Seriously? That’s brilliant! Mine were just seagulls trying to steal chips. Nothing quite as dramatic as a scone-stealing primate. Holidays are always a laugh, aren’t they? What was your favourite part of the trip then, aside from getting mugged by a monkey?” “Definitely the landscape, love. Proper lush, green. And the sunsets… absolutely incredible. But the monkey was a highlight, for sure. Gave everyone a good laugh. Right, your turn then. Best holiday memory?” “Oh, God, so many! But there’s this one time in Donegal, right? We were hiking, and there was this wee beach, hidden away. Crystal clear water, turquoise, like something you’d see in the Caribbean, only without the… you know… the tourists. And we found this field of wildflowers, bursting with colour. We just sat there, for ages, listening to the sea. It was pure magic. And my da, he bought me a stick of rock. Raspberry flavour! Best holiday ever.” “That sounds lovely, Aisling. Mine would have to be Pembrokeshire. Remember that trip we did last summer, girls? The caravan, the beach, the questionable fish and chips… good times. But honestly, just being by the sea in Wales, that’s home for me. Nothing beats it. And the wild ponies! I miss the wild ponies.” “Oh, Pembrokeshire is beautiful! I went there with me mam a few years back. Proper stunning coastline. But… best holiday? Gotta be Blackpool, innit? Don’t laugh! It's chaotic, it's loud, it’s full of cheesy arcades, but it’s brilliant. And the rock! Blackpool rock’s the best. Pineapple flavour! I buy a massive bag every time. Right, food. Favourite food, then. I’m putting it to the group – what’s your ultimate comfort food, the thing you crave when you’re feeling down?” “Oh, easy. My grandma’s parsnip cake. It’s like… a hug in cake form. Sweet, slightly spicy, and ridiculously moorish. I could eat the whole thing in one sitting, I swear.” “Ooh, that sounds delicious! Mine would have to be my mam’s shepherd’s pie. Proper hearty, loads of flavour. And potato topping browned to perfection.

Honestly, Chloe, I'm just… overwhelmed. This essay's a beast. 'The Influence of Impressionism on Early 20th Century Abstract Art' – where do you even  start ? It feels like trying to catch smoke with a sieve, innit? Tell me about it. I've got that bleedin' economics one due next week. Supply and demand... makes my brain hurt. But Impressionism? That’s lush! I love Monet's water lilies. So peaceful. You could lose yourself in 'em. Peaceful? I’m anything  but  peaceful when I’m staring at Degas’ dancers trying to figure out what postmodernist lens to view 'em through. It's all just… a lot. Makes you think, doesn’t it? About being old and reflecting on all this, and whether any of your essays will actually  matter  to anyone. You're gettin’ a bit deep for a Tuesday afternoon, aren't ya? But yeah, I get it. Sometimes I think about us being, like, seventy, and reminiscing about these days. Will we still be bickerin’ over who gets the last Hobnob? Probably! Though, hopefully, we’ll be reminiscing about travelling the world and exhibiting our art, not panicking about essay deadlines. Thinking about that makes me want to just chuck it all in and move to Italy, learn how to make pasta, and paint landscapes. See? That's the spirit! And it’s not like we  can’t  do that, is it? Eventually. Though, I reckon we need to, you know, pass our degrees first. What are you thinking of doing for your dissertation? Something Impressionist related, obviously. I’m considering focusing on Mary Cassatt. People always overlook her, don’t they? Blaming the patriarchy, I suppose. I reckon she deserves a proper look-see. What about you? Still leaning towards game design? Definitely. Professor Davies reckons I’ve got a real knack for level design. He’s even suggested I submit that little platformer I was working on for the student showcase. It's just... the art style needs a bit more polish. This is why I'm practising, see? That’s brilliant, Chloe! Seriously, that’s gorgeous. Way better than anything I can do - I draw stick figures with disproportionate limbs. You  could  totally do that, you know? Just ditch the essays and design your own video game empire. And leave you to drown in Impressionist criticism? Never! Besides, I need the qualifications, love. Gotta prove to me mum that this whole "creative" thing isn't just a phase.

Honestly, Liam just doesn’t  listen . I spent twenty minutes explaining the revised timeline for the Henderson account, and he just nodded and then asked if I’d sorted the coffee order. Coffee! Seriously? Men, eh? They’re a special breed. But twenty minutes is a  lot  of time to spend explaining something, Rach. Are you sure you weren't being a bit… layered? You know, over-explaining details he genuinely doesn't need? Layered? I was being clear! It's a critical deadline, impacting three departments. It’s not rocket science. And he’s a senior manager! Should be taking initiative. Anyway, what are you making? Smells incredible. Just a simple pasta arrabiata. Needed something comforting after a shift. It was… a day. Mrs. Davies had another meltdown about her medication, and then young Finn just wouldn't stop rocking back and forth, despite everything we tried. Oh, blimey. Sounds rough. You’re amazing, you know? Dealing with all that. I just yell at Liam about timelines. Different skillsets entirely. Is she still convinced she’s being poisoned? Pretty much. It’s the paranoia, isn't it? It's heartbreaking seeing her like that, knowing she's not well even if she can’t acknowledge it. Thinking about it makes me want a massive chunk of chocolate. Got any of that dark stuff left? Yeah, there’s a bar in the cupboard, that seriously intense 85% stuff. Prepare for a flavour explosion. Speaking of explosions, Sarah’s throwing a housewarming party next weekend. She’s badgering me to go. Oh, yeah? Where is it? The flat near the park, wasn’t it? Yep. And she's being all, "It'll be so fun! Catch up with everyone! You  have  to be there!" Like I haven’t got a million things on my plate. Plus, I'm still not entirely sure how I feel about seeing Tom. Tom? Oh. Right. Still awkward then? I thought you guys were… Were. Past tense. A very distant, blurry past tense. It ended badly. Like, really badly. And he's going. Sarah practically confirmed it. Which is just… not ideal. So, don’t go. Simple. You don’t  have  to do anything. It's her party, not yours. You need a night in with a face mask and a trashy reality show, honestly. That’s your priority. That  does  sound very appealing right now. But I feel bad saying no.

Right then. So, this consent form… honestly, it's a right faff, innit? Three pages detailing GDPR and what constitutes ‘sensitive data’ when discussing hypothetical business scenarios. Do you reckon the students will even read it, let alone understand it? It’s standard procedure, Margaret. They have to acknowledge it. Legal’s insistent on it. At least it covers us. Littlestone claims are always a worry, you know. Sensitive data, metres of coastline… it all connects somehow. I’ve drafted a short paragraph for the intro slide, just reiterating that everything’s hypothetical and anonymised. Something along the lines of "These case studies are purely illustrative and do not reflect actual individuals or companies”. How does that sound? Aye, that's decent, Caroline. Keeps us on the right side of things. I'm more worried, though, about how we’re structuring the seminar itself. We’ve got a lot to cram into just two hours, haven’t we? Going through Hofstede's cultural dimensions, non-verbal communication, email etiquette... feels a bit like throwing spaghetti at the wall. Exactly! My worry’s always been we’ll end up lecturing them rather than facilitating a discussion. Remember last year’s international marketing seminar? Half the group were asleep by the time we got to Porter’s Five Forces. We need something engaging. I was thinking we could start with a particularly disastrous email exchange - a proper howler - and then get them to dissect  why  it went wrong. Ooh, I like that, Margaret. Real-world examples are always more impactful than dry theory. I’ve got a few examples from some disastrous mergers I was involved with years ago, though I'll obviously anonymise the players. We could even present it as two separate emails and ask them to identify the cultural misunderstandings at play. From a Southern perspective, forgetting a polite formality can seem a minor indiscretion, but… But in the North East and elsewhere, it can just seem blunt, right? I reckon that’s spot on. We could follow that up with a short activity – perhaps breaking them into small groups and giving them a scenario: a British entrepreneur pitching a new product to a Japanese investor. They have to craft a brief email response, highlighting what went well and what could be improved. Now  that’s  what I’m talking about! Practical application. Much better than just reciting Hofstede. Though, we do need to touch on the theory, don’t we?

Honestly, Mark, I'm feeling utterly drained. That seminar on post-colonial literature… it was a bloodbath. Half the students seemed to think Chinua Achebe was just making things up. Rough day then, love? I thought your seminars were usually going well? You seemed quite chipper earlier. They  are  mostly, usually. But there’s this cohort, this batch of first years, who just... haven't done the reading. And when they haven’t, they get defensive. Spent a good fifteen minutes trying to explain the difference between magical realism and something they’d clearly picked up from a very unreliable online source. It’s exhausting, trying to gently steer them toward critical thinking. Right. Remember last year's group with the conspiracy theories about Shakespeare? That was something else. Still, you're good at it, you always manage to pull them back. You just have that patience. I envy it, frankly. My seminar on Victorian social reform felt like a lecture to a brick wall. Barely a peep. Oh, don’t even start about Victorian social reform. I still can’t fathom why they chose  you  to teach that. You zone out at the mention of parliamentary procedure. Hey! I gave a perfectly respectable overview of the Factory Acts. It's just… the sheer volume of detail. Honestly, I’d much rather be talking about the artistic output of the period. Give me Dickens any day over Chadwick. Exactly. Speaking of artistic output… are you any closer to finalizing the designs for the balcony? I keep picturing these rather lovely wrought iron railings, with little floral motifs. Almost there. The contractor sent over a few more options this morning. I’m leaning towards the simple, modernist style – something clean and understated. Your floral motifs are gorgeous, don't get me wrong, but I'm worried it'll clash with the overall aesthetic. We want it to feel cohesive, not like a Victorian tea room. A Victorian tea room sounds rather pleasant actually. Especially after a seminar full of arguing undergraduates. But fine, minimalism it is. As long as it  doesn’t  end up looking like a corporate office block. Remember those awful renderings we saw last week? Never. Those were truly horrific. We’re nowhere near that. I've made sure to specify good quality materials, proper lighting… Actually, I was thinking about fairy lights along the edges. Subtle, not overwhelming.

Honestly, this is lovely, Liam, but I’m still feeling a bit guilty about the amount of leftover pesto. We're throwing so much away lately. Remember Gran’s house? Nothing went to waste. Seriously, she'd pickle everything! Even slightly bruised apples ended up as chutney. Yeah, Gran was a legend. Though, I’m not sure I’d want to eat pickled apples every day. It's just... different now, isn’t it? Everything's so geared towards convenience. Ready meals, huge bags of salad you barely get through… Exactly! And the plastic bag charge hasn't seemingly done much good. People just buy more reusable bags, then leave them at the bottom of the cupboard and still get plastic ones at the supermarket. It’s ridiculous. Makes you think about the bigger picture, doesn't it? Industrialization, the relentless demand… Totally. I was reading an article the other day about urban farming initiatives. Rooftop gardens, vertical farms... Turns out, cities could feed themselves! It's pretty radical stuff, actually. Not exactly precision engineering, but there’s a lot of ingenious tech involved. Automated irrigation, nutrient recycling… See? And you, the engineer, can be part of that! You know, when I was talking to Chloe the other day at school, she's utterly lost about what to do after A-Levels. All this pressure to pick a ‘sensible’ career. I wish we could offer more practical work experience, get them out of the classroom and seeing how things  really  work. It’s tough. I had that awful placement at Harrison & Finch – you know, the aerospace company? Absolute boys' club. Nearly didn’t get a look-in. You needed connections, more than qualifications. It’s still like that in a lot of ‘closed’ industries, isn't it? Absolutely. That’s so frustrating. How can we encourage young women when they know they'll face that kind of… exclusion? It's not fair. Remember Aunt Priya’s stories about arranged marriages back in India? The whole dowry system… it feels archaic, but in some ways, careers can feel just as structured and controlled by tradition. I can’t imagine. It's a completely different culture, obviously, but the underlying theme of being steered in a certain direction… I felt a bit of that pressure to go into engineering, to be honest. Dad always wanted me to follow in his footsteps. Did you want to?

…and then Professor Davies just  looked  at me. Like I’d suggested we start sacrificing lab mice to improve the data. Honestly, you’d think after three years of meticulously gathering this information, they'd be a bit more receptive to suggesting a longitudinal study. Right, Davies. That man’s got a face like a smacked cod. Honestly, institutional inertia is the biggest obstacle to progress, isn’t it? I’m dealing with something similar at work. We're trying to introduce a new assessment framework, and half the headteachers are acting like I'm proposing we teach children to knit using barbed wire. Barbed wire knitting. That's brilliant. They just don't want to change, do they? It's a lot easier to stick with what they know, even if it’s demonstrably flawed. It just makes you want to shout sometimes, doesn’t it? It does! Especially when you've done the groundwork, presented the evidence, and they're still clinging to these outdated methods. It's exhausting. Are the kids at least benefiting from your work, though? That’s what I focus on. Knowing I'm helping those little ones, even in a small way, keeps me going. Yes, the initial results are… promising. We’re seeing a definite correlation between mindful breathing exercises and reduced anxiety in teenagers experiencing exam stress. But convincing the board that allocating further funding for a proper, large-scale trial is like pulling teeth. Apparently, “longitudinal” is a dirty word around there. They want instant gratification, you know? Quick wins. That’s the problem with research, innit? It takes time. People want results now. Speaking of time, should we put the rice on? I’m starving. Did you hear back from your mum about Christmas? Not yet. I texted her this morning. She hasn't been answering her phone either. I'm starting to worry slightly. It's just… unusual for her to be so out of touch. You know how she gets. She's probably just being stubborn and listening to Jeremy's advice to ‘stay off the smartphone and enjoy the fresh air.’ Though, knowing your dad, that probably means he's dragged her off on some obscure woodland walk. Probably. But still… I just wish I knew she was alright. Work's been such a whirlwind lately, I haven't been much of a comfort to her, have I?

…and then young Timmy, bless 'is 'eart, 'e tried to build a sandcastle bigger’n the one down at Gorleston. Just…collapsed, it did. Right in 'is face, it did. Covered 'im in wet sand, poor little fella. Made me laugh, though. A good, proper laugh. Haven’t had one of them in a while, you see. Oh, Arthur. That sounds lovely, really. A good laugh is medicine, isn't it? You really needed that. It's good you were there to see it. My Richard, he never could build a sandcastle. Not a patch on our grandson, Leo. He's a prodigy, that boy. Builds fortresses, he does. Remember that trip to Bournemouth? He built one with actual moats. Bournemouth's pricey, isn't it? Going away. We tend to stick to the West Midlands for our holidays. A caravan in Shropshire, usually. Cheaper, you know. Though, frankly, Arthur, you deserve a proper break. Something a bit… uplifting. You’ve been a bit down, haven’t you? Down's a good word for it, Mark. Down’s about right. The missus… well, she’s gone now, you know. Ten years this October. And the house… it’s just… too much, innit? Too big for one old bloke. All these rooms, echoing. Makes you feel your age, it does. Oh, Arthur. I know. Grief is a constant companion sometimes, isn't it? And a big house… it’s a burden more than a comfort when you’re on your own. Have you thought seriously about downsizing? There's that little bungalow over in New Costessey… the one with the garden? Mrs. Peterson said it was going for a decent price. That's a sensible suggestion, Sarah. Moving might be exactly what he needs. Less upkeep, less… emptiness. Financial implications, of course. How are things with the benefits, Arthur? Are you managing alright? About the same. Just about scrape by, really. Bills are a killer. And the council tax… don't even get me started on the council tax. I did try volunteering at the RSPB, you know. Down at Titchwell Marsh. Lovely place. Saw a pair of baby blue tits the other day. So small, they were. Snug in their nest. Brought a bit of… peace, I suppose. Volunteering is wonderful, Arthur. It gets you out, gives you purpose. You should definitely keep that up. Those little blue tits sound just delightful.

Honestly, it’s just… exhausting sometimes, isn’t it? Keeping up. Not that I  want  to, you know? It’s just… the pressure feels real. Especially seeing everyone’s perfect faces all over Instagram. Tell me about it! It’s madness. I was looking at Chloe's holiday pictures the other day - filter overload. She claimed she woke up looking like that. As if! I mean, she’s lovely, don't get me wrong, but the amount of contouring… I just wouldn’t have the patience. And the money! Exactly! The money! This new serum, the 'Radiance Bloom' one I was telling you about, cost me a small fortune. Fifty quid! Fifty quid for a bottle of goo that  might  make my skin look a little less tired. Fifty quid! Oh, bless you. I’m firmly in the Superdrug bargain bin camp, I am. I’ve been using this Rimmel lash mascara for ages, the one with the skinny brush. It’s like, six pounds and does the job brilliantly. No need for fancy stuff. But, Radiance Bloom… you reckon it’s  good  then? My skin’s been looking a bit dull lately. I wouldn’t say miraculous, but... Honestly, I've noticed a difference. It’s subtle, mind you. My skin feels… plumper, somehow? And the redness around my nose has definitely calmed down. It’s really hydrating. I think it’s the hyaluronic acid in it. Remember Mrs. Peterson at sixth form, always going on about hyaluronic acid? Seemed like a load of old rubbish then. Oh, Mrs. Peterson! Always with the science lessons about skincare. She used to look like she’d been drawn with a crayon, though. Not the best advert, was she? So, hydrating, you say? That might be good. My nails are always dry, even with cuticle oil. Nails are a nightmare, aren't they? I’ve been trying this OPI gel polish at home. It’s a bit fiddly to apply, let me tell you, I’ve ruined a few sets already. But when it works, it lasts ages. No chipping for weeks. It's a gamechanger, really. Though, afterwards, it feels like my nails are paper-thin. Ooh, gel polish at home! You're brave. I attempted it once and ended up looking like I’d wrestled a glitter bomb. The fumes were awful too. I just stick to regular polish, with a good top coat.

Proper scally, innit? Some people just don’t want to learn, do they? You’d think after fifteen years of using comparisons, they'd get the hang of it. So, how’s the Ms. Higgins incident affecting your blood pressure? You look a bit ropey. It’s not just Mrs. Higgins, Liam. It’s been a week of absolute chaos at work. Three referrals in, dealing with a safeguarding case all day yesterday… It takes it out of you, you know? Especially when you're constantly facing situations you wish you could change but can’t. And then trying to write reports on top of it all... Right, right. Proper grim. Social work, eh? Never been a job for the faint of heart. I mean, teaching teenagers is stressful enough, but at least I’m not dealing with… well, whatever you’re dealing with. Did you ever manage to find a parking space near the office today? It’s a nightmare. Don't even ask. Circled for twenty minutes! Ended up three streets away, cost me a fortune. Seriously thinking about taking the bus, even though it’s slower. Gotta save some pennies, anyway. Speaking of… how’s the Masters application going? Did you hear back about that interview? Aye, got the email! Interview next Tuesday. I'm proper buzzing, but simultaneously terrified, to be honest. The stuff they want me to talk about… Discourse analysis? Linguistics and second language acquisition? Sound like gobbledegook sometimes. I’m just hoping I don’t blank out and start rambling about the Beatles. You’ll be brilliant, mate. Honestly. You know your stuff, and you’re a natural teacher. Just remember what we talked about – focus on the practical application, how it’ll benefit your students. They’re not interested in jargon. And relax! Easier said than done, I know. Yeah, you're right. Still, it's a big thing, innit? This Masters... potentially changing direction a bit... Just thinking about the bills, though. Postgraduate funding can be a right minefield. Tell me about it. I’m raiding my savings to cover the application fees. This wedding next summer is eating into everything. My mum’s already going on about the seating plan - like I don't have bigger things to worry about! Your mum. Classic. Fancy her trying to organise seating for the likes of you two! So, have you sorted the venue, then?

…and honestly, Sarah, I don’t know what to do. Liam’s dad, Mark, is just… dismissive. Completely dismissive of my feelings about Elsie’s behaviour. He just says ‘kids will be kids’ whenever I bring it up. But she’s deliberately pushing boundaries, you know? Refusing to eat anything green, drawing on the walls, ignoring everything I say… It’s relentless. Oh, love. Been there. Remember when little Finn was refusing to wear shoes? He’d just fling them across the room. Drove me absolutely bonkers. But with Mark… he doesn’t seem to  see  it, does he? Just a bit of toddler mischief to him. Exactly! He’ll say, “She’s just testing you, love. She’s just being a typical three-year-old." But it’s more than that. It feels like he's undermining me, deliberately. Like he’s saying my methods aren’t good enough, without actually  saying  that. And Liam, bless him, gets caught in the middle, trying to be fair to both of us. It's a really tricky one, isn't it? Especially with step parenting. It's never going to be as straightforward as parenting your own. I’ve got a bit of experience with that, you know, with Finn and Daniel’s dad. It's like, you’re trying to build a new routine, a new dynamic, and he’s still stuck in the old way of doing things, or just… absent really. Absent, mentally, you mean? Because that’s how it feels. It's like, he’s got this image in his head of what Elsie  should  be, and when she’s not, he just glosses over it. He remembers her as this sweet, obedient little girl, and now she’s… well, she’s three. They change! They do. They absolutely do. And trying to force them back into that old image? That’s just setting everyone up for heartbreak. Look, you’re doing a good job, honestly you are. Liam’s got a good head on his shoulders, he can see that. Don’t let Mark’s comments get you down. Easier said than done, I know. It’s just… I want her to respect me, you know? I need her to understand that I'm not just a fun auntie figure. I'm part of her life, and I need to be taken seriously. I'm not trying to replace her mum, not at all.

…and honestly, Daniel, I’m  still  fuming about that baking show. The technical challenge was ridiculous! How are you supposed to make a perfectly symmetrical choux pastry swan with a blindfold on? It's just designed to fail, innit? Come on, Chloe, that's the point. It's supposed to be stressful! Creates drama. Besides, Ms. Prue Leith seemed quite pleased with Brenda’s effort. Admittedly, it  did  look a little… wonky. Wonky is an understatement! It looked like a pigeon had attacked it. And the judging! They were giving Nathan grief for a slightly uneven glaze.
