A  slightly  uneven glaze! Honestly, I could've done better and I'm about as good at baking as a badger. You say that, but you were obsessing over that lemon drizzle cake recipe you found on Pinterest last week. Remember? Pins everywhere, flour dust clinging to everything... That's different! That was for practice. Proper, controlled practice. This was… chaos. Anyway, did you hear from Liam and Sarah? They’re still trying to sort out their holiday. They said somewhere in Greece, but it’s proving tricky with the flight prices. Nah, haven't spoken to them since yesterday, when they were ranting about the same thing. Greece is a popular choice this year, clearly. They sounded pretty stressed. Speaking of things being tricky, my supervisor’s being particularly demanding this week. Wants another draft of the literature review. I’m starting to dream in footnotes. Aye, tell me about it! Research management is a constant tightrope walk. It’s not all analysing data and thinking deep thoughts, you know. Half of it's wrangling academics and chasing up paperwork. Speaking of paperwork... have you remembered about Auntie Maureen's birthday? It's next week, isn't it? Blast! I knew I’d forgotten something. I was so busy trying to decipher Foucault… it completely slipped my mind. What did she say she wanted this year? Last time it was that ridiculous ceramic squirrel. She loves those things! She's got a whole collection. I was thinking maybe a nice hamper? Like, with fancy cheeses and olives and all that posh stuff. She deserves a treat. Actually, I saw a really lovely one online – on Pinterest, obviously – with artisan crackers and fig jam... it was like £60 though. Sixty quid? Ouch. We could split it, then? I don’t mind contributing. Besides, I owe you for rescuing me from that disastrous curry night last month.

Right, so this one’s… interesting. It’s a brass Art Deco fitting, apparently. Says "genuine," naturally. You think "genuine" on eBay means anything anymore? It’s probably been polished within an inch of its life. Let me see. Hmm, yes, a bit much, isn't it? Looks like they’ve tried to make it look older than it is. And the price... £85? For something you could probably find in a charity shop for a tenner. Still, the style  is  nice. It would go well in the dining room, wouldn’t it? Less… cold than that modern thing we have now. Definitely less chilly. The current one feels like it belongs in a doctor’s surgery. But eighty-five quid is a hefty chunk for a light fitting, even a vaguely Art Deco one. Let's keep looking. We’ve barely scratched the surface. Besides, we need to sort out the kitchen lights too, remember? Right you are. Kitchen. That’s a different beast altogether. We need something tougher, less…fussy. Something that can handle a bit of condensation and the occasional splash of pasta water. Exactly. Practicality over aesthetics in the kitchen, I reckon. Though, ideally, practical and aesthetically pleasing. Is that too much to ask? Right, Rightmove… let’s see what else is lurking out there. I was having a quick look earlier, and there was a place in Henley... Henley? Oh, you know I'm wary of Henley. It's beautiful, yes, but the prices... astronomical. Remember that one we looked at last year? Three bedrooms, postage stamp garden, and a mortgage that would rival a small nation’s debt. I know, I know. Just thought I’d have a peek. This one's in Marlow, then. Slightly cheaper. Four bedrooms, garden's a decent size, and… They've got a conservatory! A conservatory? Really? Oh, wow. That  is  a nice conservatory. Flooding with light, it says. Not one of those squashed-in, plastic affairs, either. This looks proper. It does! It’s just… the pictures are a little… staged, aren’t they? Everything’s perfectly arranged. Notice how there's not a single dust bunny in sight. And the kitchen’s got that ridiculously glossy, grey-on-grey aesthetic. Absolutely. Homes are always staged to look perfect. It’s the marketing, isn’t it? Trying to project this immaculate lifestyle. Still, the layout looks good.

Tell me about it. Doreen's been complaining about her knees again. Says they're worse than ever. Had to practically carry her to the loo this morning. It’s like having a grumpy old oak tree attached to you, some days. Honestly, the lack of respect… you’re doing a job that's physically demanding, and they treat you like you’re invisible. Exactly! It’s the gratitude, isn't it? Sometimes, a simple ‘thank you’ would make all the difference. I mean, I don’t do it for the praise, mind, but it’s… demoralising. Have you heard anything back from those agencies you applied to, Sarah? Not a sausage. Sent out applications to about ten, and just radio silence. It's disheartening, isn't it? You think, ‘right, I’m putting myself out there,’ and then nothing. It's always said there's a shortage, but they certainly don’t seem to be rushing to hire. Hey! Sorry I’m late, had to finish feeding Pipkin. Isn't he just adorable? Found him abandoned near the shops yesterday, poor little thing. I've named him Pipkin. Oh, he  is  lovely! What a sweetie. You've got a good heart, Chloe. Bringing him in like that. Are you thinking of keeping him? I think so. Mum says we’ve got enough animals already, but… look at him! He needs someone. Besides, Mrs. Peterson's been saying she doesn't mind having a cat. It gives her something to look forward to. Speaking of jobs, I've been thinking about trying somewhere a bit different… somewhere with fewer… incidents, you know? Like no mashed banana walls, eh? Bless you. It's tough, isn't it? This job... it's rewarding, sometimes, really is. Seeing them smile, knowing you've made a difference… but on days like today… Absolutely. I'm thinking about retraining, actually. Maybe occupational therapy. Something that feels a bit more… impactful, a bit less reactive. It's a big commitment, mind. Sixth form was a long time ago. And the fees! It’s not like they just hand these things out. Occupational therapy? That sounds lovely, Jo. You’d be brilliant at it. You’ve got such a calm head. Better than me, that’s for sure. I’d be shouting instructions at them! You’d be amazing, Auntie Jo! I reckon you’d make a really good therapist.

…and honestly, the bit about blue light suppression being even  more  crucial than they originally thought? Incredible. I mean, I’ve been religiously using those glasses, but apparently, even with them, the wavelengths seep through a bit. They’re suggesting a complete digital detox for at least two hours before bed now. Two hours! Can you imagine? Two hours? That's a bit extreme, isn't it? I find a spot of chamomile tea does the trick. Though, I do admit, doom-scrolling on Twitter before bed is becoming a terrible habit. Did you see that article about the sleep study in Scandinavia? Apparently, they correlated the lack of daylight hours in winter with increased cases of insomnia. Yeah, I glanced at it. It reinforced what I suspected – light is the master regulator. It’s all connected, isn't it? Which reminds me, we  absolutely  need to book that camping trip. Somewhere with genuinely dark skies. Not just ‘dark’ in the sense that the streetlights aren't glaring; properly dark. Somewhere you can see the Milky Way. Oh, I’d love that. Somewhere a bit…remote, though. Remember that disastrous attempt at "glamping" in Cornwall last year? The field was practically attached to the A30. Didn't feel particularly natural. Don't remind me. That wasn't relaxing, that was stressful. I spent half the night listening to lorries thundering past. We need a proper escape. I was looking at some sites in the Peak District. Think somewhere near Castleton, maybe. The Peak District would be lovely. Though I’m terrible at navigating. Remember that time we went to Edinburgh? I swear, I got us lost  twice  in a single afternoon. It's just... cities are a labyrinth to me. I need a really clear route marked on a map – and even then, I'll probably take a wrong turning. You're much better at that sort of thing. Do you remember that app you used to find the best route into York? Citymapper, yeah. Brilliant. It knows all the backstreets and shortcuts. It’s the closest I get to having a built-in GPS. Speaking of navigating, I was listening to a podcast the other day – a pilot talking about instrument flying. Absolutely fascinating. Oh really? What about it? Apparently, it's a completely different skill to visual flying. These pilots rely entirely on instruments – altitude, speed, heading – even in zero visibility.

"Aye, reyt! A sausage hamster. Could you imagine? Is he a ginger, then, yer little fella?" "He is, actually. Lovely little ginger. His name’s Marmalade. Bit ironic, really, considering he spends most of his time hoarding sunflower seeds. It's quite comical, observing him. He’s got a specific routine. He'll stuff his cheeks, pause to look around suspiciously, as if he thinks someone’s going to steal his hoard, then bury it. And then he'll seemingly forget where he buried it!" "Ha! Like me grandad with his keys! Always lookin' for 'em, even when they're hanging round his neck. Marmalade, eh? That's a good name. You know, I fancy ginger cats. They’ve just got that…look. Proper mischievous, ya know?" "I agree about the cats. Ginger lads are always getting into trouble. But Marmalade sounds lovely. Do you let him wander about? My mum’s got a Syrian and she keeps him in a big enclosure, cos she’s terrified he’ll chew the furniture. Not that he ever has, mind." “Our hamster, Nibbles, was a right terror. He escaped once and ended up in the airing cupboard. Mum went in later and found him surrounded by towels, lookin' like a proper little king. She nearly had a heart attack! Wasn’t ginger though, he was grey. A proper scruffbag, that one.” “Marmalade’s got a wheel, a hidey-house, and plenty of toys. He’s got a little wooden bridge he likes to climb. I'm trying to make sure the cage is enriching, you know? Research shows it’s vital for their mental wellbeing. I even read that they prefer shredded paper to cedar bedding, because it feels more natural to them.” "Proper dedicated you are! Me and Chloe just bought the cheap-as-possible cage from Home Bargains. Gets the job done, though. Still, sounds like you're treatin' him right. Are you worried about his teeth getting too long?" "Oh, yeah! The teeth thing. My mum has to take her hamster to the vet to have them clipped sometimes. It's a bit pricey. Do you trim Marmalade’s nails too?" “Nah, Nibbles’ nails never bothered us. He sharpened ‘em on the bars of the cage, the cheeky beggar. You gotta watch them though, don’t you? Don't wanna be givin’ 'em a right sore foot.” “I’m trying to avoid nail clipping if possible.

Right, so, Genghis Khan is  still  dominating Europe. It's ridiculous. Seriously, Dad, you're just obliterating everyone. Well, what can I say, lad? Got a knack for it, haven't I? Liverpool lads are strategic, you know. Always have been. Strategic and... persistent. Just like the docks. Persistent is one word for it. Ruthless is another, Derek. Honestly, are you even letting anyone breathe? I’m stuck in South America with barely a handful of troops. Feel like I'm dealing with a chocolate shortage! It  is  a bit unfair, isn't it? You barely had a chance to build up, Mum. And you’re supposed to be the learning and development person. Shouldn’t you be  teaching  us better strategies? Oh, don’t you start. This is  fun , isn't it? Besides, you're not exactly brilliant at beating him, are you, James? Remember last Christmas? He took Africa off you in five minutes! That was  different . I was distracted. I’d just realised Aunt Susan was using the wrong pronunciation of 'Bologna' again. Honestly, it's Bologna, Mum. Not Bol-on-yah! Women and their pronunciation! Can't get anything right. Anyway, back to conquering the world. Where were we? I’m thinking a push into Australia… need more troops there. James, you got reinforcements coming, right? What version of Risk are we even playing? It feels like an update has happened and we missed the memo about continent value. It’s the standard one, Dad. Look, I need to record some instructions for my students later, so I can’t spend all day trying to reclaim Europe. And my glasses are slightly crooked and I can’t see the board properly. Everything smells faintly of Mum’s lavender potpourri, which is lovely, but not conducive to strategic thinking. Everything  always  smells of lavender in here, James. You’ll get used to it! Honestly, I remember when you were little... didn't believe in luck at all, you did. Thought everything was down to logic. Aye, he did. Thought he'd calculated the odds of life. Funny thing about life, though… it’s never on the map. You can plan all you want, but sometimes, the dice roll differently. Like with Aaron. Right. Don't, Dad. Don't go there. We all miss him, okay? Let’s just… play the game. He would have loved this game, you know.

Honestly, Liv, I’m just… a mess. Archaeology isn't what I thought it'd be. All lectures and essays and… well, not much actual digging, is it? Back in Falmouth, even just beachcombing felt more exciting, yeah? A mess? Come on, Daisy. You’re always being Ms. Dramatic. It's only the second semester. Archaeology  is  mostly bookwork at uni. You knew that going in, didn’t you? You love the historical side, don’t you? Remember that massive thing you went on about Roman mosaics? Yeah, but… I thought I’d be brushing dirt off pottery shards, you know? Not writing essays about the socio-political ramifications of a broken goblet. It feels so… disconnected. And everyone else seems to have it figured out. Amelia's practically got a job lined up at the British Museum. Amelia’s just good at networking, innit? Don't compare yourself to her. Honestly, the competition for those things is mad. So, what's Plan B then? You gonna chuck it all in and join a circus? Don’t be daft. But I'm worried I’ve chosen the wrong thing. What if I’m completely useless outside of, like, knowing a lot about Bronze Age burial rituals? It doesn’t exactly scream ‘employable,’ does it? What about you? Still loving law? You seem pretty settled. Law's alright. Plenty of deadlines, lots of reading, just like everything else, yeah? But I enjoy it, I reckon. It’s just… sometimes I look at people like, oh, I don't know, Florence Pugh - she's smashing it, isn't she? Proper Northern lass, doing amazing things in Hollywood. Makes you think, doesn’t it? What if I peaked at sixteen and winning the school debating competition? You peaked at debating? Liv, you're brilliant at arguing! You could charm the socks off a judge! Honestly, I think you’d make a brilliant barrister. Fierce and quick-witted. Easy for you to say, you can just bury yourself in the past. Less pressure to, like,  do  something in the future, you know? Speaking of the future... did you see Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce are reportedly getting serious? Honestly, it’s mad. I'm not even a massive Swiftie, but it’s just... a vibe. A vibe is right! It’s proper fairytale stuff, isn’t it? Though, I am getting slightly concerned about the amount of kids celebrities seem to be having lately.

…and then Mr. Davies was going on about the ethics of CRISPR, like we’re supposed to be deciding whether it’s right to edit genes! It's mental, innit? I mean, I get the potential, curing diseases and all that, but the whole thing feels… slippery. Yeah, it’s a bit much for a Tuesday afternoon, isn't it? He massively overstates our understanding. Like, he was talking about designer babies and stuff. Seriously? Ms. Patel kept having to correct him, saying the technology isn’t  there  yet. Exactly! And then he was linking it to, like, consumerism. Said corporations would just use it to create ‘better’ products, people who buy into it, you know? Like, a 'superior' athlete, or something. Ridiculous. Man. You know Liam's dad lost his job last week? At the Amazon warehouse. Said they're automating more and more, don't need as many people. Made him proper down. Yeah, I heard. That’s rough. My mum said something about Universal Basic Income being a potential solution, but my dad just rolled his eyes. Said it’s “handouts” and encourages laziness. Typical. My nan always says the same thing. She grew up in, like, really hard times, you know? Rationing and everything. She can’t get her head around the idea that people can struggle even now. Says it's just because people aren’t working hard enough. Easy for her to say, living in her little bungalow. It's like, the system is rigged, isn't it? Like, some people get born with a silver spoon, and others… well, Liam's dad is going to have a hard time finding another job paying the same. Especially with the cost of everything going up. Did you see petrol prices? Don’t even. I’m saving up for that new Spider-Man comic, 'Beyond,' but at this rate, comics are going to be a luxury. Speaking of, have you finished the background research for our history project? The one on the suffragettes? Almost. I'm stuck on the economic impact of their campaigns. It's more complicated than just women getting the vote, apparently. Loads of articles talking about how it boosted the economy slightly, freed up men to go to war, all sorts. Yeah, it’s a maze. I was reading about how the Women's Social and Political Union used newspaper advertising. Pretty clever way to get their message out.

…and honestly, the whole thing was just a mess. I started recording a voiceover for this online course, you know? “Introduction to Crochet for Beginners.” Sounds simple, right? But the microphone kept picking up every little creak in the house. The cat walking across the roof, the neighbour's dog barking… it was a nightmare. I spent three hours trying to get a decent thirty seconds. Oh, darling, technology. It’s supposed to make life easier, isn’t it? But it just adds another layer of frustration. I remember trying to edit a video last autumn – a little slideshow of the garden for my sister. Ended up throwing the laptop out of the window almost. Almost! Did you manage to salvage anything, though? I think so. I patched a few bits together, used some noise reduction software, but it still sounds a little… wonky. I’m not sure anyone will take me seriously as a crochet instructor. Mrs. Higgins next door actually popped her head over while I was recording. Said, “Sounds like a badger wrestling in there, love!” I wanted to disappear. Oh, Mrs. Higgins! Always a character. Well, at least she was honest. She’s got a good eye for a bit of chaos, that one. Tell you what, though, it’s good you’re trying new things. Trying to use your skills. I was feeling a bit down myself, after my physiotherapy appointment. Really? What happened? Just the usual. My knees, you know. They’re having a particularly grumpy day. She poked and prodded and told me I need to do  more  exercises. "Strengthen your quads,” she said. As if I haven’t been strengthening my quads for the last five years! And my shoulders are getting worse. This damp weather just seems to seep into my bones. I swear, I'm eighty years old, not sixty-two. I know how you feel about the damp. My joints always ache when it rains. Do you think it’s just the weather, or… you know? It’s a combination, I think. Age, a bit of wear and tear, maybe a touch of arthritis. Honestly, I've no idea. I’d love to lose a few pounds, that would definitely help. I've been looking at those keto diets again, but they seem so restrictive. All meat and vegetables – where’s the joy in that? I tried that for a bit.

…Honestly, it’s just the sheer weight of responsibility. They gave me this project, the ‘Phoenix’ rollout, and it's basically make-or-break for the whole department. If it fails, heads will roll. I’m checking figures three times, quadruple checking spreadsheets…it's exhausting. Aye, I get that, lass. Pressure’s a right beast, eh? Though mine's more like "don't mess up the floral arrangements" kind of pressure. Still a lot of folks relying on me, I suppose. Conference season’s been brutal this year. Last week, we had Mrs. Abernathy insisting on white lilies  only  for the gala. White lilies! In October! Like, what’s she thinkin’? Mrs. Abernathy sounds…demanding. At least you’re dealing with flowers. I’m dealing with complex supply chains and potential delays that could cost the company millions. No room for ‘white lilies only’ in  this  world. Millions, eh? That's a different league altogether! I had a bloke on Monday threaten to call the council because the chair covers weren’t  quite  the right shade of beige. Beige! Seriously, summat's gone wrong wi' folk. Back home, in Doncaster, if you had a problem, you’d just have a good moan over a pint, job done. Cambridge is just…intense. You’re not wrong. There's a weird competitiveness here, even amongst friends. Like everyone's constantly trying to one-up each other. It can be draining. Are you still finding it hard to adjust to the whole Cambridge vibe, then? A bit, yeah. I mean, I love Anon, obviously. And the jobs are good, but…it’s just a different pace of life. Everyone’s so… polished. I'm still gettin' odd looks when I use my accent. The other day, I asked for a ‘packet’ of crisps and this posh bloke looked at me like I was speakin' Martian. Oh, bless him. You've got a lovely accent, Chloe. Really. It’s refreshing. So much of London is just…generic. Everyone sounds the same. Have you managed to sort out that issue with the pianist for the Christmas do? Aye, eventually. Turns out the first one was a complete nightmare. Apparently, he thought 'Silent Night' was a challenge to improvise a polka. A polka! I nearly choked on me tea. Rest assured, the second one’s a proper classical musician. Though he’s terrified of pigeons, which is a slight problem, considering the venue.

Right? I get what they were  going  for, the whole 'kindness is the answer' thing, but it felt so forced after everything. It needed a bit more breathing space, didn't it? It was just  bam, bam, bam  emotion, non-stop. Did anyone else find it a little exhausting? Nah, I loved it! I thought it really nailed it. It felt like reflecting the chaos of life, yeah? Like, you're being bombarded with everything all the time, and sometimes, you just need a moment of profound… gentleness. And the bagel thing? Genius. Seriously, the bagel. I was with Chloe on this one, to be fair. I mean, it  was  a lot, but that's the whole point, isn't it? It visualises that feeling of being overwhelmed, and then pulls you out of it with that little bit of connection. Reminded me a bit of  Sing Street , actually, the way it uses vibrant visuals to tell a really heartfelt story. Oh,  Sing Street  is brilliant! Proper feel-good film. But going back to  EEAAO , I thought Michelle Yeoh was incredible. Like, the  acting ! She carried the whole thing. Even when the plot was going a bit bonkers, you were still invested because of her. Did you see her in  Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon ? Oh yeah! My Nan loves that one. I’ve not seen  Everything Everywhere , though. Is it… is it scary? I get easily freaked out. It’s not  scary  exactly, Evie. It's… weird. Very, very weird and visually intense. Lots of strange things happening. Though, honestly, some of the hot dog fingers were pretty unsettling. Hot dog fingers were the best bit! Don’t @ me. I thought the sheer creativity of it all was astounding. Like, who comes up with that stuff? And the fight choreography! Michelle Yeoh’s in her element. I saw it on the big screen and it was just… wow. Actually, talking about fight choreography, has everyone seen  John Wick ?  John Wick  is brilliant. So stylish. Keanu Reeves really proved he can still kick ass. My wee cousin is obsessed. He's trying to learn all the moves. Nearly broke his arm trying to do a pivot. I'm more of a  Kill Bill  girl myself. That soundtrack alone...and Uma Thurman absolutely  owned  that role. Pure, unapologetic badassery. I always preferred Tarantino's  Pulp Fiction . That film changed everything. The non-linear storytelling, the dialogue...it’s just iconic.

Honestly, Mum, Paris was  exhausting . Like, properly exhausting. Beautiful, yes, absolutely stunning, but… oh my god. Well, you said you were walking miles every day, didn't you? All those cobbled streets aren't kind to ankles, are they? You look a bit peaky, love. Did you eat properly? Properly? I ate croissants, Mum. Giant, flaky croissants. And macarons. And that amazing steak frites. But it was all so… frantic. Trying to see everything, queueing for everything. My feet are killing me, honestly. And my back! I think I pulled something on the Metro trying to heave that suitcase up the stairs. It’s just a little twinge, but still. Paris? Sounds intense. You look like you've wrestled a badger. What happened to the glamorous Parisian weekend you were envisioning? That’s what I keep saying! It was less 'Emily in Paris' and more 'Emily desperately trying not to fall into the Seine.' Seriously, Sarah, we spent two hours in that queue for the Louvre. Two hours! I could have painted the Mona Lisa myself in that time. Now, now, don't exaggerate. Two hours isn't  that  long. And you likely saw some wonderful things. Did you see the Eiffel Tower, then? Of course we saw the Eiffel Tower! We saw it from every single possible vantage point. That’s part of the problem! Constant sightseeing. My friend Chloe - you remember Chloe from sixth form – she said she went last summer, and she just spent the whole time sitting in cafes, reading. Sounds blissful, doesn't it? Blissful indeed. I need blissful right now. Shift was chaotic. Young man, wouldn’t talk, wouldn't eat, just staring at the wall. Took two hours of just… being present, you know? Just sitting with him. It's draining, but it's rewarding when you see a flicker of something. Oh, you’re a good girl, Sarah. You always were. Always helping others. Now, are you two hungry? I’ve made a cottage pie. Proper, warming comfort food. Keeps you going. Oh, Mum, that smells amazing! That’s exactly what I need. Maybe a huge dollop of mash on top? My ankles deserve it. Cottage pie sounds perfect. Thanks, Mrs. Davies. You're a lifesaver. So, Parisian mishaps aside, how was Chloe? Still dating that architect, is she? Ugh, Mark? Still obsessed with her, apparently. He follows her around Paris taking pictures of her looking thoughtfully at fountains.

…and honestly, the referencing system they’re using this year is a nightmare. It's not consistent  at all . I spent half an hour last night wrestling with a student's bibliography. It’s like they've just mashed up APA and MLA and hoped for the best. Oh, tell me about it! Retail's got its own version of that, you know? Different stores, different procedures, even within the same chain. It makes you want to scream sometimes. I'm Sarah, by the way. We haven’t properly introduced ourselves, have we? I'm a supervisor at that Boots near the Forum. Liam. Nice to meet you, Sarah. Yes, definitely. It feels like a constant battle against bureaucracy. And this British National Corpus stuff...fascinating, theoretically, but explaining it to first years who just want to know the rules of grammar is…challenging. Especially when they keep asking about passives! Passives! Don’t even get me started. They just seem to baffle everyone. It’s like their brains short circuit. Is it a Sussex thing, do you think? All this intellectual activity making their brains overheat? Possibly! I'm from Bedford originally, you know. A lot quieter. This Sussex vibe is…intense. I need a proper lie-down after a weekend of marking essays. Did you do anything fun? Croydon girl here. Monotonously familiar. Family stuff - my little brother’s obsessed with fireworks this year, apparently. It's going to be a deluge of sparklers and bangs in November. Mum’s dragging us all to Chichester next weekend, though. Apparently, there's a touring production of  Wicked  she’s desperate to see. I’m not totally sold, to be honest. Chichester’s lovely, if a bit…posh. Wicked is brilliant though! I saw it a few years ago in London. Speaking of London, have you been keeping up with Judge Judy? It’s my guilty pleasure. Oh my god, YES! Total brain candy. Escape from the realities of supervising teenagers trying to get away with overpriced moisturiser. Actually, supervising is bringing up some old feelings. My cousin just went through a divorce. Messy stuff. That’s rough. People are so complicated. I'm still single myself, by the way. Trying to navigate the dating scene after my undergrad degree. It's pretty grim. What about you? Found ‘the one’ yet? Nearly. My boyfriend, Mark, he keeps hinting… he’s got a serious proposal planned, apparently.

…and honestly, the smell was just…wrong. You know? Not like ‘needs using quickly’ wrong, but like ‘don’t even  think  about it’ wrong. It was that mince, last week. Gave me the creeps. Right, creepy meat. Got it. So, about this rice… you said it’s, like, a science? Because it's always either cement or mush with me. A science, no. But a bit of attention to detail helps. See, you’ve got to get the water ratio right. I always use about twice as much water as rice. That's a good starting point. And rinse the rice first! Really rinse it. Gets rid of all that dusty stuff. Dust? Seriously? It looks like perfectly good grains to me. It's not dust, love, it's just… excess starch. Makes it gluey. Right, pop it in the pot - that’s a big enough one, yeah? Now, bring it to a rolling boil. Proper vigorous boil, not just a gentle simmer. Rolling boil… Okay. Right, it’s boiling already. So then what? Do I just… leave it? Don’t leave it completely unattended! But you do turn the heat right down, as low as it’ll go, once it’s boiling. Cover it with a lid and let it steam for about 15 minutes. Don’t lift the lid during that time, promise? It releases all the steam and messes with the cooking process. Fifteen minutes. No peeking. Got it. So while that’s doing its thing… we should probably get the curry going. We got those vouchers for that Indian place, remember? The Golden Mahal? Oh, yes! The vouchers! Such a lifesaver. I was dreading cooking tonight, honestly. My shoulders were aching. But sixteen quid for a main course and a drink… can’t argue with that. Maybe we'll use them next week though; little Finn's teething and he's just being a nightmare with spicy food. Everything needs to be bland bland bland. Right, bland. Less exciting. Still, those poppadums are good. Remember that time we went there and I ordered the Vindaloo and nearly cried? Oh, you did! You were bright red and sweating. Honestly, you should stick to the Korma. And be careful with the jalapenos, alright? You’ve got that sensitive nose thing, remember? I worry about you sometimes with your… you know… My what? Nothing, love. Just... just try not to overdo the spice.

, sits slumped on the sofa, scrolling aimlessly on his phone. Jess , furiously highlights a textbook at the table. Freya is meticulously arranging cutlery. Chloe is stirring a mug of tea.)     Jess:   Honestly, this Biology unit is killin’ me. Ms. Davies expects us to know everything about cellular respiration. It’s like, how’s that relevant to anything?! I’m never gonna need to know that in real life.   Chloe:   Tell me about it. Remember trying to learn the periodic table? Pure torture. At least you’re actually  doing  something, Liam. Still glued to that phone, are ya?   Liam:   Aye, well, what else is there to do? Another rejection email this mornin’. "Whilst your skills are impressive..." Blah, blah, blah. Impressive enough to not get a bloody job, apparently.   Freya:   Liam, don't get yourself down. You've applied to loads. Remember that placement at the railway? That could've been somethin'.   Liam:   Aye, the railway. Remember how they said they were gonna get back to me weeks ago? They probably booked someone else ages ago. Honestly, I'm startin' to think I’m cursed. All those degrees, top o’ the class, and I can’t even get a shift in a café.   Jess:   Don't say that, Liam. It's the job market, innit? It's tough for everyone, especially now. At least you  have  a degree. Half the lads I know left school at sixteen.   Chloe:   It’s not just the jobs, Liam. It’s the money, isn’t it? Mum was on about needing the gas bill paid, and I’m trying to save for a trip to Leeds next month. It's all piling up.   Liam:   Aye, the gas bill’s a nightmare. I offered to pay it this month but… well, you know. She doesn't need to hear me moanin’ on. Gets her down.   Freya:   Your mum knows you're trying, love. She worries, that's all. And we do too, you know.   Jess:   Speaking of money, did anyone see that new show on Netflix, 'Beckham'? Apparently it's brilliant. But I'm not paying ten quid a month just for David Beckham’s autobiography in posh lights.   Chloe:   It looks good! I heard Posh Spice is a right character in it. Worth a free trial, maybe? My student discount should cover some of it.   Liam:   Student discounts. Luxury. I remember them. Used to spend all my grant on pizza and Player’s.

Tell me about it. Sounds stressful. You always look proper wiped after these things. Is it all the Yorkshire charm they can’t handle, do you reckon? Yorkshire charm? Might be somethin' in that. Though I think it’s mostly the details. You lot in the events industry, you’re just… juggling flaming torches while riding a unicycle, aren’t ya? I spent most of my life sat on the sofa, so, the concept's a bit foreign to me. That's a fair assessment. Flaming torches, definitely. Though, this one was particularly rough. We had a keynote speaker who insisted on having bottled spring water imported  from Iceland , because apparently tap water affects his voice. Iceland! And he complained it wasn’t chilled enough. Iceland! Blimey. Some people, eh? You get those sorts. Reminds me of old Mr. Peterson down the road, always moanin’ about the tea not bein’ strong enough. He’d practically have a breakdown about it. It's ridiculous. Speaking of breakdowns, I need to find some motivation. I said I’d start going to that yoga class Sarah keeps banging on about. She’s convinced it’ll sort me out. Yoga, is it? Is that the stretchy trousers thing? I tried a bit of gentle stretching once. Pulled a muscle in my back. Didn’t feel very “zen” after that. Best stick to a proper walk, I reckon. Fresh air does wonders. Get you out of that office. I know, I know. But I’m so tired, even the thought of a walk feels exhausting. Work just drains me. It's rewarding, I suppose, seeing the conferences come together, but the lead-up is just… relentless. I’m starting to think I might need to actually  talk  to someone about stress management. Now, that's no bad thing. Talkin’ things through always helps. My sister used to get right stressed with her job, teaching. Eventually, she had to take a long break. Best thing she ever did, really. Found her feet again, she did. See, that's what I'm worried about. I don't want to have to take a break! I like my job, genuinely. It’s just… a lot. And the salary’s alright, you know? Better than what I was on before. Aye, that’s important. Can’t be givin’ up a good thing for nothin’. Maybe just try those yoga classes.

Speaker_1  But Dad, Mr. Davies was saying in history, he was… you know… a really good artist! Before... everything. A really good artist who chose to use his talent to fuel an unbelievable hate campaign. There’s a difference, isn’t there, lad? Doesn't excuse anything. Besides, you were going on about his moustache. Wild claims about it giving him special powers… It did look really focused, though! Like it was designed for… commanding. Commanding what? Mass destruction? Honestly. It's fascinating, sure, from a historical perspective, understanding the propaganda and all that. But let's not romanticize the man himself. And please, let's not call him 'really good' when he's responsible for so much devastation. Less Hitler, more clearing this up, yeah? Your mother will be wanting the kitchen spotless. Fine. But I’m still not convinced he didn’t have  some  artistic talent. What about Van Gogh? He wasn’t exactly… normal. Van Gogh struggled with mental health, lad. That's a completely different situation and shouldn't be used to make excuses for atrocities. Look, I ran into Kev from the factory this morning. He was telling me he's growing a proper beard now. Full Viking, he says. Seriously? A proper one? Got like, a handlebar or something? No, nothing fancy. Just... bushy. He says it gives him confidence. Apparently, his wife wasn’t thrilled at first. Said she couldn’t see him anymore when he was kissing her. Goodness! That’s a story, that is. Though I can see it. Sometimes a bit of facial hair can look a bit… overwhelming. Right, lads, tennis tomorrow? The weather's supposed to be decent. We could get a game in before you lot start obsessing over Instagram again. Probably. Depends if Chloe’s free. She said she might be going to that music festival… Chloe? Is that your girlfriend? You hardly ever talk about her. Yeah, Chloe. We've been seeing each other for, like, a few weeks now. It’s just… you know… Instagram is where most of our communication happens. It's easier. Easier isn’t always better, son. You’re missing out on actual conversation. A phone call, a walk, just talking face to face… that’s how you  really  get to know someone. It’s just how everyone does it, though, isn't it? Like, if you don't tag something, did it even happen?

…and honestly, Mum, I just don’t  get  it. Why would anyone give you a ceramic badger? Like, seriously? What are you even supposed to  do  with a ceramic badger? Och, love, you’ll find a use for it. Gran used to get all sorts, didn't she? Remember that porcelain poodle with the wonky eye? Sat on the mantlepiece for years. It were a bit naff, mind you, but it were Gran’s. Aye, that poodle! Nobody knew where it came from. Must’ve been one o’ Brenda’s cousins, bless her. She always had a strange taste in… decorations. Right? It’s just… unnecessary. It’s like, Auntie Carol clearly thought she was being thoughtful, but… a badger! We're trying to declutter, remember? And the tip's already rammed. I volunteered to take the old sofa cushions, but even  that  felt too much. Well, you can't just chuck everything, can you? Some folk put a lot o' heart into giving gifts, even if they’re a bit…odd. Besides, we’re already going to the tip to get rid of that rickety old table, aren’t we? The one we bought for ANON’s Beaver Scout Christmas party last year? Remember that chaos? Little lads covered in glitter everywhere. Oh, goodness me. That  was  a sight. Little Thomas, bless his heart, glued a pompom to Mrs. Higgins' shoe. She didn't even notice for half an hour! Oh my god, I’d forgotten! It was madness. Right, so about this furniture… I saw a lovely set at ‘Oak & Ash’ in Macclesfield. Proper solid wood, not that flatpack stuff. But it's pricey. We'd need to save, wouldn't we? Aye, proper furniture lasts. Gran always said, “Buy good, buy once.” These flatpacks fall apart after a year. But saving… that'll take us a while. Speaking o’ saving, have you heard about ANON's friend, Sarah? Her partner’s really poorly, isn't he? I read on Facebook… Yeah, it’s awful. Apparently, it’s getting worse. They're starting to suspect dementia. It’s heartbreaking, seeing her trying to juggle everything. She’s trying to manage him and the kids, and I offered to help, but she’s determined to do it all herself. That's women for ya. Stubborn as anything. Just like my mam. You know what she did? She started washing everyone else’s clothes.

…and honestly, Mum, the way they’ve gone about it is just…shocking. No real consultation, just a blanket announcement that half the team is potentially at risk. It's all so vague. They keep using phrases like ‘restructuring’ and ‘streamlining’ – it’s corporate-speak for ‘we’re getting rid of people to save money.’ Well, that's the way things are, love. Always 've been. They don't care about little people, do they? Not like they used to. I remember when Norwich Union – bless its cotton socks – actually  explained  things. This generation, though…they just want the bottom line. Not nice, is it? It’s not. And I’m trying to be positive, you know? Putting together a decent CV, looking at other jobs, but the market's awful. All these Project Coordinator roles want five years' experience and a Masters! I’ve got three years and a degree, which is apparently not enough. Three years is decent, love. Don't undersell yourself. You're a clever girl, you always 'ave been. Remember when you built that enormous Lego castle at Christmas when you were eight? Practically an architect! So don't you worry about a bit o’ bureaucratic nonsense. We’ll figure something out. What about that recruitment agency you mentioned? The one with the bloke called…Simon? Simon from Apex Recruitment. Yes, I’m sending him my CV on Monday. I’m slightly terrified, to be honest. What are we doing this weekend, by the way? I was thinking I could come over Saturday and we could actually have a proper pottering day? Clean out the garage, maybe? That sounds lovely, duck. Saturday's good. Grandad’s coming over on Sunday for lunch though, you know. He’s been complaining about his knees again. You could bring over that protein powder you get from the gym? He says it helps with his…well, with everything, apparently. He's eating like a horse these days, the old man! More biscuits than I've ever seen him consume. Right, I’ll grab some. He's got you wrapped round his little finger, hasn't he? Still, he deserves some treating. Just wish I was as disciplined about the gym as you are! I skipped my session yesterday, felt dreadful afterwards. You’re getting seriously buff, Mum! Oh, don't be daft. It's just keeping the old bones moving, that’s all.

This is a bit… mushy, Mum. And why’s it got, like, bits of carrot in it? It's shepherd's pie, love. Finn loves shepherd’s pie, don’t you, my sweet? It's got bits of carrot and peas to be healthy. You used to love it. Remember? Like when Stick with Mick was on? Yeah, but I’m a bit older now, aren't I? I’m practically a teenager. Mick's a bit babyish. Although, that one episode, the one where he had to build a bridge out of… well, sticks… that was pretty clever. See? He’s not  all  babyish. Right, so we were talking about the summer holidays. Boring day today. What do you fancy doing? We can't go swimming 'til next week, you know. Swimming would be good. Anything would be better than sitting around. Liam said he's going to Clive’s for a kickabout tomorrow. Wanna come? Oh, that would be lovely, wouldn't it? But…Finn needs me, doesn't he? And I really need to tackle that pile of washing. It's a Mount Everest situation. Plus, remember what I said about helping around the house a bit more? Fine. But it's not fair. Liam's got loads of free time. It's not about fairness, it’s about chipping in. Maybe just an hour or two helping me with Finn, then you can zip off to Clive’s if he's still playing. What about we do some Japanese practice together afterwards? I’ve been trying to learn some phrases from that app, but it’s so confusing. I don't understand what ANON is saying half the time. He just goes…  mumble mumble, rapid noises . Japanese?! Why are you learning Japanese? It’s a challenge! And it’s good for the brain. Remember I said I wanted to learn something new? You could help me! You're good at picking things up. I’d rather be practicing guitar, to be honest. I was thinking about learning that riff from… you know… that band. The one with the really loud drums? Go for it! But after you’ve helped me sort out the laundry, agree? Do you think Finn would like to listen to your guitar playing? Maybe. He likes that weird singing you do. That’s because I’m being silly! Oh, Finn! Honestly, you’re a little rascal.

…Nah, proper dodgy, innit? Like, they tried to upsell me fluoride varnish  while  I was still strapped in the chair. Strapped in! Like I was a toddler! You got the varnish then? Was it worth it, after the trauma? Worth it? Liam, I spent half an hour afterwards trying to un-smell the mint. It was like a dentist’s office exploded in me mouth. And don’t even get me started on Dr. Henderson’s bedside manner. He kept saying “Lovely teeth, lovely teeth!” like he was commenting on me wallpaper, not me pearly whites. Sounds lovely. Proper Scouse charm, that. You know, writing’s going alright. I'm trying to get this short story down about a bloke who thinks he’s a pigeon. A pigeon? Seriously? Right, you are proper weird already. Why a pigeon? I dunno, innit? Trying to explore the anxieties of modern urban life, you know? Being lost, feeling disconnected. Plus, pigeons are ironically majestic. They just… are. Ironically majestic. You've got a way with words, ya know? Still, a pigeon? You should've gone with a badger. They're proper proper misunderstood, badgers. Badgers are already established misunderstood creatures! Pigeons have got a rough deal, they do. Blamed for everything. Just try and eat a chip in this city without getting a right mouthful from someone. True, true. Right forgetting your pigeon story for a minute, what about that gig we were thinking about next month? The one with the… what were they called? The Astral Tides? Yeah! Astral Tides. Proper indie-dream-pop, it is. Reckon it'll be a good one. Thinking of taking the Citibike down, you know, cycle down the waterfront. Bit of fresh air before drowning in swirling synths. Ooh, romantic! As long as you don’t end up tangled in the Mersey tunnel again. Remember that? Thought you were gonna end up as fish food. Don't remind me. My mum nearly had a heart attack. Nearly got doxxed on Twitter, too. "Midlands writer blunders into Mersey tunnel on Citibike!" The headlines practically wrote themselves. Proper embarrassing. Anyway, speaking of embarrassing, remember that holiday we took to Spain when we were, like, sixteen? You got spectacularly sunburnt. Like, lobster-red. Don’t, Finn! The shame! Me and the factor fifteen were not friends that year. You were drenched in factor fifty and practically glowing. Aye, I was.

…and honestly, Chloe, the florist just  didn’t  get it. I explained, several times, that I wanted something understated, you know? A sort of wild meadow feel. Instead, I got these… these enormous, perfectly symmetrical roses. Like something out of a bridal catalogue. It was just… not me, was it? No, Mum, I can picture it. Dreadful. Honestly, florists are a nightmare sometimes. They hear "Christening" and automatically think giant, pink, fluffy monstrosities. Did you at least have a word with the vicar? He’s usually quite good at smoothing things over. Not yet. Been a bit too busy trying to untangle the cake situation. Honestly, I’m starting to think baking Easter cakes is a conspiracy designed to make you look utterly incompetent. This second batch just… sank. Completely. Like a lead weight. Oh, Mum! You’re just being dramatic. Remember last year’s Christmas pudding? It was a bit… lopsided. But tasted delicious. That was different! That was a structural failure, not a complete collapse of the batter! This is… disheartening. Little Leo’s face will be so disappointed if there’s no proper Easter cake. I promised him a chocolate one, with little bunnies. Well, I can pop over this afternoon and help. Two sets of hands are better than one, especially when dealing with rebellious cake mix. It wouldn't be quite the same as having your famous recipe, but we could at least have something presentable. How's the planning going, then, for the actual Christening itself? Are you stressing? A little, if I’m honest. It's just… a lot. The catering, the flowers , the seating plan... and Auntie Brenda keeps emailing me about whether she can bring her miniature poodle, Princess Fluffybutt. Seriously! Princess Fluffybutt. Oh, goodness. You've got your work cut out for you. Absolutely no poodles! Tell her it's a church ceremony, and frankly, any animal could be disruptive. Although… Leo  would  love to see a poodle. I know! He's obsessed with dogs. It's just… Auntie Brenda. She’d wear a matching pink outfit with Princess Fluffybutt, I swear. Anyway, enough about Brenda's canine companion. How's the teaching going? Are you still enjoying it? Actually, yes! It's been really rewarding, especially with this class. They're a bit boisterous, but they’re lovely. I've been doing a project on local history - visiting the Litchfield Cathedral, learning about the Roman ruins… They’re really engaging with it.

Tell me about it, love. Happens every time, doesn’t it? The bright spark of an idea, massively over-engineered by someone who's never actually  been  in the classroom. Are you still at the same school then? Yeah, St. Jude’s. It’s… it’s fine. The kids are lovely, you know? It’s just the management, always wanting to demonstrate how much they’re 'improving' things, when they're actually making it harder. It's stressful, trying to tailor everything to the new guidelines whilst still keeping it engaging. How's retirement treating you, Carol? I can't imagine handing in that marking pile. Oh, it's lovely, absolutely lovely. Though, I do miss the children, truly. The admin, though? Don’t even get me started. I often think I traded one source of stress for another – gardening versus endless meetings! My little terrier, Winston, is keeping me busy though. He’s a right little character. Reminds me of my nephew, actually, all boundless energy. A terrier, you say? I've always wanted a dog, but living in a flat... and with the travel… it just wouldn’t work. My sister has a labrador, Daisy. She’s gentle as anything, but sheds  everywhere . It's a constant battle against tumbleweeds of fur. Labradors are like that, aren't they? Winston’s a Jack Russell cross, so he's a bit smaller, thank goodness. Less fur to hoover. Speaking of hoovering, have you seen those Dyson Airwraps? My daughter, Fiona, got one for Christmas. Honestly, the prices! It’s daylight robbery. But she swears by it. Said it’s revolutionised her hair. Oh, I've drooled over them! Absolutely gorgeous results, but… yeah, the price is just ridiculous. I stick to my trusty hairdryer and a good serum, thank you very much. Practicality, you know? Though Lizzie has been trying to convince me to have botox. Apparently, it’s all the rage. Botox? Oh, dear. Lizzie’s always been a bit… enthusiastic about those things. I’ve always thought a good moisturiser and a bit of laughter is the best treatment. You look lovely, dear, really you do. And Lizzie's got lovely children. How's Ben doing? Still studying engineering? He is! Just finished his second year at Birmingham Uni. He’s thriving, actually. He’s joined the robotics club, which is brilliant. He’s really passionate about it.

Blimey, yeah. My nan used to make the best treacle tart, swore it was all down to “a pinch of this and a smidge of that.” Never could replicate it. Proper frustrating. So, this Seder is brilliant, though. Really properly done. You’ve put loads of effort in, ANON & ANON. Thanks, Liam! It's a lot, but it’s worth it. I like making people happy with food. And the Matzah Ball Soup deserves a mention, right? It’s taken me three attempts to get it fluffy enough! You know, growing up, we always had this Seder, but it was a bit… rushed. My mum was always stressed. This is my first properly relaxed one. That’s lovely to hear, darling. It should be a joyous occasion, not a source of anxiety. The tradition is vital, you know. Connecting us to centuries of… well, everything. I was just reading an article on the etymology of the name ‘Passover’… fascinating how it links to the sparing of the firstborn. Right, proper deep dive there, Eleanor! I’m more of a ‘taste the food and enjoy the company’ kind of chap, myself. Though, I did stumble across a rather interesting article about the historical significance of maror – the bitter herbs. Apparently, it’s symbolic of the bitterness of slavery in Egypt. Bit heavy for a Friday night, eh? Yeah, a bit, Tom. Though, proper interesting. Speaking of travelling… anyone fancy Rome next year? I’m itching to see the Colosseum again, and, you know, stuff my face with pasta. Rome! I’m in! I've always wanted to go. Imagine all the incredible pastries… and maybe I could even find a decent patisserie class. Although, I doubt they’ll teach me anything Nonna didn’t already. Anyone else thinking of a trip somewhere? Rome is tempting... although Paris is calling my name. I haven’t been since… well, since Richard was alive. I’d love to revisit Le Pigeon d'Or, though I suspect their Ortolan prices would give me palpitations. Remember when we all went there after that film festival? Oh, man, that  was  a night. "Pulp Fiction" followed by a ridiculously expensive bird… what a combo! I was so broke afterwards. Speaking of films, I finally saw “Everything Everywhere All at Once.” Brilliant, absolutely brilliant. Heard good things! Need to add that to the list. Right, back to the Seder, though... Has anyone made any headway deciphering that Hebrew blessing?

Honestly, Sarah, I'm  still  fuming about the ending of 'The Silent Patient'. Absolutely baffling! I mean, I understand twists, but that felt… manufactured. Like the author just threw it in for shock value. Oh, love, you’re always so dramatic! I thought it was brilliant! Completely unexpected. Bit mad, mind you, but entertaining. Remember that awful one, years ago, with the disappearing vicar? That was  truly  baffling. This at least had a sort of… logic to it, in its own strange way. I actually preferred 'Daisy Jones & The Six'. It felt so much more…real, you know? The way they built the characters, the oral history format… it just drew you in. Plus, the audiobook was fantastic, full cast, really immersive. eBooks versus audiobooks, eh? That’s a whole other debate. I just can’t  stand  audiobooks. I need the physical feel of a book in my hands, the smell of the paper… it’s part of the experience. Can’t fault you there, love. Though my eyes aren’t what they used to be. I’ve been dabbling in eBooks a bit, especially for magazines. Easier on the old peepers. I’m attempting a bit of crocheting at the moment, actually. Started that blanket for little Leo. Oh, how’s that going? I'm trying to learn Tunisian crochet, but I'm utterly failing. It's just so confusing! All those loops and whatnot. My knitting's much better, but I want to expand my skills. Knitting's lovely. I’m working on a scarf for Daniel’s birthday. A nice chunky cable knit. He’s always complaining about being cold. He’s obsessed with that 'The Crown' series, you know. Absolutely glued to it. Are you watching it, Sarah? Course I am! Absolutely brilliant. Although, they took some liberties, didn't they? Especially with that Princess Margaret storyline. Felt a bit… embellished. Still, good entertainment. Leo’s been watching Peppa Pig again. Drives me barmy! I swear, I’m going to start talking like that pig! My nephew’s the same! Utterly addicted. We had his birthday party last weekend - bouncy castle, cake, the whole shebang. Exhausting, but worth it to see his little face light up. Speaking of exhausting, did you see that film 'Barbie'? I did. Didn’t like it. Found it terribly preachy. And frankly, rather silly. All that pink! Overwhelming. Oh, come on, Helen!

Right, then. Show me this… this beauty. You’ve got it all unpacked, I see? Feels a bit… rectangular, doesn’t it? Not like the old Nokias, all sturdy and curved. Remember those? You could drop a 3310 and it'd laugh in your face. This… this feels like it’d shatter if you looked at it wrong. Don't be such a drama queen, Dad! It's got Gorilla Glass, it's tougher than it looks. And it's so much faster! Honestly, waiting for pages to load on your ancient thing was a torture test. I nearly forfeited my sanity just trying to look up the pub's address. Ancient? It's perfectly serviceable! And it knows how to be a phone. You know,  make calls . This just seems like a miniature computer you’re desperately clinging to. It’s a bit… distracting, innit? All them flashing pictures and notifs. Distracting? It's  efficient . And I need it for my research. I’ve got databases and papers and PDFs crammed onto here. I can translate Finnish instantly if I need to! Trying to use your brick to access that would have been impossible. Listen, can you show me how you’ve got your data roaming set up? I'm trying to avoid astronomical charges. Roaming? Right, let’s see… Now, I’ve got that trick where you turn it off completely unless you’re actively searching for a signal. That usually works a treat. See? It’s grayed out. Makes ‘em panic when you’re away from a signal, used to do it for me when I were a lad. Brings you back to earth a bit. Just click that little menu button… there you go. Now, you need to do the same. Don't just leave it on ‘automatic’ – Elomatic's burnin' a hole in your pocket I reckon. Okay, okay, I get it. It's just… hiding. Right, greyed out. Posh. I swear, you’ve got some sort of wizardry about phones. I’m just lost in the menus with this thing. There's a ‘Preferred Network Type’ option... 5G, 4G LTE, 3G... which one should I choose? I’m never sure. Right, leave it on 4G LTE. Reliable enough. 5G’s all flash and bother, aye. You rarely get a decent signal anyway. Plus, saves your battery. Speaking of which, this thing’s battery life looks appalling.

But Mum, I already told you! Red Pandas are way cooler than cats. They’re like, fluffy and they climb trees and eat bamboo! My friend, Liam, he showed me a video of one balancing on a branch, it was proper awesome. Liam always did have a thing for weird animals, didn't he? Finn, darling, down now. No climbing on the sofa. See, Jack? Even Finn knows that’s not safe. Cats are lovely though, aren’t they? You know, I always wanted a Malamooche. A big fluffy one. You ever seen one, Jack? They're huge! Like a giant teddy bear. A Malamooche? Seriously, Mum? They look a bit… hairy. And they drool a lot, don't they? My cat, Winston, is much more refined. He doesn’t drool. He just… judges me. Winston  does  look like he's judging everyone. He's got that permanent frown. Right, speaking of presents, we need to sort something out for Emily’s birthday. You’re still thinking Red Panda themed, yeah? Yeah! A little Red Panda plushie, maybe? Or one of those sticker books. She's really getting into animals, isn’t she? Do you think she'd like that board game we got last Christmas? The one with the animals on it? Mmm, maybe. Let me have a think. Remember how excited she was last year? It's getting closer, isn't it? We need to firm up the party details. Auntie Sarah said she can bring the fairy lights. Yeah, and Dad's building the bouncy castle! He was moaning about it for ages, but he’s actually pretty excited. I'm thinking a Japanese theme, maybe? Like, we could watch one of those Japanese films afterwards – the ones with the robots? Oh, dear. I'm not sure Finn would be too keen on robots battling it out. He gets scared easily. Although… he  does  like that cartoon about the pandas. Maybe a little bit of both? Red Pandas and some gentle robots? We need to keep it simple for him. We could have a panda-shaped cake! And those little fortune cookies with silly jokes inside. Definitely. It’ll be brilliant. Oh, and I need to finish my homework. Can I use the iPad for that? It’s easier than using the laptop. It’s lighter. Yes, dear, you can use the iPad. Just remember to log off when you're done.

Aye, right? My Gran used to do that, too. Always had a candle too close to somethin’. Remember that year she tried to roast chestnuts over the fireplace? Ended up with charcoal and a load of soot all over the living room. Mum were fumin’. That sounds… chaotic. My Christmases were always a lot quieter. My mum, being Filipino, we’d always have a Noche Buena feast – roast pig, pancit, lumpia… it’s a huge deal. The whole family descends. Mass first, then the food, then presents. Very structured. Noche Buena, you say? How interesting! I do love hearing about different traditions. We were always very traditional here. Christmas pudding, of course, always made weeks in advance, stirred with a silver spoon - a little superstition, you see. My mother always said it brought good luck. And carols, of course. Lots and lots of carols. Now, carols… my wife, bless her, always said I murdered those carols. Couldn’t hold a tune to save my life. But I wasn't one for the traditional pudding. Too heavy for me! We always had a turkey, naturally, but with a proper gravy. None of that powdered stuff! And Brussels sprouts, cooked properly, not boiled to death. Brussels sprouts… right. Not my favourite, to be honest. My Mum always makes this weird stew with them, though, with sausages and potatoes. It’s proper hearty, though. Gets you through the cold. What’s the strangest Christmas tradition you’ve ever heard of, yeah? I think the strangest one I encountered was in Sweden. They have this goat… a giant straw goat that stands in the town square. And people keep trying to set it on fire! It’s supposed to bring good luck, but it's constant chaos. They rebuild it every year. Goodness me! That does sound rather… alarming. My goodness. Though, I suppose fire has always been a part of Christmas. Remember those flaming Christmas puddings they used to serve? Set alight with brandy – very dramatic, but quite dangerous. We had a terrible incident one year with my nephew… Now, now, Margaret, let’s not dwell on unfortunate events. Speaking of traditions, I remember when they started putting those electric fairy lights everywhere. Do you recall, Margaret? It was considered quite modern back then. My colleagues at the design firm were all experimenting with different circuits. Quite the novelty, you see. Aye, I can imagine.

"BritBox, eh? Bit niche for me, Sarah. I’m more of a ‘Line of Duty’ man. Though, I did try ‘The Shadow Syndicate’ a few weeks back. Didn’t quite grab me, to be honest. A bit too convoluted, I thought." "Convoluted? That's David's default assessment of anything that requires a degree of brainpower. Honestly, darling, it's clever, not complicated. Though I agree, 'Line of Duty' reigns supreme. The acting, the writing... simply brilliant." "See! Eleanor gets it. It’s the little details, the subtle shifts in character motivation… it's gorgeous storytelling! Anyway, enough about telly. How's work going, David? Still battling the spreadsheet monster?" "You have no idea. Johnson's decided he needs a weekly report on paperclip usage. Paperclip usage, Sarah! Apparently, it's a key performance indicator. I’m seriously considering requesting a transfer to the stationery department." He sighs dramatically. "And the new HR system? Utter chaos. I spent half the morning trying to input Mrs. Higgins' pet hamster's vaccination records." "Oh, David. You’re a saint. Sounds positively Dickensian. My writing, on the other hand, is… progressing. Slowly. I’m wrestling with the antagonist again. He's just not evil enough for my liking. Needs more… nuance, I suppose. But nuance is hard to inject effectively without making him just… boring." "You always were a perfectionist, Eleanor. That's why your books are so good. Have you decided yet if you're bringing that short story to the writing group next week?" "I'm thinking about it. It's a bit raw, a bit... personal. But feedback is essential, isn’t it? Speaking of essential, Sarah, did you ever order that new Kindle case? The one with the stand?" "Yes! It arrived yesterday. Absolutely lovely. Teal blue, just like I wanted. I was thinking of loading up a few detective novels for this weekend. Maybe I'll give 'The Shadow Syndicate' another shot. You've piqued my interest, David, even if you thought it was over-the-top." "Don’t hold your breath. I'll stick to my gritty police procedurals. Much more… grounded. Though, I did finish that biography of Churchill you lent me, Sarah. Quite fascinating, actually. All those cigar fumes!" "Speaking of lending, I’m nearly finished with 'The Nightingale’s Song'. You can borrow it after me, David. It's a real tearjerker. And Sarah, are you still seeing Fiona?

Timothy, eh? Good lad. Always offerin’ a ‘and, that one. Still, sheds…sheds are a worry, aren’t they? Always somethin’ about ‘em. Damp, rust... used to have a grand shed back in Costessey, I did. Full o’ tools. Wouldn’t be without my tools, you know. It’s very generous of him, Arthur. A fresh coat of paint will make a world of difference. You worry too much. You've been fretting over that shed for weeks. Honestly, it’s just a shed. Just a shed? Doreen, you wouldn't understand. A shed ain’t just a shed. It’s... it’s security, innit? A place to keep things safe, out of the weather. My granddad built that shed, you know. Used to keep ‘is prize-winning marrows in there. Big ‘uns they were, too. Proper whoppers. While I admire the sentimental value, Arthur, and the marrows do sound impressive, you're letting it consume you. Timothy’s offer is perfectly sound. He's a handyman, isn't he? And you know, even a professional painter wouldn't guarantee a shed will last forever. It's Norfolk weather, after all. Constant damp. Easy for you to say, Edward, livin’ in your fancy apartment with concierge service. Don’t have to worry about rust and rot settlin’ in. I’m just sayin’, I’ve had bad experiences with painters. Always cuttin’ corners. Last one tried to use that cheapo emulsion and I told ‘im where to go, I did. Oh, Arthur. You and your painters. It’s always a drama. Look, Timothy's different. He’s a good lad, from a good family. I’ve seen 'im around. He's reliable. And if it  does  need repainting again in a few years, well, you’ll just get Timothy to do it again. No need to get yourself knotted up now. Doreen’s right, Arthur. Focus on the positive. A freshly painted shed, a helpful grandson…and perhaps you could give Timothy a wee bonus for his trouble? It’s not an unreasonable request, and it’ll encourage him. A bonus, eh? I suppose… I suppose that wouldn’t go amiss. Wouldn’t want to be stingy, would I? Especially with Timothy. He’s a good lad, like I said. Always bringin' round biscuits, ‘e does. But what about the wood underneath? Is it sound, that’s what I’m wonderin’.

Right, so, final decisions then? We’re really pushing ahead with this leaving do for Horace, aren’t we? Feels a bit mad, five years with the man. It does, doesn't it? But he deserves a proper send-off, especially after all that grant wrangling. I reckon the pub crawl’s still the best plan. We’ve got Ms. Eleanor’s blessing, haven't we? Yes, Eleanor confirmed it’s permissible, as long as we adhere to the agreed upon noise levels and curfews. I’ve compiled the pub list, factoring in proximity and, crucially, decent vegetarian options. Aye, decent grub is essential! Last thing we need is a load of hungry researchers downing pints and getting grumpy. I've secured a booking at The Eagle. They do good platters, and apparently, they’ve got a fancy cocktail menu. Horace  is  a connoisseur, innit? The Eagle is a great choice, Chloe! Solid reputation. I just hope Horace isn’t expecting a full-blown American-style retirement bash. He’s got some old habits, that man, talking about luaus and whatnot. Don’t remind me! He keeps suggesting we get a limbo competition. I think we should gently steer him away from that. Anyway, I think we’re pretty much set then. I'll finalise the invites and circulate them. Before we get completely lost in pub plans, did anyone see that bee trapped in the window earlier? Poor thing was absolutely frantic. Yes, I did. I tried to shoo it out, but it just kept buzzing against the glass. Such a shame. I had a similar thing happen at home last week. Little thing trapped in the bathroom. I managed to guide it out with a newspaper, though. Took a good twenty minutes and a lot of patience! I’m terrible with insects! Absolutely petrified. You know, in Pennsylvania, we have these giant dragonflies… they're beautiful, but I still scream. My sister's the bee-whisperer, she's always rescuing them. Honestly, it's heartbreaking when they're trapped like that. They’re so vital, aren’t they? I was reading about the decline in bee populations – it’s terrifying. We really should have a little water station outside with flowers to help them when the weather’s like this. We  are  researchers, after all – maybe a little study on bee behaviour around the building? Now  that’s  a project I could get behind!

Honestly, Mrs. Davies is  determined  to make our lives miserable. What now? Don't tell me another pop quiz? She’s been throwing them at us like confetti lately. Worse, actually. Remember how I was saying I was struggling a bit with the Shakespeare extract? "Romeo and Juliet," you know? The bit with the balcony? Vaguely. You said you were finding it a bit…flowery? Too much "wherefore art thou" and not enough, like, actual understanding. Exactly! And she’s decided my "lack of comprehension" warrants a presentation in front of the whole class. A PRESENTATION, Anya! On Shakespeare! Like I'm some sort of literary expert. No way! That's brutal. She's got it in for you, hasn't she? Did you try asking her for extra help? Yeah, I did. She just said I needed to "engage with the text more deeply" and “cultivate a more proactive learning approach.” Honestly, Anya, what is she even saying? It’s teacher-speak for "figure it out yourself, you're struggling." She’s definitely got a way with words, hasn’t she? Look, don't panic. It’s just one class, right? And it's not like you can't do it. We can totally work on it. We'll break it down. Which bit are you finding the hardest? Honestly, all of it! The language is just so… old! And the metaphors! Like, what even  is  a “starry host” supposed to mean? It’s confusing! And then trying to  explain  that to everyone else... I’ll just freeze up and blush. Okay, okay. Deep breaths. Right, "starry host"... Think of it like a group of stars. Like, a whole bunch of them all shining together. It's just a poetic way of saying… it’s a lot of stars! See? Not so scary. I guess not. But I still have to  analyse  it. Why Romeo used that phrase. What it means about his character. It's just...a lot. Right. Okay. Let's start with the basics. Why do you think Romeo uses such… extravagant language in the first place? He’s clearly smitten, isn't he? Well, yeah. He's obsessed! He’s like, completely head over heels. Which is a bit ridiculous, isn’t it? All that poetic rambling. Exactly! It shows how intensely he feels. He's trying to impress her, you know? Like, 'look how clever and romantic I am!'

Honestly, Mum, I'm  still  stressed about that presentation. It's next Tuesday, and I’m nowhere near polished. I feel like I'm just throwing words at a screen. Aye, lass, you always were a worrier. Remember when you were little, and you’d fret for a week about the school nativity? You were a shepherd, for goodness sake! What could possibly go wrong? It felt  very  important at the time. This is different, though. This presentation is affecting the whole restructure in the admin department. If it doesn't go well, it could… well, you know. Relax, Elara. You're brilliant. You always overthink things. Remember the Henderson accounts fiasco last year? You sorted that out in a week. This is just another Tuesday. That was  different , Liam. That was a genuine crisis. This is just… pressure. And Mr. Davies is being particularly… intense. He keeps dropping hints about needing “results” and “streamlining.” It’s awful. Aye, some managers are like that. All bark and no bite, usually. Still, you’ve got a good head on your shoulders, love. What’s the main thing you're struggling with? Is it the data itself, or just explaining it? It’s explaining it simply, I think. It’s really complicated stuff - the new budget allocation, the software integration… I don't want to bore them to tears but I also want to sound competent. The irony! Okay, so break it down. Think about the key takeaways. What’s the one thing you  need  them to remember? Focus on that. And practice! Record yourself, embarrassing as it is. I wouldn’t put that past me. I probably look like a strangled cat. You're far too hard on yourself, pet. Now, let's talk about something more pleasant. Your Auntie Brenda rang yesterday, did you hear? She's finally getting that hip replacement she’s been moaning about for years. Oh, that's fantastic news! I'll give her a call tomorrow. It's about time. How’s she been managing? Struggling, to be honest. She was using a walking stick just to get to the shops. It affected her a lot. She’s worried about the recovery, of course, but she's mostly just relieved. She was saying she misses coming down for Sunday lunches. Speaking of Sunday lunches… Mum, you’re making roast chicken again next week, right? I’m officially claiming dibs on the drumstick.

…and honestly, the consultant just kept saying, "We're doing everything we can, Sarah. Everything.” It’s infuriating, isn’t it? Like I’m supposed to just  believe  that. I asked about trial options, different specialists… they just brushed it off. Said this is the standard protocol. Standard protocol for  who  exactly? Well, love, you know how these things are. They’ve got their processes. Doesn't mean they aren't trying, mind. Though, I know exactly what you mean about feeling brushed off. Happened to my Nan with her hip replacement, same song and dance. It's not just the feeling brushed off, it's… I’m feeling utterly powerless. And it's impacting everything. Like, I had that meeting with Carter & Hughes today, the one I was telling you about? Complete disaster. Couldn't focus, kept thinking about the scans. Lost a potential deal, probably. Oh, love, that's rotten. Proper rotten. You've worked so hard for that account. Did you tell them what was going on? No! Absolutely not. Can't. They'd treat me like I'm made of glass. "Don't stress yourself, Emily," they’d say. "Take some time off." As if that’s going to solve anything! It's a tricky balance, isn't it? Keeping things professional, but also… needing to be honest about why I’m slightly off my game. Aye, it is. Let me get you a biscuit. So, how’s Finn doing? Still struggling with maths? Don’t even get me started on Finn. He got detention this week. For apparently "disruptive behaviour." When I spoke to the teacher, she said he was arguing about the fairness of the homework. Said it was too hard! Honestly, at fifteen, they think they know everything. They do, don't they? They’re practicing. Remember when you were that age? Arguing with your dad about curfew? Oh god, don’t remind me. My dad was terrifying! Still, I can see Finn's point. The homework was ridiculously complex. And he’s putting so much pressure on himself to get into Cambridge. It’s exhausting just watching him. Cambridge's a long way off yet, love. He needs to enjoy being fifteen. Tell him to go see his mate Liam this weekend. A bit of fresh air and a bit of football will do him good. Liam seems a sensible lad. Yes, Liam’s a good influence.

Right, I’m officially knackered. Another double shift down The Heron. Honestly, I feel like I've aged about ten years in the last six months. Six months? Still? I thought you said you were only doing it until Christmas to pay off that… documentary film equipment, was it? Aye, that’s right. The camera gear. Fancy, innit? But Christmas came and went, and then… well, then Mum’s washing machine decided to give up the ghost, and then Uncle Barry needed a new hip. It just… spiralled, didn’t it? Suddenly, I was relying on those tips more than I’d planned. Sounds rough. So, you're still slinging pints then? I mean, it’s good money, I guess. Much better than the call centre jobs everyone’s applying for. It is, that’s true. Gotta pay bills, don’t I? It’s just… soul-destroying sometimes. You get all sorts in there, you know? So many lads on their stag dos, roaring about. And then there's the older ladies, coming in for a quiet sherry and a moan about the weather. I try and give everyone a bit of a smile, keep things pleasant, but after eight hours on my feet, wiping spillage and listening to football results… it takes it out of ya. I can imagine. It's definitely a different vibe to lectures. I mean, at least lectures are... intellectually stimulating, mostly. Though Professor Davies last week spent twenty minutes debating the socioeconomic impact of badger setts. Truly bizarre. Badger setts, eh? Sounds about right for university. You’re studying history, aren't you? Still enjoying it? Yeah, mostly. Some weeks I feel like I’m drowning in primary sources, others I’m actually fascinated. Trying to piece together a genuine human narrative from dusty old documents… it’s pretty cool. But the pressure's building up for the dissertation. I'm stuck on choosing a topic. I liked the bit on Tudor embroidery, but my tutor said it wasn't…  substantial  enough. Substantial! Sounds like those posh lecturers who look down their noses at you because you haven’t got a silver spoon. Don’t you let him squash your interest. Tudor embroidery sounds dead interesting to me. That's what I thought! But he's got this reputation. Everyone's terrified of him. Anyway, what about you? Anything interesting happening at The Heron besides drunk stag parties?

Sounds… memorable, at least. Blackpool, eh? Bold choice for a relaxing getaway. I went last year, you know, just a weekend with the missus. The Pleasure Beach is a proper assault on the senses. My head was spinning for hours afterwards. Blackpool's got a certain… charm. Don’t get me wrong, I love a bit of seaside kitsch, but it ain’t exactly Barbados, is it? I’m proper jealous of Moira though, going to Ireland. Always wanted to see the Cliffs of Moher. Oh, the Cliffs! They're even grander than the pictures, love. Breathtaking. I spent a good hour just standing there, feeling like a tiny speck in the universe. Dublin itself is lovely too, of course, but I always head straight out to the countryside. Gets too much hustle and bustle in the city for me. Did you know, when I was a wee girl, growing up near… well, let’s just say a small village in County Kerry… we’d collect shells and make little fairy houses on the beach. Fairy houses. Charming. I was battling rush hour on the M6 this weekend. Went down to the Cotswolds, needed a bit of green, you know? Escaping the urban sprawl and all that. Found a lovely little pub in Bourton-on-the-Water, proper picturesque. Had a pint of Old Speckled Hen. Bliss. Though, the price of a Sunday roast these days… outrageous. Tell me about it! Everything's gone up. My missus wanted to go to the Lake District this year. I had to gently suggest a picnic in Peel Park instead. Saved us a fortune. Though, she did threaten to replace all my socks with flamingo ones… Flamingo socks! That's wicked, love! You’re a brave man. I reckon a picnic's a good shout. We had one by the canal last week. Simple pleasures, eh? Though, the ducks kept trying to steal our sandwiches. Little blighters. I swear, one of them looked me right in the eye, like it was judging my choice of fillings. Ducks are cheeky things, alright. They've got a right to the crumbs, I suppose. It reminds me of a story my grandmother used to tell...About a Leprechaun who'd steal your dinner if he thought you were being greedy… a wee fellow with a mischievous grin. Leprechauns and ducks… sounds like a wonderfully chaotic holiday. My week was less supernatural, more spreadsheet-based, to be honest.
